akhfash:8-8.t: He said: ﴿وَٱلْخَيْلَ وَٱلْبِغَالَ وَٱلْحَمِيرَ لِتَرْكَبُوهَا﴾, accusative, i.e. "and Allah made the horses, the mules and the donkeys and made them (زِينَةً, an adornment)".

akhfash:9-9.t: He said: ﴿وَمِنْهَا جَآئِرٌ﴾, i.e. "and of the way (السبيل)", because it is feminine in the dialect of the people of the Ḥijāz.

akhfash:12-12.t:
He said: ﴿وَٱلْنُّجُومُ مُسَخَّرَاتٌ﴾, on the sense of "سُخِّرَتْ النُّجُومُ" (the stars were made subservient), or [the accusative] "جَعَلَ النُّجُومَ مُسَخَّراتٍ" (He made the stars subservient). It is permissible to imply a verb other than the first because that implied verb is like the overt one in meaning. The Arabs do what is more extreme than this. The rajaz poet said [and it is the two hundred and thirty-eighth poetic witness]:
تَسْمَعُ فِي أَجْوافِهِنَّ صَرَدَا * وَفِي اليَدَيْنِ جُسْأَةً وَبَدَدا
(You hear a rumbling in their bellies, and [see] in the forelegs stiffness and wide spacing.)
This is in the sense of ﴿وَتَرَى في اليَدَيْنِ الجُسْأَة﴾ (and you see in the forelegs the stiffness) — [which is] dryness — and "البَدَد" [which is] "wide spacing". [Translator's note: the source sets this paraphrase in ﴿…﴾ although it is not a Qur'anic text.]

akhfash:13-13.t: He said: ﴿وَمَا ذَرَأَ لَكُمْ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ مُخْتَلِفاً أَلْوَانُهُ﴾; he says: He created for you and spread out for you.

akhfash:21-21.t: He said: ﴿أَمْواتٌ غَيْرُ أَحْيَآءٍ﴾, by way of tawkīd (emphasis).

akhfash:30-30.t: He said: ﴿وَقِيلَ لِلَّذِينَ ٱتَّقَوْاْ مَاذَا أَنْزَلَ رَبُّكُمْ قَالُواْ خَيْراً﴾: He made "ماذا" have the status of "ما" alone.

akhfash:37-37.t: He said: ﴿إِن تَحْرِصْ﴾, because it is from "حَرَصَ" "يَحْرِصُ".

akhfash:48-48.t:
When you pause on (يَتَفَيّؤُا) you say "يَتَفَيَّأْ", just as you say with the ʿayn "تَتَفَّيعْ" with jussive-like sukūn; and if you wish you may give it a trace of the ḍamma (ishmām) or a slurred vowel (rawm), as you do in "هذا حَجَرُ".
And He said ﴿عَنِ ٱلْيَمِينِ وَٱلْشَّمَآئِلِ سُجَّداً لِلَّهِ وَهُمْ دَاخِرُونَ﴾: He made them masculine though they are not humans, because when He described them as obedient they resembled rational beings. And He made "اليمين" (the right) apply to the group, like ﴿وَيُوَلُّونَ ٱلدُّبُرَ﴾.

akhfash:49-49.t: He said: ﴿وَلِلَّهِ يَسْجُدُ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي ٱلأَرْضِ مِن دَآبَّةٍ﴾, meaning "of the creatures", and made do with the singular, as you say "ما أَتاَنِي من رَجُلٍ" (no man came to me), i.e. none of the men like him came to me.

akhfash:53-53.t: He said: ﴿وَمَا بِكُم مِّن نِّعْمَةٍ فَمِنَ ٱللَّهِ﴾: because (ما) has the status of (من) [i.e. a conditional/relative], He introduced the khabar with fāʾ.

akhfash:67-67.t: He said: ﴿وَمِن ثَمَرَاتِ ٱلنَّخِيلِ وَٱلأَعْنَابِ تَتَّخِذُونَ مِنْهُ سَكَراً وَرِزْقاً حَسَناً﴾ and did not say "مِنها" (from them), because He implied "الشَيْءَ" (something), as though He said "and of them is something from which you take intoxicant".

akhfash:68-68.t: He said: ﴿إِلَىٰ ٱلنَّحْلِ أَنِ ٱتَّخِذِي﴾, in the feminine, in the dialect of the people of the Ḥijāz; others say "هُوَ النَّحْل" (masculine). Likewise every collective plural which differs from its singular only by the hāʾ, such as "البُرُّ" (wheat) and "الشَعِيرُ" (barley), is feminine in their dialect.

akhfash:69-69.t: He said: ﴿ذُلُلاً﴾; its singular is "الذَلُولُ" (tractable), and the plural of "الذَّلُول" is "الذُلُل".

akhfash:72-72.t: He said: ﴿بَنِينَ وَحَفَدَةً﴾; their singular is "الحافِدُ" (grandson, helper).

akhfash:73-73.t: He said: ﴿رِزْقاً مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ شَيْئاً﴾: He made "الشَيْء" a badal (substitute) for "الرِّزْق", and it means "they do not possess any provision, little or much". Some said: "الرِّزْقُ is an action that falls on the thing", meaning "they are not able to provide anything".

akhfash:76-76.t: He said: ﴿أَيْنَمَا يُوَجِّههُّ لاَ يَأْتِ بِخَيْرٍ﴾, because (أينّما) is one of the particles of condition (ḥurūf al-mujāzāt).

akhfash:81-81.t: He said: ﴿مِّنَ ٱلْجِبَالِ أَكْنَاناً﴾; its singular is "الكِنّ" (shelter).

akhfash:91-91.t: He said: ﴿وَأَوْفُواْ بِعَهْدِ ٱللَّهِ﴾. You say "أَوْفَيْتُ بالعَهْد" and "وَفَيْتُ بالعَهْد" (I fulfilled the covenant); and when you say "العَهْدَ" [as a direct object], you say "أَوْفَيْتُ العَهْدَ" with the alif.

akhfash:92-92.t: He said: ﴿أَنكَاثاً﴾; its singular is "النِّكْثُ" (untwisted strand).

akhfash:106-106.t: He said: ﴿مَن كَفَرَ بِٱللَّهِ مِن بَعْدِ إيمَانِهِ إِلاَّ مَنْ أُكْرِهَ وَقَلْبُهُ مُطْمَئِنٌّ بِٱلإِيمَانِ وَلَـٰكِن مَّن شَرَحَ بِالْكُفْرِ صَدْراً فَعَلَيْهِمْ غَضَبٌ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ﴾: [فعليهم غضب] is the khabar (predicate) of His words (وَلَكِنْ مَنْ شَرَحَ); then His words ﴿مَن كَفَرَ بِٱللَّهِ مِن بَعْدِ إيمَانِهِ﴾ entered with it, so He gave a single predicate about them both, since that indicates the meaning.

akhfash:111-111.t: He said: ﴿كُلُّ نَفْسٍ تُجَادِلُ عَن نَّفْسِهَا﴾, because the meaning of (كلُّ نَفْسٍ) is "every human being"; He used the feminine because "النفس" (soul) is treated as feminine and masculine. One says "ما جَاءَتْنِي نَفْسٌ واحدةٌ" and "ما جاءَنِي نَفْسٌ واحدٌ" (not a single soul came to me).

akhfash:116-116.t: He said: ﴿أَلْسِنَتُكُمُ ٱلْكَذِبَ﴾: He made (ما تَصِفُ) [what] their tongues [describe] a noun for the action [a maṣdar], as though He said: "and do not say, because of your tongues' describing, (الكَذِبَ هذا حَلاَلٌ, the lie: this is lawful)". Some read (الكَذِبِ) in the genitive; he says: "and do not say of the lie that your tongues describe". Some read (الكُذُبُ) in the nominative and made (الكُذُبَ) an adjective of "the tongues", as though He said "lying tongues".

akhfash:121-121.t: He said: ﴿شَاكِراً لأَنْعُمِهِ﴾ and He said ﴿فَكَفَرَتْ بِأَنْعُمِ ٱللَّهِ﴾: He made "النِّعْمَة" (favour) plural as "أَنْعُمٍ", as He said ﴿حَتَّىٰ إِذَا بَلَغَ أَشُدُّه﴾, which they claimed is the plural of "الشِدَّة".

celaleyn:1-1.t: When the idolaters thought the punishment slow in coming, there was revealed ﴿أَتَى أَمْرُ اللَّهِ﴾ i.e. the Hour; it comes in the past-tense form because its occurrence is certain, i.e. it has drawn near ﴿فَلَا تَسْتَعْجِلُوهُ﴾ do not seek it before its time, for it will inevitably occur ﴿سُبْحَانَهُ﴾ declaring Him transcendent ﴿وَتَعَالَى عَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ﴾ with Him, of others.

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿يُنَزِّلُ الْمَلَائِكَةَ﴾ i.e. Jibrīl ﴿بِالرُّوحِ﴾ with the revelation ﴿مِنْ أَمْرِهِ﴾ by His will ﴿عَلَى مَنْ يَشَاءُ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ﴾ and they are the prophets ﴿أَنْ﴾ explicative (mufassira) ﴿أَنْذِرُوا﴾ warn the disbelievers of the punishment and inform them ﴿أَنَّهُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنَا فَاتَّقُونِ﴾ fear Me.

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿خَلَقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ بِالْحَقِّ﴾ i.e. rightfully ﴿تَعَالَى عَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ﴾ with Him, of idols.

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿خَلَقَ الْإِنْسَانَ مِنْ نُطْفَةٍ﴾ semen, until He made him strong and robust ﴿فَإِذَا هُوَ خَصِيمٌ﴾ intensely disputatious ﴿مُبِينٌ﴾ making it plain in denying the resurrection, saying {مَنْ يُحْيِي الْعِظَامَ وَهِيَ رَمِيمٌ}.

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿وَالْأَنْعَامَ﴾ camels, cattle and sheep; it is accusative by an implied (muqaddar) verb, explained by ﴿خَلَقَهَا لَكُمْ﴾ among people in general ﴿فِيهَا دِفْءٌ﴾ that by which you keep warm, of garments and cloaks made from their hair and wool ﴿وَمَنَافِعُ﴾ of offspring, milk and riding ﴿وَمِنْهَا تَأْكُلُونَ﴾ the ẓarf (adverbial phrase) is placed first for the sake of the verse-ending (fāṣila).

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿وَلَكُمْ فِيهَا جَمَالٌ﴾ adornment ﴿حِينَ تُرِيحُونَ﴾ you bring them back to their resting place in the evening ﴿وَحِينَ تَسْرَحُونَ﴾ you take them out to pasture in the morning.

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿وَتَحْمِلُ أَثْقَالَكُمْ﴾ your loads ﴿إِلَى بَلَدٍ لَمْ تَكُونُوا بَالِغِيهِ﴾ reaching it, without camels ﴿إِلَّا بِشِقِّ الْأَنْفُسِ﴾ with their exertion ﴿إِنَّ رَبَّكُمْ لَرَءُوفٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾ to you, in that He created them for you.

celaleyn:8-8.t: ﴿وَ﴾ He created ﴿الْخَيْلَ وَالْبِغَالَ وَالْحَمِيرَ لِتَرْكَبُوهَا وَزِينَةً﴾ a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose); and giving these two as the reason, by way of making the blessings known, does not exclude their having been created for other purposes, such as eating in the case of horses, which is established by a hadith in the two Ṣaḥīḥs ﴿وَيَخْلُقُ مَا لَا تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ of wondrous, strange things.

celaleyn:9-9.t: ﴿وَعَلَى اللَّهِ قَصْدُ السَّبِيلِ﴾ i.e. making clear the straight path ﴿وَمِنْهَا﴾ i.e. of the paths ﴿جَائِرٌ﴾ deviating from straightness ﴿وَلَوْ شَاءَ﴾ your guidance ﴿لَهَدَاكُمْ﴾ to the straight path ﴿أَجْمَعِينَ﴾ so that you would be guided to it by your own choice.

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿هُوَ الَّذِي أَنْزَلَ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مَاءً لَكُمْ مِنْهُ شَرَابٌ﴾ which you drink ﴿وَمِنْهُ شَجَرٌ﴾ which grows because of it ﴿فِيهِ تُسِيمُونَ﴾ you pasture your animals.

celaleyn:11-11.t: ﴿يُنْبِتُ لَكُمْ بِهِ الزَّرْعَ وَالزَّيْتُونَ وَالنَّخِيلَ وَالْأَعْنَابَ وَمِنْ كُلِّ الثَّمَرَاتِ إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ﴾ which has been mentioned ﴿لَآيَةً﴾ indicating His oneness, exalted is He ﴿لِقَوْمٍ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ﴾ about His making, and so believe.

celaleyn:12-12.t: ﴿وَسَخَّرَ لَكُمُ اللَّيْلَ وَالنَّهَارَ وَالشَّمْسَ﴾ in the accusative, conjoined to what precedes, and in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) ﴿وَالْقَمَرَ وَالنُّجُومُ﴾ in both ways ﴿مُسَخَّرَاتٍ﴾ in the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and in the nominative as a khabar (predicate) [مُسَخَّرَاتٌ] ﴿بِأَمْرِهِ﴾ by His will ﴿إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لَآيَاتٍ لِقَوْمٍ يَعْقِلُونَ﴾ who reflect.

celaleyn:13-13.t: ﴿وَ﴾ He subjected to you ﴿مَا ذَرَأَ﴾ He created ﴿لَكُمْ فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ of animals, plants and so on ﴿مُخْتَلِفًا أَلْوَانُهُ﴾ such as red, yellow, green and others ﴿إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لَآيَةً لِقَوْمٍ يَذَّكَّرُونَ﴾ who take heed.

celaleyn:14-14.t: ﴿وَهُوَ الَّذِي سَخَّرَ الْبَحْرَ﴾ made it tractable for sailing and for diving in it ﴿لِتَأْكُلُوا مِنْهُ لَحْمًا طَرِيًّا﴾ it is fish ﴿وَتَسْتَخْرِجُوا مِنْهُ حِلْيَةً تَلْبَسُونَهَا﴾ it is pearls and coral ﴿وَتَرَى﴾ you see ﴿الْفُلْكَ﴾ the ships ﴿مَوَاخِرَ فِيهِ﴾ ploughing the water, i.e. cleaving it as they run through it, coming and going with one and the same wind ﴿وَلِتَبْتَغُوا﴾ conjoined to لِتَأْكُلُوا: that you may seek ﴿مِنْ فَضْلِهِ﴾ the Exalted's, by trade ﴿وَلَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ﴾ Allah for that.

celaleyn:15-15.t: ﴿وَأَلْقَى فِي الْأَرْضِ رَوَاسِيَ﴾ firm mountains ﴿أَنْ﴾ not ﴿تَمِيدَ﴾ shake ﴿بِكُمْ﴾ He placed in it ﴿وَأَنْهَارًا﴾ such as the Nile ﴿وَسُبُلًا﴾ roads ﴿لَعَلَّكُمْ تَهْتَدُونَ﴾ to your destinations.

celaleyn:16-16.t: ﴿وَعَلَامَاتٍ﴾ by which you find your way along the roads, such as mountains by day ﴿وَبِالنَّجْمِ﴾ in the sense of "the stars" ﴿هُمْ يَهْتَدُونَ﴾ to the roads and the qibla by night.

celaleyn:17-17.t: ﴿أَفَمَنْ يَخْلُقُ﴾ and He is Allah ﴿كَمَنْ لَا يَخْلُقُ﴾ and they are the idols, since you associate them with Him in worship? No! ﴿أَفَلَا تَذَكَّرُونَ﴾ this, and so believe?

celaleyn:18-18.t: ﴿وَإِنْ تَعُدُّوا نِعْمَةَ اللَّهِ لَا تُحْصُوهَا﴾ you could not reckon it exactly, let alone be capable of thanking [Him] for it ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَغَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾ in that He bestows blessings on you despite your shortcomings and disobedience.

celaleyn:19-19.t: ﴿وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ مَا تُسِرُّونَ وَمَا تُعْلِنُونَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:20-20.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ تَدْعُونَ﴾ with tāʾ, and with yāʾ [يَدْعُونَ]: you worship ﴿مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾ and they are the idols ﴿لَا يَخْلُقُونَ شَيْئًا وَهُمْ يُخْلَقُونَ﴾ they are fashioned from stone and other things.

celaleyn:21-21.t: ﴿أَمْوَاتٌ﴾ with no spirit in them; a second khabar (predicate) ﴿غَيْرُ أَحْيَاءٍ﴾ an emphasis (tawkīd) ﴿وَمَا يَشْعُرُونَ﴾ i.e. the idols ﴿أَيَّانَ﴾ when ﴿يُبْعَثُونَ﴾ i.e. creation. How then can they be worshipped, when none can be a god except the Creator, the Living, the Knower of the unseen?

celaleyn:22-22.t: ﴿إِلَهُكُمْ﴾ the one deserving of worship from you ﴿إِلَهٌ وَاحِدٌ﴾ having no equal in His essence or His attributes, and He is Allah the Exalted ﴿فَالَّذِينَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْآخِرَةِ قُلُوبُهُمْ مُنْكِرَةٌ﴾ denying the oneness ﴿وَهُمْ مُسْتَكْبِرُونَ﴾ too proud to believe in it.

celaleyn:23-23.t: ﴿لَا جَرَمَ﴾ truly ﴿أَنَّ اللَّهَ يَعْلَمُ مَا يُسِرُّونَ وَمَا يُعْلِنُونَ﴾ and will requite them for it ﴿إِنَّهُ لَا يُحِبُّ الْمُسْتَكْبِرِينَ﴾ in the sense that He will punish them. And there was revealed concerning al-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith:

celaleyn:24-24.t: ﴿وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمْ مَاذَا﴾ interrogative [mā with] relative [dhā] ﴿أَنْزَلَ رَبُّكُمْ﴾ to Muhammad ﴿قَالُوا﴾ it is ﴿أَسَاطِيرُ﴾ the lies ﴿الْأَوَّلِينَ﴾ in order to lead people astray.

celaleyn:25-25.t: ﴿لِيَحْمِلُوا﴾ in the outcome of the matter ﴿أَوْزَارَهُمْ﴾ their sins ﴿كَامِلَةً﴾ none of them expiated ﴿يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ وَمِنْ﴾ some ﴿أَوْزَارِ الَّذِينَ يُضِلُّونَهُمْ بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ﴾ because they invited them to misguidance and they followed them, so they share in the sin ﴿أَلَا سَاءَ﴾ evil is ﴿مَا يَزِرُونَ﴾ what they bear, this bearing of theirs.

celaleyn:26-26.t: ﴿قَدْ مَكَرَ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ﴾ and that is Namrūdh (Nimrod), who built a tall tower to climb up to the sky by it and fight its inhabitants ﴿فَأَتَى اللَّهُ﴾ set upon ﴿بُنْيَانَهُمْ مِنَ الْقَوَاعِدِ﴾ the foundation, and sent against it the wind and an earthquake, which demolished it ﴿فَخَرَّ عَلَيْهِمُ السَّقْفُ مِنْ فَوْقِهِمْ﴾ i.e. while they were under it ﴿وَأَتَاهُمُ الْعَذَابُ مِنْ حَيْثُ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ﴾ from a direction that did not occur to them. And it is said: this is a parable for the undoing of the plots they had contrived against the messengers.

celaleyn:27-27.t: ﴿ثُمَّ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ يُخْزِيهِمْ﴾ He will humiliate them ﴿وَيَقُولُ﴾ Allah to them, on the tongues of the angels, by way of rebuke ﴿أَيْنَ شُرَكَائِيَ﴾ as you claim ﴿الَّذِينَ كُنْتُمْ تُشَاقُّونَ﴾ you opposed the believers ﴿فِيهِمْ﴾ concerning them ﴿قَالَ﴾ i.e. will say ﴿الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْعِلْمَ﴾ of the prophets and the believers ﴿إِنَّ الْخِزْيَ الْيَوْمَ وَالسُّوءَ عَلَى الْكَافِرِينَ﴾ they say it rejoicing over their misfortune.

celaleyn:28-28.t: ﴿الَّذِينَ تَتَوَفَّاهُمْ﴾ with tāʾ and with yāʾ ﴿الْمَلَائِكَةُ ظَالِمِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ﴾ through disbelief ﴿فَأَلْقَوُا السَّلَمَ﴾ they yielded and surrendered at death, saying ﴿مَا كُنَّا نَعْمَلُ مِنْ سُوءٍ﴾ idolatry; and the angels will say ﴿بَلَى إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ بِمَا كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ and will requite you for it; and it will be said to them:

celaleyn:29-29.t: ﴿فَادْخُلُوا أَبْوَابَ جَهَنَّمَ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا فَلَبِئْسَ مَثْوَى﴾ abode ﴿الْمُتَكَبِّرِينَ﴾

celaleyn:30-30.t: ﴿وَقِيلَ لِلَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا﴾ idolatry ﴿مَاذَا أَنْزَلَ رَبُّكُمْ قَالُوا﴾ He sent down ﴿خَيْرًا لِلَّذِينَ أَحْسَنُوا﴾ through faith ﴿فِي هَذِهِ الدُّنْيَا حَسَنَةٌ﴾ a good life ﴿وَلَدَارُ الْآخِرَةِ﴾ i.e. the Garden ﴿خَيْرٌ﴾ than this world and what is in it. The Exalted said concerning it: ﴿وَلَنِعْمَ دَارُ الْمُتَّقِينَ﴾ it is

celaleyn:31-31.t: ﴿جَنَّاتُ عَدْنٍ﴾ of abiding; a mubtadaʾ (subject), whose khabar (predicate) is ﴿يَدْخُلُونَهَا تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ لَهُمْ فِيهَا مَا يَشَاءُونَ كَذَلِكَ﴾ [like that] requital ﴿يَجْزِي اللَّهُ الْمُتَّقِينَ﴾

celaleyn:32-32.t: ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ a naʿt (adjective) ﴿تَتَوَفَّاهُمُ الْمَلَائِكَةُ طَيِّبِينَ﴾ pure of disbelief ﴿يَقُولُونَ﴾ to them at death ﴿سَلَامٌ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ and it will be said to them in the Hereafter ﴿ادْخُلُوا الْجَنَّةَ بِمَا كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ﴾

celaleyn:33-33.t: ﴿هَلْ﴾ not ﴿يَنْظُرُونَ﴾ do the disbelievers await [anything] ﴿إِلَّا أَنْ تَأْتِيَهُمُ﴾ with tāʾ and with yāʾ ﴿الْمَلَائِكَةُ﴾ to take their souls ﴿أَوْ يَأْتِيَ أَمْرُ رَبِّكَ﴾ the punishment, or the Resurrection which includes it ﴿كَذَلِكَ﴾ just as these have done ﴿فَعَلَ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ﴾ of the nations; they denied their messengers and were destroyed ﴿وَمَا ظَلَمَهُمُ اللَّهُ﴾ by destroying them without a sin [on their part] ﴿وَلَكِنْ كَانُوا أَنْفُسَهُمْ يَظْلِمُونَ﴾ through disbelief.

celaleyn:34-34.t: ﴿فَأَصَابَهُمْ سَيِّئَاتُ مَا عَمِلُوا﴾ i.e. their requital ﴿وَحَاقَ﴾ descended ﴿بِهِمْ مَا كَانُوا بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِئُونَ﴾ i.e. the punishment.

celaleyn:35-35.t: ﴿وَقَالَ الَّذِينَ أَشْرَكُوا﴾ of the people of Mecca ﴿لَوْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ مَا عَبَدْنَا مِنْ دُونِهِ مِنْ شَيْءٍ نَحْنُ وَلَا آبَاؤُنَا وَلَا حَرَّمْنَا مِنْ دُونِهِ مِنْ شَيْءٍ﴾ such as the baḥīras and the sāʾibas; so our idolatry and our prohibiting are by His will, and He is pleased with it. The Exalted said: ﴿كَذَلِكَ فَعَلَ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ﴾ i.e. they denied their messengers in what they brought ﴿فَهَلْ﴾ so not ﴿عَلَى الرُّسُلِ إِلَّا الْبَلَاغُ الْمُبِينُ﴾ the clear conveying; guidance is not their responsibility.

celaleyn:36-36.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ بَعَثْنَا فِي كُلِّ أُمَّةٍ رَسُولًا﴾ just as We sent you among these ﴿أَنِ﴾ i.e. "bi-an" (that) ﴿اعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ﴾ affirm His oneness ﴿وَاجْتَنِبُوا الطَّاغُوتَ﴾ the idols, lest you worship them ﴿فَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ هَدَى اللَّهُ﴾ so he believed ﴿وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ حَقَّتْ﴾ became due ﴿عَلَيْهِ الضَّلَالَةُ﴾ in the knowledge of Allah, so he did not believe ﴿فَسِيرُوا﴾ O disbelievers of Mecca ﴿فِي الْأَرْضِ فَانْظُرُوا كَيْفَ كَانَ عَاقِبَةُ الْمُكَذِّبِينَ﴾ of their messengers, of destruction.

celaleyn:37-37.t: ﴿إِنْ تَحْرِصْ﴾ O Muhammad ﴿عَلَى هُدَاهُمْ﴾ when Allah has led them astray, you are not able to do that ﴿فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يُهْدَى﴾ in the passive and in the active [لَا يَهْدِي] ﴿مَنْ يُضِلُّ﴾ whom He wills to lead astray ﴿وَمَا لَهُمْ مِنْ نَاصِرِينَ﴾ protectors from the punishment of Allah.

celaleyn:38-38.t: ﴿وَأَقْسَمُوا بِاللَّهِ جَهْدَ أَيْمَانِهِمْ﴾ i.e. with the utmost effort in them ﴿لَا يَبْعَثُ اللَّهُ مَنْ يَمُوتُ﴾ The Exalted said: ﴿بَلَى﴾ He will resurrect them ﴿وَعْدًا عَلَيْهِ حَقًّا﴾ two emphatic maṣdars (verbal nouns), accusative by their implied (muqaddar) verbs, i.e. "He promised that, and made it true, truly" ﴿وَلَكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ﴾ i.e. the people of Mecca ﴿لَا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ that.

celaleyn:39-39.t: ﴿لِيُبَيِّنَ﴾ attached (mutaʿalliq) to the implied (muqaddar) "yabʿathuhum" ﴿لَهُمُ الَّذِي يَخْتَلِفُونَ﴾ with the believers ﴿فِيهِ﴾ the matter of religion, by punishing them and rewarding the believers ﴿وَلِيَعْلَمَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا أَنَّهُمْ كَانُوا كَاذِبِينَ﴾ in denying the resurrection.

celaleyn:40-40.t: ﴿إِنَّمَا قَوْلُنَا لِشَيْءٍ إِذَا أَرَدْنَاهُ﴾ i.e. We will to bring it into existence; "qawlunā" is a mubtadaʾ (subject), whose khabar (predicate) is ﴿أَنْ نَقُولَ لَهُ كُنْ فَيَكُونُ﴾ i.e. "and so it is"; in one reading it is accusative, conjoined to "naqūla". The verse serves to establish [His] power over the resurrection.

celaleyn:41-41.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ هَاجَرُوا فِي اللَّهِ﴾ to establish His religion ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا ظُلِمُوا﴾ by the harm from the people of Mecca; they are the Prophet ﷺ and his Companions ﴿لَنُبَوِّئَنَّهُمْ﴾ We shall settle them ﴿فِي الدُّنْيَا﴾ an abode ﴿حَسَنَةً﴾ it is Medina ﴿وَلَأَجْرُ الْآخِرَةِ﴾ i.e. the Garden ﴿أَكْبَرُ﴾ greater ﴿لَوْ كَانُوا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ i.e. the disbelievers, or those who stayed behind from the emigration, [if they knew] the honour that belongs to the emigrants, they would have joined them.

celaleyn:42-42.t: ﴿الَّذِينَ صَبَرُوا﴾ on the harm of the idolaters, and on emigration for the sake of making the religion manifest ﴿وَعَلَى رَبِّهِمْ يَتَوَكَّلُونَ﴾ so He provides for them from where they do not expect.

celaleyn:43-43.t: ﴿وَمَا أَرْسَلْنَا مِنْ قَبْلِكَ إِلَّا رِجَالًا نُوحِي إِلَيْهِمْ﴾ not angels ﴿فَاسْأَلُوا أَهْلَ الذِّكْرِ﴾ the scholars of the Torah and the Gospel ﴿إِنْ كُنْتُمْ لَا تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ that; for they know it, and you are more likely to believe them than to believe the believers in Muhammad ﷺ.

celaleyn:44-44.t: ﴿بِالْبَيِّنَاتِ﴾ attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted [verb], i.e. We sent them with the clear proofs ﴿وَالزُّبُرِ﴾ the scriptures ﴿وَأَنْزَلْنَا إِلَيْكَ الذِّكْرَ﴾ the Quran ﴿لِتُبَيِّنَ لِلنَّاسِ مَا نُزِّلَ إِلَيْهِمْ﴾ in it, of the lawful and the unlawful ﴿وَلَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ﴾ about that, and so take a lesson.

celaleyn:45-45.t: ﴿أَفَأَمِنَ الَّذِينَ مَكَرُوا﴾ the plots ﴿السَّيِّئَاتِ﴾ against the Prophet ﷺ in Dār al-Nadwa, of binding him, killing him or expelling him, as mentioned in [Sūrat] al-Anfāl ﴿أَنْ يَخْسِفَ اللَّهُ بِهِمُ الْأَرْضَ﴾ like Qārūn ﴿أَوْ يَأْتِيَهُمُ الْعَذَابُ مِنْ حَيْثُ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ﴾ i.e. from a direction that does not occur to them; and they were destroyed at Badr, and they had not reckoned on that.

celaleyn:46-46.t: ﴿أَوْ يَأْخُذَهُمْ فِي تَقَلُّبِهِمْ﴾ in their journeys for trade ﴿فَمَا هُمْ بِمُعْجِزِينَ﴾ escaping the punishment.

celaleyn:47-47.t: ﴿أَوْ يَأْخُذَهُمْ عَلَى تَخَوُّفٍ﴾ diminishing little by little until all are destroyed; a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the agent or of the object ﴿فَإِنَّ رَبَّكُمْ لَرَءُوفٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾ in that He did not hasten the punishment upon them.

celaleyn:48-48.t: ﴿أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا إِلَى مَا خَلَقَ اللَّهُ مِنْ شَيْءٍ يَتَفَيَّؤُا﴾ having a shadow, such as a tree or a mountain ﴿ظِلَالُهُ﴾ incline ﴿عَنِ الْيَمِينِ وَالشَّمَائِلِ﴾ plural of "shimāl", i.e. from both their sides, at the beginning of the day and at its end ﴿سُجَّدًا لِلَّهِ﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. submitting to Him in what is willed of them ﴿وَهُمْ﴾ i.e. the shadows ﴿دَاخِرُونَ﴾ humbled; they are treated as rational beings.

celaleyn:49-49.t: ﴿وَلِلَّهِ يَسْجُدُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ مِنْ دَابَّةٍ﴾ i.e. a living creature that creeps upon it, i.e. submits to Him in what is willed of it; and in using "mā" the non-rational has been given precedence because of its greater number ﴿وَالْمَلَائِكَةُ﴾ they are singled out for mention as a mark of preference ﴿وَهُمْ لَا يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ﴾ they are not too proud to worship Him.

celaleyn:50-50.t: ﴿يَخَافُونَ﴾ i.e. the angels; a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun of يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ ﴿رَبَّهُمْ مِنْ فَوْقِهِمْ﴾ a ḥāl of "[رَبَّ]هُمْ", i.e. exalted above them in dominion ﴿وَيَفْعَلُونَ مَا يُؤْمَرُونَ﴾ [to do].

celaleyn:51-51.t: ﴿وَقَالَ اللَّهُ لَا تَتَّخِذُوا إِلَهَيْنِ اثْنَيْنِ﴾ an emphasis (tawkīd) ﴿إِنَّمَا هُوَ إِلَهٌ وَاحِدٌ﴾ He brought it to affirm divinity and oneness ﴿فَإِيَّايَ فَارْهَبُونِ﴾ fear Me and none other; in it there is a shift (iltifāt) from the third person.

celaleyn:52-52.t: ﴿وَلَهُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ as possession, creation and servants ﴿وَلَهُ الدِّينُ﴾ obedience ﴿وَاصِبًا﴾ perpetual; a ḥāl (circumstantial) of الدِّينُ, and what governs it is the sense of the ẓarf (adverbial phrase) ﴿أَفَغَيْرَ اللَّهِ تَتَّقُونَ﴾ when He is the true God and there is no god besides Him; the question is for disapproval and rebuke.

celaleyn:53-53.t: ﴿وَمَا بِكُمْ مِنْ نِعْمَةٍ فَمِنَ اللَّهِ﴾ none but He brings it; "mā" is conditional or relative ﴿ثُمَّ إِذَا مَسَّكُمُ﴾ befalls you ﴿الضُّرُّ﴾ poverty and illness ﴿فَإِلَيْهِ تَجْأَرُونَ﴾ you raise your voices in calling for help and in supplication, and you call on none other than Him.

celaleyn:54-54.t: ﴿ثُمَّ إِذَا كَشَفَ الضُّرَّ عَنْكُمْ إِذَا فَرِيقٌ مِنْكُمْ بِرَبِّهِمْ يُشْرِكُونَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:55-55.t: ﴿لِيَكْفُرُوا بِمَا آتَيْنَاهُمْ﴾ of blessing ﴿فَتَمَتَّعُوا﴾ in your gathering together to worship the idols; an imperative of threat ﴿فَسَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ the outcome of that.

celaleyn:56-56.t: ﴿وَيَجْعَلُونَ﴾ i.e. the idolaters ﴿لِمَا لَا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ that they harm or benefit, and they are the idols ﴿نَصِيبًا مِمَّا رَزَقْنَاهُمْ﴾ of crops and cattle, by their saying "this is for Allah and this is for our partners" ﴿تَاللَّهِ لَتُسْأَلُنَّ﴾ a questioning of rebuke; in it there is a shift (iltifāt) from the third person ﴿عَمَّا كُنْتُمْ تَفْتَرُونَ﴾ against Allah, claiming that He commanded you to do that.

celaleyn:57-57.t: ﴿وَيَجْعَلُونَ لِلَّهِ الْبَنَاتِ﴾ by their saying the angels are the daughters of Allah ﴿سُبْحَانَهُ﴾ declaring Him transcendent above what they claim ﴿وَلَهُمْ مَا يَشْتَهُونَ﴾ i.e. sons; the clause is in the position of the nominative, or of the accusative by يَجْعَلُونَ. The meaning: they assign to Him the daughters, whom they dislike, though He is far above having offspring, and they assign to themselves the sons, whom they choose, so that they keep the more excellent for themselves, as in His saying {فَاسْتَفْتِهِمْ أَلِرَبِّكَ الْبَنَاتُ وَلَهُمُ الْبَنُونَ}.

celaleyn:58-58.t: ﴿وَإِذَا بُشِّرَ أَحَدُهُمْ بِالْأُنْثَى﴾ being born to him ﴿ظَلَّ﴾ becomes ﴿وَجْهُهُ مُسْوَدًّا﴾ altered with the alteration of one grieved ﴿وَهُوَ كَظِيمٌ﴾ filled with grief. How then can daughters be ascribed to Him, the Exalted?

celaleyn:59-59.t: ﴿يَتَوَارَى﴾ he hides ﴿مِنَ الْقَوْمِ﴾ i.e. his people ﴿مِنْ سُوءِ مَا بُشِّرَ بِهِ﴾ fearing reproach, hesitating over what to do with it ﴿أَيُمْسِكُهُ﴾ leave it without killing it ﴿عَلَى هُونٍ﴾ in disgrace and humiliation ﴿أَمْ يَدُسُّهُ فِي التُّرَابِ﴾ by burying it alive ﴿أَلَا سَاءَ﴾ evil is ﴿مَا يَحْكُمُونَ﴾ this judgement of theirs, in that they ascribe to their Creator the daughters, who in their view have this standing.

celaleyn:60-60.t: ﴿لِلَّذِينَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْآخِرَةِ﴾ i.e. the disbelievers ﴿مَثَلُ السَّوْءِ﴾ i.e. the evil description, in the sense of the ugly one, and that is their burying daughters alive while needing them for marriage ﴿وَلِلَّهِ الْمَثَلُ الْأَعْلَى﴾ the highest description, and that is that there is no god but He ﴿وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ﴾ in His dominion ﴿الْحَكِيمُ﴾ in His creation.

celaleyn:61-61.t: ﴿وَلَوْ يُؤَاخِذُ اللَّهُ النَّاسَ بِظُلْمِهِمْ﴾ through acts of disobedience ﴿مَا تَرَكَ عَلَيْهَا﴾ i.e. the earth ﴿مِنْ دَابَّةٍ﴾ a living creature that creeps upon it ﴿وَلَكِنْ يُؤَخِّرُهُمْ إِلَى أَجَلٍ مُسَمًّى فَإِذَا جَاءَ أَجَلُهُمْ لَا يَسْتَأْخِرُونَ﴾ beyond it ﴿سَاعَةً وَلَا يَسْتَقْدِمُونَ﴾ before it.

celaleyn:62-62.t: ﴿وَيَجْعَلُونَ لِلَّهِ مَا يَكْرَهُونَ﴾ for themselves, of daughters, partnership in authority, and the slighting of messengers ﴿وَتَصِفُ﴾ say ﴿أَلْسِنَتُهُمْ﴾ besides that ﴿الْكَذِبَ﴾ which is ﴿أَنَّ لَهُمُ الْحُسْنَى﴾ with Allah, i.e. the Garden, as in his saying {وَلَئِنْ رُجِعْتُ إِلَى رَبِّي إِنَّ لِي عِنْدَهُ لَلْحُسْنَى}. The Exalted said: ﴿لَا جَرَمَ﴾ truly ﴿أَنَّ لَهُمُ النَّارَ وَأَنَّهُمْ مُفْرَطُونَ﴾ left in it, or sent ahead into it; and in one reading with kasra on the rāʾ, i.e. transgressing the bounds.

celaleyn:63-63.t: ﴿تَاللَّهِ لَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنَا إِلَى أُمَمٍ مِنْ قَبْلِكَ﴾ messengers ﴿فَزَيَّنَ لَهُمُ الشَّيْطَانُ أَعْمَالَهُمْ﴾ evil ones, so they saw them as good and denied the messengers ﴿فَهُوَ وَلِيُّهُمْ﴾ the one in charge of their affairs ﴿الْيَوْمَ﴾ i.e. in this world ﴿وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ﴾ painful, in the Hereafter. And it is said: what is meant by "the day" is the Day of Resurrection, by way of narrating a future state, i.e. they have no protector but him, and he is unable to help himself, so how could he help them?

celaleyn:64-64.t: ﴿وَمَا أَنْزَلْنَا عَلَيْكَ﴾ O Muhammad ﴿الْكِتَابَ﴾ the Quran ﴿إِلَّا لِتُبَيِّنَ لَهُمْ﴾ to people ﴿الَّذِي اخْتَلَفُوا فِيهِ﴾ of the matter of religion ﴿وَهُدًى﴾ conjoined to لِتُبَيِّنَ ﴿وَرَحْمَةً لِقَوْمٍ يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ in it.

celaleyn:65-65.t: ﴿وَاللَّهُ أَنْزَلَ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مَاءً فَأَحْيَا بِهِ الْأَرْضَ﴾ with vegetation ﴿بَعْدَ مَوْتِهَا﴾ its dryness ﴿إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ﴾ which has been mentioned ﴿لَآيَةً﴾ indicating the resurrection ﴿لِقَوْمٍ يَسْمَعُونَ﴾ with the hearing of reflection.

celaleyn:66-66.t: ﴿وَإِنَّ لَكُمْ فِي الْأَنْعَامِ لَعِبْرَةً﴾ a lesson ﴿نُسْقِيكُمْ﴾ an explanation of the lesson ﴿مِمَّا فِي بُطُونِهِ﴾ i.e. of the cattle ﴿مِنْ﴾ for the beginning [of the extent], attached (mutaʿalliq) to نُسْقِيكُمْ ﴿بَيْنِ فَرْثٍ﴾ the dregs of the rumen ﴿وَدَمٍ لَبَنًا خَالِصًا﴾ not mixed with anything of the dung or the blood, of taste, smell or colour, though it lies between them ﴿سَائِغًا لِلشَّارِبِينَ﴾ passing easily down their throats; one does not choke on it.

celaleyn:67-67.t: ﴿وَمِنْ ثَمَرَاتِ النَّخِيلِ وَالْأَعْنَابِ﴾ fruit ﴿تَتَّخِذُونَ مِنْهُ سَكَرًا﴾ intoxicating wine, called by the maṣdar (verbal noun); this was before its prohibition ﴿وَرِزْقًا حَسَنًا﴾ such as dates, raisins, vinegar and date syrup ﴿إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ﴾ which has been mentioned ﴿لَآيَةً﴾ indicating the power of Allah the Exalted ﴿لِقَوْمٍ يَعْقِلُونَ﴾ who reflect.

celaleyn:68-68.t: ﴿وَأَوْحَى رَبُّكَ إِلَى النَّحْلِ﴾ a revelation of inspiration ﴿أَنْ﴾ explicative (mufassira) or maṣdariyya ﴿اتَّخِذِي مِنَ الْجِبَالِ بُيُوتًا﴾ in which you take shelter ﴿وَمِنَ الشَّجَرِ﴾ houses ﴿وَمِمَّا يَعْرِشُونَ﴾ i.e. what people build for you of places; otherwise you would not take shelter in them.

celaleyn:69-69.t: ﴿ثُمَّ كُلِي مِنْ كُلِّ الثَّمَرَاتِ فَاسْلُكِي﴾ enter ﴿سُبُلَ رَبِّكِ﴾ His paths, in seeking pasture ﴿ذُلُلًا﴾ plural of "dhalūl"; a ḥāl (circumstantial) of السُّبُلِ, i.e. made subservient to you, so that they are not hard for you even if they are rugged, and you do not lose your way back from them even if they are far. And it is said: [a ḥāl] of the pronoun in اسْلُكِي, i.e. compliant with what is willed of you ﴿يَخْرُجُ مِنْ بُطُونِهَا شَرَابٌ﴾ it is honey ﴿مُخْتَلِفٌ أَلْوَانُهُ فِيهِ شِفَاءٌ لِلنَّاسِ﴾ from ailments; it is said: for some of them, as the indefiniteness of "shifāʾ" indicates, or for all of them when combined with something else. I say: and without that, by intention [for it]. He ﷺ commanded it for one whose bowels were loose; narrated by the two Shaykhs [al-Bukhārī and Muslim] ﴿إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لَآيَةً لِقَوْمٍ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ﴾ about His making, exalted is He.

celaleyn:70-70.t: ﴿وَاللَّهُ خَلَقَكُمْ﴾ when you were nothing ﴿ثُمَّ يَتَوَفَّاكُمْ﴾ at the end of your lifespans ﴿وَمِنْكُمْ مَنْ يُرَدُّ إِلَى أَرْذَلِ الْعُمُرِ﴾ i.e. its basest part, of decrepitude and senility ﴿لِكَيْ لَا يَعْلَمَ بَعْدَ عِلْمٍ شَيْئًا﴾ ʿIkrima said: whoever recites the Quran will not come to this state ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ﴾ of the ordering of His creation ﴿قَدِيرٌ﴾ over whatever He wills.

celaleyn:71-71.t: ﴿وَاللَّهُ فَضَّلَ بَعْضَكُمْ عَلَى بَعْضٍ فِي الرِّزْقِ﴾ so among you are rich and poor, owner and owned ﴿فَمَا الَّذِينَ فُضِّلُوا﴾ i.e. the masters ﴿بِرَادِّي رِزْقِهِمْ عَلَى مَا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَانُهُمْ﴾ i.e. would make what We have provided them of wealth and other things a partnership between them and their slaves ﴿فَهُمْ﴾ i.e. the slaves and the masters ﴿فِيهِ سَوَاءٌ﴾ partners. The meaning: they have no partners from among their slaves in their wealth, so how can they make some of Allah's slaves partners to Him? ﴿أَفَبِنِعْمَةِ اللَّهِ يَجْحَدُونَ﴾ they disbelieve, in that they assign partners to Him.

celaleyn:72-72.t: ﴿وَاللَّهُ جَعَلَ لَكُمْ مِنْ أَنْفُسِكُمْ أَزْوَاجًا﴾ so He created Ḥawwāʾ (Eve) from a rib of Adam, and the rest of women from the seed of men and women ﴿وَجَعَلَ لَكُمْ مِنْ أَزْوَاجِكُمْ بَنِينَ وَحَفَدَةً﴾ children's children ﴿وَرَزَقَكُمْ مِنَ الطَّيِّبَاتِ﴾ of the kinds of fruits, grains and animals ﴿أَفَبِالْبَاطِلِ﴾ the idol ﴿يُؤْمِنُونَ وَبِنِعْمَتِ اللَّهِ هُمْ يَكْفُرُونَ﴾ by their associating [partners with Him].

celaleyn:73-73.t: ﴿وَيَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾ i.e. other than Him ﴿مَا لَا يَمْلِكُ لَهُمْ رِزْقًا مِنَ السَّمَاوَاتِ﴾ by rain ﴿وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ by vegetation ﴿شَيْئًا﴾ a badal (substitute) for رِزْقًا ﴿وَلَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ﴾ they are not able to do anything; and they are the idols.

celaleyn:74-74.t: ﴿فَلَا تَضْرِبُوا لِلَّهِ الْأَمْثَالَ﴾ do not make likenesses for Allah whom you associate with Him ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَعْلَمُ﴾ that there is nothing like Him ﴿وَأَنْتُمْ لَا تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ that.

celaleyn:75-75.t: ﴿ضَرَبَ اللَّهُ مَثَلًا﴾ and there is substituted for it ﴿عَبْدًا مَمْلُوكًا﴾ a description that distinguishes him from the free man, for he [too] is a servant of Allah ﴿لَا يَقْدِرُ عَلَى شَيْءٍ﴾ because he owns nothing ﴿وَمَنْ﴾ an indefinite noun that is described, i.e. a free man ﴿رَزَقْنَاهُ مِنَّا رِزْقًا حَسَنًا فَهُوَ يُنْفِقُ مِنْهُ سِرًّا وَجَهْرًا﴾ i.e. he disposes of it as he wishes. The first is the likeness of the idols, and the second the likeness of Him, exalted is He ﴿هَلْ يَسْتَوُونَ﴾ i.e. the incapable slaves and the free man who disposes [of his wealth]? No! ﴿الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ﴾ alone ﴿بَلْ أَكْثَرُهُمْ﴾ i.e. of the people of Mecca ﴿لَا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ the punishment they are heading for, and so they associate [partners with Him].

celaleyn:76-76.t: ﴿وَضَرَبَ اللَّهُ مَثَلًا﴾ and there is substituted for it ﴿رَجُلَيْنِ أَحَدُهُمَا أَبْكَمُ﴾ born mute ﴿لَا يَقْدِرُ عَلَى شَيْءٍ﴾ because he neither understands nor makes himself understood ﴿وَهُوَ كَلٌّ﴾ a burden ﴿عَلَى مَوْلَاهُ﴾ the one in charge of his affairs ﴿أَيْنَمَا يُوَجِّهْهُ﴾ he sends him ﴿لَا يَأْتِ﴾ from him ﴿بِخَيْرٍ﴾ with success; and this is the likeness of the disbeliever ﴿هَلْ يَسْتَوِي هُوَ﴾ the mute man mentioned ﴿وَمَنْ يَأْمُرُ بِالْعَدْلِ﴾ i.e. one who speaks and benefits people, in that he commands it and urges it ﴿وَهُوَ عَلَى صِرَاطٍ﴾ a path ﴿مُسْتَقِيمٍ﴾ and he is the second, the believer? No! And it is said: this is a likeness for Allah, and the mute one for the idols, while the one before it is the likeness of the disbeliever and the believer.

celaleyn:77-77.t: ﴿وَلِلَّهِ غَيْبُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ i.e. the knowledge of what is hidden in them ﴿وَمَا أَمْرُ السَّاعَةِ إِلَّا كَلَمْحِ الْبَصَرِ أَوْ هُوَ أَقْرَبُ﴾ than that, because it is by the word "Be!" and it is ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ﴾

celaleyn:78-78.t: ﴿وَاللَّهُ أَخْرَجَكُمْ مِنْ بُطُونِ أُمَّهَاتِكُمْ لَا تَعْلَمُونَ شَيْئًا﴾ the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) ﴿وَجَعَلَ لَكُمُ السَّمْعَ﴾ in the sense of "hearings" ﴿وَالْأَبْصَارَ وَالْأَفْئِدَةَ﴾ the hearts ﴿لَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ﴾ for that, and so believe.

celaleyn:79-79.t: ﴿أَلَمْ يَرَوْا إِلَى الطَّيْرِ مُسَخَّرَاتٍ﴾ made tractable for flight ﴿فِي جَوِّ السَّمَاءِ﴾ i.e. the air between the sky and the earth ﴿مَا يُمْسِكُهُنَّ﴾ from falling, when they fold their wings or spread them ﴿إِلَّا اللَّهُ﴾ by His power ﴿إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لَآيَاتٍ لِقَوْمٍ يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ they are: His creating them such that they are able to fly, His creating the air such that flight in it is possible, and His holding them up.

celaleyn:80-80.t: ﴿وَاللَّهُ جَعَلَ لَكُمْ مِنْ بُيُوتِكُمْ سَكَنًا﴾ a place in which you dwell ﴿وَجَعَلَ لَكُمْ مِنْ جُلُودِ الْأَنْعَامِ بُيُوتًا﴾ such as tents and domed tents ﴿تَسْتَخِفُّونَهَا﴾ for carrying ﴿يَوْمَ ظَعْنِكُمْ﴾ your travelling ﴿وَيَوْمَ إِقَامَتِكُمْ وَمِنْ أَصْوَافِهَا﴾ i.e. of sheep ﴿وَأَوْبَارِهَا﴾ i.e. of camels ﴿وَأَشْعَارِهَا﴾ i.e. of goats ﴿أَثَاثًا﴾ furnishings for your houses, such as carpets and coverings ﴿وَمَتَاعًا﴾ which you enjoy ﴿إِلَى حِينٍ﴾ in which it wears out.

celaleyn:81-81.t: ﴿وَاللَّهُ جَعَلَ لَكُمْ مِمَّا خَلَقَ﴾ of houses, trees and clouds ﴿ظِلَالًا﴾ plural of "ẓill", which protect you from the heat of the sun ﴿وَجَعَلَ لَكُمْ مِنَ الْجِبَالِ أَكْنَانًا﴾ plural of "kinn", which is that in which one takes shelter, such as a cave or a tunnel ﴿وَجَعَلَ لَكُمْ سَرَابِيلَ﴾ shirts ﴿تَقِيكُمُ الْحَرَّ﴾ i.e. and the cold ﴿وَسَرَابِيلَ تَقِيكُمْ بَأْسَكُمْ﴾ your warfare, i.e. thrusting and striking in it, such as coats of mail and breastplates ﴿كَذَلِكَ﴾ just as He created these things ﴿يُتِمُّ نِعْمَتَهُ﴾ in this world ﴿عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ by creating what you need ﴿لَعَلَّكُمْ﴾ O people of Mecca ﴿تُسْلِمُونَ﴾ affirm His oneness.

celaleyn:82-82.t: ﴿فَإِنْ تَوَلَّوْا﴾ turn away from Islam ﴿فَإِنَّمَا عَلَيْكَ﴾ O Muhammad ﴿الْبَلَاغُ الْمُبِينُ﴾ the clear conveying; this was before the command to fight.

celaleyn:83-83.t: ﴿يَعْرِفُونَ نِعْمَتَ اللَّهِ﴾ i.e. they acknowledge that it is from Him ﴿ثُمَّ يُنْكِرُونَهَا﴾ by their associating [partners with Him] ﴿وَأَكْثَرُهُمُ الْكَافِرُونَ﴾

celaleyn:84-84.t: ﴿وَ﴾ remember ﴿يَوْمَ نَبْعَثُ مِنْ كُلِّ أُمَّةٍ شَهِيدًا﴾ and that is its prophet, who testifies for it and against it; and that is the Day of Resurrection ﴿ثُمَّ لَا يُؤْذَنُ لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾ to make excuses ﴿وَلَا هُمْ يُسْتَعْتَبُونَ﴾ the ʿutbā is not asked of them, i.e. a return to what pleases Allah.

celaleyn:85-85.t: ﴿وَإِذَا رَأَى الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا﴾ disbelieved ﴿الْعَذَابَ﴾ the Fire ﴿فَلَا يُخَفَّفُ عَنْهُمْ﴾ the punishment ﴿وَلَا هُمْ يُنْظَرُونَ﴾ granted respite from it when they see it.

celaleyn:86-86.t: ﴿وَإِذَا رَأَى الَّذِينَ أَشْرَكُوا شُرَكَاءَهُمْ﴾ of the devils and others ﴿قَالُوا رَبَّنَا هَؤُلَاءِ شُرَكَاؤُنَا الَّذِينَ كُنَّا نَدْعُوا﴾ worship ﴿مِنْ دُونِكَ فَأَلْقَوْا إِلَيْهِمُ الْقَوْلَ﴾ i.e. they said to them ﴿إِنَّكُمْ لَكَاذِبُونَ﴾ in your saying that you worshipped us, as in another verse: {مَا كَانُوا إِيَّانَا يَعْبُدُونَ}, [and] they will deny their worship.

celaleyn:87-87.t: ﴿وَأَلْقَوْا إِلَى اللَّهِ يَوْمَئِذٍ السَّلَمَ﴾ i.e. they submitted to His judgement ﴿وَضَلَّ﴾ vanished ﴿عَنْهُمْ مَا كَانُوا يَفْتَرُونَ﴾ of [their claim] that their gods would intercede for them.

celaleyn:88-88.t: ﴿الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَصَدُّوا﴾ people ﴿عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ﴾ His religion ﴿زِدْنَاهُمْ عَذَابًا فَوْقَ الْعَذَابِ﴾ which they deserved by their disbelief. Ibn Masʿūd said: scorpions whose fangs are like tall palm trees ﴿بِمَا كَانُوا يُفْسِدُونَ﴾ by their turning people away from faith.

celaleyn:89-89.t: ﴿وَ﴾ remember ﴿يَوْمَ نَبْعَثُ فِي كُلِّ أُمَّةٍ شَهِيدًا عَلَيْهِمْ مِنْ أَنْفُسِهِمْ﴾ he is their prophet ﴿وَجِئْنَا بِكَ﴾ O Muhammad ﴿شَهِيدًا عَلَى هَؤُلَاءِ﴾ i.e. your people ﴿وَنَزَّلْنَا عَلَيْكَ الْكِتَابَ﴾ the Quran ﴿تِبْيَانًا﴾ an exposition ﴿لِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ﴾ that people need of the matters of the Sharia ﴿وَهُدًى﴾ from misguidance ﴿وَرَحْمَةً وَبُشْرَى﴾ of the Garden ﴿لِلْمُسْلِمِينَ﴾ those who affirm [Allah's] oneness.

celaleyn:90-90.t: ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَأْمُرُ بِالْعَدْلِ﴾ affirmation of oneness (tawḥīd), or fairness ﴿وَالْإِحْسَانِ﴾ fulfilling the obligations, or that you worship Allah as though you see Him, as in the hadith ﴿وَإِيتَاءِ﴾ giving ﴿ذِي الْقُرْبَى﴾ kinship; He singled it out for mention out of concern for it ﴿وَيَنْهَى عَنِ الْفَحْشَاءِ﴾ fornication ﴿وَالْمُنْكَرِ﴾ by the Sharia, of disbelief and acts of disobedience ﴿وَالْبَغْيِ﴾ wronging people; He singled it out for mention out of concern, just as He began with al-faḥshāʾ ﴿يَعِظُكُمْ﴾ with the command and the prohibition ﴿لَعَلَّكُمْ تَذَكَّرُونَ﴾ take heed; in it the original tāʾ is assimilated (idghām) into the dhāl. And in al-Mustadrak, from Ibn Masʿūd: this is the most comprehensive verse in the Quran for good and evil.

celaleyn:91-91.t: ﴿وَأَوْفُوا بِعَهْدِ اللَّهِ﴾ of the pledge of allegiance, oaths and other things ﴿إِذَا عَاهَدْتُمْ وَلَا تَنْقُضُوا الْأَيْمَانَ بَعْدَ تَوْكِيدِهَا﴾ their confirmation ﴿وَقَدْ جَعَلْتُمُ اللَّهَ عَلَيْكُمْ كَفِيلًا﴾ for fulfilment, since you swore by Him; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَعْلَمُ مَا تَفْعَلُونَ﴾ a threat to them.

celaleyn:92-92.t: ﴿وَلَا تَكُونُوا كَالَّتِي نَقَضَتْ﴾ spoiled ﴿غَزْلَهَا﴾ what she had spun ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِ قُوَّةٍ﴾ its firm making and twisting ﴿أَنْكَاثًا﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial); plural of "nikth", which is what is unravelled, i.e. whose firmness is undone. She was a foolish woman of Mecca who used to spin all day long and then unravel it ﴿تَتَّخِذُونَ﴾ a ḥāl of the pronoun of تَكُونُوا, i.e. do not be like her in your taking ﴿أَيْمَانَكُمْ دَخَلًا﴾ it is that which enters into a thing and is not part of it, i.e. corruption and deceit ﴿بَيْنَكُمْ﴾ by breaking them ﴿أَنْ﴾ i.e. "li-an" (because) ﴿تَكُونَ أُمَّةٌ﴾ a group ﴿هِيَ أَرْبَى﴾ more numerous ﴿مِنْ أُمَّةٍ﴾ They used to make alliances with allies, and when they found others more numerous and mightier than them, they broke the alliance with those and allied themselves with these ﴿إِنَّمَا يَبْلُوكُمْ﴾ tests you ﴿اللَّهُ بِهِ﴾ i.e. by what He commanded of fulfilling the covenant, to see who among you is obedient and who is disobedient; or by one group's being more numerous, to see whether you will keep faith or not ﴿وَلَيُبَيِّنَنَّ لَكُمْ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ مَا كُنْتُمْ فِيهِ تَخْتَلِفُونَ﴾ in this world, of the matter of the covenant and other things, by punishing the one who breaks it and rewarding the one who keeps it.

celaleyn:93-93.t: ﴿وَلَوْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ لَجَعَلَكُمْ أُمَّةً وَاحِدَةً﴾ people of one religion ﴿وَلَكِنْ يُضِلُّ مَنْ يَشَاءُ وَيَهْدِي مَنْ يَشَاءُ وَلَتُسْأَلُنَّ﴾ on the Day of Resurrection, a questioning of reproach ﴿عَمَّا كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ so that you are requited for it.

celaleyn:94-94.t: ﴿وَلَا تَتَّخِذُوا أَيْمَانَكُمْ دَخَلًا بَيْنَكُمْ﴾ He repeated it for emphasis ﴿فَتَزِلَّ قَدَمٌ﴾ i.e. your feet, from the highway of Islam ﴿بَعْدَ ثُبُوتِهَا﴾ their being steady upon it ﴿وَتَذُوقُوا السُّوءَ﴾ i.e. the punishment ﴿بِمَا صَدَدْتُمْ عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ﴾ i.e. by your turning away from fulfilling the covenant, or by your turning others away from it, because they follow your example ﴿وَلَكُمْ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمٌ﴾ in the Hereafter.

celaleyn:95-95.t: ﴿وَلَا تَشْتَرُوا بِعَهْدِ اللَّهِ ثَمَنًا قَلِيلًا﴾ of this world, by breaking it for its sake ﴿إِنَّمَا عِنْدَ اللَّهِ﴾ of reward ﴿هُوَ خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ﴾ than what is in this world ﴿إِنْ كُنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ that; so do not break [it].

celaleyn:96-96.t: ﴿مَا عِنْدَكُمْ﴾ of this world ﴿يَنْفَدُ﴾ perishes ﴿وَمَا عِنْدَ اللَّهِ بَاقٍ﴾ everlasting ﴿وَلَنَجْزِيَنَّ﴾ with yāʾ and with nūn ﴿الَّذِينَ صَبَرُوا﴾ in fulfilling covenants ﴿أَجْرَهُمْ بِأَحْسَنِ مَا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ﴾ "aḥsan" in the sense of "ḥasan" (good).

celaleyn:97-97.t: ﴿مَنْ عَمِلَ صَالِحًا مِنْ ذَكَرٍ أَوْ أُنْثَى وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌ فَلَنُحْيِيَنَّهُ حَيَاةً طَيِّبَةً﴾ it is said: it is the life of the Garden; and it is said: in this world, through contentment or lawful provision ﴿وَلَنَجْزِيَنَّهُمْ أَجْرَهُمْ بِأَحْسَنِ مَا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ﴾

celaleyn:98-98.t: ﴿فَإِذَا قَرَأْتَ الْقُرْآنَ﴾ i.e. you wish to recite it ﴿فَاسْتَعِذْ بِاللَّهِ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ الرَّجِيمِ﴾ i.e. say: "aʿūdhu bi-Llāhi mina l-shayṭāni l-rajīm".

celaleyn:99-99.t: ﴿إِنَّهُ لَيْسَ لَهُ سُلْطَانٌ﴾ domination ﴿عَلَى الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَلَى رَبِّهِمْ يَتَوَكَّلُونَ﴾

celaleyn:100-100.t: ﴿إِنَّمَا سُلْطَانُهُ عَلَى الَّذِينَ يَتَوَلَّوْنَهُ﴾ by obeying him ﴿وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ بِهِ﴾ i.e. with Allah ﴿مُشْرِكُونَ﴾

celaleyn:101-101.t: ﴿وَإِذَا بَدَّلْنَا آيَةً مَكَانَ آيَةٍ﴾ by abrogating it and sending down another, for the benefit of the servants ﴿وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا يُنَزِّلُ قَالُوا﴾ i.e. the disbelievers, to the Prophet ﷺ ﴿إِنَّمَا أَنْتَ مُفْتَرٍ﴾ a liar who says it of his own accord ﴿بَلْ أَكْثَرُهُمْ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ the reality of the Quran and the benefit of abrogation.

celaleyn:102-102.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾ to them ﴿نَزَّلَهُ رُوحُ الْقُدُسِ﴾ Jibrīl ﴿مِنْ رَبِّكَ بِالْحَقِّ﴾ attached (mutaʿalliq) to نَزَّلَ ﴿لِيُثَبِّتَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ through their faith in it ﴿وَهُدًى وَبُشْرَى لِلْمُسْلِمِينَ﴾

celaleyn:103-103.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ﴾ for affirmation (taḥqīq) ﴿نَعْلَمُ أَنَّهُمْ يَقُولُونَ إِنَّمَا يُعَلِّمُهُ﴾ the Quran ﴿بَشَرٌ﴾ and he was a Christian blacksmith whom the Prophet ﷺ used to visit. The Exalted said: ﴿لِسَانُ﴾ the language ﴿الَّذِي يُلْحِدُونَ﴾ they incline ﴿إِلَيْهِ﴾ [claiming] that he teaches him ﴿أَعْجَمِيٌّ وَهَذَا﴾ the Quran ﴿لِسَانٌ عَرَبِيٌّ مُبِينٌ﴾ possessed of clarity and eloquence; so how could a non-Arab teach it to him?

celaleyn:104-104.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِآيَاتِ اللَّهِ لَا يَهْدِيهِمُ اللَّهُ وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ﴾ painful.

celaleyn:105-105.t: ﴿إِنَّمَا يَفْتَرِي الْكَذِبَ الَّذِينَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِآيَاتِ اللَّهِ﴾ the Quran, by their saying "this is the speech of a human being" ﴿وَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الْكَاذِبُونَ﴾ and the emphasis (tawkīd) by repetition, by inna and by other means is a rebuttal of their saying {إِنَّمَا أَنْتَ مُفْتَرٍ}.

celaleyn:106-106.t: ﴿مَنْ كَفَرَ بِاللَّهِ مِنْ بَعْدِ إِيمَانِهِ إِلَّا مَنْ أُكْرِهَ﴾ to utter disbelief and so uttered it ﴿وَقَلْبُهُ مُطْمَئِنٌّ بِالْإِيمَانِ﴾ "man" is a mubtadaʾ (subject) or conditional, and the khabar (predicate) or the apodosis (jawāb) is "for them is a severe threat", indicated by this: ﴿وَلَكِنْ مَنْ شَرَحَ بِالْكُفْرِ صَدْرًا﴾ to it, i.e. opened and widened it, in the sense that his soul was content with it ﴿فَعَلَيْهِمْ غَضَبٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمٌ﴾

celaleyn:107-107.t: ﴿ذَلِكَ﴾ threat to them ﴿بِأَنَّهُمُ اسْتَحَبُّوا الْحَيَاةَ الدُّنْيَا﴾ chose it ﴿عَلَى الْآخِرَةِ وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَهْدِي الْقَوْمَ الْكَافِرِينَ﴾

celaleyn:108-108.t: ﴿أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ طَبَعَ اللَّهُ عَلَى قُلُوبِهِمْ وَسَمْعِهِمْ وَأَبْصَارِهِمْ وَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الْغَافِلُونَ﴾ of what is intended for them.

celaleyn:109-109.t: ﴿لَا جَرَمَ﴾ truly ﴿أَنَّهُمْ فِي الْآخِرَةِ هُمُ الْخَاسِرُونَ﴾ because their destination is the Fire, made everlasting for them.

celaleyn:110-110.t: ﴿ثُمَّ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ لِلَّذِينَ هَاجَرُوا﴾ to Medina ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا فُتِنُوا﴾ they were tortured and uttered disbelief; and in one reading in the active voice, i.e. they disbelieved, or they seduced people away from faith ﴿ثُمَّ جَاهَدُوا وَصَبَرُوا﴾ in obedience ﴿إِنَّ رَبَّكَ مِنْ بَعْدِهَا﴾ i.e. the trial ﴿لَغَفُورٌ﴾ to them ﴿رَحِيمٌ﴾ to them. The khabar (predicate) of the first inna is indicated by the khabar of the second.

celaleyn:111-111.t: Remember ﴿يَوْمَ تَأْتِي كُلُّ نَفْسٍ تُجَادِلُ﴾ argues ﴿عَنْ نَفْسِهَا﴾ concerned with no one else; and that is the Day of Resurrection ﴿وَتُوَفَّى كُلُّ نَفْسٍ﴾ the requital of ﴿مَا عَمِلَتْ وَهُمْ لَا يُظْلَمُونَ﴾ in anything.

celaleyn:112-112.t: ﴿وَضَرَبَ اللَّهُ مَثَلًا﴾ and there is substituted for it ﴿قَرْيَةً﴾ it is Mecca, and its people are meant ﴿كَانَتْ آمِنَةً﴾ from raids, undisturbed ﴿مُطْمَئِنَّةً﴾ there being no need to move away from it because of hardship or fear ﴿يَأْتِيهَا رِزْقُهَا رَغَدًا﴾ abundant ﴿مِنْ كُلِّ مَكَانٍ فَكَفَرَتْ بِأَنْعُمِ اللَّهِ﴾ by denying the Prophet ﷺ ﴿فَأَذَاقَهَا اللَّهُ لِبَاسَ الْجُوعِ﴾ so they suffered drought for seven years ﴿وَالْخَوْفِ﴾ through the raiding parties of the Prophet ﷺ ﴿بِمَا كَانُوا يَصْنَعُونَ﴾

celaleyn:113-113.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ جَاءَهُمْ رَسُولٌ مِنْهُمْ﴾ Muhammad ﷺ ﴿فَكَذَّبُوهُ فَأَخَذَهُمُ الْعَذَابُ﴾ hunger and fear ﴿وَهُمْ ظَالِمُونَ﴾

celaleyn:114-114.t: ﴿فَكُلُوا﴾ O believers ﴿مِمَّا رَزَقَكُمُ اللَّهُ حَلَالًا طَيِّبًا وَاشْكُرُوا نِعْمَتَ اللَّهِ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ إِيَّاهُ تَعْبُدُونَ﴾

celaleyn:115-115.t: ﴿إِنَّمَا حَرَّمَ عَلَيْكُمُ الْمَيْتَةَ وَالدَّمَ وَلَحْمَ الْخِنْزِيرِ وَمَا أُهِلَّ لِغَيْرِ اللَّهِ بِهِ فَمَنِ اضْطُرَّ غَيْرَ بَاغٍ وَلَا عَادٍ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:116-116.t: ﴿وَلَا تَقُولُوا لِمَا تَصِفُ أَلْسِنَتُكُمْ﴾ i.e. because of your tongues' describing ﴿الْكَذِبَ هَذَا حَلَالٌ وَهَذَا حَرَامٌ﴾ of what Allah has neither made lawful nor forbidden ﴿لِتَفْتَرُوا عَلَى اللَّهِ الْكَذِبَ﴾ by attributing that to Him ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَفْتَرُونَ عَلَى اللَّهِ الْكَذِبَ لَا يُفْلِحُونَ﴾ for them [Translator's note: this «لَهُمْ» introduces the next verse: "for them is a little enjoyment".]

celaleyn:117-117.t: ﴿مَتَاعٌ قَلِيلٌ﴾ in this world ﴿وَلَهُمْ﴾ in the Hereafter ﴿عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ﴾ painful.

celaleyn:118-118.t: ﴿وَعَلَى الَّذِينَ هَادُوا﴾ i.e. the Jews ﴿حَرَّمْنَا مَا قَصَصْنَا عَلَيْكَ مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾ in the verse {وَعَلَى الَّذِينَ هَادُوا حَرَّمْنَا كُلَّ ذِي ظُفُرٍ} to its end ﴿وَمَا ظَلَمْنَاهُمْ﴾ by forbidding that ﴿وَلَكِنْ كَانُوا أَنْفُسَهُمْ يَظْلِمُونَ﴾ by committing the acts of disobedience that necessitated it.

celaleyn:119-119.t: ﴿ثُمَّ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ لِلَّذِينَ عَمِلُوا السُّوءَ﴾ idolatry ﴿بِجَهَالَةٍ ثُمَّ تَابُوا﴾ returned ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِ ذَلِكَ وَأَصْلَحُوا﴾ their deeds ﴿إِنَّ رَبَّكَ مِنْ بَعْدِهَا﴾ i.e. the ignorance, or the repentance ﴿لَغَفُورٌ﴾ to them ﴿رَحِيمٌ﴾ to them.

celaleyn:120-120.t: ﴿إِنَّ إِبْرَاهِيمَ كَانَ أُمَّةً﴾ a leader, an exemplar combining all good qualities ﴿قَانِتًا﴾ obedient ﴿لِلَّهِ حَنِيفًا﴾ inclining to the upright religion ﴿وَلَمْ يَكُ مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ﴾

celaleyn:121-121.t: ﴿شَاكِرًا لِأَنْعُمِهِ اجْتَبَاهُ﴾ chose him ﴿وَهَدَاهُ إِلَى صِرَاطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ﴾

celaleyn:122-122.t: ﴿وَآتَيْنَاهُ﴾ in it there is a shift (iltifāt) from the third person ﴿فِي الدُّنْيَا حَسَنَةً﴾ it is good praise among the people of all religions ﴿وَإِنَّهُ فِي الْآخِرَةِ لَمِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ﴾ who have the highest ranks.

celaleyn:123-123.t: ﴿ثُمَّ أَوْحَيْنَا إِلَيْكَ﴾ O Muhammad ﴿أَنِ اتَّبِعْ مِلَّةَ﴾ the religion ﴿إِبْرَاهِيمَ حَنِيفًا وَمَا كَانَ مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ﴾ it is repeated in rebuttal of the claim of the Jews and the Christians that they follow his religion.

celaleyn:124-124.t: ﴿إِنَّمَا جُعِلَ السَّبْتُ﴾ its veneration was made obligatory ﴿عَلَى الَّذِينَ اخْتَلَفُوا فِيهِ﴾ with their prophet, and they are the Jews. They were commanded to devote themselves to worship on Friday, but they said: "We do not want it", and chose the Sabbath, so it was made strict for them ﴿وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَيَحْكُمُ بَيْنَهُمْ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ فِيمَا كَانُوا فِيهِ يَخْتَلِفُونَ﴾ concerning it, by rewarding the obedient and punishing the disobedient for violating its sanctity.

celaleyn:125-125.t: ﴿ادْعُ﴾ people, O Muhammad ﴿إِلَى سَبِيلِ رَبِّكَ﴾ His religion ﴿بِالْحِكْمَةِ﴾ with the Quran ﴿وَالْمَوْعِظَةِ الْحَسَنَةِ﴾ its admonitions, or gentle speech ﴿وَجَادِلْهُمْ بِالَّتِي﴾ i.e. with the disputation which ﴿هِيَ أَحْسَنُ﴾ such as calling to Allah by His signs and calling to His proofs ﴿إِنَّ رَبَّكَ هُوَ أَعْلَمُ﴾ i.e. knowing ﴿بِمَنْ ضَلَّ عَنْ سَبِيلِهِ وَهُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِالْمُهْتَدِينَ﴾ and will requite them. This was before the command to fight. And [the following] was revealed when Ḥamza was killed and mutilated, and he ﷺ said, having seen him: "I shall mutilate seventy of them in your place."

celaleyn:126-126.t: ﴿وَإِنْ عَاقَبْتُمْ فَعَاقِبُوا بِمِثْلِ مَا عُوقِبْتُمْ بِهِ وَلَئِنْ صَبَرْتُمْ﴾ from taking revenge ﴿لَهُوَ﴾ i.e. patience ﴿خَيْرٌ لِلصَّابِرِينَ﴾ So he ﷺ refrained, and made expiation for his oath; narrated by al-Bazzār.

celaleyn:127-127.t: ﴿وَاصْبِرْ وَمَا صَبْرُكَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ﴾ by His granting of success ﴿وَلَا تَحْزَنْ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ i.e. the disbelievers, if they do not believe, because of your eagerness for their faith ﴿وَلَا تَكُ فِي ضَيْقٍ مِمَّا يَمْكُرُونَ﴾ i.e. do not be troubled by their plotting, for I am your helper against them.

celaleyn:128-128.t: ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَ الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا﴾ disbelief and acts of disobedience ﴿وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ مُحْسِنُونَ﴾ by obedience and patience; [He is with them] with aid and help.

daas-irab:1-4.t: ﴿أَتى أَمْرُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿فَلا تَسْتَعْجِلُوهُ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction and lā is prohibitive; the imperfect verb is jussive (majzūm) by the deletion of the nūn; the wāw is its fāʿil and the hāʾ its object; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa). ﴿سُبْحانَهُ﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being "أسبح"; the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَتَعالى﴾ a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa implied (muqaddara) on the alif owing to impossibility; its fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the clause is conjoined. ﴿عَمَّا﴾ mā is a relative, and [the preposition and its genitive noun are] attached to (mutaʿalliq) سبحان. ﴿يُشْرِكُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿يُنَزِّلُ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative, whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is resumptive. ﴿الْمَلائِكَةَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿بِالرُّوحِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ينزل. ﴿مِنْ أَمْرِهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿عَلى مَنْ﴾ man is a relative noun; [the preposition and its genitive noun are] attached to ينزل. ﴿يَشاءُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿مِنْ عِبادِهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl; the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿أَنْ﴾ the lightened (mukhaffafa) an; its noun is the omitted pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn); an and what follows it are interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun), badal (substitute) of الروح. ﴿أَنْذِرُوا﴾ an imperative verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar (predicate). ﴿أَنَّهُ﴾ anna and its noun; the interpreted maṣdar is in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi. ﴿لا﴾ the lā of generic negation, operating like inna. ﴿إِلهَ﴾ its noun, indeclinable on the fatḥa; the khabar is omitted; the clause is the khabar of أنه. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿أَنَا﴾ badal of the pronoun in the omitted khabar. ﴿فَاتَّقُونِ﴾ the fāʾ is the faṣīḥa fāʾ (al-fāʾ al-faṣīḥa) and an imperative verb indeclinable on the deletion of the nūn; the nūn is the nūn of protection (wiqāya); the yāʾ of the first person was deleted for lightness, and it is mafʿūl bihi. ﴿خَلَقَ السَّماواتِ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent, and السموات is its object, accusative (manṣūb) with the kasra because it is a sound feminine plural. ﴿وَالْأَرْضَ﴾ conjoined to السموات. ﴿بِالْحَقِّ﴾ ḥāl; the clause is resumptive. ﴿تَعالى﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿عَمَّا﴾ عن is a preposition and mā is a relative; [the preposition and its genitive noun are] attached to تعالى; the clause is resumptive. ﴿يُشْرِكُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿خَلَقَ الْإِنْسانَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent, and الإنسان is its object; the clause is resumptive. ﴿مِنْ نُطْفَةٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to خلق. ﴿فَإِذا﴾ the fāʾ is redundant (zāʾida) and إذا is the إذا of surprise (al-fujāʾiyya). ﴿هُوَ خَصِيمٌ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar. ﴿مُبِينٌ﴾ naʿt (adjective).

daas-irab:5-7.t: ﴿وَالْأَنْعامَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction and الأنعام is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to الإنسان. ﴿خَلَقَها﴾ a past verb and its object; the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) خلقها; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause. ﴿فِيها دِفْءٌ﴾ دفء is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), and فيها is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the fronted khabar (predicate); the clause is a ḥāl clause. ﴿وَمَنافِعُ﴾ conjoined to دفء. ﴿وَمِنْها﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تأكلون. ﴿تَأْكُلُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is conjoined. ﴿وَلَكُمْ فِيها جَمالٌ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; لكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to a fronted khabar; فيها is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl; جمال is a postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause is conjoined. ﴿حِينَ﴾ an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān), attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of جمال. ﴿تُرِيحُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَحِينَ تَسْرَحُونَ﴾ the clause is conjoined to the one before it, and its i'rab is like its i'rab. ﴿وَتَحْمِلُ أَثْقالَكُمْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction and an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; أثقالكم is mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is conjoined. ﴿إِلى بَلَدٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تحمل. ﴿لَمْ﴾ a particle of jussive, negation and conversion [of tense] (qalb). ﴿تَكُونُوا﴾ a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb and the wāw is its noun; the clause is a naʿt of بلد. ﴿بالِغِيهِ﴾ khabar, accusative (manṣūb) with the yāʾ; the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿بِشِقِّ الْأَنْفُسِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl; الأنفس is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿إِنَّ رَبَّكُمْ﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿لَرَؤُفٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾ the two khabars of inna, both nominative, and the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); the clause is resumptive.

daas-irab:8-10.t: ﴿وَالْخَيْلَ﴾ conjoined to الأنعام. ﴿وَالْبِغالَ وَالْحَمِيرَ﴾ conjoined to what precedes. ﴿لِتَرْكَبُوها﴾ the lām is the lām of causation (taʿlīl); an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied (muḍmara) an after the lām of causation; the wāw is the fāʿil (agent) and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); an and what follows it are interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of genitive, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) خلقها. ﴿وَزِينَةً﴾ mafʿūl bihi of an omitted verb, its implied form being "جعلها زينة" (He made them an adornment), and it is conjoined. ﴿وَيَخْلُقُ﴾ the wāw is resumptive and an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿ما﴾ a relative, mafʿūl bihi. ﴿لا﴾ negating. ﴿تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative. ﴿وَعَلَى اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty is genitive by على; [the preposition and its genitive noun are] attached to the khabar (predicate) of قصد. ﴿قَصْدُ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative; the clause is resumptive. ﴿السَّبِيلِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَمِنْها جائِرٌ﴾ جائر is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "منها سبيل جائر" (of them is a deviating path); the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the fronted khabar; the clause is conjoined to the one before it. ﴿وَلَوْ﴾ the wāw is resumptive; law is a non-jussive conditional particle. ﴿شاءَ﴾ [الله]: a past verb and the Name of Majesty is its fāʿil; the clause has no grammatical position because it is initial (ibtidāʾiyya). ﴿لَهَداكُمْ﴾ the lām occurs in the response to law, and a past verb whose fāʿil is latent; the kāf is its object. ﴿أَجْمَعِينَ﴾ tawkīd (emphasis) of the mafʿūl bihi; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition. ﴿هُوَ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿الَّذِي﴾ a relative noun, khabar. ﴿أَنْزَلَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿مِنَ السَّماءِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أنزل. ﴿ماءً﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the fronted khabar. ﴿مِنْهُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to شراب. ﴿شَرابٌ﴾ mubtadaʾ; the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَمِنْهُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the fronted khabar. ﴿شَجَرٌ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause is conjoined to what precedes. ﴿فِيهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تسيمون. ﴿تُسِيمُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is a naʿt of شجر.

daas-irab:11-13.t: ﴿يُنْبِتُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ينبت. ﴿بِهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ينبت. ﴿الزَّرْعَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَالزَّيْتُونَ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to الزرع. ﴿وَالنَّخِيلَ وَالْأَعْنابَ﴾ conjoined to what precedes. ﴿وَمِنْ كُلِّ﴾ conjoined to what has gone before. ﴿الثَّمَراتِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿إِنَّ فِي ذلِكَ لَآيَةً﴾ inna; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the fronted khabar (predicate); ذا is a demonstrative, the lām is for distance and the kāf for address; آية is the noun of inna, and the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); the clause is resumptive. ﴿لِقَوْمٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of آية. ﴿يَتَفَكَّرُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is a naʿt of قوم. ﴿وَسَخَّرَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is conjoined. ﴿لَكُمُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to سخر. ﴿اللَّيْلَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَالنَّهارَ﴾ conjoined to الليل. ﴿وَالشَّمْسَ وَالْقَمَرَ﴾ conjoined to what precedes. ﴿وَالنُّجُومُ مُسَخَّراتٌ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar; the clause is conjoined. ﴿بِأَمْرِهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to مسخرات. ﴿إِنَّ﴾ inna, a particle resembling the verb. ﴿فِي ذلِكَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the fronted khabar. ﴿لَآياتٍ لِقَوْمٍ يَعْقِلُونَ﴾ the shifted lām, and آيات is the noun of inna, accusative (manṣūb) with the kasra because it is a sound masculine feminine [plural] [Translator's note: the source reads «مؤنث مذكر سالم» as written; a sound feminine plural (jamʿ muʾannath sālim) is evidently meant]; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted naʿt of آيات; and the clause يتفكرون is in the position of genitive as a naʿt of قوم. [Translator's note: the verb in this verse is يعقلون; the source writes يتفكرون, carried over from the previous verse.] ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is a conjunction and mā is a relative. ﴿ذَرَأَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ذرأ. ﴿فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ذرأ. ﴿مُخْتَلِفاً﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿أَلْوانُهُ﴾ fāʿil of مختلف. ﴿إِنَّ فِي ذلِكَ لَآيَةً لِقَوْمٍ يَذَّكَّرُونَ﴾ see the i'rab of the end of the two preceding verses; this verse is resumptive.

daas-irab:14-16.t: ﴿وَهُوَ الَّذِي﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; هو is mubtadaʾ (subject) and الذي is a relative noun, its khabar (predicate); the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa). ﴿سَخَّرَ الْبَحْرَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), and البحر is its object; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿لِتَأْكُلُوا﴾ the lām is for causation (taʿlīl), and an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied (muḍmara) an after the lām of causation; the wāw is the fāʿil; an and what follows it are interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of genitive; [the preposition and its genitive noun are] attached to (mutaʿalliq) سخر. ﴿مِنْهُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تأكلوا. ﴿لَحْماً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿طَرِيًّا﴾ naʿt (adjective). ﴿وَتَسْتَخْرِجُوا﴾ an imperfect verb and the wāw is its fāʿil; it is conjoined to تأكلوا and accusative like it, by the deletion of the nūn. ﴿مِنْهُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تستخرجوا. ﴿حِلْيَةً﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿تَلْبَسُونَها﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi; the clause is a naʿt of حلية. ﴿وَتَرَى الْفُلْكَ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent, and الفلك is its object; the clause is parenthetical (iʿtirāḍiyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿مَواخِرَ﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿فِيهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to مواخر. ﴿وَلِتَبْتَغُوا﴾ its i'rab is like the i'rab of لتأكلوا, and it is conjoined to it. ﴿مِنْ فَضْلِهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to مواخر. ﴿وَلِتَبْتَغُوا﴾ its i'rab is like the i'rab of لتأكلوا, and it is conjoined to it. ﴿مِنْ فَضْلِهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تبتغوا. [Translator's note: the source repeats ﴿وَلِتَبْتَغُوا﴾ ﴿مِنْ فَضْلِهِ﴾ twice, the first time attaching من فضله to مواخر and the second time to تبتغوا; both are translated as written.] ﴿وَلَعَلَّكُمْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; لعل, and the kāf is its noun; the clause is conjoined. ﴿تَشْكُرُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of لعل. ﴿وَأَلْقى فِي الْأَرْضِ رَواسِيَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa implied (muqaddara) on the alif owing to impossibility; its fāʿil is latent; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ألقى; رواسي is a naʿt of an omitted mafʿūl bihi, its implied form being "جبالا رواسي" (firm mountains). ﴿أَنْ تَمِيدَ﴾ an, the particle of the subjunctive (al-nāṣiba), and تميد is an imperfect verb, accusative. ﴿بِكُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تميد; an and what follows it are in the position of accusative as mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. "out of aversion to its shaking". ﴿وَأَنْهاراً وَسُبُلًا﴾ conjoined to رواسي. ﴿لَعَلَّكُمْ تَهْتَدُونَ﴾ its i'rab has already been given. ﴿عَلاماتٍ﴾ conjoined to رواسي and accusative like it. ﴿وَبِالنَّجْمِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يهتدون. ﴿هُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿يَهْتَدُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the khabar.

daas-irab:17-20.t: ﴿أَفَمَنْ﴾ the hamza is for interrogation, the fāʾ is a conjunction, and man is a relative, mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is conjoined to what precedes. ﴿يَخْلُقُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿كَمَنْ﴾ the kāf is a preposition and man is a relative; [the preposition and its genitive noun are] attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of man. ﴿لا يَخْلُقُ﴾ lā is negating and يخلق is an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿أَفَلا﴾ the hamza is for interrogation, the fāʾ is a conjunction and lā is negating. ﴿تَذَكَّرُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. [Translator's note: there is no relative here for this clause to be a ṣila of; the source says "ṣila" as written.] ﴿وَإِنْ﴾ the wāw is resumptive and in is conditional. ﴿تَعُدُّوا﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) because it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), the sign of its jussive being the deletion of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil; the conditional sentence is resumptive, and the clause of the protasis is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿نِعْمَةَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿لا تُحْصُوها﴾ lā is negating, and an imperfect verb, jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); the wāw is the fāʿil and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a condition not joined to the fāʾ. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَغَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾ inna, and the Name of Majesty is its noun; غفور and رحيم are its two khabars, and the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَاللَّهُ﴾ the wāw is resumptive and the Name of Majesty is mubtadaʾ. ﴿يَعْلَمُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿ما﴾ a relative, mafʿūl bihi; the clause is the khabar. ﴿تُسِرُّونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿وَما تُعْلِنُونَ﴾ conjoined to the one before it, and its i'rab is like its i'rab. ﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾ the wāw is resumptive and the relative noun is mubtadaʾ. ﴿يَدْعُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿مِنْ دُونِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يدعون. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿لا يَخْلُقُونَ﴾ lā is negating, and an imperfect verb, nominative, and its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of الذين. ﴿شَيْئاً﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَهُمْ﴾ the wāw is the wāw of ḥāl (circumstantial) and هم is mubtadaʾ. ﴿يَخْلُقُونَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is the khabar, and the clause هم is a ḥāl clause.

daas-irab:21-24.t: ﴿أَمْواتٌ﴾ khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "هم أموات" (they are dead); the clause is resumptive. ﴿غَيْرُ﴾ naʿt (adjective) of أموات. ﴿أَحْياءٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is a conjunction and mā is negating. ﴿يَشْعُرُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa). ﴿أَيَّانَ﴾ an interrogative noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of accusative as an adverb of time. ﴿يُبْعَثُونَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause أيان يبعثون is in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿إِلهُكُمْ إِلهٌ﴾ mubtadaʾ and khabar; the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿واحِدٌ﴾ naʿt; the clause is resumptive. ﴿فَالَّذِينَ﴾ the fāʾ is resumptive and الذين is a relative noun, mubtadaʾ. ﴿لا يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ lā is negating, and an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause), and the sentence of mubtadaʾ and khabar is resumptive. ﴿بِالْآخِرَةِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) يؤمنون. ﴿قُلُوبُهُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ; the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿مُنْكِرَةٌ﴾ khabar; the clause is the khabar of الذين. ﴿وَهُمْ مُسْتَكْبِرُونَ﴾ mubtadaʾ and khabar; the clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿لا جَرَمَ﴾ it means "it is true and established" (ḥaqqa wa-thabata), a past verb, and what follows it — inna, its noun and its khabar — stands in place of the fāʿil. [Translator's note: the particle that follows is أنّ (anna); the source writes «إن» as written.] ﴿أَنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ anna, and the Name of Majesty is its noun. ﴿يَعْلَمُ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative. ﴿ما﴾ a relative, mafʿūl bihi; the fāʿil of يعلم is latent (mustatir). ﴿يُسِرُّونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿وَما يُعْلِنُونَ﴾ its i'rab is like the one before it, and it is conjoined to it. ﴿إِنَّهُ﴾ inna and its noun; the clause is resumptive. ﴿لا يُحِبُّ﴾ lā is negating, and an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿الْمُسْتَكْبِرِينَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb) with the yāʾ; the clause is the khabar of inna. ﴿وَإِذا﴾ the wāw is resumptive and إذا is an adverb containing the sense of condition. ﴿قِيلَ﴾ a passive past verb; the clause is muḍāf ilayhi, and the nāʾib fāʿil is the clause ماذا أنزل ربكم. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to قيل. ﴿ماذا﴾ mā is an interrogative noun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ, and dhā is a relative noun in the position of nominative as khabar; the clause is the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿أَنْزَلَ رَبُّكُمْ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the object of speech. ﴿قالُوا﴾ a past verb and fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿أَساطِيرُ﴾ khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "هي". ﴿الْأَوَّلِينَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is the object of speech.

daas-irab:25-26.t: ﴿لِيَحْمِلُوا﴾ the lām is for causation (taʿlīl); يحملوا is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied (muḍmara) an after the lām of causation; the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); the lām and what follows it are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb قالوا; the clause is resumptive. ﴿أَوْزارَهُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿كامِلَةً﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿يَوْمَ﴾ an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān). ﴿الْقِيامَةِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَمِنْ أَوْزارِ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to أوزارهم. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ a relative noun, muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿يُضِلُّونَهُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil and its object; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿بِغَيْرِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl from the hāʾ. ﴿عِلْمٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿أَلا﴾ a particle of drawing attention (tanbīh). ﴿ساءَ﴾ a past verb for expressing blame (inshāʾ al-dhamm). ﴿ما﴾ a relative noun in the position of nominative as fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿يَزِرُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿قَدْ﴾ a particle of realisation (taḥqīq). ﴿مَكَرَ﴾ a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ a relative noun in the position of nominative as fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ṣila. ﴿فَأَتَى﴾ the fāʾ is resumptive, and a past verb indeclinable on the fatḥa implied (muqaddara) owing to impossibility. ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ the Name of Majesty, fāʿil. ﴿بُنْيانَهُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿مِنَ الْقَواعِدِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أتى; the clause is resumptive. ﴿فَخَرَّ عَلَيْهِمُ السَّقْفُ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb and its fāʿil; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to خر. ﴿مِنْ فَوْقِهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl; the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَأَتاهُمُ الْعَذابُ﴾ a past verb, its fronted object and its postponed fāʿil; the clause is conjoined. ﴿مِنْ حَيْثُ﴾ حيث is indeclinable on the ḍamma, in the position of genitive by min; [the preposition and its genitive noun are] attached to أتاهم. ﴿لا يَشْعُرُونَ﴾ lā is negating; يشعرون is an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is muḍāf ilayhi.

daas-irab:27-29.t: ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿يَوْمَ﴾ an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān). ﴿الْقِيامَةِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿يُخْزِيهِمْ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) with the ḍamma implied (muqaddara) on the yāʾ owing to heaviness; the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa). ﴿وَيَقُولُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is conjoined. ﴿أَيْنَ شُرَكائِيَ﴾ شركائي is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject) and the yāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi; أين is an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as an adverb of place, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted, fronted khabar (predicate); the clause is the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ a relative noun in the position of nominative, naʿt (adjective) of شركائي. ﴿كُنْتُمْ﴾ kāna and its noun. ﴿تُشَاقُّونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of kāna. ﴿فِيهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تشاقون. ﴿قالَ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ a relative noun, fāʿil. ﴿أُوتُوا الْعِلْمَ﴾ a passive past verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and العلم and its object [Translator's note: the source reads «والعلم ومفعوله» as written; العلم is evidently meant as its (second) object]; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿إِنَّ الْخِزْيَ﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿الْيَوْمَ﴾ an adverb of time attached to الخزي. ﴿وَالسُّوءَ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to الخزي. ﴿عَلَى الْكافِرِينَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the khabar; the clause is the object of speech. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ a relative noun, naʿt of الكافرين. ﴿تَتَوَفَّاهُمُ الْمَلائِكَةُ﴾ an imperfect verb, its fronted object and its postponed fāʿil. ﴿ظالِمِي﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative (manṣūb) with the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural, and the nūn was deleted for the construct (iḍāfa). ﴿أَنْفُسِهِمْ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿فَأَلْقَوُا السَّلَمَ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb, its fāʿil and its object; the clause is conjoined to the ṣila clause. ﴿ما كُنَّا﴾ the negating mā; كنا is kāna and its noun; the clause is the object of speech of an omitted verb, its implied form being "يقولون" (they say) ... etc. ﴿نَعْمَلُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is the khabar of كنا. ﴿مِنْ سُوءٍ﴾ min is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and سوء is mafʿūl bihi, genitive in form and accusative in position. ﴿بَلى﴾ a particle of reply. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ﴾ inna, and the Name of Majesty is its noun and عليم its khabar; the clause is the object of speech of an omitted verb, namely "قالوا بلى" (they said: yes indeed). ﴿بِما﴾ mā is a relative, and [the preposition and its genitive noun are] attached to عليم. ﴿كُنْتُمْ﴾ kāna and its noun; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of كنتم. ﴿فَادْخُلُوا﴾ the fāʾ is resumptive, and an imperative verb and its fāʿil. ﴿أَبْوابَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the clause has no grammatical position because it is resumptive. ﴿جَهَنَّمَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿خالِدِينَ﴾ ḥāl, accusative with the yāʾ. ﴿فِيها﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to خالدين. ﴿فَلَبِئْسَ﴾ the fāʾ is resumptive, the lām is the lām of inception (ibtidāʾ), and بئس is a past verb for expressing blame (inshāʾ al-dhamm). ﴿مَثْوَى﴾ fāʿil, nominative with the ḍamma implied on the alif owing to impossibility. ﴿الْمُتَكَبِّرِينَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr) with the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural; the clause is resumptive.

daas-irab:30-31.t: ﴿وَقِيلَ﴾ the wāw is resumptive, and a passive past verb. ﴿لِلَّذِينَ﴾ a relative noun; [the preposition and its genitive noun are] attached to (mutaʿalliq) قيل; the clause is resumptive. ﴿اتَّقَوْا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿ماذا﴾ mā is an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject), and dhā is a relative noun, khabar (predicate); the clause is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). ﴿أَنْزَلَ رَبُّكُمْ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is the ṣila. ﴿قالُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿خَيْراً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being "أنزل خيرا" (He sent down good), and it is the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿لِلَّذِينَ﴾ الذين is a relative noun, and [the preposition and its genitive noun are] attached to a fronted khabar. ﴿أَحْسَنُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿فِي هذِهِ﴾ the hāʾ is for drawing attention (tanbīh) and ذه is a demonstrative in the position of genitive; [the preposition and its genitive noun are] attached to أحسنوا. ﴿الدُّنْيا﴾ badal (substitute) of the demonstrative, in the position of genitive. ﴿حَسَنَةٌ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَلَدارُ﴾ the lām is the lām of inception (ibtidāʾ) and دار is mubtadaʾ. ﴿الْآخِرَةِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿خَيْرٌ﴾ khabar; the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَلَنِعْمَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, the lām is the lām of inception, and نعم is a past verb for expressing praise (inshāʾ al-madḥ). ﴿دارُ﴾ fāʿil. ﴿الْمُتَّقِينَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa). ﴿جَنَّاتُ﴾ khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "هي"; the clause is resumptive. ﴿عَدْنٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿يَدْخُلُونَها﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil and its object; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause. ﴿تَجْرِي﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) with the ḍamma implied (muqaddara) on the yāʾ owing to heaviness. ﴿مِنْ تَحْتِهَا﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تجري; the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿الْأَنْهارُ﴾ fāʿil; the clause is a ḥāl clause. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the fronted khabar. ﴿فِيها﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl. ﴿ما﴾ a relative, postponed mubtadaʾ. ﴿يَشاؤُنَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿كَذلِكَ﴾ ذا is a demonstrative, and [the preposition and its genitive noun are] attached to a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿يَجْزِي اللَّهُ الْمُتَّقِينَ﴾ an imperfect verb; the Name of Majesty is its fāʿil and المتقين its object; the clause is resumptive.

daas-irab:32-33.t:
﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ a relative, mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿تَتَوَفَّاهُمُ الْمَلائِكَةُ﴾ an imperfect verb, its fronted object and its postponed fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿طَيِّبِينَ﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative (manṣūb) with the yāʾ. ﴿يَقُولُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of الذين. ﴿سَلامٌ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar; the clause is the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿ادْخُلُوا الْجَنَّةَ﴾ an imperative verb, its fāʿil and its object; the clause is the object of speech. ﴿بِما﴾ mā is a relative; [the preposition and its genitive noun are] attached to ادخلوا. ﴿كُنْتُمْ﴾ kāna and its noun; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar.
[Translator's note: from this point to the end of the entry the source's markup is corrupted — the opening brackets and first letters of the Quranic words are fused onto the preceding line (e.g. «خبرَلْ»», «حرف استفهامَ نْظُرُونَ»»). The Quranic words below are restored from the muṣḥaf; the analyses are translated as written.]
