(الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَصَدُّوا عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ زِدْناهُمْ عَذاباً فَوْقَ الْعَذابِ بِما كانُوا يُفْسِدُونَ) الذين is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the clause زدناهم, and the clause كفروا is a ṣila; وصدوا عن سبيل الله is conjoined to كفروا. زدناهم: a verb, an agent and a direct object; عذابا is a second direct object; فوق العذاب is an adverbial attached to an omitted adjective of عذابا; بما is attached to زدناهم, and the bāʾ is causal, and ما is maṣdar-forming, that is, "because of their turning away and their corruption"; and كان and its noun, and the clause يفسدون is its khabar.
(وَيَوْمَ نَبْعَثُ فِي كُلِّ أُمَّةٍ شَهِيداً عَلَيْهِمْ مِنْ أَنْفُسِهِمْ) The adverbial is attached to an omitted element, its implied form being "mention"; this clause has been repeated as hyperbole in threat and warning. The clause نبعث is annexed to the adverbial; في كل أمة is attached to نبعث; شهيدا is a direct object; عليهم is attached to شهيدا; and من أنفسهم is an adjective of شهيدا. (وَجِئْنا بِكَ شَهِيداً عَلى هؤُلاءِ) وجئنا: the wāw is a conjunction and جئنا is a verb and an agent; بك is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to جئنا; شهيدا is a ḥāl; and على هؤلاء is attached to شهيدا.
(وَنَزَّلْنا عَلَيْكَ الْكِتابَ تِبْياناً لِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ وَهُدىً وَرَحْمَةً وَبُشْرى لِلْمُسْلِمِينَ) ونزلنا is conjoined to جئنا and نا is the agent; عليك is attached to نزلنا; الكتاب is a direct object; تبيانا is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi or a ḥāl, that is, "making clear"; لكل شيء is attached to تبيانا; هدى, رحمة and بشرى are conjoined to تبيانا; and للمسلمين is attached to بشرى, and it is attached in meaning to the other preceding maṣdars.
(إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَأْمُرُ بِالْعَدْلِ وَالْإِحْسانِ وَإِيتاءِ ذِي الْقُرْبى) إن and its noun, and the clause يأمر is the khabar of inna; بالعدل is attached to يأمر; الإحسان is conjoined to العدل, and likewise إيتاء; and ذي القربى is annexed to إيتاء. (وَيَنْهى عَنِ الْفَحْشاءِ وَالْمُنْكَرِ وَالْبَغْيِ يَعِظُكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَذَكَّرُونَ) وينهى is conjoined to يأمر and the agent is latent; عن الفحشاء is attached to ينهى and what follows is conjoined to it; the clause يعظكم is a ḥāl from the agent of يأمر and ينهى; and لعل and its noun, and the clause تذكرون, that is, tatadhakkarūn, is its khabar.

* Rhetoric:
The scholars of rhetoric and the exegetes all agreed that this verse is the most comprehensive verse in the Qur'an for good and evil, namely His saying, Exalted is He: «إن الله يأمر بالعدل والإحسان إلخ». ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, the righteous caliph, ordered its recitation in place of the cursing of Imam ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib that used to follow the Friday sermons, and because of it ʿUthmān ibn Maẓʿūn became a Muslim. It is reported that the Prophet ﷺ recited it to al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra, who said to him: "O son of my brother, repeat it." So the Prophet ﷺ repeated its recitation to him, and he said to him: "It has sweetness, it has charm, its top is fruitful and its bottom is abundant, and it is not the speech of a human being."
In reality it contains varieties of rhetoric, which we explain in what follows:
1- Concision (al-ījāz): At the beginning of the verse He commanded every good deed, then after that forbade every evil deed, and concluded the verse with the most eloquent admonitions, framing that in the most concise expressions.
2- Soundness of division (ṣiḥḥat al-taqsīm): He covered in it all divisions of the meaning, so that no good deed remains that does not fall within the scope of the command, and no evil deed remains that does not fall within the range of the prohibition. He put the mention of justice first because it is obligatory and followed it with benevolence because it is recommended, so that the arrangement of the speech might fall in the finest order. He coupled them in the command because the obligatory is not free of some defect and shortcoming which the recommended and supererogatory make good. And He singled out the kinsfolk for mention after their inclusion in the generality of those whom one is commanded to treat with justice and benevolence, to show the excellence of the kinsfolk and the excellence of the reward upon it.
3- Verbal antithesis (ṭibāq) and contrast (muqābala): between "commands" and "forbids", between justice, benevolence and giving to kinsfolk, and between indecency, wrongdoing and oppression.
4- Beauty of arrangement (ḥusn al-nasaq): in the ordering of the clauses and their conjoining one with another as is fitting, where He put justice first and conjoined benevolence to it, since benevolence is a general noun and giving to kinsfolk is specific, so it is as if it were a kind of that genus; then He brought the clause of command first and conjoined the clause of prohibition to it.
5- Tasḥīm (the opening indicates the end): because the beginning of the speech points to its end, as the beginning of a "striped" verse points to its end.
6- Beauty of exposition (ḥusn al-bayān): because the one who hears the wording of the verse does not hesitate in understanding its meaning, as it is free of obscurity in its wording and points to its meaning clearly by the nearest and easiest ways, and the intelligent and the dull are equal in understanding it.
7- Harmony (al-iʾtilāf): because every word is such that no other can take its place.
8- Equivalence (al-musāwāt): because the words of the speech are moulds for its meanings, neither exceeding them nor falling short of them.
9- Firm placing of the rhyme-ending (tamkīn al-fāṣila): because the closing of the verse sits settled in its place, firm in its resting place, its meaning connected to what precedes up to the beginning of the speech; and because admonition is not good except after the charge of making the command and prohibition clear; and because whichever word you remove from the words of the verse, the meaning is plainly disturbed by its removal and clearly diminished.

dervis-irab:91-93.t:
* Vocabulary:
(تَوْكِيدِها): Their ratification. Al-Tawkīd is the maṣdar of wakkada yuwakkidu with wāw, and in it is another dialect, akkada yuʾakkidu with hamza, and its meaning is strengthening. This is like their saying warrakhtu l-kitāb and arrakhtuhu (I dated the book); the hamza is not a replacement for a wāw, as some claimed, because the two usages in the two roots are equal, so claiming that one of them is the origin is no better than the other.
(أَنْكاثاً): The plural of nikth, with kasra on the nūn, which is that whose twisting has been undone. In al-Miṣbāḥ: «nakatha l-rajulu l-ʿahd nakthan (pattern qatala) means he broke it and cast it aside, so it was undone (intakatha), like naqaḍahu fa-ntaqaḍa; and nakatha l-kisāʾ and others means he also unravelled it. And al-nikth, with kasra, is what is unravelled in order to be spun a second time, and the plural is ankāth, like ḥiml and aḥmāl.» And in al-Qāmūs: «al-Nikth, with kasra, is what is unravelled of cloaks and tents to be spun a second time, and its plural is ankāth. It is said: ḥablun nikthun and ankāthun, that is, an unravelled rope (mankūth).»
(دَخَلًا): Corruption and treachery (daghal). In al-Ṣiḥāḥ: «al-Daghal, vocalised, is corruption, like al-dakhal.» In the dictionaries: «al-Dakhal is a defect.» In al-Qāmūs and al-Tāj: «al-Dakhal, with two fatḥas, is the corruption that enters a person in intellect or body; deceit; a flaw in lineage; and people who ascribe themselves to those they are not of. Among the strange things about the letters dāl and khāʾ is that they do not come together except to point to corruption or darkness: al-dakh and al-dukh, with fatḥa or ḍamma on the dāl, is smoke, and enough for you is its darkness and dinginess. A Bedouin woman said to her husband, who had grown old:
لا خير في الشيخ إذا ما اجلخا ... وسال غرب عينه ولخا
وكان أكلا قاعدا وشخا ... تحت رواق البيت يغشى الدخا
وانثنت الرجل فصارت فخا ... وصار وصل الغانيات أخا
(There is no good in an old man when he grows bent, and the tear-duct of his eye runs and is gummed; when he is an eater, sitting, passing water under the awning of the tent, enveloped in smoke; when his leg is bent and becomes a snare, and the favour of fair women becomes for him a brother's [mere kinship].)
And dakhara means he became abased and small, and adkharahu means he abased him. Dakhisa l-ḥāfir, with kasra on the khāʾ, means the hoof was struck by the disease of al-dakhas, with sukūn on the khāʾ, which is a swelling in the hoof; and al-dukhas, with ḍamma on the dāl and sukūn on the khāʾ, is a creature of the sea. Al-Dakhīs is the entangled part of pasture; and when it is entangled it nears blackness and large number, and the plump flesh. Tadākhalat al-umūr means the affairs became confused and resembled each other. And al-dakhl, with fatḥa on the dāl and sukūn on the khāʾ, is what comes in to you of your wealth, and its opposite is al-kharj (expenditure); it is a corruption for its owner unless he pays its zakāh and what follows from it, and from it the income tax was named. Dukhla (with the three vowels on the dāl) of a man is his inner part, hidden in the darkness of concealment. Al-Dakhīl is one who has entered a people and ascribed himself to them but is not of them, so he is in confusion about his affair and is seldom righteous; and "a dakhīl disease" means one entering the depths of the body; and every foreign word that has been brought into the speech of the Arabs. Dakhamahu means he pushed him with disturbance. Dakhkhana l-ṭaʿām wa-l-laḥm and the like means smoke reached it while it was cooked or grilled, so the smell of smoke overcame its taste, so it is dakhin. Al-Dakhan, with two fatḥas, is rancour, corruption, and a change of mind, religion and lineage. It is said: "I will not make peace with him on a dakhan", that is, on deceit and corruption. Al-Dukhiyy, with fatḥa on the shaddated dāl, is darkness, and a dukhyāʾ night is dark. And this is among the wonders of languages.»
(أَرْبى): More numerous in number and more abundant in wealth.

* I'rab:
(وَأَوْفُوا بِعَهْدِ اللَّهِ إِذا عاهَدْتُمْ) The wāw is a conjunction; أوفوا is an imperative verb and an agent; بعهد الله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أوفوا; إذا is a future adverbial including the meaning of a condition; and the clause عاهدتم is annexed to the adverbial. (وَلا تَنْقُضُوا الْأَيْمانَ بَعْدَ تَوْكِيدِها وَقَدْ جَعَلْتُمُ اللَّهَ عَلَيْكُمْ كَفِيلًا) The wāw is a conjunction; لا is prohibitive; تنقضوا is an imperfect verb jussive by لا and the wāw is the agent; الأيمان is a direct object; بعد is an adverbial attached to تنقضوا; توكيدها is a muḍāf ilayhi; the wāw is circumstantial and the clause is a ḥāl from the agent of تنقضوا; قد is a particle of certainty; جعلتم الله: a verb, an agent and a direct object; عليكم is attached to كفيلا; and كفيلا is a second direct object of جعلتم. (إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَعْلَمُ ما تَفْعَلُونَ) The i'rab of its like has often preceded. (وَلا تَكُونُوا كَالَّتِي نَقَضَتْ غَزْلَها مِنْ بَعْدِ قُوَّةٍ أَنْكاثاً) The wāw is a conjunction; لا is prohibitive and تكونوا is jussive by it; كان and its noun, and the kāf is its khabar; the clause نقضت is a ṣila; غزلها is a direct object; من بعد قوة is a ḥāl from the agent of نقضت or from its object, that is, "making it firm" or "made firm"; and أنكاثا is accusative by an omitted verb, that is, "and so she made it ankāth", or because نقضت is made to include the meaning of "she turned into", in which case it is a second object. Al-Zajjāj allowed another aspect for it, namely accusative as a maṣdar, because the meaning of naqaḍat is nakathat, so it agrees in meaning with its governor. It was also said that it is a ḥāl from غزلها, that is, "unravelled". The story of this woman will come in the section on Benefits. (تَتَّخِذُونَ أَيْمانَكُمْ دَخَلًا بَيْنَكُمْ أَنْ تَكُونَ أُمَّةٌ هِيَ أَرْبى مِنْ أُمَّةٍ) The clause تتخذون is a ḥāl from the pronoun of تكونوا, that is, "do not be like her, taking your oaths as a means of deceit"; تتخذون is an imperfect verb and an agent; أيمانكم is a first direct object and دخلا is a second direct object; بينكم is an adjective of دخلا; أن and what is within its scope is an interpreted maṣdar in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl li-ajlihi, that is, "for fear that there should be"; أمة is the noun of تكون, هي is a mubtadaʾ and أربى its khabar, and the clause is the khabar of تكون; and من أمة is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أربى. They used to make alliances with allies and cut agreements and covenants, and when they found others more numerous and mightier in side, they broke the alliance of the former and allied with the latter.
(إِنَّما يَبْلُوكُمُ اللَّهُ بِهِ وَلَيُبَيِّنَنَّ لَكُمْ يَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ ما كُنْتُمْ فِيهِ تَخْتَلِفُونَ) إنما is a kāffa and makfūfa, and it is for restriction; يبلوكم الله: a verb, a fronted object and a delayed agent; به is attached to يبلوكم. وليبيننّ: the wāw is a conjunction, the lām is the preparatory lām of the oath, and يبينّ is an imperfect verb indeclinable on fatḥa because of the obligatory attachment of the heavy nūn of emphasis; لكم is attached to يبينن; يوم القيامة is an adverbial attached to an omitted ḥāl; ما is a direct object; كنتم is a ṣila, being kāna and its noun; فيه is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تختلفون; and the clause تختلفون is the khabar of كنتم. (وَلَوْ شاءَ اللَّهُ لَجَعَلَكُمْ أُمَّةً واحِدَةً) The wāw is a conjunction; لو is conditional; شاء الله is a verb and an agent; the lām occurs in the apodosis of لو; جعلكم is a verb, a latent agent and a first direct object; أمة is a second direct object; and واحدة is an adjective. (وَلكِنْ يُضِلُّ مَنْ يَشاءُ وَيَهْدِي مَنْ يَشاءُ) The wāw is circumstantial; لكن is a particle of rectification, inoperative because it has been lightened; يضل is an imperfect verb whose agent is latent, its implied form being "He"; من is a direct object and يشاء is a ṣila; and ويهدي من يشاء is conjoined to what preceded. (وَلَتُسْئَلُنَّ عَمَّا كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ) The wāw is a conjunction; the lām is the preparatory lām of the oath; تسألن is an imperfect verb that is declined, because the nūn did not directly attach to it, so it is nominative, and the sign of its nominative is the presence of the nūn that has been omitted because of the succession of similar letters; the wāw, omitted because of the meeting of two sukūns, is the deputy agent; the doubled nūn is the heavy nūn of emphasis; عما is attached to تسألن; and the clause كنتم تعملون is the khabar of كنتم.

* Benefits:
History reports that a foolish woman named Rayṭa bint Saʿd ibn Taymī, of Mecca, took a spindle about a cubit long, a hook like a finger and a great whorl proportionate to it, and she would spin, she and her maidservants, from the morning until noon, then order them and they would unravel what they had spun. So the speech is a representational simile (tashbīh tamthīlī) in unrestricted form (mursal), and the thing likened to is specified.

farraa:101-101.t: His saying: ﴿وَإِذَا بَدَّلْنَآ آيَةً مَّكَانَ آيَةٍ﴾ (and when We substitute a verse in place of a verse): when We abrogate a verse in place of a verse that is gentler than it, the idolaters said: "He is only making it up himself and learning it from ʿĀʾish", a slave owned by Ḥuwayṭib ibn ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā, who had become Muslim and whose Islam was good, and who was a non-Arab. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said:

farraa:103-103.t: His saying: ﴿لِّسَانُ ٱلَّذِي يُلْحِدُونَ إِلَيْهِ﴾ (the tongue of the one they allude to): they incline towards him and are fond of him, (أعْجَمِىٌّ) (is foreign). So Allah said: and this is the tongue of Muhammad ﷺ, and the Qurʾān is Arabic.

farraa:110-110.t: His saying: ﴿ثُمَّ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ لِلَّذِينَ هَاجَرُواْ مِن بَعْدِ مَا فُتِنُواْ﴾ (then indeed your Lord, to those who emigrated after they had been put to trial): he says: (after) they were tortured. It was revealed concerning ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir and his companions who were tortured, until some of them uttered polytheism with their tongues while believing in their hearts; so Allah forgave them. That is His saying ﴿إِنَّ رَبَّكَ مِن بَعْدِهَا لَغَفُورٌ رَّحِيمٌ﴾ (indeed your Lord, after it, is Forgiving, Merciful): after the deed.

farraa:112-112.t:
His saying: ﴿قَرْيَةً كَانَتْ آمِنَةً مُّطْمَئِنَّةً﴾ (a town that was secure and at rest) means Mecca: it was not raided, as the Arabs used to do — they used to raid one another. (مُّطْمَئِنَّةً) (at rest): it did not move about, as the Arabs move in search of pasture by migrating.
His saying ﴿مِّن كُلِّ مَكَانٍ﴾ (from every place): from every direction. ﴿فَكَفَرَتْ﴾ (but it was ungrateful) — then He said ﴿بِمَا كَانُواْ يَصْنَعُونَ﴾ (for what they used to do) «[Translator's note: i.e. the feminine singular "town" is followed by a masculine plural referring to its people.]». There is much like this in the Qurʾān. Among it is His saying ﴿فَجَاءَهَا بَأْسُنَا بَيَاتاً أَوُهُمْ قائِلونَ﴾ (Our punishment came to it by night or while they were resting at midday), and He did not say قائلة. When He says (قائلون) He has the men in view, and when He says (قائلة) He means only its people; and His saying ﴿فحاسَبْنَاهَا حِسَاباً شدِيداً وعَذّبْنَاهَا عَذَابا نُكْراً فَذَاقَتْ﴾ (so We called it to a severe account and punished it with a terrible punishment, and it tasted).
His saying ﴿لِبَاسَ ٱلْجُوعِ وَٱلْخَوْفِ﴾ (the garment of hunger and fear): they were afflicted with hunger for seven years, until they ate burnt bones and carrion. The fear was the expeditions and raiding parties of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Then the Prophet ﷺ felt pity for them and sent them food while they were idolaters. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said to them: eat ﴿وَاشْكُرُوا﴾ (and be grateful).

farraa:119-119.t: His saying: ﴿لِلَّذِينَ عَمِلُواْ ٱلسُّوۤءَ بِجَهَالَةٍ﴾ (to those who do evil in ignorance): everyone who does an evil deed is ignorant when he does it.

farraa:120-120.t: His saying: ﴿أُمَّةً قَانِتاً﴾ (an umma, devoutly obedient): a teacher (a marker) of good.

farraa:124-124.t: His saying: ﴿إِنَّمَا جُعِلَ ٱلسَّبْتُ عَلَىٰ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱخْتَلَفُواْ فِيهِ﴾ (the Sabbath was only imposed on those who differed over it): Moses came to his followers and said: "Devote yourselves to Allah on Friday and do no work on it." They said: "No, rather on Saturday, on which Allah finished creating the heavens and the earth." So it was made strict for them. Jesus also brought Friday to the Christians, and they said: "Their festival shall not come after ours", and so they turned to Sunday. That is their disagreement. It is also read (إنما جَعَل [98] «[Translator's note: "98" is a manuscript folio marker.]» السبتَ — with the accusative, i.e. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, made (it)).

farraa:126-126.t: His saying: ﴿وَإِنْ عَاقَبْتُمْ فَعَاقِبُواْ بِمِثْلِ مَا عُوقِبْتُمْ بِهِ﴾ (and if you retaliate, retaliate with the like of what you were made to suffer) (it was revealed concerning Ḥamza): when the idolaters mutilated Ḥamza on the day of Uḥud, the Prophet ﷺ said: "I shall mutilate seventy elders of Quraysh." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed ﴿وَإِنْ عَاقَبْتُمْ فَعَاقِبُواْ بِمِثْلِ مَا عُوقِبْتُمْ بِهِ﴾, then He commanded him to be patient, saying ﴿وَلَئِن صَبَرْتُمْ لَهُوَ خَيْرٌ لِّلصَّابِرينَ﴾ (but if you are patient, it is better for those who are patient); then He commanded him to be patient as a firm resolve.

farraa:127-127.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱصْبِرْ وَمَا صَبْرُكَ إِلاَّ بِٱللَّهِ﴾ (and be patient, and your patience is only through Allah), and His saying ﴿وَلاَ تَكُ فِي ضَيْقٍ مِّمَّا يَمْكُرُونَ﴾ (and do not be in distress over what they plot): الضَّيق (ḍayq) is that by which your breast is straitened, while الضِّيق (ḍīq) is what occurs in something that can be wide, such as a house, a garment and the like. When you see الضَّيْق occurring in the place of الضِّيق, it is on one of two aspects: one is that it is a plural whose singular is ضَيْقة, as (the poet) said:
* كَشَف الضيْقة عَنا وفَسَحْ *
(He removed the straits from us and made room.)
The other aspect is that a "narrow thing" (شىء ضَيِّق) is meant, so it is lightened (by dropping the doubling), its origin being the doubled form, like هَيْن and لَيْن, by which you mean هيِّن and لَيّن (easy, gentle).

farraa:81-81.t:
His saying: ﴿سَرَابِيلَ تَقِيكُمُ ٱلْحَرَّ﴾ (garments that protect you from the heat).
He did not say "the cold", although they protect from both heat and cold; it was left out because its meaning is known — and Allah knows best — as in the poet's words:
وما أدْرِى إذا يمَّمت وجهاً * أريد الخير أيُّهما يلينى
(I do not know, when I set my face in some direction seeking good, which of the two will befall me.)
He means: which of good and evil will befall me, because when he seeks good he is guarding against evil.
And His saying ﴿لَعَلَّكُمْ تُسْلِمُونَ﴾ (so that you may submit): it has reached us from Ibn ʿAbbās that he read it as (لعَلكم تَسْلَمُونَ) (so that you may be kept safe) — from wounds.

farraa:83-83.t: His saying: ﴿يَعْرِفُونَ نِعْمَتَ ٱللَّهِ﴾ (they recognise the favour of Allah) means the disbelievers: when they are asked, "Who provides for you?", they say, "Allah", but then they say, "Through the intercession of our gods", and so they associate partners with Him. That is their denial of ( نِعْمَتَ ٱللَّهِ).

farraa:86-86.t:
[His saying]: ﴿فَألْقَوْا إِلَيْهِمُ ٱلْقَوْلَ﴾ (but they will throw back the word at them): their gods will throw their words back at them: ﴿إِنَّكُمْ لَكَاذِبُونَ﴾ (indeed you are liars), i.e. "We did not call you to worship us."
And His saying: ﴿فَألْقَوْا إِلَيْهِمُ ٱلْقَوْلَ إِنَّكُمْ لَكَاذِبُونَ﴾: it (إنّ) takes kasra because it belongs to the ṣila (complement) of "the word" (القول). Whoever would give it fatḥa — had there been no lām in His saying لكاذبون — would make it an explanation of "the word": "they threw at them that you are liars" (ألقَوْ إليهم أنكم كاذبون), and it would then be in the accusative (naṣb), had there been no lām; just as you say: ألقيت إليك أنك كاذب (I put it to you that you are a liar). But only kasra is permitted once the lām comes in, so you say: ألقيت إليك إنّك لكاذب.

farraa:92-92.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلاَ تَكُونُواْ كَٱلَّتِي نَقَضَتْ غَزْلَهَا مِن بَعْدِ قُوَّةٍ﴾ (and do not be like the woman who unravelled her spun thread after it was strong): "after strength" means after twisting it firm. She used to spin wool thread and twist it firm, and then order a slave-girl of hers to unravel it. It is said that she was Rayṭa. ﴿تَتَّخِذُونَ أَيْمَانَكُمْ دَخَلاً بَيْنَكُمْ﴾ (taking your oaths as a means of deceit among you): he says: as treachery (دَغَل) and deception.
His saying ﴿أَن تَكُونَ أُمَّةٌ هِيَ أَرْبَى مِنْ أُمَّةٍ﴾ (because one community is more numerous than another): he says: it is greater in number. Its meaning is: do not betray a people because of their fewness and your great number, or your fewness and their great number, when you have lured them with oaths and they have come to rely on them. [97b] «[Translator's note: "97 ب" in the text is a manuscript folio marker.]» The position of (أدْنَى) «[Translator's note: so in the text; the verse has أَرْبَى.]» is accusative (naṣb). If you wish you may make it nominative (rafʿ), just as you say: ما أظن رجلاً يكون هو أفضلَ منك and وأفضلُ منك (I do not think any man is better than you): the accusative is on the basis of the ʿimād (the support pronoun, i.e. the separating pronoun), and the nominative is on the basis of making (هو) a noun (i.e. a mubtadaʾ (subject)). Similar is the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿تَجِدُوهُ عِنْدَ اللهِ هُوَ خَيراً وَأَعْظَمَ أَجْراً﴾ (you will find it with Allah, better and greater in reward) — accusative; had it been nominative it would have been correct.

farraa:1-1.t: His saying: ﴿سُبْحَانَهُ وَتَعَالَىٰ عَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ﴾ ("glorified and exalted is He above what they associate"). Muḥammad ibn al-Jahm narrated to us, saying: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: ʿImād ibn al-Ṣalt al-ʿUklī narrated to me from Saʿīd ibn Masrūq Abū Sufyān, from al-Rabīʿ ibn Khaytham, that he read (سُبْحَانَهُ وَتَعَالى عَمَّا تُشْرِكُون) ("above what you associate") — the first and the one after it, both with tāʾ. It is also read with yāʾ. Whoever reads with tāʾ, it is as though He addressed them; and whoever reads with yāʾ, it is as though the Qurʾān was sent down to Muḥammad ﷺ and then He said ﴿سُبْحانَهُ﴾, making him marvel at their disbelief and their associating partners.

farraa:2-2.t: His saying: ﴿يُنَزِّلُ ٱلْمَلاۤئِكَةَ﴾ ("He sends down the angels") with yāʾ, and (تَنَزَّلُ المَلائِكَةُ) ("the angels descend") with tāʾ. The reading of the companions of ʿAbd Allāh is ﴿يُنَزِّل الملائكة﴾ with yāʾ.

farraa:5-5.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱلأَنْعَامَ خَلَقَهَا لَكُمْ﴾ ("and the cattle, He created them for you"). You put (الأنعامَ) in the accusative by "created them", since there is a wāw [before] "the cattle". So it is with every verb that returns to a noun by a pronoun referring to it, when before the noun there is a wāw, or a fāʾ, or speech that allows the verb to be transferred to that particle preceding the noun: there are two ways in it, the nominative and the accusative. As for the accusative, it is that you make the wāw a container (ẓarf) for the verb; and the nominative is that you make the wāw a container for the noun that is with it. Similar to it are ﴿وَالْقَمَرَ قَدَّرْنَاهُ مَنَازِلَ﴾ ("and the moon We have determined for it phases") and ﴿والسَّمَاءَ بَنَينْاهَا بأَيْدٍ﴾ ("and the heaven We built with might"); and it is frequent.
Similar to it are ﴿وكُلَّ إنْسَانٍ أَلْزَمْنَاهُ طَائِرَهُ﴾ ("and every man We have fastened his fate to him") and ﴿وكُلَّ شىء أَحْصَيْنَاهُ﴾ ("and everything We have enumerated").
The proper way in the speech of the Arabs is to make kull nominative in these two words, whether or not there is a pronoun referring back at its end, because it is in the sense of "there is nothing but We have enumerated it in a clear register" — and Allah knows best. I heard the Arabs recite:

ما كلُّ مَنْ يظَّنُّنِى أَن مُعْتب * ولا كلُّ ما يَرْوَى عَليَّ أقول
(Not everyone who suspects me — I [will] placate, nor everything that is reported of me do I say.)

He did not make (أقول) fall upon the last kull, nor (مُعتب) upon the first. And one of them recited to me:

قد حَلِقت أَمُّ الخِيَار تَدَّعِى * علىَّ ذَنْبا كلُّه لم أصْنِع
(Umm al-Khiyār has taken to claiming against me a sin, all of which I did not commit.)

And one of the Arabs recited to me from Sūrat Yā Sīn: ﴿وَكُلَّ شَيىءٍ أَحْصَيْنَاهُ فى إِمَامٍ مُبِين﴾ ("and everything We have enumerated in a clear register") in the nominative; he recited it so more than once.
As for His saying: ﴿وكلُّ شَىْءِ فَعَلُوهُ فى الزْبُر﴾ ("and everything they did is in the scriptures"), it can only be nominative, because the meaning — and Allah knows best — is: all their deeds are written in the scriptures. So it is nominative by fī, and (فعلوه) is a ṣila (relative clause) of "thing". Had fī been connected with faʿalūhu in speech like this, both the nominative and accusative of kull would be permissible; as you say: "Every man they beat in the house": if you mean "they beat every man in the house", you use the nominative or the accusative; and if you mean "everyone they beat is in the house", you use the nominative.
His saying: ﴿لَكُمْ فِيهَا دِفْءٌ﴾ ("in them there is warmth for you"): it is what is made use of from their hair. It was written without hamza because when what precedes the hamza is quiescent the hamza is dropped in writing; that is due to the faintness of the hamza when one pauses on it. Since what preceded it was quiescent and they could not pronounce its hamza in pause, their pausing was as though on the fāʾ. Likewise His saying: ﴿يُخْرِجُ الخَبْء﴾ ("He brings forth what is hidden"), ﴿النَشْأَةَ﴾ ("the creation"), and ﴿مِلْء الأَرْضِ﴾ ("the earth's fill"). Apply to the hamza what you found in these two words.
If in speech you wrote al-difʾ with wāw in the nominative, yāʾ in the genitive and alif in the accusative, it would be correct. That is on the basis of dropping the hamza and transferring the hamza's case vowel to the letter before it. Of that is the saying of the Arabs: "These are a true generation (nashʾu ṣidqin)"; when they drop the hamza they say: "These are nashū ṣidq", "I saw nashā ṣidq" and "I passed by nashī ṣidq". Better than that is to drop the wāw, the alif and the yāʾ, because their saying yasal is more frequent than yasāl, and masala more than masāla; likewise "between al-mar' [Translator's note: written «المَرِ», i.e. al-marʾ without its hamza] and his wife", when the hamza is dropped.
The benefits (al-manāfiʿ): their carrying them on their backs, their offspring and their milk. Al-difʾ: what they wear from them and build from their hair.

farraa:6-6.t: His saying: ﴿حِينَ تُرِيحُونَ﴾ ("when you bring them home in the evening"), i.e. when you bring your camels home: you bring them back between the pasture and their resting place, which is called al-murāḥ. And al-surūḥ is in the morning (al-Farrāʾ said), when they go out to graze.

farraa:7-7.t: His saying: ﴿بِشِقِّ ٱلأَنفُسِ﴾ ("except with great hardship to yourselves"). Most of the readers have kasra on the shīn, and its meaning is: except with the exertion of the selves. It is as though [al-shiqq] is a noun and al-shaqq is a verbal noun, just as it was imagined that al-kurh is the noun and al-karh the verbal noun. Some read it so: (إلاّ بِشَقِّ الأَنْفُسِ). It is also possible in His saying ﴿بِشِقِّ ٱلأَنفُسِ﴾ that you take the view that exertion diminishes a man's strength and himself until it makes him as though half of his strength had gone; so the kasra is on the basis that it is like the half. The Arabs say: "Take this shiqq", for a half of a sheep. And it is said: "The wealth between me and you is shaqq al-shaʿra and shiqq al-shaʿra (split down the hair)", and the two are close. When they say "I caused you hardship (shaqaqtu ʿalayka shaqqan)", they use fatḥa, and we have not heard anything else.

farraa:8-8.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱلْخَيْلَ وَٱلْبِغَالَ وَٱلْحَمِيرَ﴾ ("and horses, mules and donkeys"): you put them in the accusative by referring back to "created". And if you wish, you make it accusative by implying sakhkhara ("He subjected"); its implication is then permissible like His saying: ﴿خَتَمَ اللهُ عَلَى قُلُوبِهِمْ وَعلَى سَمْعِهِمْ وَعَلَى أَبْصَارِهم غِشَاوَةً﴾ ("Allah has sealed their hearts and their hearing, and over their eyes is a covering") — whoever reads the accusative in al-Baqara puts "covering" in the accusative by implying (وجعل) ("and He placed"). Had you made ﴿ٱلْخَيْلَ وَٱلْبِغَالَ وَٱلْحَمِيرَ﴾ nominative, it would be correct in two ways. One of them is that you say: since the verb with them is not overt, I make it nominative by resumption. The other is to imagine that the nominative in "the cattle" would have been proper, and refer them back to that, as though you said: "and the cattle, He created them, and the horses and the mules", in the nominative.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿لِتَرْكَبُوهَا وَزِينَةً﴾ ("for you to ride, and as adornment"): we put it in the accusative, and we make it "as adornment" by an implied verb, like ﴿وَحِفْظاً مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْطَانٍ﴾ ("and as protection against every devil"), i.e. We made it. Had there been no wāw with "adornment" nor with (وَحِفْظاً), you would put it in the accusative by the verb before it, not by implication. Similar to it is: "I gave you a dirham, and out of desire for the reward", the meaning being "I gave it to you out of desire". Were you to drop the wāw you would not need an implied [verb], because it is connected with the verb before it.

farraa:9-9.t: His saying: ﴿وَعَلَىٰ ٱللَّهِ قَصْدُ ٱلسَّبِيلِ﴾ ("and upon Allah is [showing] the straight path"). It is said: the guidance of the ways. And it is said: the path is Islam. (وَمِنْهَا جَائِرٌ) ("and of them are deviating ones"): it is said that the deviating ones are Judaism and Christianity. What indicates that this is the [correct] view is His saying: ﴿وَلَوْ شَاءَ لَهَدَاكمْ أَجْمَعِينَ﴾ ("and had He willed, He would have guided you all").

farraa:10-10.t: His saying: ﴿تُسِيمُونَ﴾ means: you pasture your camels.

farraa:14-14.t: His saying: ﴿مَوَاخِرَ فِيهِ﴾ ("ploughing through it"): its singular is mākhira, and it is the sound of the ships running with the winds; one says makharat, tamkhiru and tamkharu.

farraa:16-16.t: His saying: ﴿وَبِٱلنَّجْمِ هُمْ يَهْتَدُونَ﴾ ("and by the star they are guided"): it is said [this means] al-Jady (the Pole Star) and al-Farqadān.

farraa:17-17.t: His saying: ﴿أَفَمَن يَخْلُقُ كَمَن لاَّ يَخْلُقُ﴾ ("is He who creates like one who does not create?"). He used (مَن) for other than people since He distinguished it and placed it alongside the Creator, and that was proper; as He said: ﴿فَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَمْشِى عَلَى بَطْنِهِ وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَمْشِى عَلَى رِجْلَيْنِ وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَمْشِى عَلَى أَرْبَعٍ﴾ ("of them are some that walk on their bellies, some that walk on two legs, and some that walk on four"). The Arabs say: "The rider and his mount became confused to me, so I do not know which (man) is which (man)": since he combined the two and one of them was a human, (مَن) was proper for both of them together.

farraa:21-21.t:
His saying: ﴿أَمْواتٌ غَيْرُ أَحْيَآءٍ﴾ ("dead, not living"): you make it nominative by resumption. And if you wish, you refer it back as a khabar (predicate) of "those who", as though He said: "and those whom you call upon besides Allah are dead". "Dead" in this place [means] that they have no spirit in them, meaning the idols. And had it been accusative, on the basis of your saying "they are created dead", as qaṭʿ (cut off, i.e. ḥāl) and by the verb falling on it, i.e. "and they are created dead, not living" [Translator's note: the sentence is left without a conclusion in the text; the sense is "it would be permissible"].
His saying: ﴿وَمَا يَشْعُرُونَ أَيَّانَ يُبْعَثُونَ﴾ ("and they do not perceive when they will be raised"). He is saying: they are dead, so how could they perceive when they will be raised? — meaning the idols. And it is said of the disbelievers: "and they do not perceive when…". Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī read (إيَّانَ يُبْعَثُونَ) with kasra on the alif of (إيَّان); it is a dialect of Sulaym. I heard one of the Arabs say: "When is the īwān of that?", while [regular] speech is "the awān (time) of that".

farraa:30-31.t: His saying: ﴿وَلَنِعْمَ دَارُ ٱلْمُتَّقِينَ﴾ ﴿جَنَّاتُ عَدْنٍ﴾ ("and excellent is the abode of the God-fearing: Gardens of Eden"). You make "gardens" nominative because it is the noun [specified] for niʿma, as you say: "Excellent is the abode, an abode you dwell in". And if you wish, you make ﴿وَلَنِعْمَ دَارُ المُتَّقِينَ﴾ self-sufficient with what precedes it, then resume "gardens", so that its nominative is by resumption. And if you wish, you make it nominative by the pronoun referring back to it in ﴿يَدْخُلُونَهَا﴾ ("which they will enter").

farraa:37-37.t:
His saying: ﴿إِن تَحْرِصْ عَلَىٰ هُدَاهُمْ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لاَ يَهْدِي مَن يُضِلُّ﴾ ("if you are eager for their guidance, Allah does not guide those whom He leads astray"). The companions of ʿAbd Allāh read it (يَهدِّى), meaning: "the one whom He leads astray will not be guided (yahtadī)". The Arabs say of a man: "hadda al-rajul", meaning: he was guided (ihtadā). Similar to it is ﴿أَمْ مَنْ لاَ يَهِدِّى إلاَّ أَنْ يُهْدَى﴾ ("or one who is not guided unless he is guided?"). Muḥammad narrated to us, saying: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAyyāsh, the brother of Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh, and Qays ibn al-Rabīʿ and others narrated to me from al-Aʿmash, from al-Shaʿbī, from ʿAlqama, that he read (لا يَهْدِى مَنْ يُضِل) likewise.
The people of the Ḥijāz read it (لا يُهْدَى من يُضلُّ) ("whoever He leads astray is not guided"), and that is a good way, because in the reading of Ubayy it is (لا هادى لمن أضل الله) ("there is no guide for whom Allah leads astray"). Man in both ways is in the position of the nominative: whoever reads ﴿يُهْدَى﴾ — it is nominative since its agent is not named [i.e. as nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent)]; and whoever reads ﴿لا يَهْدِى﴾ meaning yahtadī — the verb belongs to man [as its fāʿil (agent)].

farraa:38-38.t: His saying: ﴿بَلَىٰ وَعْداً عَلَيْهِ حَقّاً﴾ ("yes indeed — a promise binding upon Him, true"): yes, He will surely raise them, as a promise binding upon Him, true. Had it been nominative, according to [a reading like] ﴿بَلَىٰ وَعْد عَلَيْهِ حَقٌّ﴾, it would be correct.

farraa:40-40.t: His saying: ﴿إِنَّمَا قَوْلُنَا لِشَيْءٍ إِذَآ أَرَدْنَاهُ أَن نَّقُولَ لَهُ كُنْ فَيَكُونُ﴾ ("Our word to a thing, when We will it, is only that We say to it 'Be', and it is"). "Word" is nominative by His saying (أَنْ نَقُولَ), as you say: "Our word is only the truth". As for His saying ﴿فيَكُون﴾, it is accusative by being referred back to naqūla. Similar is the one in Yā Sīn, accusative, though most of the readers have made it nominative. Al-Kisāʾī used to reject the nominative in al-Naḥl [ms. 94b] and in Yā Sīn; yet it is permissible on the basis that you make ﴿أَنْ تَقُولَ لَهُ﴾ [Translator's note: so in the text, with tāʾ] a complete statement and then report that it will be, as you say of a man: "It only suffices him that I command him", and then you say: "and then he does (fa-yafʿalu) what he is commanded after that".

farraa:41-41.t: His saying: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ هَاجَرُواْ فِي ٱللَّهِ مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا ظُلِمُواْ﴾ ("and those who emigrated for Allah after they had been wronged"). It is mentioned that it was revealed concerning ʿAmmār, Ṣuhayb, Bilāl and their like, who were tortured in Mecca. ﴿لَنُبَوِّئَنَّهُمْ فِي ٱلدُّنْيَا حَسَنَةً﴾ ("We shall surely settle them in this world in a good place"): settling in Medina, and "We shall surely make the spoils lawful for them". The position of (الذين) is nominative.

farraa:43-44.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمَآ أَرْسَلْنَا مِن قَبْلِكَ إِلاَّ رِجَالاً﴾ ("We sent none before you but men"), then He said: ﴿بِٱلْبَيِّنَاتِ وَٱلزُّبُرِ﴾ ("with clear proofs and scriptures") after illā, whereas what is connected to what precedes illā is not put after illā. That is permissible on the basis of two statements. Of that is that you say: "None struck Zayd but your brother" and "None passed by Zayd but your brother". (If you say: "None struck [missing in ms. A] but your brother — Zayd", or "None passed but your brother — by Zayd"), it is on the basis of two statements: you mean "none passed but your brother", and then you say "he passed by Zayd". Similar to it is the saying of al-Aʿshā:

وليس مُجيراً إن أتى الحىَّ خائف * ولا قائِلاً إلا هو المتَعَيَّبَا
(He does not give protection if a fearful man comes to the tribe, nor does he say anything but what is shameful.)

Had it been a single statement it would be wrong, because "the shameful" belongs to the ṣila of "saying"; he placed it after [illā] and intended two statements, so that was permissible. And another said:

نُبِّئْتُهُمْ عَذَّبُوا بالنار جارتهُمْ * وهل يعِّذب إلاّ اللهُ بالنارِ
(I was told they tortured their female neighbour with fire — and does anyone but Allah torture with fire?)

I saw al-Kisāʾī treat (إِلاّ), with negation and interrogation, as equivalent to ghayr, putting in the accusative whatever resembles this as a single statement. He adduced the saying of the poet:

فلم يَدْر إِلاّ اللهُ ما هيَّجت لَنَا * أَهِلَّةُ أنآءِ الديار وشامُهَا
(None but Allah knows what the new moons over the distant abodes, and their marks, have stirred in us.)

But he has no proof in that, because (ما) is in the position of ayy ("which"), so it has an implied verb, on the basis of two statements. Yet his view is good: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿لَوْ كانَ فِيهِمَا آلِهَةٌ إلاّ اللهُ لَفَسَدَتَا﴾ ("had there been in them gods other than Allah, they would both have been ruined"), and he said: I find no meaning for it except "had there been in them gods other than Allah, they would have been ruined". And he adduced the saying of the poet:

أبنى لُبَيْنَى لَسْتُم بيدٍ * إلاّ يدٍ ليست لها عضد
(O sons of Lubaynā, you are nothing but a hand — a hand that has no upper arm.)

He said: had the meaning been illā [as exception], the speech would be corrupt here, because in this verse I cannot repeat a genitive-governing particle with an implied [element]. And he has taken a [defensible] line here.

farraa:47-47.t: His saying: ﴿أَوْ يَأْخُذَهُمْ عَلَىٰ تَخَوُّفٍ﴾ ("or that He should seize them by gradual diminution"). The exegesis came that it is diminution. The Arabs say: taḥawwaftuhu, with ḥāʾ: I diminished it from its edges (ḥāfāt). This is what I have heard. But the exegesis has come with khāʾ (and it is a [valid] meaning). Similar to it, among what has been read in two ways, is His saying: ﴿إنَّ لَكَ فِى النَّهَارِ سَبْحاً طَوِيلاً﴾ ("you have by day a long occupation") and (سَبْخاً), with ḥāʾ and with khāʾ. Al-sabkh is ampleness. I heard the Arabs say: "sabbikhī your wool", which is like carding; and al-sabḥ is close to that. All are correct, praise be to Allah.

farraa:48-48.t:
His saying: ﴿يَتَفَيَّأُ ظِلاَلُهُ﴾ ("its shadows turn"): the shadow comes back onto everything from its sides; that is its turning (tafayyuʾ). Then He explained, saying: ﴿عَنِ ٱلْيَمِينِ وَٱلْشَّمَآئِلِ﴾ ("to the right and the lefts"), making "right" singular and "lefts" plural. All of that is permissible in Arabic. The poet said:

بِفِى الشامتين الصخر إن كان هدّنى * رَزِيّة شِبْلَىْ مُخْدر فى الضراغم
(In the mouth of the gloaters be stones, if the loss of the two cubs of a lion in his den among the lions has broken me.)

He did not say "in the mouths of the gloaters". And another said:

الواردون وثَيْم فى ذُرَاسَبَأ * قد عضَّ أعناقَهم جلدُ الجواميس
(Those who come down [to water], and Taym, in the heights of Sabaʾ — the leather of buffaloes has bitten into their necks.)

And another said [ms. 95]:

فباست بنى عَبْس وأسْتَاه طيّء * وباست بنى دُودان حَاشا بنى نَصْرِ
(Shame on the rump of Banū ʿAbs and the rumps of Ṭayyiʾ, and on the rump of Banū Dūdān — except Banū Naṣr.)

So he used both plural and singular. And another said:

كلوا فى نصف بطنكم تعيشوا * فإنَّ زمانكم زَمَنٌ خميصُ
(Eat to half your belly and you will live, for your time is a time of hunger.)

The singular came because most speech is addressed to a single person: one says "take to your right and to your left", because the one addressed is one and so is the speaker. So it is as though, when he uses the singular, he has one of the people in mind; and when he uses the plural, there is no question about it. Likewise his saying:

بنى عُقَيل ماذِهِ الخنافِقُ * المالُ هَدْىٌ والنساء طالق
* وجبل يأوى إليه السارق *
(Banū ʿUqayl, what are these slanders? [Swear:] "The wealth is an offering, the women divorced", and a mountain where the thief takes refuge.)

He said ṭāliq [singular] because the administering of oaths mostly takes place between one disputant and another; so in the plural it ran on the most frequent usage in the original case. Similar is (بِفِى الشامتين) and the like.

farraa:49-49.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلِلَّهِ يَسْجُدُ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي ٱلأَرْضِ مِن دَآبَّةٍ﴾ ("and to Allah prostrates whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth, of creatures"). He said (مِن دابة) because (ما), even though it can take the course of (الذى), is indefinite (ghayr muʾaqqata); and when it is left vague and indefinite it resembles the conditional (al-jazāʾ). In the conditional, (مِن) enters an indefinite noun that comes after it; one says: "Whoever has struck him, of a man, strike him", and min is not dropped in this place. This is frequent in the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿مَا أَصَابَكَ مِنْ حَسَنَةٍ فَمِنَ اللهِ﴾ ("whatever good befalls you is from Allah"); and He said: ﴿وَمَنْ يَعْمَلْ مِنَ الصَّالِحَاتِ مِنْ ذَكَرٍ أَوْ أُنْثِى وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌ﴾ ("whoever does righteous deeds, of male or female, being a believer"); and He said: ﴿أَوَلم يَرَوْا إلى مَا خَلَقَ اللهُ مِنْ شىء﴾ ("have they not looked at whatever thing Allah has created"). In none of it did He say [it] dropping (مِنْ), disliking that it should look like a ḥāl (circumstantial) of man and mā; so they used min with it to indicate that it is an explanation of mā and man, because both are indefinite; so the entry of (مِن) into what follows them was an explanation of their meaning, and the entry of (مِن) indicated better what is indefinite in man and mā. That is why they were not dropped. Similar to it is the saying of the poet:

حاز لك الله ما آتاك من حَسَنٍ * وَحيثما يقضِ أمراً صَالحاً تكُنِ
(May Allah secure for you whatever good He has given you; and wherever He decrees a good thing, may you be there.)

And another said:

عُمْرا حَييت ومَن يشناكَ من أحد * يَلْق الهوان ويلق الذلّ والغِيَرا
(May you live long; and whoever hates you, of anyone, will meet contempt, humiliation and reverses.)

The coming of aḥad here indicated that he did not intend the indefinites that came [Translator's note: the text has «ن النكرات», evidently for «من النكرات»] to be ḥāl of the nouns before them, and indicated that it interprets the meaning of man and mā. Also indicating it is the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَمَا أَنْفَقْتُمْ مِنْ شَىءٍ فَهُوَ يُخْلِفُهُ﴾ ("and whatever thing you spend, He will replace it"), because "thing" cannot be a ḥāl, but it is an interpreting noun. I only mentioned this because the Arabs say: "How excellent he is, of a man (min rajulin)!", and then they drop min and say: "How excellent he is — a man (rajulan)!" So "man" interprets (what precedes it) and is not a ḥāl; a ḥāl is only something that changes, like standing and sitting. You do not mean "How excellent he is in the state of his manhood only"; had you meant that, you would not be praising him with full praise, because when you say "How excellent you are, standing!", you only praise him in standing alone.
If you say: how then is dropping min permissible in this place? I say: because what precedes it is definite (muʾaqqat), so I did not mind it coming out, with min dropped, like a ḥāl; whereas in the conditional it was indefinite, and they disliked a ḥāl being explained from an indefinite noun, so they made min obligatory with it. If you say: [ms. 95b] the Arabs have said "mā atānī min aḥadin" and "mā atānī aḥadun", and allowed themselves to drop min — I say: that was permissible since there is nothing before aḥad, or what is like it, of which aḥad could be a ḥāl. That is why they said: "No man came to me (min rajulin)" and "No man came to me (rajulun)".

farraa:52-52.t: His saying: ﴿وَلَهُ ٱلدِّينُ وَاصِباً﴾ ("and His is the religion, constantly"): its meaning is "perpetually". One says: waṣaba, yaṣibu: it lasted. And it is said: "purely".

farraa:53-53.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمَا بِكُم مِّن نِّعْمَةٍ فَمِنَ ٱللَّهِ﴾ ("and whatever blessing you have, it is from Allah"). (ما) is in the sense of a conditional and has an implied verb, as though you said: "Whatever blessing there is (yakun) with you is from Allah", because the conditional must have a jussive verb: if it is overt it is jussive, and if it is not overt it is implied, as the poet said:

إنِ العَقْلُ فى أموالنا لا نضِق به * ذِراعاً وإن صبراً فنَعْرِفُ للصبر
(If blood-money is [demanded] from our wealth, we are not distressed by it; and if [the demand is for] endurance, we know how to endure.)

He meant "if there be (in yakun)", and implied it. Had you made (ما بكم) in the sense of (الذى) it would be permissible, making (بِكُم) its ṣila (relative clause), and (ما) would then be in the position of the nominative by His saying ﴿فَمِنَ ٱللَّهِ﴾, the fāʾ being brought in as Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿قُلْ إِنَّ المَوْتَ الذِى تَفِرُّونَ مِنْهُ فإنَّهُ مُلاَقِيكُم﴾ ("say: the death from which you flee will surely meet you"). With every relative noun, such as man, mā and alladhī, the entry of fāʾ into its khabar (predicate) is permissible, because it resembles the conditional, and the conditional may be answered with fāʾ. But "Your brother, so he is standing" is not permissible, because it is not a relative noun; likewise "Your property (mālu-ka) is mine". But if you say "What you have (mā laka)", it is permissible to say [Translator's note: the text has «جاز أنت قول», evidently for «جاز أن تقول»]: "then it is mine"; and if you drop the fāʾ it is correct. Whatever you meet, judge it by analogy with this. Likewise an indefinite noun with a ṣila: you say: "A man who speaks the truth — then he is dearer to me than one who speaks falsehood". Dropping the fāʾ is better in all of it than bringing it in.
Al-juʾār is a loud voice. Of an ox one says: jaʾara, yajʾaru, juʾāran, when its voice rises from hunger or something else — with jīm. Likewise ﴿فَإِلَيْهِ تَجْأَرُونَ﴾ ("then to Him you cry out").

farraa:57-57.t:
His saying: ﴿وَيَجْعَلُونَ لِلَّهِ ٱلْبَنَاتِ سُبْحَانَهُ﴾ ("and they assign daughters to Allah — glory be to Him!"): [سبحانه is] accusative because it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), and it carries a sense of seeking refuge and declaring Allah, Mighty and Majestic, free [of such things]. So it is like His saying ﴿مَعَاذَ اللهِ﴾ ("Allah forbid") and like ﴿غَفْرَانَكَ رَبَنَا﴾ ("Your forgiveness, our Lord").
His saying: ﴿لَهُمْ مَّا يَشْتَهُونَ﴾ ("and for themselves what they desire"): (ما) is in the position of the nominative. Had it been accusative, on the basis of "and they assign to themselves what they desire", that would be correct. I only chose the nominative because in speech like this one puts "to themselves (li-anfusihim)" in the place of "to them (lahum)" — do you not see that you say "You have assigned to yourself such-and-such", and you do not say "You have assigned to you"? With every verb or preposition that you mention from a pronoun and that returns upon it as a pronoun, make its second genitive [object] with nafs; so you say "You are for yourself, not for others"; then in the accusative you say "You killed yourself", and in the nominative "Your self destroyed you"; and you do not say ahlaktaka ("you destroyed you"). By bringing in nafs he only intended to distinguish between the self of the speaker and others. But when the verb falls from one pronoun onto another pronoun distinct from it, you do not bring in nafs. You say: "Your slave destroyed your wealth"; then you substitute pronouns for the slave and the wealth and say: "He destroyed it"; and you do not say "He destroyed himself" when you mean the wealth. The Arabs do say it with ẓanantu and its sisters raʾaytu, ʿalimtu and ḥasibtu: they say "aẓunnunī standing" (I think myself standing) and "wajadtunī righteous" (I found myself righteous), because of their incompleteness and their need for a predicate besides the noun. A poet, under constraint, may say ʿadimtunī and faqadtunī ("may I lose myself"); it is permissible, though rare. The poet said — he is Jirān al-ʿAwd:

لقد كان بى عن ضَرَّتين عدِمتُنى * وعمّا ألاقِي منهما متَزحزَح
هى الغُول والسعلاة حَلْقى منهما * مُخَدَّشُ فوق التراقى مكدَّح
(I had — may I lose myself! — a way to stay clear of two co-wives and of what I suffer from them. They are the ghoul and the she-demon; my throat, because of them, is scratched and bruised above the collarbones.)

farraa:58-58.t: His saying: ﴿ظَلَّ وَجْهُهُ مُسْوَدّاً﴾ ("his face becomes darkened"). Had it been (ظلَّ وجههُ مُسْوَدٌ), it would be correct: you make the ẓulūl (becoming) belong to the man, and "face" and "darkened" are in the position of the accusative, as He said: ﴿وَيَوْمَ القِيَامَةِ تَرَىَ الذِينَ كَذَبُوا عَلَى اللهِ وُجُوهُهُمْ مُسْوَدَّةٌ﴾ ("on the Day of Resurrection you will see those who lied about Allah, their faces blackened"). And the ẓulūl, when you say [ms. 96a] (مُسْوَدَّاً), belongs to the face.

farraa:59-59.t: His saying: ﴿أَيُمْسِكُهُ عَلَىٰ هُونٍ﴾ ("shall he keep it in humiliation?"). Al-hūn in the dialect of Quraysh is al-hawān (humiliation), and some of Banū Tamīm make al-hūn a maṣdar (verbal noun) for a thing that is light (hayyin). Al-Kisāʾī said: I heard the Arabs say: "You have been, since today, light (hūn) of provision indeed." And he said: I heard al-hawān in a similar sense from Banū Insān [Translator's note: so in the text]: he said: someone said of a camel of his: "There is nothing wrong with it except its hawān", meaning that it is cheap, light in price. When the Arabs say "So-and-so came walking ʿalā hawnihi (at his ease)", they only say it with fatḥa on the hāʾ, as in His saying: ﴿يَمْشُونَ عَلَى الأرْضِ هَوْناً﴾ ("they walk upon the earth gently"); it is tranquillity and dignity. Muḥammad narrated to us, saying: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: Sharīk narrated to me from Jābir, from ʿIkrima and Mujāhid, concerning His saying ﴿يَمْشُونَ عَلَى الأَرْض هَوْنا﴾: they both said: with tranquillity and dignity. And His saying: ﴿أَيُمْسِكُهُ عَلَىٰ هُونٍ أَمْ يَدُسُّهُ﴾ ("shall he keep it in humiliation or bury it [in the dust]?"): He is saying: he does not know which of the two he will do — keep it, or bury it in the dust. He is saying: will he bury her, or bear with her and with what he dislikes in her? She is the girl buried alive (al-mawʾūda). It is a parable struck by Allah, Blessed and Exalted.

farraa:60-60.t: His saying: ﴿لِلَّذِينَ لاَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِٱلآخِرَةِ مَثَلُ ٱلسَّوْءِ﴾ ("for those who do not believe in the Hereafter is the evil description"). Had it been ﴿مَثَلَ ٱلسَّوْءِ﴾ in the accusative it would be permissible; it would then be, in meaning, like your saying: "He struck for those who do not believe the evil description", just as in the reading of Ubayy: (وَضَرَبَ مَثَلاً كَلِمةً خَبِيثَةً) ("and He struck as a likeness an evil word"). The reading of the generality here and in Ibrāhīm is with the nominative; we have not heard anyone use the accusative.

farraa:62-62.t:
His saying: ﴿وَتَصِفُ أَلْسِنَتُهُمُ ٱلْكَذِبَ أَنَّ لَهُمُ ٱلْحُسْنَىٰ﴾ ("and their tongues assert the lie that theirs is the best"). Anna is in the position of the accusative because it expresses the lie [i.e. it is a badal (substitute) from it]. And it might be said: ﴿وَتَصِفُ أَلْسِنَتُهُمُ ٱلْكُذُبُ﴾, making al-kudhub an attribute of the tongues, its singular being kadhūb, [plural] kudhub, like rasūl and rusul. Similar to it is His saying: ﴿وَلاَ تَقُولُوا لِمَا تَصِفُ أَلْسِنَتُكُمُ الكُذُبُ﴾ ("and do not say, of what your lying tongues assert…"). Some put (الكَذِبَ) in the genitive, making it genitive by the lām in His saying (لِمَا), because it expresses (ما). The accusative in it is the proper way of the speech, and the generality read with it. Its meaning is: "and do not say, because of their asserting the lie…".
His saying: ﴿وَأَنَّهُمْ مُّفْرَطُونَ﴾ ("and that they will be abandoned"). He is saying: forgotten in the Fire. The Arabs say: "I left behind (afraṭtu) some people of them", i.e. I left them behind and forgot them. It is also read ﴿وَأَنَّهُمْ مُّفْرِطُونَ﴾ with kasra on the rāʾ: they were going to excess in evil deeds against themselves, in sins. And it is read ﴿مُفرِّطُونَ﴾, as in His saying: ﴿يَا حَسْرَتَا عَلَى مَا فَرَّطْتُ فِي جَنْبِ الله﴾ ("alas for my neglect in regard to Allah"); He is saying: in what I left and neglected.

farraa:66-66.t:
His saying: ﴿نُّسْقِيكُمْ مِّمَّا فِي بُطُونِهِ﴾ ("We give you to drink from what is in their bellies"). The Arabs say asqaytu for everything that comes from the bellies of cattle, from the sky, or from a river flowing for a people. When a man gives you water for your lips, they say saqāhu, and they do not say asqāhu; as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿وَسَقَاهُمْ رَبُّهُمْ شَرَاباً طَهُوراً﴾ ("and their Lord will give them a pure drink"), and said: ﴿وَالّذِى هُوَ يُطْعِمُنِى وَيَسْقِينِ﴾ ("and who feeds me and gives me drink"). Sometimes they say both saqā and asqā for what is in the bellies of cattle and for rain-water, as Labīd said:

سَقَى قومى بنى مَجْد وأسقى * نُمَيرَا والقبائلَ من هلال
رَعَوه مُربِعاً وتَصيّفوه * بلا وَبَأٍ سُمَىَّ ولا وَبَالِ
(May He water my people, Banū Majd, and water Numayr and the tribes of Hilāl; they grazed it [the rain-fed land] in spring and summered on it, with no pestilence — it was named [so] — and no ill effect.)

The readers differed: some read ﴿نَسْقِيكم﴾ and some ﴿نُسْقِيكم﴾.
As for His saying ﴿مِّمَّا فِي بُطُونِهِ﴾ — He did not say buṭūnihā — it has been said — and Allah knows best — that al-naʿam and al-anʿām are one thing, and both are plurals; so the masculine refers back to the meaning of al-naʿam, since it stands for al-anʿām. One of them recited to me:

إذا رأيتَ أنجما من الأَسد * جَبْهته أو الخرَاة والكَتَدْ
بال سُهَيل فى الفضِيح. ففسد * وطاب أَلْبانُ الِّلقَاح وبَردْ
(When you see stars of Leo — its forehead, or its rump and its shoulders — Canopus has "urinated" into the milk-and-water drink, and it spoils; and the milk of the milch-camels becomes good and cool.)

He referred [the masculine "baruda"] back to "milk" (al-laban), because al-laban and al-albān have one meaning. Al-Kisāʾī said (نُسْقِيكم مِمَّا بُطُونِهِ): [i.e.] the bellies of what we have mentioned; and that is correct. One of them recited to me:

* مثل الفراخ نَتَقَتْ حواصلهْ *
(Like chicks whose crops have swollen.)

And another said:

* كذاك ابنةَ الأَعيار خافى بسالة الرجال وأصلال الرجال أقاصرُهْ *
(Thus, O daughter of al-Aʿyār, fear the valour of men; and the vipers among men are the shortest of them.)

He did not say aqāṣiruhum. Aṣlāl al-rijāl: the strong ones among them.
His saying: ﴿سَآئِغاً لِلشَّارِبِينَ﴾ ("palatable to those who drink"): He is saying: one does not choke on the milk nor gag on it.

farraa:68-68.t:
His saying: ﴿وَأَوْحَىٰ رَبُّكَ إِلَىٰ ٱلنَّحْلِ﴾ ("and your Lord inspired the bee"): He inspired it by instinct (alhamahā), and no messenger came to it.
His saying: ﴿أَنِ ٱتَّخِذِي مِنَ ٱلْجِبَالِ بُيُوتاً وَمِنَ ٱلشَّجَرِ وَمِمَّا يَعْرِشُونَ﴾ ("take dwellings in the mountains and the trees and in what they construct"): these are the roofs of houses.

farraa:69-69.t:
His saying: ﴿ذُلُلاً﴾ ("made easy") is a naʿt (adjective) of "the ways". One says "a dhalūl (smooth) way", and dhulul for the plural. And it is said that al-dhulul is an attribute of the bees, i.e. they were made submissive so that the drink comes out of their bellies.
His saying: ﴿شِفَآءٌ لِلنَّاسِ﴾ ("healing for people"), meaning that honey is a remedy. And it is said that in ﴿فِيهِ شِفَآءٌ لِلنَّاسِ﴾ the hāʾ means the Qurʾān: in it is the explanation of the lawful and the unlawful.

farraa:70-70.t: His saying: ﴿لِكَيْ لاَ يَعْلَمَ﴾ ("so that he knows nothing"). He is saying: so that he does not comprehend (شَيْئاً) ("anything") after his former understanding.

farraa:71-71.t: His saying: ﴿فَمَا ٱلَّذِينَ فُضِّلُواْ بِرَآدِّي رِزْقِهِمْ عَلَىٰ مَا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَانُهُمْ﴾ ("those who were favoured would not hand over their provision to those their right hands possess"). This is a parable Allah struck for those who said that ʿĪsā is His son — exalted is Allah high above what the wrongdoers say! He said: you do not make your slaves partners in what you own so that you are equal in it; so how have you made His servant a partner to Him, Blessed and Exalted?

farraa:72-72.t: His saying: ﴿وَحَفَدَةً﴾ ("and grandchildren"): al-ḥafada are the in-laws; and they said: the helpers. Had it been said al-ḥafad it would be correct, because their singular is ḥāfid, so it would be like ghāʾib and ghayab, and qāʿid and qaʿad.

farraa:73-73.t:
His saying: ﴿وَيَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ مَا لاَ يَمْلِكُ لَهُمْ رِزْقاً مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ شَيْئاً﴾ ("and they worship besides Allah what has no power to provide for them anything from the heavens and the earth").
You put (شيئاً) in the accusative by the "providing" (al-rizq) falling on it [as its mafʿūl bihi (direct object)], as He, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿أَلَمْ نَجْعَل الأَرْضَ كَفَاتاً أَحْيَاءً وَأَمْوَاتاً﴾ ("have We not made the earth a receptacle, for the living and the dead?"), i.e. it holds the living and the dead. Similar to it is ﴿أَوْ إِطْعَامٌ فِى يَوْمٍ ذِى مَسْغَبَة يَتِيماً﴾ ("or feeding, on a day of hunger, an orphan"). Had al-rizq been [annexed] to "thing", its genitive would be permissible: "has no power to provide them the provision of anything from the heavens". Similar to it is the reading of whoever reads ﴿فَجَزَاءُ مِثْلِ مَا قَتَلَ مِنَ النِّعَمِ﴾ ("then the compensation of the like of what he killed, of cattle").
His saying: ﴿وَلاَ يَسْتَطِيعُونَ﴾ ("nor are they able"), while He said at the beginning of the statement (يَمْلِكُ) [in the singular]: that is because (ما) has the sense of a plural, for their gods which they worship; so (يَملك) was made singular according to the form of (ما) and its singularity, and it was made plural in (يستطيعون) according to the meaning.
Similar to it is His saying: ﴿وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَسْتَمِعُ إِلَيْكَ﴾ ("and among them is he who listens to you"), and in another place: ﴿وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَسْتَمِعُون إليك﴾ ("and among them are those who listen to you"). Similar is: ﴿وَمَنْ يَقْنُتْ مِنكُنَّ لِلّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ وَتَعْمَلْ صَالحاً﴾ ("and whoever of you is obedient to Allah and His Messenger and does [fem.] righteousness") and ﴿يَعملْ صَالحاً﴾ [masc.]: whoever uses the masculine refers its end back to its beginning; and whoever uses the feminine takes the view that (مَن) stands in a feminine position, and so goes by its femininity. One of the Arabs recited to us:

هَيَا أُمَّ عمرو مَن يكن عُقْرَ دارِه * جِوَاءٌ عَدِىّ يأكلِ الحشرات
ويسودَّ من لفْح السموم جَبينُهُ * ويَعْرَ وإن كانوا ذوى نَكَرات
(O Umm ʿAmr, whoever has as the heart of his home the hollows of ʿAdī will eat vermin; his brow will be blackened by the scorching of the hot wind, and he will go bare, even though they are men of cunning.)

So in (كانوا) he returned to the plural meaning. And in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh — as far as I know — it is (ومِنْكُمْ من يكون شُيُوخاً) ("and among you are those who become old men"), and he did not say (شَيْخاً). Al-Farazdaq said:

تَعَشَّ فإن واثقتنى لا تخونُنى * نكن مثل مَن يا ذئب يصطحبان
وأنت امرؤ يا ذئب والغدرُ كنتما * أُخَيَّيْنِ كانا أُرضِعا بِلِبان
(Have your supper; and if you pledge to me not to betray me, we will be, O wolf, like two who keep company. But you, O wolf, and treachery have been like two little brothers suckled at one breast.)

He made (يصطحبان) dual, though it is the verb of man, because he intended [the wolf] and himself.

farraa:75-75.t: His saying: ﴿ضَرَبَ ٱللَّهُ مَثَلاً عَبْداً مَّمْلُوكاً﴾ ("Allah strikes a parable: a slave who is owned"). He struck a parable for the idol (al-ḍamm) [Translator's note: so in the text, here and below; evidently al-ṣanam, "the idol"] which they worship, that it has power over nothing. ﴿وهُوَ كَلٌّ على مولاه﴾ ("and he is a burden on his master"), i.e. he carries it. So He said: is this idol equal ﴿وَمَنْ يَأْمُرُ بالعَدْلِ﴾ ("to one who commands justice")? He said: do not make the idol equal to Allah, Blessed and Exalted.

farraa:80-80.t:
His saying: ﴿وَجَعَلَ لَكُمْ مِّن جُلُودِ ٱلأَنْعَامِ﴾ ("and He made for you, from the hides of cattle, [tents]"), meaning tents for travel and the dwellings of the Arabs that are of wool and hair. Al-ẓaʿn ("travelling") is read heavy [i.e. ẓaʿan] and light, because its second letter is ʿayn; the Arabs do that with words whose second letter is one of the six [guttural] letters, like al-shaʿr, al-baḥr and al-nahr. One of the Arabs recited to me:

له نَعَل لا تَطَّبِى الكلبَ ريحُها * وإن وُضِعت بين المجالس شُمَّت
(He has a sandal whose smell does not attract the dog, and if it is set down among the gatherings it is sniffed [with pleasure].)

His saying: ﴿أَثَاثاً وَمَتَاعاً﴾ ("furnishings and enjoyment") — "enjoyment for a time": He is saying: they make do with their wool until they die. And it is said: [for] time after time.

harrat-mujtaba:36-36.t: The clause «ولقد بعثنا» is resumptive; «أن» is explicative (tafsīriyya), and the clause «اعبدوا» is explicative, because the sending mentioned before it implies the sense of saying. The clause «فمنهم من هدى الله» is conjoined to the clause «بعثنا», with no grammatical position. «مَنْ»: a relative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject). The clause «فسيروا» is resumptive. His words «كيف»: an interrogative noun, the khabar (predicate) of the abrogating «كان», and «عاقبة» is its noun; the clause is the object of the looking, which is suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative and carries the sense of knowing.

harrat-mujtaba:37-37.t: His words «وما لهم من ناصرين»: the wāw is a conjunction; «ما» is negating; the preposition «لهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate); «مِن» is redundant (zāʾida); and «ناصرين» is the mubtadaʾ (subject). The clause «وما لهم من ناصرين» is conjoined to the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ).

harrat-mujtaba:38-38.t: «جهد»: a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) (nāʾib mafʿūl muṭlaq). The clause «لا يبعث الله» is the apodosis of the oath; it is not emphasised with the nūn because it is negated. His words «بلى»: a particle of answer. «وعدا»: mafʿūl muṭlaq of an implied governor, i.e.: وعد ذلك وعدا; the preposition «عليه» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «وعدا»; and «حقا» is a mafʿūl muṭlaq of an omitted governor, i.e.: حقَّ ذلك حقا. The two clauses «وعد وعدا» and «وحق حقا» are parenthetical between the two conjoined elements. The clause «ولكن أكثر الناس لا يعلمون» is conjoined to an implied clause, i.e.: بلى يبعثهم ولكن أكثر ...

harrat-mujtaba:39-39.t: The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) «ليبيِّن» is genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied «يبعثهم»; and the interpreted maṣdar «أنهم كانوا» stands in place of the two objects of «علم».

harrat-mujtaba:40-40.t: «إنما»: the restraining particle and the restrained (kāffa wa-makfūfa). The preposition «لشيء» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «قولنا»; «إذا» is a pure adverb attached to a ḥāl of «قولنا»; the maṣdar (verbal noun) «أن نقول له» is the khabar (predicate) of «قولنا». His words «كن»: a complete imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) the pronoun "you" (أنت). The fāʾ in «فيكون» is resumptive, and «يكون» is a complete imperfect verb whose fāʿil is the pronoun "he" (هو); the clause «يكون» is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being هو, i.e.: فهو يكون. The clause «فهو يكون» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:41-41.t: (والذين هاجروا) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause of the relative noun is resumptive; the two preposition and its genitive nouns are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; «ما» is maṣdariyya, and the maṣdar (verbal noun) is muḍāf ilayhi. His words «حسنة»: a second object, on the basis that the verb is made to contain the sense of نعطيهم (we give them). The clause «لنبوئنَّهم» is the apodosis of the oath, and the oath with its apodosis is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) «الذين». The clause «ولأجر الآخرة أكبر» is resumptive, and the clause «لو كانوا يعلمون» is resumptive; the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, i.e.: لآمنوا (they would have believed).

harrat-mujtaba:42-42.t: (الذين صبروا) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The relative noun is a badal (substitute) of the preceding relative noun, and the clause «يتوكلون» is conjoined to the ṣila (relative clause).

harrat-mujtaba:43-43.t: The clause «وما أرسلنا» is resumptive; «إلا» is for restriction (ḥaṣr); the clause «نوحي» is a naʿt (adjective) of «رجالا»; the clause «فاسألوا» is resumptive; and the clause «إن كنتم لا تعلمون» is resumptive, its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) being omitted, indicated by what precedes it.

harrat-mujtaba:44-44.t: The preposition «بالبينات» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) {تَعْلَمُونَ} in the preceding verse. The clause «أنزلنا» is resumptive. The clause «ولعلهم يتفكرون» is conjoined to the purpose expressed earlier, as a case of conjoining a clause to a single word, i.e.: للتبيين ولعلهم يتفكرون.

harrat-mujtaba:45-45.t: The clause «أفَأَمِنَ» is resumptive. «السيئات» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of «مكروا», on the basis that مكروا is made to contain the sense of فَعَلوا (they did). The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) is the object of «أمن», and the clause «لا يشعرون» is muḍāf ilayhi.

harrat-mujtaba:46-46.t: The preposition «في تقلبهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the object, i.e.: ملتبسين في تقلبهم (while engaged in their going about). The clause «فما هم بمعجزين» is conjoined to the clause «يأخذهم», and the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida) in the khabar (predicate) of «ما», which operates like ليس.

harrat-mujtaba:47-47.t: The preposition «على تخوف» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the hāʾ, and the clause «فإن ربكم لرءوف» is conjoined to the clause «يأخذهم».

harrat-mujtaba:48-48.t: The preposition «من شيء» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «ما»; the clause «يتفيأ» is a naʿt (adjective) of «شيء». His words «سجَّدا»: a ḥāl of «الظلال»; the preposition «لله» is attached to «سجدا»; and the clause «وهم داخرون» is a ḥāl of the latent (mustatir) pronoun in «سجَّدا».

harrat-mujtaba:49-49.t: «ما»: a relative noun, fāʿil (agent); the preposition and its genitive noun is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied ṣila (relative clause); the preposition «من دابة» is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «ما»; «الملائكة» is a noun conjoined to «ما»; and the clause «وهم لا يستكبرون» is a ḥāl of the fāʿil of «يسجد».

harrat-mujtaba:50-50.t: The clause «يخافون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of {لا يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ}. The preposition «من فوقهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl of «ربهم».

harrat-mujtaba:51-51.t: «اثنين»: a naʿt (adjective); the second object of اتخذ is omitted, i.e.: معبودا (an object of worship). The clause «إنما هو إله واحد» is resumptive within the scope of the saying. His words «فإياي فارهبون»: the fāʾ is a conjunction; a detached accusative pronoun is a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an implied verb explained by what follows, its implied form being: ارهبوا; the yāʾ is for the first person; the fāʾ is redundant (zāʾida); and the yāʾ implied in the verb is the verb's object. The implied clause «فارهبوا» is conjoined to the clause «لا تتخذوا», and the clause «فارهبون» is explicative of the implied one.

harrat-mujtaba:52-52.t: «واصبا»: a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «الدين». The clause «أفغير الله تتقون» is conjoined to the clause «له الدين». The fāʾ is a conjunction, and «غير» is a fronted object.

harrat-mujtaba:53-53.t: His words «وما بكم من نعمة»: the wāw is resumptive; «ما» is a relative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject); the preposition and its genitive noun is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied ṣila (relative clause); the preposition «من نعمة» is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «ما»; the fāʾ is redundant (zāʾida); and the preposition «من الله» is attached to the khabar (predicate) of «ما». The conditional clause is conjoined to the resumptive one: «وما بكم من نعمة فمن الله». The clause «فإليه تجأرون» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), with no grammatical position; the fronting of the preposition and its genitive noun before the verb is what licensed the fāʾ. The clause «مسَّكم» is muḍāf ilayhi.

harrat-mujtaba:54-54.t: The conditional clause is conjoined to the preceding conditional. «إذا»: a conditional adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) the sense of the apodosis, its implied form being: أشرك بعضكم إذا كشف; the second «إذا» is of surprise (fujāʾiyya). The clause «إذا فريق يشركون» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). «فريق» is the mubtadaʾ (subject); beginning with an indefinite noun is licensed by its being qualified by «منكم». The preposition «بربهم» is attached to «يشركون».

harrat-mujtaba:55-55.t: The maṣdar (verbal noun) «ليكفروا» is genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the preceding {يُشْرِكُونَ}. The clause «فتمتعوا» is resumptive, and the clause «فسوف تعلمون» is conjoined to the clause «تمتعوا».

harrat-mujtaba:56-56.t: The clause «ويجعلون» is resumptive. «لما»: the lām is a preposition; «ما» is a relative noun, [the phrase] attached to (mutaʿalliq) the second object of «يجعلون»; «نصيبا» is the first object; the preposition «مما» is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of «نصيبا». The genitive [phrase of] the oath is attached to an implied أقسم. His words «لتسألن»: the lām occurs in the apodosis of the oath; an imperfect passive verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, which was dropped because of the succession of like letters; the implied wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters; and the nūn is for emphasis. The implied oath clause is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:57-57.t: The clause «ويجعلون» is conjoined to the earlier clause «يجعلون». His words «سبحانه»: a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), and the clause is parenthetical between the ḥāl (circumstantial) and the one it describes. The clause «لهم ما يشتهون» is a ḥāl of the fāʿil (agent) of «يجعلون». His words «ولهم ما يشتهون»: the wāw is circumstantial; the preposition and its genitive noun is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of the relative «ما», which is the mubtadaʾ (subject). It is not permissible to conjoin «لهم» to «لله», because the verb of a connected pronoun may not pass over to its own pronoun, either by itself or by a preposition, except in the chapter of ظن, as in ظننتُني (I thought myself); so one does not say: زيد غضب عليه, meaning: on himself.

harrat-mujtaba:58-58.t: The conditional clause is conjoined to the conditional clause in verse (54). The clause «بُشِّر» is muḍāf ilayhi, and «إذا» is a conditional adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) the sense of the apodosis; it is not attached to «ظلَّ» because that is defective (nāqiṣa). The implied form is: بقي وجهه إذا بُشِّر. The clause «وهو كظيم» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «وجهه».

harrat-mujtaba:59-59.t: The clause «يتوارى» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in {كَظِيمٌ}. The two preposition and its genitive nouns are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; this is permitted even though they have the same wording, because their meanings differ: the first is for the beginning of the extent, and the second for causation. «ما»: a relative noun, muḍāf ilayhi. The clause «أيمسكه» is resumptive; the preposition «على هون» is attached to a ḥāl of the fāʿil (agent) of يمسكه; «أم» is a conjunction; and the clause «ألا ساء ما يحكمون» is resumptive. «ما» is a relative noun, fāʿil; the one specified for blame is omitted, its implied form being: حكمهم (their judgement).

harrat-mujtaba:60-60.t: The clause «للذين لا يؤمنون ... » is resumptive. «مثل» is the mubtadaʾ (subject), and the preposition and its genitive noun before it is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate). The clause «وهو العزيز» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:61-61.t: The conditional clause is resumptive, and the clause «ما ترك» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). «دابة» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and «من» is redundant (zāʾida). The clause «ولكن يؤخرهم» is conjoined to the clause «يؤاخذ»; the clause «فإذا جاء أجلهم» is conjoined to the clause «يؤخرهم»; the clause «جاء» is muḍāf ilayhi; and «ساعة» is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb.

harrat-mujtaba:62-62.t: The preposition «لله» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the second object of «يجعلون», and the relative noun is the first object. «الكذب» is the object of «تصف», and the maṣdar (verbal noun) «أن لهم الحسنى» is a badal (substitute) of «الكذب», whole for whole. His words «لا جرم»: «لا» is the lā of generic negation with its noun; the khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being موجود (existing); and the interpreted maṣdar is accusative by removal of the preposition (في). The clause «وتصف» is conjoined to the clause «يجعلون», and the clause «لا جرم موجود» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:63-63.t: The oath expression «تالله» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an implied أقسم; the preposition «من قبلك» is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of «أمم». The clause «فزين» is conjoined to the clause «أرسلنا»; the clause «فهو وليهم» is conjoined to the clause «زيَّن»; «اليوم» is an adverb attached to the khabar (predicate); and the clause «ولهم عذاب» is conjoined to the clause «فهو وليهم».

harrat-mujtaba:64-64.t: The maṣdar (verbal noun) «لتبيِّن» is genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أنزلنا». His words «وهدى»: a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose) of an implied governor, i.e.: وأنزلناه هدى. Since the agent is one and the same, the verb reached it by itself; but it is not one and the same in His words «وما أنزلنا إلا لتبين», for the agent of the sending down is Allah and the agent of the explaining is the Messenger, so the verb was connected with the lām. The clause «وأنزلناه هدى» is conjoined to the clause «ما أنزلنا».

harrat-mujtaba:65-65.t: The clause «فأحيا» is conjoined to the clause «أنزل», and the lām in «لآية» is for emphasis.

harrat-mujtaba:66-66.t: The clause «نسقيكم» is explicative of the lesson (ʿibra), with no grammatical position. The preposition «مما» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb, and the preposition «في بطونه» is attached to the implied ṣila (relative clause). The pronoun in «في بطونه» refers back to «الأنعام» in the masculine singular form, because this word may be either a singular or a broken plural. The preposition «من بين» is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «لبنا», and «خالصا سائغا» are two naʿts (adjectives).

harrat-mujtaba:67-67.t: His words «ومن ثمرات»: conjoined to the preposition and its genitive noun {فِي الأَنْعَامِ}, and in meaning it is a khabar (predicate) about the noun of «إن» in His words: {وَإِنَّ لَكُمْ فِي الأَنْعَامِ لَعِبْرَةً}; the implied form is: وإن لكم في الأنعام، ومن ثمرات النخيل لعبرة. The clause «تتخذون» is explicative of the lesson from the fruits of the date palms, with no grammatical position. The clause «يعقلون» is a naʿt (adjective).

harrat-mujtaba:68-68.t: «أن» is explicative (tafsīriyya), and the clause «اتخذي» is explicative.

harrat-mujtaba:69-69.t: «ذللا»: a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «سبل»; «مختلف» is a naʿt (adjective); «ألوانه» is the fāʿil (agent) of «مختلف». The clause «يخرج» is resumptive; the clause «فيه شفاء» is a second naʿt of «شراب»; and the clause «إن في ذلك لآية» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:70-70.t: The clause «ومنكم مَنْ يرد» is resumptive; «من» is a relative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject); «شيئا» is the object of «عِلْم»; and the object of «يعلم» is latent (mustatir), referring back to «شيئا» by way of contention (tanāzuʿ).

harrat-mujtaba:71-71.t: The clause «فما الذين فضلوا» is conjoined to the clause «الله فضَّل». His words «برادّي»: the khabar (predicate) of «ما», which operates like ليس, and the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida). The clause «فهم فيه سواء» is conjoined to the clause «ما الذين فُضِّلوا برادِّي». The preposition «فيه» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «سواء». The clause «يجحدون» is resumptive, and the fāʾ is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:72-72.t: «بنين»: a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative with the yāʾ because it is assimilated to the sound masculine plural. The clause «يؤمنون» is resumptive, and the clause «هم يكفرون» is conjoined to the clause «يؤمنون».

harrat-mujtaba:73-73.t: The preposition «لهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «رزقا». The preposition «من السماوات» is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of «رزقا». His words «شيئا»: a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e.: little or much.

harrat-mujtaba:74-74.t: The clause «فلا تضربوا» is resumptive, and so is the clause «إن الله يعلم». The clause «وأنتم لا تعلمون» is conjoined to the clause «إن الله يعلم», with no grammatical position.

harrat-mujtaba:75-75.t: «عبدا»: a badal (substitute) of «مثلا», and the clause «لا يقدر» is a second naʿt (adjective) of «عبدا». His words «ومَن»: a relative noun conjoined to «عبدا». The clause «فهو ينفق» is conjoined to the clause «رزقناه»; «سرا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial); the clause «هل يستوون» is resumptive, and so are the two clauses «الحمد لله» and «أكثرهم لا يعلمون». He used the plural in His words «يستوون» even though two preceded it, because what is meant is the genus of slaves and free men.
