He means Himself, Mighty and Majestic is He.
Qatāda said likewise: Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, commands us to justice, and He is on a straight path.
On this basis, the meaning of His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He, ﴿ضَرَبَ اللَّهُ مَثَلاً عَبْداً مَمْلُوْكاً﴾ is that He means by it what is worshipped besides Him, because it possesses neither harm nor benefit; and ﴿مَن رَزَقْنَاهُ مِنَّا رِزْقاً حَسَناً فَهُوَ يُنْفِقُ مِنْهُ سِرّاً وَجَهْراً﴾ refers to Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, because He is the Generous One who provides for man from where he knows and from where he does not know.
It is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās — and this is his wording as narrated from him — that he said: "This verse ﴿ضَرَبَ اللَّهُ مَثَلاً عَبْداً مَمْلُوْكاً لاَ يَقْدِرُ عَلَى شَيْءٍ﴾ was revealed concerning "Hishām ibn ʿAmr"; he is the one who spends from it secretly and openly, and his client (mawlā) was Abū al-Jawāb, who used to forbid him. And it has been said: it was revealed concerning two men: ﴿وَضَرَبَ اللهُ مَثَلاً رَّجُلَيْنِ﴾ — the dumb one of them, the burden upon his master, is "Usayd ibn Abī al-ʿĀṣ", and the one who commands justice and is on a straight path is "ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān", Allah's mercy be upon him. ʿUthmān used to support his client; so ʿUthmān is the one who spends with justice and is on a straight path, and the other is the dumb one."
Al-Ḥasan said: ﴿عَبْداً مَمْلُوكاً﴾ is the idol.
The most fitting of the views on this is the saying of Ibn ʿAbbās, narrated from him by Ḥammād ibn Salama, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUthmān ibn Khuthaym, from Ibrāhīm, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās. Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah have mercy on him, made clear that this verse was revealed about a particular slave who had no wealth — for it is not said of every slave (that he is not able to do anything). So it was revealed about him and about a master who had wealth from which he spent; and that the other verse was revealed about a particular man who had no wealth and was a burden upon his mawlā, i.e. his cousin or relative.
Allah struck these parables so that it be known that He is one God, and that nothing else should be likened to Him.
The saying of whoever said that it is an idol is not sound, because the name "slave" does not apply to an idol.

nahhas-meani:77-77.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلِلَّهِ غَيْبُ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ﴾.
[That is: the knowledge of what in them is hidden from the servants.]
Then He said: ﴿وَمَآ أَمْرُ ٱلسَّاعَةِ إِلاَّ كَلَمْحِ ٱلْبَصَرِ أَوْ هُوَ أَقْرَبُ﴾.
Qatāda said: it is that He, Mighty and Majestic is He, says (كُنْ) "Be!", and that is like the twinkling of an eye, or nearer.
Someone else said: the meaning is: or it is nearer in your estimation; He did not mean that it is this near, but He meant to make His power known to us.

nahhas-meani:79-79.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَلَمْ يَرَوْاْ إِلَىٰ ٱلطَّيْرِ مُسَخَّرَاتٍ فِي جَوِّ ٱلسَّمَآءِ﴾.
«الجوّ» is the distant air, and farther than it is «السُّكَاك»; the singular is «سُكَاكة».

nahhas-meani:80-80.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱللَّهُ جَعَلَ لَكُمْ مِّن بُيُوتِكُمْ سَكَناًً﴾.
That is: a place in which you dwell.
* Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَجَعَلَ لَكُمْ مِّن جُلُودِ ٱلأَنْعَامِ بُيُوتاً﴾.
He means houses (tents) of leather and the like; and «الأنعام» are camels, cattle and sheep.
* Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿تَسْتَخِفُّونَهَا يَوْمَ ظَعْنِكُمْ وَيَوْمَ إِقَامَتِكُمْ﴾.
That is: carrying them is light for you, in your travelling and your residing.
* Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿وَمِنْ أَصْوَافِهَا وَأَوْبَارِهَا وَأَشْعَارِهَآ أَثَاثاً وَمَتَاعاً إِلَىٰ حِينٍ﴾.
Wool is from sheep, fur (awbār) from camels, and hair from goats.
Qatāda said: «الأثاث» is wealth.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: «الأثاث» is wealth and adornment.
«الأثاث» according to the lexicographers is household goods such as furnishings and coverings; and «أثَّ يئِثُّ أثّاً» is said when someone has come to possess household goods. Abū Zayd said: the singular of «الأَثاث» is «أَثَاثَة».
* Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿وَمَتَاعاً إِلَىٰ حِينٍ﴾.
Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda: until a term, and as sufficient provision (bulgha).

nahhas-meani:81-81.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱللَّهُ جَعَلَ لَكُمْ مِّمَّا خَلَقَ ظِلاَلاً﴾.
He means the shade of trees; and Allah knows best.
* Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿وَجَعَلَ لَكُمْ مِّنَ ٱلْجِبَالِ أَكْنَاناً﴾.
That is: what shelters you; the singular is «كِنّ».
* Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿وَجَعَلَ لَكُمْ سَرَابِيلَ تَقِيكُمُ ٱلْحَرَّ﴾.
Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda that he said: He means linen shirts.
* Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿وَسَرَابِيلَ تَقِيكُم بَأْسَكُمْ﴾.
Qatāda said: He means coats of mail.
ʿUthmān ibn ʿAṭāʾ narrated from his father that he said: they were addressed only with what they knew. He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said ﴿وَجَعَلَ لَكُمْ مِّنَ ٱلْجِبَالِ أَكْنَاناً﴾, while what He made for them of the plains is more and greater, but they were people of mountains; ﴿وَجَعَلَ لَكُمْ سَرَابِيلَ تَقِيكُمُ ٱلْحَرَّ﴾, while what protects from cold is more, but they were people of heat.
Al-Farrāʾ, "Yaḥyā ibn Ziyād", said: the meaning is: protecting you from heat and protecting you from cold; then it was omitted, as the poet said:
 فَمَا أَدْرِي إذَا يَمَّمتُّ وَجْهاً * أريدُ الخَيْرَ أيُّهُما يَلِيني
(I do not know, when I set out in some direction seeking good, which of the two will befall me.)
The meaning is: which of good and evil, because when he seeks good he guards against evil.
* Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿كَذَلِكَ يُتِمُّ نِعْمَتَهُ عَلَيْكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُسْلِمُونَ﴾.
It is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās [that he read] ﴿لَعَلَّكُمْ تَسْلَمُونَ﴾ and said: i.e. [safe] from wounds; but its chain is weak: ʿAbbād ibn al-ʿAwwām narrated it from Ḥanẓala, from Shahr ibn Ḥawshab, from Ibn ʿAbbās.
The apparent sense of the Qurʾān indicates Islam, because He enumerated the blessings and then said ﴿لَعَلَّكُمْ تُسْلِمُونَ﴾.

nahhas-meani:82-82.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿فَإِن تَوَلَّوْاْ فَإِنَّمَا عَلَيْكَ ٱلْبَلاَغُ ٱلْمُبِينُ. يَعْرِفُونَ نِعْمَتَ ٱللَّهِ ثُمَّ يُنكِرُونَهَا﴾.
Sufyān narrated from al-Suddī that he said: He means Muḥammad ﷺ.
Abū Jaʿfar said: this view is good, and the meaning is: they know that the matter of the Prophet ﷺ is true, then they deny it.
Warqāʾ narrated from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, that he said: He means the dwellings, the livestock and what they are provided from them, and the garments of iron and clothing; Allah bestowed that upon them, but they did not give thanks, and they said: it belonged only to our forefathers and we inherited it from them.

nahhas-meani:84-84.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيَوْمَ نَبْعَثُ مِن كُلِّ أُمَّةٍ شَهِيداً﴾.
It is narrated that the prophet of every nation is a witness against it.

nahhas-meani:86-86.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَألْقَوْا إِلَيْهِمُ ٱلْقَوْلَ إِنَّكُمْ لَكَاذِبُونَ﴾.
That is: their gods disowned them, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿سَيكْفُرونَ بِعِبَادَتِهِمْ وَيَكُونُونَ عَلَيْهِمْ ضِدَّاً﴾.
[Translator's note: the Arabic reads «جحدتم آلهتم», literally "their gods denied you"; rendered according to the evident sense.]

nahhas-meani:87-87.t:
Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَأَلْقَوْاْ إِلَىٰ ٱللَّهِ يَوْمَئِذٍ ٱلسَّلَمَ وَضَلَّ عَنْهُم مَّا كَانُواْ يَفْتَرُونَ﴾.
Saʿīd narrated from Qatāda that he said: they surrendered and were humbled; ﴿وَضَلَّ عَنْهُم مَّا كَانُواْ يَفْتَرُونَ﴾, i.e. [what] they associated [with Him].

nahhas-meani:88-88.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ وَصَدُّواْ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ زِدْنَاهُمْ عَذَاباً فَوْقَ ٱلْعَذَابِِ﴾ [verse 88].
Masrūq narrated from ʿAbd Allāh that he said: they will be given in addition scorpions whose fangs are like tall palm trees.

nahhas-meani:89-89.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَنَزَّلْنَا عَلَيْكَ ٱلْكِتَابَ تِبْيَاناً لِّكُلِّ شَيْءٍ﴾.
Abān ibn Thaʿlab narrated from Mujāhid that he said: an explanation of the lawful as distinct from the unlawful.

nahhas-meani:91-91.t:
And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿وَلاَ تَنقُضُواْ ٱلأَيْمَانَ بَعْدَ تَوْكِيدِهَا﴾.
Mujāhid said: He means making the oath solemn.

nahhas-meani:92-92.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلاَ تَكُونُواْ كَٱلَّتِي نَقَضَتْ غَزْلَهَا مِن بَعْدِ قُوَّةٍ أَنكَاثاً تَتَّخِذُونَ أَيْمَانَكُمْ دَخَلاً بَيْنَكُمْ أَن تَكُونَ أُمَّةٌ هِيَ أَرْبَى مِنْ أُمَّةٍ﴾.
This is a difficult verse that requires reflection.
Qatāda said: «الدَّخَل» is treachery.
Someone else said: the meaning is: do not swear, or make oaths binding upon yourselves, and then break them, so that you would be like a woman who spun yarn, twisted it firmly and made it strong, then undid it.
«الأنكاث» is what is unravelled of silk, camel hair and the like, in order to be spun a second time; and from it one says «ناكث» (one who breaks [a pledge]).
It is narrated in the exegesis that a woman called Rabṭa bint Saʿd used to spin with a large spindle, and when she had twisted it firmly and perfected it, she would order her slave-girl and she would undo it.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said concerning His saying, the Exalted, ﴿أَن تَكُونَ أُمَّةٌ هِيَ أَرْبَى مِنْ أُمَّةٍ﴾: i.e. more numerous. He said: so they were commanded to fulfil the covenant, even if they [the others] were many.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated from Mujāhid that he said: they used to make alliances with a people and make covenants with them, and when they learned that others were more numerous and stronger than them, they would break their covenant and ally themselves with the others; so Allah, exalted be His mention, forbade them that.
The meaning according to the lexicographers is: because a nation is, or on account of a nation being, more abundant than another nation, i.e. richer and more numerous. That is: do not make a covenant with a people and then, when they feel secure, break the covenant so that your associates may be richer and stronger.

nahhas-meani:97-97.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مَنْ عَمِلَ صَالِحاً مِّن ذَكَرٍ أَوْ أُنْثَىٰ وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌ فَلَنُحْيِيَنَّهُ حَيَاةً طَيِّبَةً وَلَنَجْزِيَنَّهُمْ أَجْرَهُم بِأَحْسَنِ مَا كَانُواْ يَعْمَلُونََ﴾.
It is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: the good life is lawful provision; then he goes to Allah, and He rewards him according to the best of what he used to do.
It is also narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās — al-Ḥakam narrated it from ʿIkrima from him — that he said: the good life is contentment.
Ibn Kathīr narrated from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr concerning His saying, the Exalted, ﴿فَلَنُحْيِيَنَّهُ حَيَاةً طَيِّبَةً﴾ that he said: in the Hereafter He will give him a good life.
ʿAwf narrated from al-Ḥasan: no one has a good life except in Paradise.

nahhas-meani:98-98.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَإِذَا قَرَأْتَ ٱلْقُرْآنَ فَٱسْتَعِذْ بِٱللَّهِ مِنَ ٱلشَّيْطَانِ ٱلرَّجِيمِ﴾.
The meaning is: when you intend to recite; this is as you say: "when you eat, say: In the name of Allah"; and similar to it in the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَا أَيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إذَا قُمْتُمْ إلى الصَلاَةِ﴾.

nahhas-meani:100-100.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّمَا سُلْطَانُهُ عَلَىٰ ٱلَّذِينَ يَتَوَلَّوْنَهُ وَٱلَّذِينَ هُم بِهِ مُشْرِكُونَ﴾.
Ibn [Abī] Najīḥ narrated from Mujāhid that he said: ﴿سُلْطَانُهُ﴾ is his argument; and he said: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ هُم بِهِ مُشْرِكُونَ﴾: they make him equal to the Lord of the worlds.
[Translator's note: the text has «ابنُ نجيح»; elsewhere this narrator appears as Ibn Abī Najīḥ.]
Someone other than Mujāhid said: if the meaning were that they associated [others] with Satan, they would be believers; rather the meaning is: and those who, on account of him, are associators — as you say: "So-and-so became learned through you (بِكَ)", i.e. on account of you.

nahhas-meani:101-101.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِذَا بَدَّلْنَآ آيَةً مَّكَانَ آيَةٍٍ﴾.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated from Mujāhid that he said: We lifted it and put another in its place.
Someone else said: i.e. We abrogated a verse with a verse that is harder on them than it. ﴿قَالُوۤاْ إِنَّمَآ أَنتَ مُفْتَرٍ﴾, i.e. a liar. So He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿إنَّمَا يَفْتَرِي الكَذِبَ الَّذِينَ لاَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِآيَاتِ اللَّهِ﴾, i.e. those who, when they see a sign which none but a prophet brings, deny it — these are the greatest liars of all.

nahhas-meani:103-103.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَقَدْ نَعْلَمُ أَنَّهُمْ يَقُولُونَ إِنَّمَا يُعَلِّمُهُ بَشَرٌ لِّسَانُ ٱلَّذِي يُلْحِدُونَ إِلَيْهِ أَعْجَمِيٌّ وَهَـٰذَا لِسَانٌ عَرَبِيٌّ مُّبِينٌ﴾.
Sufyān narrated from Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit, from ʿIkrima, that he said: he was a slave-boy of the Banū ʿĀmir ibn Luʾayy, called — I think — Yaʿīsh.
ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam narrated from al-Ḍaḥḥāk that he said: he is "Salmān al-Fārisī", may Allah have mercy on him.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated from Mujāhid: he is "ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥaḍramī", and he was a Byzantine (Rūmī) who wrote well.
Abū ʿUbayd said: someone other than Mujāhid said: his name was "Jabr".
Abū Jaʿfar said: these views are not contradictory, because it is possible that they pointed to all of these and claimed that they were teaching him. The root meaning of «الإلحاد» in the language is inclining.

nahhas-meani:106-106.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مَن كَفَرَ بِٱللَّهِ مِن بَعْدِ إيمَانِهِ إِلاَّ مَنْ أُكْرِهَ وَقَلْبُهُ مُطْمَئِنٌّ بِٱلإِيمَانِ﴾.
The exegetes [hold] that this verse was revealed concerning "ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir", may Allah have mercy on him, because he came close to some of what they urged him to do.
* Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿وَلَـٰكِن مَّن شَرَحَ بِالْكُفْرِ صَدْراً فَعَلَيْهِمْ غَضَبٌ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
That is: whoever opened his breast to accept it.

nahhas-meani:110-110.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ثُمَّ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ لِلَّذِينَ هَاجَرُواْ مِن بَعْدِ مَا فُتِنُواْ ثُمَّ جَاهَدُواْ وَصَبَرُواْ﴾.
All of this is about ʿAmmār; and the meaning is: and they were patient in jihād.

nahhas-meani:111-111.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَوْمَ تَأْتِي كُلُّ نَفْسٍ تُجَادِلُ عَن نَّفْسِهَا﴾.
It is narrated that Kaʿb said to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah have mercy on him: Hell will give a great roar on the Day of Resurrection, and there will remain no angel brought near nor prophet sent but that he falls to his knees, saying: "My Lord, myself!" — so much so that Ibrāhīm, the intimate friend of the All-Merciful, will fall to his knees and say: "I ask You only for myself." Then Kaʿb said: this is indeed in the Book of Allah, and he recited ﴿يَوْمَ تَأْتِي كُلُّ نَفْسٍ تُجَادِلُ عَن نَّفْسِهَا﴾.
Someone else said: this is indicated by ﴿يَوْمَ يَفِرُّ المَرْءُ مِن أَخِيهِ. وَأُمِّهِ وَأَبِيهِ﴾.

nahhas-meani:112-112.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَضَرَبَ ٱللَّهُ مَثَلاً قَرْيَةً كَانَتْ آمِنَةً مُّطْمَئِنَّةً﴾.
Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda that he said: it is Mecca.
Someone else said: its people were in security and ease, then Allah tested them with killing and hunger for seven years. He, the Exalted, said: ﴿فَأَذَاقَهَا ٱللَّهُ لِبَاسَ ٱلْجُوعِ وَٱلْخَوْفِ﴾. The root meaning of tasting (al-dhawq) is with the mouth; then it came to be used for trial and testing.

nahhas-meani:115-115.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَمَنِ ٱضْطُرَّ غَيْرَ بَاغٍ وَلاَ عَادٍٍ﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar said: we have mentioned it in Sūrat al-Baqara.
It is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: whoever eats carrion while not compelled to it is a transgressor (bāghin) and one who exceeds the limit (ʿādin).
And it is narrated from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and Mujāhid that they both said: if he makes the road unsafe and commits highway robbery, carrion is not made lawful for him. This is the meaning of what they said.

nahhas-meani:116-116.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلاَ تَقُولُواْ لِمَا تَصِفُ أَلْسِنَتُكُمُ ٱلْكَذِبَ هَـٰذَا حَلاَلٌ وَهَـٰذَا حَرَامٌٌ﴾.
Mujāhid said: He means the baḥāʾir and the suyyab [camels dedicated to the idols].

nahhas-meani:118-118.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَعَلَىٰ ٱلَّذِينَ هَادُواْ حَرَّمْنَا مَا قَصَصْنَا عَلَيْكَ مِن قَبْلُ﴾.
Qatāda said: it is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿وَعَلى الَّذِينَ هَادُوا حَرَّمْنَا كُلَّ ذِي ظُفُرٍ﴾.

nahhas-meani:124-124.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّمَا جُعِلَ ٱلسَّبْتُ عَلَىٰ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱخْتَلَفُواْ فِيهِ﴾.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr narrated from Qatāda that he said: some of them made it lawful and some of them made it unlawful.
[Translator's note: the text reads «سعيدُ بن جُبَيرٍ عن قتادةَ»; Saʿīd ibn Jubayr was older than Qatāda, and the usual narrator from Qatāda in this book is Saʿīd (ibn Abī ʿArūba).]
Mujāhid said: they abandoned Friday and chose Saturday.

nahhas-meani:125-125.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ٱدْعُ إِلَىٰ سَبِيلِ رَبِّكَ بِٱلْحِكْمَةِ وَٱلْمَوْعِظَةِ ٱلْحَسَنَةِ وَجَادِلْهُم بِٱلَّتِي هِيَ أَحْسَنُ﴾.
﴿وَجَادِلْهُم بِٱلَّتِي هِيَ أَحْسَنُ﴾ — this is abrogated.

nahhas-meani:126-126.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِنْ عَاقَبْتُمْ فَعَاقِبُواْ بِمِثْلِ مَا عُوقِبْتُمْ بِهِ﴾.
Qatāda said: when they mutilated Ḥamza, may Allah be pleased with him, they [the Muslims] said: we shall certainly mutilate them; so Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, revealed this verse.
ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam narrated from al-Ḍaḥḥāk that he said: this verse was revealed before fighting [was prescribed], and before Sūrat Barāʾa.
Abū Jaʿfar said: this view is more fitting, and Zayd ibn Aslam said something similar.
He said: when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to Medina, he was given permission to wage jihād against the polytheists and to be harsh with them.
What shows you that this was revealed in Mecca is His saying, the Exalted, ﴿وَلاَ تَكُ في ضَيْقٍ مِمَّا يَمْكُرُونَ﴾; and most of their plotting, and his grief ﷺ over them, was in Mecca.
As for the ḥadīth of Abū Hurayra and Ibn ʿAbbās — "when Ḥamza was killed, Allah's mercy be upon him, the Prophet ﷺ said: I shall surely mutilate seventy of them", whereupon ﴿وَإِنْ عَاقَبْتُمْ فَعَاقِبُواْ بِمِثْلِ مَا عُوقِبْتُمْ بِهِ﴾ was revealed — the chains of both are weak.

nahhas-meani:128-128.t:
And His saying, exalted be His name: ﴿إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ مَعَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّقَواْ وَّٱلَّذِينَ هُم مُّحْسِنُونََ﴾.
It is narrated from al-Ḥasan that he said: fear Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, in what He has forbidden you, and do well in performing His obligations.

nahhas-meani:1-1.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَتَىٰ أَمْرُ ٱللَّهِ فَلاَ تَسْتَعْجِلُوهُُ﴾.
Some of them said: ﴿أَتَى﴾ ("has come") means "will come," because the meaning is known, so it becomes like your saying: "If you honour me, I honoured you" (i.e. I will honour you).
And it was said: Allah's informing in the past and in the future are one and the same, because it is known that it will happen, so it is in the position of what has already happened.
A third view — and it is the best of them — is that they considered far off the punishment Allah had promised them, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, informed them that it was near, saying: ﴿أَتَىٰ أَمْرُ ٱللَّهِ﴾,
i.e. in its nearness it is in the position of what has already come, as the Exalted said: ﴿إقْتَرَبَتِ السَّاعةُ﴾, and as one says: "The news has come to you," i.e. it has drawn near to you.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: That is, the Qurʾān has come with the obligations, the rulings and the legal limits.

nahhas-meani:10-10.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿هُوَ ٱلَّذِي أَنْزَلَ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَاءِ مَآءً لَّكُم مَّنْهُ شَرَابٌ وَمِنْهُ شَجَرٌ فِيهِ تُسِيمُونَ﴾.
Qatāda and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: ﴿فِيهِ تُسِيمُونَ﴾ — in it you pasture (your herds).
Abū Jaʿfar said: And so it is in the language: one says أسَمتُ الإبلَ, i.e. I pastured them, so I am musīm, and they are musāma and sāʾima.

nahhas-meani:13-13.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَا ذَرَأَ لَكُمْ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ مُخْتَلِفاً أَلْوَانُهُُ﴾.
Qatāda said: Of beasts, trees and fruits.

nahhas-meani:14-14.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَتَرَى ٱلْفُلْكَ مَوَاخِرَ فِيهِِ﴾.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: Going and coming.
Al-makhr in the language is cleaving. One says مَخَرتِ السفينةُ تمخَرُ وتمخُرُ when the ship cleaves the water and you hear a sound from it, and that is when the winds blow. And makhr of the earth is only the water's cleaving it.

nahhas-meani:15-15.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأَلْقَىٰ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ رَوَاسِيََ﴾.
Al-Ḥasan said: That is, mountains.
Abū Jaʿfar said: One says رَسَا يرسُو when something is firm and stays fixed. Then the Exalted said: ﴿أَن تَمِيدَ بِكُمْ﴾.
Ibrāhīm said: That is, lest it tip over.
Abū Jaʿfar said: One says ماد يميد when something moves and sways.
And Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda, who said: I heard al-Ḥasan say: When Allah created the earth it was about to sway, so they (the angels) said: This will not keep anyone settled upon it. Then in the morning Allah had created the mountains, and the angels did not know from what the mountains had been created.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأَنْهَاراً وَسُبُلاً﴾.
That is, and He made in it rivers and ways.
Qatāda said: That is, roads.

nahhas-meani:16-16.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَعَلامَاتٍ وَبِٱلنَّجْمِ هُمْ يَهْتَدُونَ﴾.
Sufyān narrated from Manṣūr, from Ibrāhīm, who said: Among the stars are landmarks, and among them are those by which one is guided.
Al-Farrāʾ said: (The star is) al-Jady (the Pole Star) and the two Farqads.
Abū Jaʿfar said: What the exegetes and the people of language hold, other than him, is that al-najm here means the stars.
Allah created the stars as an adornment for the heaven, as missiles against the devils, so that the number of years and reckoning may be known by them, and so that guidance may be found by them.

nahhas-meani:2-2.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يُنَزِّلُ ٱلْمَلاۤئِكَةَ بِٱلْرُّوحِ مِنْ أَمْرِهِ عَلَىٰ مَن يَشَآءُ مِنْ عِبَادِهِِ﴾.
Hushaym narrated from Abū Bishr, from Mujāhid, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: al-Rūḥ is a creation among Allah's creations and a command among His commands; their forms are like the forms of the children of Ādam; no angel descends in the heaven but that one of them is with him.
And Ibn Jurayj [Translator's note: printed «ابن جريح»] narrated from Mujāhid, who said: No angel descends but that a rūḥ is with him.
Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Khālid said: I asked Abū Ṣāliḥ about al-rūḥ, and he said: They have forms like the forms of the children of Ādam, but they are not of them.
Al-Ḥasan said: The angels descend with al-rūḥ, i.e. with prophethood.
And Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda: "The angels descend with al-rūḥ" — he said: with revelation and mercy.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is a good view, and ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa narrated it from Ibn ʿAbbās;
i.e. He sends them down with what is in the position of spirit and life, as the Exalted said: ﴿فَرَوْحٌ وَرَيْحَانٌ﴾.
And it was said: its meaning is mercy.

nahhas-meani:20-20.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ لاَ يَخْلُقُونَ شَيْئاً وَهُمْ يُخْلَقُونَ﴾.
Meaning the idols.
Muḥammad al-Yamānī read ﴿والذين يُدْعَوْنَ منْ دونِ اللَّهِ﴾ ("and those who are called upon besides Allah") with ḍamma on the yāʾ and fatḥa on the ʿayn.

nahhas-meani:21-21.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَمْواتٌ غَيْرُ أَحْيَآءٍٍ﴾.
That is, they are dead, not living. ﴿وَمَا يَشْعُرُونَ أَيَّانَ يُبْعَثُونَ﴾.
It is possible that the meaning is: and the idols do not perceive.
And it is possible that the meaning is: and the polytheists do not perceive when they will be raised.

nahhas-meani:5-5.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلأَنْعَامَ خَلَقَهَا لَكُمْ فِيهَا دِفْءٌ وَمَنَافِعُ وَمِنْهَا تَأْكُلُونََ﴾.
Isrāʾīl narrated from Simāk ibn Ḥarb, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: Offspring.
And Ibn Jurayj [Translator's note: printed «ابن جريح»] narrated from Mujāhid, who said: al-dif' (warmth) is clothing that is woven, and the benefits are riding, milk and meat.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is a good view, i.e. what gives warmth from their hair and other things. I reckon that Ibn ʿAbbās's position is that the benefits are the offspring, not the warmth; although al-Umawī narrated that al-dif' among the Arabs is the breeding of camels and the benefit derived from them, so this would be included in it.

nahhas-meani:6-6.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَكُمْ فِيهَا جَمَالٌ حِينَ تُرِيحُونَ وَحِينَ تَسْرَحُونََ﴾.
Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda, who said: When they come back in the evening, their humps at their largest from fatness and their udders full.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The meaning according to the people of language is: and (when) you bring them back in the evening. One says أَرْحتُ الإبلَ when you bring them back from the pasture to the place where they stay at night; the place is called al-murāḥ, and in the ḥadīth: "If he steals it from the murāḥ, (his hand) is cut off."
And the meaning of ﴿تَسْرحُون﴾ is: you take them out in the morning to the pasture. سَرحْتُ الإبلَ أَسْرحُها سَرْحاً وسُروحاً — when you go out with them in the morning to the pasture and leave them to graze. And سَرَّحتُ هي [Translator's note: printed thus with ḍamma on the tāʾ; the sense "they went out to pasture" (سَرَّحَتْ هي) seems intended]: transitive and intransitive are the same.

nahhas-meani:7-7.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَتَحْمِلُ أَثْقَالَكُمْ إِلَىٰ بَلَدٍ لَّمْ تَكُونُواْ بَالِغِيهِ إِلاَّ بِشِقِّ ٱلأَنفُسِِ﴾.
Ibn Jurayj [Translator's note: printed «ابن جريح»] narrated from Mujāhid, who said: except with hardship.
Others said: the meaning is: were it not for the camels, you would not reach the lands except with hardship.
And it has been read ﴿إلاَّ بِشَقِّ الأَنْفُسِ﴾ (with fatḥa on the shīn), and it has the meaning of the first, except that it is a maṣdar (verbal noun).

nahhas-meani:8-8.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ٱلْخَيْلَ وَٱلْبِغَالَ وَٱلْحَمِيرَ لِتَرْكَبُوهَا وَزِينَةًً﴾.
A group, among them ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās, interpreted this as meaning that it is not lawful to eat these, because He said regarding camels ﴿وَمِنْهَا تَأْكُلُونَ﴾ and did not say this regarding "horses, mules and donkeys."
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيَخْلُقُ مَا لاَ تَعْلَمُونَ﴾.
Its apparent sense is general, except that ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Muʿāwiya al-Qurashī narrated to us, saying: Mūsā ibn Muḥammad narrated to us from Ibn al-Suddī, from his father, regarding His saying, the Exalted, ﴿وَيَخْلُقُ مَا لاَ تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ — he said: the moth in clothes.

nahhas-meani:9-9.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَعَلَىٰ ٱللَّهِ قَصْدُ ٱلسَّبِيلِِ﴾.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: That is, the making clear of guidance and misguidance.
Mujāhid said: That is, the path of truth. And this resembles ﴿قَالَ هَذَا صِرَاطٌ عَلَيَّ مُسْتَقِيمٌ﴾,
i.e. according to My way and My religion. So too ﴿وَعَلَىٰ ٱللَّهِ قَصْدُ ٱلسَّبِيلِ﴾, i.e. the straight course among them is whatever is according to Allah's religion.
And it was said: it is the making clear of the truth, the proofs and the arguments.
And it was said: by "the way" here Islam is meant.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمِنْهَا جَآئِرٌ﴾.
That is, and among the ways there is one that is jāʾiz [Translator's note: so printed («جائز»), for «جائر»], i.e. deviating from the truth. Abū Bakr ibn Abī l-Azhar recited to me, saying: Bundār recited to me:
لَمَّا خَلَطْتُ دِمَاءَنَا بِدِمَائِهَا * ساَرَ الثِّفَالُ بهَا وجَارَ العَاذِلُ
(When I mingled our blood with hers, the slow beast went off with her, and the reproacher strayed.)
And it is narrated from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, that he read ﴿ومنكُمْ جَائِرٌ﴾ ("and among you is one who deviates").
And ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd likewise read this, by way of interpretation.
* Then the Exalted said: ﴿وَلَوْ شَآءَ لَهَدَاكُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ﴾.
That is, had He willed, He would have sent down a sign compelling you to believe; but He willed to reward and to punish.

nahhas-meani:25-25.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لِيَحْمِلُواْ أَوْزَارَهُمْ كَامِلَةً يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَامَةِِ﴾.
Al-wizr in the language is the heavy load, and sin is called wizr by way of likeness.
* Then the Exalted said: ﴿وَمِنْ أَوْزَارِ ٱلَّذِينَ يُضِلُّونَهُمْ بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ﴾.
Mujāhid said: They are made to bear the sin of those whom they led astray, without anything being diminished from the sin of the one led astray.

nahhas-meani:26-26.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَدْ مَكَرَ ٱلَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ فَأَتَى ٱللَّهُ بُنْيَانَهُمْ مِّنَ ٱلْقَوَاعِدِ فَخَرَّ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلسَّقْفُ مِن فَوْقِهِمْ﴾.
Al-Aʿraj read ﴿السُّقُّفُ﴾ (plural, "the roofs").
Mujāhid said: By this He means "Nimrod son of Canaan," who disputed with Ibrāhīm about his Lord; and it is narrated that he built a great building, and it collapsed.
And it was said: This is a likeness, i.e. Allah destroyed them, so they were like one upon whom his building fell and who perished.
And it was said: Allah nullified their deeds, so they were like one upon whom his building fell.
The benefit of His saying, the Exalted, ﴿مِنْ فَوْقِهِمْ﴾ is that one may say "such-and-such a house fell on me" when he owns it, even if it did not fall on him.

nahhas-meani:27-27.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ثُمَّ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَامَةِ يُخْزِيهِمْ وَيَقُولُ أَيْنَ شُرَكَآئِيَ ٱلَّذِينَ كُنْتُمْ تُشَاقُّونَ فِيهِمْ﴾.
The meaning is: Where are those whom you used to claim were My partners? i.e. Where are My partners according to your claim?! And Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, has no partner.

nahhas-meani:28-28.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَأَلْقَوُاْ ٱلسَّلَمَ﴾.
That is, surrender; i.e. they yielded and surrendered.

nahhas-meani:33-33.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿هَلْ يَنْظُرُونَ إِلاَّ أَن تَأْتِيَهُمُ ٱلْمَلائِكَةُ﴾.
That is, to take their souls; ﴿أَوْ يَأْتِيَ أَمْرُ رَبِّكَ﴾, i.e. with the punishment [the earthquake and the swallowing up by the earth].

nahhas-meani:35-35.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَشْرَكُواْ لَوْ شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ مَا عَبَدْنَا مِن دُونِهِ مِن شَيْءٍ نَّحْنُ وَلاۤ آبَاؤُنَا﴾.
[Some said: Allah censured these people who made their shirk a matter of His will.]
And some said: Whoever says this has disbelieved.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This is an error in interpretation and is not accepted in exegesis; rather, they said this by way of mockery, as the people of Shuʿayb said to their prophet: ﴿إنَّكَ لأَنْتَ الحَلِيمُ الرَّشِيدُ﴾?, i.e. you are the forbearing, the right-minded, according to your own claim?
This is made clear by His saying: ﴿إنْ تَحْرِصْ عَلَى هُدَاهُمْ، فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لاَ يَهْدِي مَنْ يُضِلُّ﴾. And in the reading of Ubayy: ﴿فإن اللَّهَ لا هادي لمن أضَلَّ اللَّهُ﴾ ("for Allah — there is no guide for whom Allah leads astray"), and it is a witness for those who read ﴿لا يُهْدَى﴾ (passive: "is not guided"), and it is the clear reading, as He said: ﴿وَمَا تَوْفِيقي إلاَّ باللَّهِ﴾.
And it is narrated from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd that he read ﴿لا يَهِدِّي مَنْ يَضِلُّ﴾ ("whoever goes astray is not guided"). The best of what has been said on this is what Abū ʿUbayd narrated from al-Farrāʾ: that one says هَدَى يَهْدي in the sense of اهتدى يهتدى ("to be guided"); the Exalted said: ﴿أَمَّنْ لاَ يَهْدِي إلاَّ أَنْ يُهْدَى﴾, meaning yahtadī.
Abū ʿUbayd said: We know of no one who narrated this other than al-Farrāʾ, and he is not suspect in what he reports.
Abū Jaʿfar said: It was reported to me from Muḥammad ibn Yazīd (al-Mubarrad) — as if the meaning of ﴿لا يَهْدِي مَنْ يُضِلُّ﴾ were: whoever He knows that of, and for whom that has been decreed beforehand in His knowledge. He said: «يَهْدي» does not mean yahtadī unless you say يَهَدِّي or يَهِدِّي.

nahhas-meani:39-39.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لِيُبَيِّنَ لَهُمُ ٱلَّذِي يَخْتَلِفُونَ فِيهِِ﴾.
It admits two meanings:
One of them: that it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted verb, indicated by the whole of the statement, the meaning being: rather, He will raise them, to make clear to them that wherein they differ.
The other view: that it is attached to His saying ﴿ولقَدْ بَعَثْنَا في كلِّ أُمَّةٍ رَسُولاً﴾, so the meaning is: and We have sent to every community a messenger, to make clear to them that wherein they differ, and so that those who disbelieve may know that they were liars.

nahhas-meani:41-41.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ هَاجَرُواْ فِي ٱللَّهِ مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا ظُلِمُواْ﴾.
It is said that Bilāl and Ṣuhayb are meant by it; but what the whole of the statement requires is that it be general.
And it is narrated that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him, when he handed the Emigrants their stipends, used to say to them: This is what Allah promised you in this world, and what He has stored up for you in the Hereafter is more. Then he would recite ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ هَاجَرُواْ فِي ٱللَّهِ مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا ظُلِمُواْ لَنُبَوِّئَنَّهُمْ فِي ٱلدُّنْيَا حَسَنَةً وَلأَجْرُ ٱلآخِرَةِ أَكْبَرُ﴾.
And Hushaym narrated from Dāwūd ibn Abī Hind, from al-Shaʿbī, regarding His saying ﴿لَنُبَوِّئَنَّهُمْ فِي ٱلدُّنْيَا حَسَنَةً﴾ — he said: Medina.
Al-Ḥasan said likewise.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: By the good (ḥasana) He means victory and conquest; ﴿وَلأَجْرُ ٱلآخِرَةِ أَكْبَرُ﴾ — Paradise.
And Ibn Jurayj [Translator's note: printed «ابن جريح»] narrated from Mujāhid: ﴿لَنُبَوِّئَنَّهُمْ فِي ٱلدُّنْيَا حَسَنَةً﴾ — he said: a good reputation (lisān ṣidq).

nahhas-meani:43-43.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَآ أَرْسَلْنَا مِن قَبْلِكَ إِلاَّ رِجَالاً نُّوحِيۤ إِلَيْهِمْ﴾.
This was said to them because they said: ﴿أَبَعَثَ اللَّهُ بَشَرَاً رَسُولاَ﴾?
* Then the Exalted said: ﴿فَٱسْأَلُواْ أَهْلَ ٱلذِّكْرِ إِن كُنْتُم لاَ تَعْلَمُونَ﴾.
It was said: He means the People of the Book, because they acknowledge that the messengers were of the children of Ādam.
Wakīʿ said: I asked Sufyān about His saying ﴿فَٱسْأَلُواْ أَهْلَ ٱلذِّكْرِ﴾, and he said: We have heard that they are those of the people of the Torah and the Gospel who embraced Islam.
* Then the Exalted said: ﴿بِالبَيِّنَاتِ وَالزُّبُرِ﴾, i.e. with the proofs and the books.

nahhas-meani:46-46.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَوْ يَأْخُذَهُمْ فِي تَقَلُّبِهِمْ فَمَا هُم بِمُعْجِزِينَ﴾.
Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda, who said: In their journeys.
And ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam narrated from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, who said: By night and by day.

nahhas-meani:47-47.t:
Then the Exalted said: ﴿أَوْ يَأْخُذَهُمْ عَلَىٰ تَخَوُّفٍ﴾.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: I take one group and leave another group, so the remaining group fears that what befell its fellow will befall it.
And ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurāsānī narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿أَوْ يَأْخُذَهُمْ عَلَىٰ تَخَوُّفٍ﴾ — he said: by gradual diminution and tafarruʿ. [Translator's note: «تفرّع» is as printed; the sense is unclear, perhaps «تفزيع», "frightening," is meant.]
And Ibn Jurayj [Translator's note: printed «ابن جريح»] narrated from Ibn Kathīr, from Mujāhid, who said: by diminution.
Abū Jaʿfar said: This view is the one known among the people of language. One says أخَذَهم على خَوْفٍ and على تخوُّفٍ when he diminishes them gradually, as Ibn ʿAbbās and Mujāhid said.
The meaning of diminution is that He diminishes them in their wealth, their crops and their good, one thing after another, until He destroys them.
Al-Layth said: «على تخوُّف» — I have heard that it means "in haste."
And al-Ḍaḥḥāk's saying ﴿عَلَىٰ تَخَوُّفٍ﴾ means: He takes this town and leaves that one beside it, so that it becomes afraid.

nahhas-meani:48-48.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَتَفَيَّأُ ظِلاَلُهُ عَنِ ٱلْيَمِينِ وَٱلْشَّمَآئِلِ سُجَّداً لِلَّهِ﴾.
Qatāda said: al-fayʾ is the shade.
Others said: al-tafayyuʾ is its returning from place to place, submissive and yielding; and such is the meaning of prostration.
Qatāda said: ﴿عَنِ ٱلْيَمِينِ﴾ — in the morning; and His saying ﴿وَٱلْشَّمَآئِلِ﴾ — in the evening.
Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَهُمْ دَاخِرُونَ﴾.
Qatāda said: That is, humbled.

safi-cedvel:41-41.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); (هاجروا) a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); (في الله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (هاجروا), on the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "in the way of Allah", or "in raising the word of Allah"; (من بعد a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (هاجروا) [Translator's note: the closing parenthesis after «من بعد» is missing in the source]; (ما) a maṣdar-forming (verbal-noun) particle; (ظلموا) a past verb in the passive, indeclinable on the ḍamma.. and (الواو) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (اللام) the lām of the oath, for an implied oath; (نبوّئنّهم) an imperfect verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of nominative.. and (النون) is the nūn of emphasis, and (هم) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the agent is "we"; (في الدنيا) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (نبوّئنّ), and the sign of the genitive is the implied (muqaddar) kasra; (حسنة) a second direct object, accusative, by the verb's being made to carry the meaning of «نعطينّ» ("we shall surely give") [Note: Or in the meaning of «ننزلنّهم», i.e. "a good abode".. Abū Ḥayyān chose that it be a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar, i.e. "a good settling", or that the verb means «نحسننّ إليهم حسنة» ("we shall surely do them good").]; (الواو) conjunction; (اللام) the lām of inception (lām al-ibtidāʾ), for emphasis; (أجر) mubtadaʾ, nominative [Translator's note: the source spells it «مبتدا»]; (الاخرة) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive; (أكبر) khabar (predicate), nominative; (لو) a non-jussive conditional particle; (كانوا يعلمون) like «كانوا يظلمون» [Note: In verse (33) of this sūra.].
The clause «الذين هاجروا ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «هاجروا ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الّذين).
The clause «ظلموا ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the particle relative (ما).
The clause «نبوّئنّهم» has no grammatical position: the answer to an implied oath, and the implied oath clause is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الذين) [Note: According to some, the khabar is omitted, indicated by the answer of the oath.].
The clause «أجر الآخرة أكبر» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «كانوا يعلمون ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يعلمون» is in the position of accusative as the khabar of «كانوا».. and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of «لو» is omitted, i.e. "if those who stayed behind from the emigration knew the measure of the reward of the emigrants, they would have joined them."

safi-cedvel:42-42.t:
* I'rab:
(الّذين) a relative, khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being «هم»; (صبروا) like «هاجروا» [Note: In the preceding verse (41).]; (الواو) conjunction; (على ربّهم) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يتوكّلون), and (هم) is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (يتوكّلون) an imperfect verb, nominative.. and (الواو) is the fāʿil (agent).
The clause «(هم) الذين ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive, giving a reason.
The clause «صبروا ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «يتوكّلون» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause — or to the ṣila.

* Rhetoric:
- Reporting the past with the imperfect: it is more eloquent than reporting with the past verb. That is in the words of the Exalted «وَعَلى رَبِّهِمْ يَتَوَكَّلُونَ»: the apparent meaning is past, and the expression with the imperfect is to bring that wonderful image to mind, as if the listener were witnessing it.

safi-cedvel:43-44.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (ما) negating; (أرسلنا) a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); (من قبلك) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أرسلنا).. and (الكاف) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (إلّا) a particle of restriction; (رجالا) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative; (نوحي) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the sign of the nominative is the implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the yāʾ.. and the agent is "we", for majesty; (إلى) a preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (نوحي); (الفاء) connecting the apodosis of an implied condition; (اسألوا) an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn.. and (الواو) is the agent; (أهل) direct object, accusative; (الذّكر) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (إن) a jussive conditional particle; (كنتم) a defective past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ).. and (تم) is a pronoun, the noun (ism) of «كان»; (لا) negating; (تعلمون) an imperfect verb, nominative.. and (الواو) is the agent.
The clause «أرسلنا..» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «نوحي ...» is in the position of accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of (رجالا).
The clause «اسألوا ...» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, i.e. "if you do not know of our sending men as prophets, then ask ..."
The clause «إن كنتم لا تعلمون» has no grammatical position: parenthetical, between the preposition-phrase — «بالبيّنات» — and what it is attached to.
The clause «لا تعلمون» is in the position of accusative as the khabar of «كنتم».. and the apodosis is omitted, indicated by what precedes it [Note: It is permissible for the clause «كنتم لا تعلمون» to be explicative of the implied condition in the other cases of attaching the preposition-phrase..].
(بالبيّنات) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (نوحي) [Note: It may be attached to an omitted naʿt of (رجالا), i.e. "men laden with the clear proofs" or "accompanied by them".. or it is attached to the verb «أرسلنا», entering into the restriction together with «رجال», i.e. "We sent none but men with the clear proofs".. It may also be attached to something omitted after «إلّا», its implied form being «أرسلناهم».]; (الواو) conjunction; (الزّبر) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to «البيّنات», genitive; (الواو) conjunction; (أنزلنا الذّكر) like «أرسلنا رجالا»; (إليك) like «إليهم», attached to (أنزلنا); (اللام) of reason (taʿlīl); (تبيّن) an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied «أن» after the lām, and the agent is "you"; (للناس) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (تبيّن); (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of accusative as direct object; (نزّل) a past verb in the passive, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being «هو», and it is the referring pronoun (ʿāʾid); (إليهم) like the first, attached to (نزّل).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تبيّن ...) is in the position of genitive by the lām, attached to (أنزلنا).
(الواو) conjunction; (لعلّهم) a particle resembling the verb, for hope.. and (هم) is a pronoun in the position of accusative as the noun of «لعلّ»; (يتفكّرون) like «تعلمون».
The clause «أنزلنا إليك ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause «أرسلنا».
The clause «تبيّن ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the implied particle relative (أن).
The clause «نزّل ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative (ما).
The clause «لعلّهم يتفكّرون» has no grammatical position: conjoined to something implied, i.e. "so they hear that, and perhaps they will reflect".

* Morphology:
(الذّكر): it is the Noble Qur'an, and it came in the form of the maṣdar (verbal noun) because it contains admonitions and alerting for the heedless.

* Benefits:
- Exegesis of the Qur'an:
The Companions at the dawn of Islam were reluctant to plunge into explaining what was obscure among the words of the Qur'an; among this group were Abū Bakr and ʿUmar, even though ʿUmar had pointed to the poetry of the Arabs in their Jāhiliyya, and that it is the register (dīwān) of the Arabs, and that in it is the explanation of their Book. But this reluctance did not prevent a group of the Companions from rising up and making their way in explaining the rare words of the Qur'an; at the head of this group were ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās and ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, followed by Ibn Masʿūd and Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī, Mujāhid, ʿIkrima, Qatāda and al-Suddī. Aḥmad Amīn says in his book Fajr al-Islām, in substance: these exegetes among the Companions and the Successors followed a method that can be summed up as seeking guidance from the ḥadīth of the Messenger of Allah, from the spirit of the Qur'an, and from Arabic poetry and pre-Islamic literature in general, then from the customs of the Arabs in their Jāhiliyya and the dawn of their Islam, and the events they faced, and the hostility, disputes, emigration and wars that the Messenger met.

safi-cedvel:45-47.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) for reproachful interrogation; (الفاء) resumptive; (أمن) a past verb; (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as fāʿil (agent); (مكروا) a past verb and its agent; (السيّئات) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative [Note: Or a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar, being its adjective, i.e. "they plotted the evil plots"; «المكرات», with fatḥa on the kāf, is the plural of «مكرة», with sukūn on the kāf, the maṣdar of single occurrence from «المكر».. It may also be a direct object of (أمن), i.e. "they felt secure from the evil punishments", and on this view the interpreted maṣdar (أن يخسف) is a badal (substitute) from it.], by the verb's being made to carry the meaning of «عملوا» ("they did"), and the sign of the accusative is the kasra; (أن) a maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle; (يخسف) an imperfect verb, accusative; (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil; (الباء) a preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يخسف); (الأرض) direct object, accusative.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يخسف) is in the position of accusative as direct object, its governor being «أمن».
(أو) a conjunction; (يأتيهم) like «يخسف» and conjoined to it, and (هم) is a pronoun, direct object; (العذاب) fāʿil, nominative; (من) a preposition; (حيث) a noun indeclinable on the ḍamma, in the position of genitive, attached to (يأتيهم); (لا يشعرون) like «لا تعلمون» [Note: In verse (43) of this sūra.].
The clause «أمن الذين ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive [Note: Or it is conjoined by the conjunction to something implied and resumptive, i.e. "did they not reflect, so they felt secure?" — said by al-Zamakhsharī — but what we have followed keeps us away from interpretive supplying, and neither the meaning nor the rules of i'rab reject it.].
The clause «مكّروا ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين). [Translator's note: the source writes «مكّروا» with a shadda here; the Quranic word is «مكروا».]
The clause «يخسف بهم ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the particle relative (أن).
The clause «يأتيهم العذاب ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause «يخسف ...».
The clause «لا يشعرون ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
(أو) like the first; (يأخذهم) like «يأتيهم»; (في تقلّبهم) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the object, i.e. "while engaged in their going about"; (الفاء) of reason (taʿlīl); (ما) negating, operating as «ليس»; (هم) a detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as the noun (ism) of «ما»; (الباء) a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; (معجزين) genitive in form, accusative in position, the khabar of «ما», and the sign of the genitive is the yāʾ.
The clause «يأخذهم ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause «يأتيهم».
The clause «ما هم بمعجزين ...» has no grammatical position: giving a reason (taʿlīliyya).
(أو يأخذهم على تخوّف) like «أو يأخذهم في تقلّبهم»; (الفاء) of reason; (إنّ) a particle of emphasis and accusative; (ربّكم) the noun of «إنّ», accusative.. and (كم) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (اللام) the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), for emphasis; (رؤف) the khabar of «إنّ», nominative; (رحيم) a second khabar, nominative.
The clause «يأخذهم ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the first clause «يأخذهم».
The clause «إنّ ربّكم لرؤوف ...» has no grammatical position: giving a reason.

safi-cedvel:48-48.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) for reproachful interrogation; (الواو) resumptive; (لم) a particle of negation and jussive; (يروا) an imperfect verb, jussive, and the sign of the jussive is the dropping of the nūn.. and (الواو) is the fāʿil (agent); (إلى) a preposition; (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يروا), by the verb's being made to carry the meaning of «ينظروا» ("they look"); (خلق) a past verb; (الله) the Name of Majesty, agent, nominative; (من شيء) a preposition and its genitive noun, ḥāl (circumstantial) [Note: Or a tamyīz (specification) of the relative (ما).] of the omitted referring pronoun; (يتفيّأ) an imperfect verb, nominative; (ظلاله) agent, nominative.. and (الهاء) is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (عن اليمين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يتفيّأ) [Note: Or attached to an omitted ḥāl of «الظلال».]; (الواو) conjunction; (الشمائل) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to «اليمين», genitive; (سجّدا) a ḥāl of «الظلال», accusative; (لله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (سجّدا); (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya); (هم) a detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and it refers back to «الظلال», which have been treated as rational beings; (داخرون) khabar (predicate), nominative, and the sign of the nominative is the wāw.
The clause «يروا ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «خلق الله ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (ما).
The clause «يتفيّأ ظلاله» is in the position of genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of «شيء».
The clause «هم داخرون» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl.

* Morphology:
(اليمين): a noun for the direction opposite to the left; its pattern is فعيل.
(داخرون): plural of «داخر», active participle of the triliteral «دخر»; its pattern is فاعل.

safi-cedvel:49-50.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (لله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يسجد), which is an imperfect verb, nominative; (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as fāʿil (agent); (في السموات) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of «ما»; (الواو) conjunction; (ما في الأرض) like its counterpart and conjoined to it; (من دابّة) a preposition and its genitive noun, ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun of settledness (ḍamīr al-istiqrār) in the ṣila [Note: Or a tamyīz (specification) of the second relative (ما).]; (الملائكة) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the first relative (ما) by the wāw, nominative; (وهم لا يستكبرون): and (هم) is like the first [Note: In the preceding verse (48).]; (لا) negating; (يستكبرون) an imperfect verb, nominative.. and (الواو) is the agent.
The clause «يسجد ما في السموات» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «هم لا يستكبرون» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl.
The clause «لا يستكبرون» is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (هم).
(يخافون) an imperfect verb, nominative.. and (الواو) is the agent; (ربّهم) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative.. and (هم) is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (من فوقهم) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a ḥāl of «ربّ» [Note: Or attached to (يخافون) on the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "they fear the punishment of their Lord from above them", because punishment descends from above.], i.e. "being high above them by dominion".. and (هم) is muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) conjunction; (يفعلون) like «يخافون»; (ما) a relative noun in the position of accusative as direct object; (يؤمرون) an imperfect verb in the passive.. and (الواو) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and the referring pronoun is omitted.
The clause «يخافون ...» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl of the agent of «يستكبرون» [Note: Or it is a ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) of the negation of arrogance.].

* Rhetoric:
(1) Predominance (taghlīb): in the words of the Exalted «وَلِلَّهِ يَسْجُدُ ما فِي السَّماواتِ وَما فِي الْأَرْضِ».
If you say: why was «من» not brought instead of «ما», giving predominance to the rational beings among the creatures over the others?
I say: because if «من» had been brought, there would have been no indication of predominance in it, and it would have covered rational beings specifically; so that which is suitable for rational beings and others was brought, intending generality. It is mentioned in Rūḥ al-Maʿānī that if we say «ما» is specific to non-rational beings, then its use here for rational beings and others is for predominance.

* Benefits:
Ibn al-Ṣāʾigh said: "He made it singular and plural with regard to the two extremes, because the shade of the morning shrinks until only a little of it remains, so it is as if it were in one direction; and in the evening it is the reverse, because it takes over all directions; so the two extremes were regarded in the verse. This is from the side of meaning. From the side of wording there is agreement in it, because «سجّدا» is plural, so the plural «الشمائل» agrees with it, being adjacent to it. So in the verse there occurred the agreement of the wording with the meaning, and the regard of both together, and that is the utmost of inimitability."

safi-cedvel:51-52.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (قال) a past verb; (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil (agent), nominative; (لا) prohibitive, jussive-governing; (تتّخذوا) an imperfect verb, jussive, and the sign of the jussive is the dropping of the nūn.. and (الواو) is the agent; (إلهين) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative [Note: The second object is omitted, its implied form being «معبودين» ("as objects of worship"); and if the verb is made to carry the meaning of «تعبدوا» ("worship"), it has a single object.], and the sign of the accusative is the yāʾ; (اثنين) a naʿt (adjective) of «إلاهين», accusative, and the sign of the accusative is the yāʾ, as it is annexed to the dual [Note: Or it is a ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) by way of clarification and elucidation..]; (إنّما) a restraining particle and the restrained (kāffa wa-makfūfa); (هو) a detached pronoun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); (إله) khabar (predicate), nominative; (واحد) a naʿt of «إله», nominative like it; (الفاء) connecting the apodosis of an implied condition; (إيّاي) a detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of accusative as the direct object of an omitted verb explained by the mentioned one, and the pronoun comes after it, i.e. «إيّاي ارهبوا»; (الفاء) redundant (zāʾida), for embellishment; (ارهبون) an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn.. and (الواو) is the agent, and (النون) is for protection (wiqāya), and the omitted (الياء) is a pronoun, direct object.
The clause «قال الله ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «لا تتّخذوا ...» is in the position of accusative as the speech reported by «قال» (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «هو إله واحد ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «إيّاي (ارهبوا) ...» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, i.e. "if fear reaches you, then fear Me alone and none other."
The clause «ارهبون (the mentioned one)» has no grammatical position: explicative.
(الواو) conjunction; (اللام) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) a fronted khabar; (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as a delayed mubtadaʾ; (في السموات) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of «ما»; (الأرض) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to «السموات» by the wāw, and genitive; (الواو) conjunction; (له الدين) like «له ما في السموات»; (واصبا) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun concealed in the khabar, i.e. "religion is established for Him, being perpetual"; (الهمزة) for interrogation of disapproval (istifhām inkārī); (الفاء) conjunction; (غير) direct object, fronted, accusative; (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive; (تتّقون) an imperfect verb, nominative, and (الواو) is the agent.
The clause «له ما في السموات ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause «هو إله واحد».
The clause «له الدين ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause «له ما في السموات».
The clause «تتّقون» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause «له الدين» [Note: It is — on the view of al-Zamakhsharī — conjoined to an implied resumption, i.e. "are you ignorant, so you fear other than Allah?"..].

* Morphology:
(واصبا): active participle from «وصب الشيء يصب», of the bāb «ضرب», meaning "it lasted and was firm"; its pattern is فاعل.

* Rhetoric:
(1) Precaution (iḥtirās): that is in the words of the Exalted «وَقالَ اللَّهُ لا تَتَّخِذُوا إِلهَيْنِ اثْنَيْنِ إِنَّما هُوَ إِلهٌ واحِدٌ». It is well known that the number and the counted noun are not combined except beyond one and two; so they say «عندي رجال ثلاثة ونساء ثلاث» ("I have three men and three women"), because the counted noun is devoid of indicating the specific number, so if you did not accompany it with its adjective, the intended number would not be understood. As for «رجل», «امرأة», «رجلان» and «امرأتان», they are counted nouns in which there is an indication of the number, so there is no need to say «رجل واحد», «امرأة واحدة», «رجلان اثنان», «امرأتان اثنتان». As for the noble verse, the noun carrying the meaning of singularity and duality indicates two things: the genus and the specific number; so when it is intended to indicate which of the two is meant, and that what the discourse is driven toward is the number, it is accompanied by what emphasises it, thereby indicating the aim toward it and the concern with it. Do you not see that if you said «إنما هو إله» and did not emphasise it with «واحد», it would not be good, and it would be imagined that you are affirming divinity, not oneness? So precaution was necessary.
(2) Shift of person (iltifāt): in the words of the Exalted «وَإِيَّايَ فَارْهَبُونِ» there is a shift from the third person to the first person, according to the doctrine of the majority, for intensity in frightening and threatening, for frightening one who is present face to face is more effective than frightening one who is absent, especially after describing Him with oneness and divinity, which entail greatness and complete power to take revenge.

safi-cedvel:53-55.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (ما) a relative, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject) [Note: It was not parsed as a conditional noun so that a verb need not be supplied after it, since the verb of the condition is not omitted except after «إن» in two places: the first in the chapter of preoccupation (ishtighāl), as in the words of the Exalted «وإن أحد من المشركين استجارك فأجره», and the second when «إن» is followed by «لا» and what precedes it indicates the condition, as in the words of the poet:
فطلّقها فلست لها بكفء ... وإلّا يعل مفرقك الحسام
(So divorce her, for you are no match for her; otherwise the sword will come down upon the parting of your hair).]; (الباء) a preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of «ما»; (من نعمة) a preposition and its genitive noun, ḥāl (circumstantial) of the referring pronoun in the ṣila — or a tamyīz (specification) of «ما»; (الفاء) redundant (zāʾida), because «ما» resembles the conditional; (من الله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted khabar (predicate) of «ما»; (ثمّ) a conjunction; (إذا) an adverb of future time containing the meaning of condition, indeclinable, in the position of accusative, attached to the content of the apodosis; (مسّكم) a past verb.. and (كم) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (الضمير) fāʿil (agent), nominative [Translator's note: so in the source; the Quranic word is «الضرّ», as the clause list below shows]; (الفاء) connecting the apodosis; (إلى) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (تجأرون), which is an imperfect verb, nominative.. and (الواو) is the agent.
The clause «ما بكم من نعمة ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «مسّكم الضرّ ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
The clause «تجأرون ...» has no grammatical position: the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition [Note: The coming of the preposition-phrase before it is what called for the fāʾ.. It may also be that the clause is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being «أنتم», and the nominal clause is the apodosis of the non-jussive condition.].
(ثمّ إذا كشف) like «ثمّ إذا مسّكم» [Note: The adverb is attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being «أشرك بعضكم» ("some of you associate partners"), because what comes after the «إذا» of surprise does not govern what precedes it.]; (الضرّ) direct object, accusative; (عنكم) like «بكم», attached to (كشف); (إذا) of surprise (fujāʾiyya); (فريق) mubtadaʾ, nominative [Note: It may be a mubtadaʾ while indefinite because it is qualified.]; (منكم) like «بكم», attached to a naʿt (adjective) of «فريق»; (بربّهم) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يشركون).. and (هم) is muḍāf ilayhi; (يشركون) like «تجأرون».
The clause «كشف ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «فريق منكم.. يشركون» has no grammatical position: the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. And the clause «يشركون» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (فريق).
(اللام) the lām of consequence (lām al-ʿāqiba) [Note: Or the lām of reason (taʿlīl).]; (يكفروا) an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied «أن» after the lām, and the sign of the accusative is the dropping of the nūn.. and (الواو) is the agent; (الباء) a preposition; (ما) a relative in the position of genitive, attached to (يكفروا); (آتيناهم) a past verb and its agent.. and (هم) is the direct object.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يكفروا ...) is in the position of genitive by the lām, attached to (يشركون).
(الفاء) resumptive; (تمتّعوا) an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn ... and (الواو) is the agent; (الفاء) of reason (taʿlīliyya); (سوف) a particle of the future; (تعلمون) like «تجأرون».
The clause «يكفروا ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the implied particle relative (أن).
The clause «آتيناهم ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative (ما).
The clause «تمتّعوا ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «سوف تعلمون» has no grammatical position: giving a reason.

* Rhetoric:
- Shift of person (iltifāt): in the words of the Exalted «فَتَمَتَّعُوا» there is a shift to direct address, to announce the utmost of displeasure.

safi-cedvel:56-59.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (يجعلون) an imperfect verb, nominative.. and (الواو) is the fāʿil (agent); (اللام) a preposition; (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يجعلون) [Note: Or attached to an omitted second mafʿūl bihi (direct object).]; (لا) negating; (يعلمون) like «يجعلون»; (نصيبا) direct object, accusative; (من) a preposition; (ما) like the first, attached to a naʿt (adjective) of (نصيبا); (رزقناهم) a past verb and its agent.. and (هم) is a pronoun, direct object; (تالله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being «أقسم» ("I swear"); (اللام) the lām of the oath; (تسألنّ) an imperfect verb in the passive, nominative, and the sign of the nominative is the retention of the nūn, which has been dropped because of the succession of identical letters, and the wāw — dropped because of the meeting of two quiescents — is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and (النون) is the nūn of emphasis; (عن) a preposition; (ما) a maṣdar-forming particle [Note: Or a relative noun in the position of genitive, and the referring pronoun is omitted, and the clause is the ṣila. — Translator's note: the source writes «العائذ» for «العائد».]; (كنتم) a defective past verb.. and (تم) is the noun (ism) of «كان»; (تفترون) like «يجعلون».
The interpreted maṣdar (ما كنتم تفترون) is in the position of genitive by the preposition, attached to (تسألنّ).
The clause «يجعلون ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «لا يعلمون ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the first relative (ما).
The clause «رزقناهم ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the second relative (ما).
The clause «of the implied oath ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «تسألنّ ...» has no grammatical position: the answer to the oath.
The clause «كنتم تفترون ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the particle relative (ما).
The clause «تفترون ...» is in the position of accusative as the khabar of «كنتم».
(الواو) conjunction; (يجعلون لله البنات) like «يجعلون لما.. نصيبا», and the sign of the accusative of the object is the kasra; (سبحان) a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, and (الهاء) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (الواو) conjunction; (اللام) a preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to the second (يجعلون), so it is conjoined to the preposition-phrase «لله».. [Note: Or a fronted khabar (predicate), and (ما يشتهون) a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject).. and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the agent in (يجعلون).. or resumptive.]; (ما) a relative in the position of accusative, conjoined to «البنات», the objects of «يجعلون» [Note: The meaning is: "and they assign to themselves what they desire", i.e. they choose for themselves what they desire; and the i'rab is the one given in footnote (2) of the previous page.]; (يشتهون) like «يجعلون».
The clause «يجعلون ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the (first) clause «يجعلون».
The clause «(نسبّح) سبحانه» has no grammatical position: parenthetical, of supplication [Note: It is permissible for the clause to be a ḥāl of the Name of Majesty, i.e. "they assign daughters to Allah while He is exalted above their claim" — and this is not permissible according to Ibn Hishām, because the clause is one of supplication, and it is performative (inshāʾ).].
The clause «يشتهون» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative (ما).
(الواو) conjunction; (إذا) an adverb of future time containing the meaning of condition, in the position of accusative, attached to (ظلّ); (بشّر) a past verb in the passive; (أحدهم) nāʾib fāʿil, nominative.. and (هم) is muḍāf ilayhi; (بالأنثى) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (بشّر), and the sign of the genitive is the implied (muqaddar) kasra on the alif; (ظلّ) a past verb — an abrogating (nāsikh) one; (وجهه) the noun of «ظلّ», nominative.. and (الهاء) is muḍāf ilayhi; (مسودّا) the khabar of «ظلّ», accusative; (الواو) the wāw of ḥāl; (هو) a detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ; (كظيم) khabar, nominative.
The clause «بشّر أحدهم ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «ظلّ وجهه مسودّا ...» has no grammatical position: the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «هو كظيم ...» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl.
(يتوارى): an imperfect verb, nominative, and the sign of the nominative is the implied ḍamma on the alif, and the agent is «هو», i.e. «أحدهم»; (من القوم) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يتوارى); (من سوء) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يتوارى) [Note: Two prepositions of the same wording are attached to the same verb because their meanings differ: the first is for the starting point, and the second for reason, i.e. "because of the evil of what he was given tidings of".. It may also be that the first preposition-phrase is a ḥāl of the agent of «يتوارى».]; (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; (بشّر) like the first; (الباء) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (بشّر); (الهمزة) for interrogation; (يمسكه) an imperfect verb, nominative, and (الهاء) is a pronoun, direct object, and the agent is «هو», i.e. «أحدهم»; (على هون) a preposition and its genitive noun, a ḥāl of the object of «يمسكه»; (أم) a conjunction; (يدسّه) like «يمسكه»; (في التراب) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يدسّه); (ألا) a particle of alerting; (ساء) a past verb for expressing blame, and the agent is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being «هو»; (ما) a qualified indefinite noun in the position of accusative as a tamyīz (specification) of the agent pronoun [Note: Or it is a maṣdar-forming particle, and the interpreted maṣdar is the agent of «ساء».]; (يحكمون) like «يجعلون».
The clause «يتوارى ...» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl of the pronoun in «كظيم» [Note: Or it is a second khabar of the mubtadaʾ «هو», in the position of nominative.. or it is an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).].
The clause «بشّر ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative (ما).
The clause «يمسكه ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption [Note: Or it is the speech reported by an implied verb of saying, which is a ḥāl of the agent of «يتوارى», i.e. "saying to himself: shall he keep it ..."].
The clause «يدسّه ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause «يمسكه».
The clause «ساء ما يحكمون» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يحكمون» is in the position of accusative as a naʿt of (ما).

* Morphology:
(مسودّا): an active participle — or a passive participle — of the five-letter verb «اسودّ»; its pattern is مفعلّ, with ḍamma on the mīm, shadda on the lām and fatḥa on the ʿayn; and the apparent view is that it is an active participle, because the passive participle needs a preposition.

* Benefits:
The tāʾ:
The tāʾ is of six kinds, namely:
a- «تا», a demonstrative for the feminine singular, indeclinable on the sukūn.
b- The "tāʾ of the feminine", which comes on the verb quiescent and vowelled, while on the noun it is only vowelled; and since it is for distinguishing between masculine and feminine, it does not enter adjectives specific to women, such as: «حامل» (pregnant), «حائض» (menstruating), «عانس» (spinster), «مرضع» (nursing).. etc.
c- The tāʾ of the broken plural of foreign words, such as: «صولج» and «صوالجة», «طيلسان» and «طيالسة», «صيرف» and «صيارفة».
d- The tāʾ of distinction, to distinguish the single unit from its genus, such as: «تمر» and «تمرة».
e- The tāʾ of compensation: it is the one that attaches to a noun whose first radical has been dropped, such as «زنة», whose origin is «وزن».
And the tāʾ of the oath, as it is in the verse before us. Sībawayh says: the Arabs do not use the tāʾ of the oath with anything other than "the Name of Majesty". So one does not say «تربّ الكعبة».

safi-cedvel:60-62.t:
* I'rab:
(اللام) a preposition; (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) a fronted khabar (predicate); (لا) negating; (يؤمنون) an imperfect verb, nominative.. and (الواو) is the fāʿil (agent); (بالآخرة) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يؤمنون); (مثل) a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative; (السوء) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive; (الواو) conjunction; (لله المثل) like «للذين مثل»; (الأعلى) a naʿt (adjective) of «المثل», nominative, and the sign of the nominative is the implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the alif; (الواو) conjunction; (هو) a detached pronoun, mubtadaʾ; (العزيز) khabar, nominative; (الحكيم) a second khabar, nominative.
The clause «للذين ... مثل السوء» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «لا يؤمنون» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «لله المثل ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «هو العزيز ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause «لله المثل ...».
(الواو) conjunction; (لو) a non-jussive conditional particle; (يؤاخذ) an imperfect verb, nominative; (الله) the Name of Majesty, agent, nominative; (الناس) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative; (بظلمهم) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يؤاخذ), and (الباء) is causal.. and (هم) is muḍāf ilayhi; (ما) negating; (ترك) a past verb, and the agent is «هو»; (على) a preposition and (ها) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (ترك); (من) a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; (دابّة) genitive in form, accusative in position, direct object; (الواو) conjunction; (لكن) a particle of rectification (istidrāk); (يؤخّرهم) like «يؤاخذ»..
and (هم) is a pronoun, direct object; (إلى أجل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يؤخّرهم); (مسمّى) a naʿt of «أجل», genitive, and the sign of the genitive is the implied kasra on the alif; (الفاء) conjunction; (إذ) an adverb of the future containing the meaning of condition, in the position of accusative, attached to (لا يستأخرون) [Translator's note: so in the source; the Quranic word is «إذا» («فإذا جاء أجلهم»), as the clause list below shows]; (جاء) a past verb; (أجلهم) agent, nominative, and (هم) is muḍāf ilayhi; (لا) negating; (يستأخرون) an imperfect verb, nominative.. and (الواو) is the agent; (الواو) conjunction; (لا يستقدمون) like «لا يستأخرون».
The clause «يؤاخذ الله ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «ما ترك ...» has no grammatical position: the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «يؤخّرهم ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause «يؤاخذ الله..».
The clause «جاء أجلهم ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «لا يستأخرون ...» has no grammatical position: the apodosis of the non-jussive condition (إذا).
The clause «لا يستقدمون» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause «لا يستأخرون».
(الواو) conjunction; (يجعلون لله ما) like «يجعلون لله البنات» [Note: In verse (57) of this sūra.]; (يكرهون) like «يستأخرون»; (الواو) conjunction; (تصف) like «يؤاخذ»; (ألسنتهم) agent, nominative..
and (هم) is muḍāf ilayhi; (الكذب) direct object, accusative; (أنّ) a particle resembling the verb; (اللام) a preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to a fronted khabar; (الحسنى) the delayed noun (ism) of «أنّ», accusative, and the sign of the accusative is the implied fatḥa on the alif.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّ لهم الحسنى) is in the position of accusative as a badal (substitute) of «الكذب» [Note: Or in the position of genitive by an omitted preposition, i.e. «بأنّ لهم الحسنى», and the preposition is attached to «الكذب».].
(لا) of generic negation; (جرم) the noun of «لا», indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of accusative [Note: See the cases of the i'rab of «لا جرم» in verses (22) of Sūrat Hūd and (23) of this sūra.]; (أنّ لهم النار) like «أنّ لهم الحسنى».
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّ لهم النار) is in the position of genitive by an omitted preposition, its implied form being «في أنّ لهم..», attached to the khabar of «لا».
(الواو) conjunction; (أنّ) like the first, and (هم) is a pronoun in the position of accusative as the noun of «أنّ»; (مفرطون) the khabar of «أنّ», nominative, and the sign of the nominative is the wāw.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنهم مفرطون) is in the position of genitive, conjoined to the interpreted maṣdar (أنّ لهم النار).
The clause «يجعلون ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause «يؤاخذ الله».
The clause «يكرهون ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative (ما).
The clause «تصف ألسنتهم ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause «يجعلون».
The clause «لا جرم أنّ ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.

* Morphology:
(مفرطون): passive participle from «أفرط فلانا», i.e. "he left him"; its pattern is مفعلون, with ḍamma on the mīm and fatḥa on the ʿayn.

* Benefits:
- One of the grammarians said: the conjunctive fāʾ is for sequence and immediate succession; so if you say «جاء علي فسعيد» ("ʿAlī came, then Saʿīd"), the meaning is that ʿAlī came first and Saʿīd came after him, with no interval between their coming.
Some grammarians objected to this stipulation and said: immediate succession is not stipulated for it; rather it is for succession in the light of rational or customary convention. He gave an example of that, saying: for this reason it is correct to say «دخلت البصرة فبغداد» ("I entered Basra, then Baghdad"), even if there is a long time between entering the two. But it is understood from the speech that he passed through the stages after Basra and did not stay in any of them a stay that would take him out of the bounds of travel until he entered Baghdad.
Thus it becomes clear to us that the fāʾ is not for real immediacy. Similar to it are the words of the Exalted: «فإذا جاء أجلهم», for the coming of the term is delayed beyond immediate succession; so reflect ... !

safi-cedvel:63-64.t:
* I'rab:
(تالله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb, its implied form being «أقسم» ("I swear"); (اللام) the lām of the oath; (قد) a particle of realization (taḥqīq); (أرسلنا) a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); (إلى أمم) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أرسلنا); (من قبلك) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a naʿt (adjective) of «أمم»..
and (الكاف) is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (الفاء) conjunction; (زيّن) a past verb; (اللام) a preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (زيّن); (الشيطان) agent, nominative; (أعمالهم) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative.. and (هم) is muḍāf ilayhi; (الفاء) conjunction; (هو) a detached pronoun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); (وليّهم) khabar (predicate), nominative.. and (هم) is like the last; (اليوم) an adverb of time, accusative, attached to «وليّ» [Note: In past or present time.. And if the adverb (اليوم) indicates the future, i.e. the Day of Resurrection, then it is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in «وليّهم», i.e. "being punished today".]; (الواو) conjunction; (اللام) a preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to a fronted khabar; (عذاب) a delayed mubtadaʾ, nominative; (أليم) a naʿt of «عذاب», nominative.
The clause «of the oath ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «أرسلنا ...» has no grammatical position: the answer to the oath.
The clause «زيّن لهم الشيطان» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause of the answer to the oath.
The clause «هو وليّهم ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause «زيّن.. الشيطان».
The clause «لهم عذاب ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause «هو وليّهم».
