(أن): a particle of explanation, because بعثنا is in the sense of "We said".. [Note: It is permissible for (أن) to be a maṣdar particle, with the interpreted maṣdar in the position of the genitive by an omitted preposition, i.e. "with: worship..", and the preposition and its noun are attached to (بعثنا).]. (اعبدوا): an imperative verb, indeclinable on the omission of the nūn ... and (الواو) is the agent. (الله): the word of majesty, direct object, accusative. (الواو): conjunctive. (اجتنبوا الطاغوت): like اعبدوا الله. (الفاء): conjunctive, expressing ramification. (من): a preposition, and (هم) is a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to a preposed khabar. (من): a relative noun, indeclinable in the position of the nominative, postposed mubtadaʾ [Note: or it is an indefinite noun in the position of the nominative, mubtadaʾ.]. (هدى): a past verb, indeclinable on an implied fatḥa. (الله): the word of majesty, agent, nominative. (الواو): conjunctive. (منهم من حقّت.. الضلالة): "منهم من هدى الله", and (التاء) is for the feminine. (على): a preposition, and (الهاء) is a pronoun in the position of ..., attached to (حقّت) [Translator's note: the source text is incomplete here, giving "في محلّ" without "جرّ"; translated as written.]. (الفاء): linking the apodosis of an implied condition. (سيروا): like اعبدوا. (في الأرض): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (سيروا) [Note: or attached to a ḥāl from the agent of سيروا, i.e. "reflecting or taking heed in the earth".]. (الفاء): conjunctive. (انظروا): like اعبدوا. (كيف): an interrogative noun, indeclinable in the position of the accusative, the khabar of the defective verb كان. (عاقبة): the noun of كان, nominative. (المكذّبين): muḍāf ilayhi, genitive ...
The clause «بعثنا..» has no grammatical position; it is the answer to an implied oath.. and the clause of the implied oath has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «اعبدوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is explicative.
And the clause «اجتنبوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the explicative.
And the clause «منهم من هدى الله ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to an implied resumption, i.e. "so they were of divisions, and some of them are those whom..".
And the clause «هدى الله» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the first relative noun (من) [Note: or it is in the position of the nominative, naʿt of the qualified indefinite (من).].
And the clause «منهم من حقّت ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause منهم من هدى الله.
And the clause «حقّت عليه الضلالة..» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the second relative noun (من).
And the clause «سيروا ... » is in the position of the jussive, the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if you want proof and certainty, then travel".
And the clause «انظروا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause سيروا.
And the clause «كان عاقبة ... » is in the position of the accusative, direct object of the verb of looking, which is suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative.

safi-cedvel:37-37.t:
* I'rab:
(إن): a jussive conditional particle. (تحرص): a jussive imperfect verb, the protasis; the agent is "you". (على هداهم): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (تحرص), its genitive marker being the kasra implied on the alif.. and (هم) is a muḍāf ilayhi. (الفاء): causal. (إنّ): a particle resembling the verb. (الله): the word of majesty, the noun of inna, accusative. (لا): negative. (يهدي): an imperfect verb, nominative, its nominative marker being the ḍamma implied on the yāʾ.. and the agent is a latent pronoun (huwa). (من): a relative noun, indeclinable in the position of the accusative, direct object; the returning pronoun is omitted, i.e. "يضلّه". (يضلّ): an imperfect verb, nominative; the agent is "He", i.e. Allah. (الواو): conjunctive. (ما): negative. (اللام): a preposition. (هم): a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to a preposed khabar. (من): a redundant preposition. (ناصرين): genitive in form, nominative in position, postposed mubtadaʾ.
The clause «تحرص ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «إنّ الله لا يهدي ... » has no grammatical position; it is the reason for the implied apodosis, i.e. "if you are eager for their guidance, you will not be able to, because Allah does not guide...".
And the clause «لا يهدي ... » is in the position of the nominative, khabar of inna.
And the clause «يضلّ ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (من).
And the clause «ما لهم من ناصرين» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the causal clause.

safi-cedvel:38-39.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو): resumptive [Note: or conjunctive, with the clause after it — أقسموا — conjoined to the clause: قال الذين أشركوا — verse (35) — and what lies between the conjoined and that to which it is conjoined is of the kind of parenthesis.]. (أقسموا): a past verb and its agent. (بالله): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (أقسموا). (جهد): an absolute object (mafʿūl muṭlaq) substituting for the maṣdar, specifying its kind. (أيمانهم): muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, and (هم) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (لا): negative. (يبعث): an imperfect verb, nominative. (الله): agent, nominative. (من): a relative noun, indeclinable in the position of the accusative, direct object. (يموت): like يبعث, and the agent is a latent pronoun (huwa), which is the returning pronoun. (بلى): a particle of response affirming what was negated, i.e. "Yes, He will resurrect them". (وعدا): an absolute object of an omitted verb, i.e. "He promised that a promise". (على): a preposition, and (الهاء) is a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (وعدا). (حقّا): an absolute object of an omitted verb, i.e. "it is true, truly" [Note: It is permissible for the maṣdar to be a naʿt of (وعدا), accusative like it.]. (الواو): conjunctive. (لكنّ): a particle of correction and accusative. (أكثر): the noun of lākinna, accusative. (الناس): muḍāf ilayhi, genitive. (لا): negative. (يعلمون): an imperfect verb, nominative, its nominative marker being the retention of the nūn.. and (الواو) is the agent.
The clause «أقسموا ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «لا يبعث الله..» has no grammatical position; it is the answer to the oath.
And the clause «يموت ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (من).
And the clause «لكنّ أكثر الناس ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the implied clause يبعثهم.
And the clause «لا يعلمون» is in the position of the nominative, khabar of lākinna.. And the clause (وعد) وعدا and the clause substituting for it, حقّ حقّا.. are of the kind of parenthesis, with no grammatical position.
(اللام): for causation. (يبيّن): an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām; the agent is "He", i.e. Allah. (اللام): a preposition, and (هم) is a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (يبيّن). (الّذي): a relative noun, indeclinable in the position of the accusative, direct object. (يختلفون): an imperfect verb like يعلمون. (في): a preposition, and (الهاء) is a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (يختلفون).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يبيّن) is in the position of the genitive by the lām, attached to the implied verb يبعثهم.
(الواو): conjunctive. (ليعلم): like ليبيّن. (الذين): a relative noun, agent. (كفروا): like أقسموا. (أنّهم): a particle of emphasis and accusative.. and (هم) is a pronoun in the position of the noun of anna. (كانوا): a defective past verb, a naskh verb.. and (الواو) is the noun of kāna. (كاذبين): the khabar of كانوا, accusative, its accusative marker being the yāʾ.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يعلم..) is in the position of the genitive by the lām, attached to the implied verb يبعثهم, so it is conjoined to the first interpreted maṣdar.
And the interpreted maṣdar (أنّهم كانوا ... ) is in the position of the accusative, standing in place of the two objects of يعلم.
And the clause «يبيّن ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the implied particle-relative (أن).
And the clause «يختلفون ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الّذي).
And the clause «يعلم الذين ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the implied particle-relative (أن).
And the clause «كفروا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الّذين).
And the clause «كانوا ... » is in the position of the nominative, khabar of anna.

safi-cedvel:40-40.t:
* I'rab:
(إنّما): kāffa and makfūfa (a restraining particle and what is restrained). (قولنا): mubtadaʾ, nominative.. and (نا) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (لشيء): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to قولنا. (إذا): an adverb of future time, stripped of conditionality, attached to (قولنا). (أردناه): a past verb and its agent, and (الهاء) is the direct object. (أن): a maṣdar particle and accusative. (نقول): an imperfect verb, accusative; the agent is "we". (اللام): a preposition, and (الهاء) is a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (نقول). (كن): a complete imperative verb; the agent is "you". (الفاء): resumptive. (يكون): a complete imperfect verb, nominative; the agent is a latent pronoun (huwa).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن نقول) is in the position of the nominative, khabar of the mubtadaʾ قولنا..
The clause «قولنا.. أن نقول» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «أردناه ... » is in the position of the genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause «نقول ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle-relative (أن).
And the clause «كن ... » is in the position of the accusative, the quoted speech.
And the clause «يكون» is in the position of the nominative, the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "هو", i.e. "so it comes to be", and the clause is resumptive [Note: or the clause يكون.. is originally resumptive, contrary to Ibn Hishām; and see verse (117) of sūrat al-Baqara, verse (47) of sūrat Āl ʿImrān, and verse (73) of sūrat al-Anʿām.].

* Rhetoric:
- Representational metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-tamthīliyya): in His saying, Exalted is He, كُنْ فَيَكُونُ — it is a representation of the ease with which things within His power come about according to the attachment of His will to them, and a depiction of the speed of their coming into being by what is known from that of the obedience of the obedient one commanded to the order of the obeyed one who commands. So the meaning is: our bringing something into existence, when our will attaches to it, is only that we bring it into being in the fastest manner possible. In the verse there is a majesty and eloquence at which minds and intellects are bewildered.

* Benefits:
- «Innamā»:
Imām ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī holds that stopping, regarding «innamā», at the grammarians' statement that there is no benefit in the joining of «mā» to «inna» other than that it nullifies its operation, is a clear error, since the basis of «innamā» is that it comes for a report which the addressee is not ignorant of and does not deny the soundness of, as in His saying, Exalted is He, «إنما يستجيب الذين يسمعون», and from it is the verse of Ibn Qays al-Ruqayyāt:
انما مصعب شهاب من الله ... تجلّت بوجهه الظلماء
(Muṣʿab is but a flame from Allah; by his face the darkness was cleared.)
It likewise gives, for the speech that follows it, the affirmation of the action for one thing and its negation from another. So if you say: innamā jāʾanī Khālid ("Only Khālid came to me"), it is as though you said: Khālid came to me and not Saʿīd.
So you perceive with it the affirmation of the action for one party and its negation from another party, all at once.
So verify this; you have been guided to the right.

safi-cedvel:97-97.t:
* I'rab:
(من): a jussive conditional noun, indeclinable in the position of the nominative, mubtadaʾ. (عمل): a past verb; the agent is a latent pronoun (huwa) referring to the conditional noun. (صالحا): direct object, accusative. (من ذكر): a preposition and its genitive noun, ḥāl from the agent of عمل [Note: or tamyīz (specification) of the relative noun (من).]. (أو): a conjunction. (أنثى): conjoined to ذكر, genitive, its genitive marker being the kasra implied on the alif. (الواو): the wāw of ḥāl. (هو): a detached pronoun, mubtadaʾ. (مؤمن): khabar, nominative. (الفاء): linking the apodosis of the condition. (اللام): the lām of an oath, for an implied oath. (نحيينّه): an imperfect verb like نجزينّ «1», and (الهاء) is the direct object. (حياة): absolute object, accusative. (طيّبة): naʿt of حياة, accusative. (الواو): conjunctive. (لنجزينّهم أجرهم.. يعملون): like the preceding verse «2».
The clause «من عمل ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «عمل صالحا ... » is in the position of the nominative, khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) [Note: It is permissible for the khabar to be the two clauses of the protasis and the apodosis together.].
And the clause «هو مؤمن ... » is in the position of the accusative, ḥāl.
And the clause «نحيينّه ... » has no grammatical position; it is the answer to the implied oath.. and the clause of the oath and its answer are the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "نحن".. and the nominal clause is in the position of the jussive, the apodosis of the condition.
And the clause «نجزينّهم ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause of the answer to the oath.
And the clause «كانوا يعملون» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the nominal or particle-relative (ما).
And the clause «يعملون» is in the position of the accusative, khabar of كانوا.

* Rhetoric:
- Completion (tatmīm): in His saying, Exalted is He, مَنْ عَمِلَ صالِحاً مِنْ ذَكَرٍ أَوْ أُنْثى وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌ to the end of the verse.
The tatmīm is repeated here twice. The first: in His saying, Exalted is He, مِنْ ذَكَرٍ وَأُنْثى, because the conditional or relative من gives generality, so it had to be completed with that, for emphasis and to remove the notion of restriction, in keeping with the ancient beliefs of the Arabs in preferring the male over the female and favouring him with everything that is good.
The second: in His saying وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌ. Opinions differ about this tatmīm and about what is meant by the good life which one in this condition attains. The best of what we choose of them is the statement of al-Zamakhsharī in his book al-Kashshāf, and we quote it verbatim for its benefit, for he said, and excelled: "That is because the believer, together with righteous action, lives a good life, whether well-off or in straitened circumstances. If he is well-off, there is nothing to say about him; and if he is in straitened circumstances, he has with him what makes his life good, namely contentment and satisfaction with Allah's apportioning. As for the wicked, his case is the reverse: if he is in straitened circumstances, there is no difficulty in his case."

safi-cedvel:98-100.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء): resumptive. (إذا): an adverb of future time containing the sense of a condition, in the position of the accusative, attached to the content of the apodosis. (قرأت): a past verb and its agent. (القرآن): direct object, accusative. (الفاء): linking the apodosis of the condition. (استعذ): an imperative verb; the agent is "you". (بالله): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (استعذ). (من الشيطان): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (استعذ). (الرّجيم): naʿt of الشيطان, genitive.
The clause «قرأت ... » is in the position of the genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause «استعذ ... » has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
(إنّ): a particle of emphasis and accusative, and (الهاء) is a pronoun in the position of the accusative, the noun of inna. (ليس): an inert defective past verb. (اللام): a preposition, and (الهاء) is a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to the khabar of ليس. (سلطان): the postposed noun of ليس, nominative. (على): a preposition. (الّذين): a relative noun, indeclinable in the position of the genitive, attached to (سلطان), which is in the sense of domination. (آمنوا): a past verb and its agent. (الواو): conjunctive. (على ربّهم): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يتوكّلون), and (هم) is a muḍāf ilayhi. (يتوكّلون): an imperfect verb, nominative.. and (الواو) is the agent.
And the clause «إنّه ليس له سلطان ... » has no grammatical position; it is the reason for an omitted element, namely the answer to the command, i.e. "seek refuge with Allah from Satan and you will be spared his evil".
And the clause «ليس له سلطان» is in the position of the nominative, khabar of inna.
And the clause «آمنوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الّذين).
And the clause «يتوكّلون» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the ṣila clause.
(إنّما): kāffa and makfūfa. (سلطانه): mubtadaʾ, nominative.. and (الهاء) is a muḍāf ilayhi. (على الذين): like the first, attached to the khabar of the mubtadaʾ. (يتولّونه): like يتوكّلون.. and (الهاء) is a pronoun, direct object. (الواو): conjunctive. (الّذين): in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the preceding relative noun. (هم): a detached pronoun, indeclinable in the position of the nominative, mubtadaʾ. (الباء): a preposition, and (الهاء) is in the position of the genitive, attached to (مشركون), which is the khabar, nominative, its nominative marker being the wāw.
And the clause «سلطانه على الذين ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.
And the clause «يتولّونه....» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الّذين).
And the clause «هم به مشركون» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the second relative noun (الّذين).

* Morphology:
(سلطان): the word is used here in the sense of domination, so it is a maṣdar. Its wazn is فعلان (ḍamma on the fāʾ).

safi-cedvel:101-101.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو): conjunctive. (إذا بدّلنا آية): like إذا قرأت القرآن [Note: in verse (98) of this sūra.]. (مكان): second direct object, accusative. (آية): muḍāf ilayhi, genitive. (الواو): parenthetical — or circumstantial. (الله): the word of majesty, mubtadaʾ, nominative. (أعلم): khabar, nominative. (الباء): a preposition. (ما): a relative noun, indeclinable in the position of the genitive, attached to (أعلم). (ينزّل): an imperfect verb, nominative; the agent is a latent pronoun (huwa). (قالوا): a past verb and its agent. (إنّما): kāffa and makfūfa. (أنت): a detached pronoun, indeclinable in the position of the nominative, mubtadaʾ. (مفتر): khabar, nominative, its nominative marker being the ḍamma implied on the omitted yāʾ, for it is a defective noun (ism manqūṣ). (بل): for transitional exit (iḍrāb intiqālī). (أكثرهم): mubtadaʾ, nominative.. and (هم) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (لا): negative. (يعلمون): an imperfect verb, nominative.. and (الواو) is the agent.
The clause «بدّلنا ... » is in the position of the genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause «الله أعلم ... » has no grammatical position; it is parenthetical.
And the clause «ينزّل ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
And the clause «قالوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
And the clause «أنت مفتر» is in the position of the accusative, the quoted speech.
And the clause «أكثرهم لا يعلمون» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «لا يعلمون» is in the position of the nominative, khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أكثرهم).

safi-cedvel:102-102.t:
* I'rab:
(قل): an imperative verb; the agent is "you". (نزّله): a past verb, and (الهاء) is a pronoun, direct object. (روح): agent, nominative. (القدس): muḍāf ilayhi, genitive. (من ربّك): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (نزّل), and (الكاف) is a muḍāf ilayhi. (بالحقّ): a preposition and its genitive noun, ḥāl from the agent or from the genitive second-person pronoun. (اللام): for causation. (يثبّت): an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām; the agent is a latent pronoun (huwa). (الّذين): a relative noun, indeclinable in the position of the accusative, direct object. (آمنوا): a past verb and its agent.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يثبّت..) is in the position of the genitive by the lām, attached to (نزّله).
(الواو): conjunctive — or circumstantial. (هدى): conjoined to the interpreted maṣdar, genitive, its genitive marker being the kasra implied on the alif [Note: or it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "هو", and the nominal clause is in the position of the accusative.]. (الواو): conjunctive. (بشرى): conjoined to هدى, genitive like it. (للمسلمين): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (بشرى).
The clause «قل ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «نزّله روح ... » is in the position of the accusative, the quoted speech.
And the clause «يثبّت ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the implied particle-relative (أن).
And the clause «آمنوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).

* Benefits:
1- Returning to the hamza: we elaborated in our earlier discussion on the hamza and the rules of its writing, and since the Qur'anic orthography differs from those rules, here is the hamza of «ءامنوا», written on the line. Likewise the hamza of «ءاية», as you see, contrary to the rules we laid down for writing it. We repeat here what we said earlier, that the Qur'anic orthography is not relied upon in the orthography of ordinary writing.
2- Bal: a conjunction. If it occurs after affirmative speech, it is for iḍrāb, turning away from one thing to another, as in the verse before us.
If it occurs after a negation or a prohibition, it is for istidrāk (correction), in the position of lākin, as in: "Saʿīd did not stand, but Khalīl."
It may also be a particle of inception, if a clause follows it, as in His saying, Exalted is He: وَقالُوا اتَّخَذَ الرَّحْمنُ وَلَداً سُبْحانَهُ بَلْ عِبادٌ مُكْرَمُونَ, i.e. "rather, they are honoured servants".
Abrogating and abrogated rulings in the Sharia:
The hypocrites, the weak in belief, and those in whose hearts faith had not taken hold took the abrogation of rulings as a pretext for attacking the religion and accusing the Messenger ﷺ of fabrication. Some of them would apostatise because of that.
But the intelligent and discerning person knows that the gradual introduction of rulings is a matter of wisdom, especially when the rulings of the Sharia relate to the abrogation of a deep-rooted custom or an entrenched belief, such as the drinking of wine and the change of the qibla.
Abrogation may also have some connection with the development that accompanied the stages of the conveying of the message, which led the mujtahid imams, afterwards, to lay down their principle that states:
"The change of rulings with the change of time and place is not denied."
And this is what we see as requiring the changing of man-made laws from time to time, in response to development and in keeping with the state's social, economic and intellectual condition, etc.

safi-cedvel:103-103.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو): resumptive. (اللام): the lām of an oath, for an implied oath. (قد): a particle of verification [Note: because Allah's knowledge is verified, constant and continuous.]. (نعلم): an imperfect verb, nominative; the agent is "we", for exaltation. (أنّهم): a particle of emphasis and accusative.. and (هم) is in the position of the accusative, the noun of anna. (يقولون): an imperfect verb, nominative..
and (الواو) is the agent.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّهم يقولون..) is in the position of the accusative, standing in place of the two objects of نعلم.
(إنّما): kāffa and makfūfa. (يعلّمه): an imperfect verb, nominative.. and (الهاء) is a pronoun, direct object. (بشر): agent, nominative. (لسان): mubtadaʾ, nominative. (الّذي): a relative noun in the position of the genitive, muḍāf ilayhi. (يلحدون): like يقولون. (إلى): a preposition, and (الهاء) is a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (يلحدون). (أعجميّ): khabar, nominative. (الواو): conjunctive [Note: or circumstantial, with the clause after it as a ḥāl.]. (ها): a particle of alerting. (ذا): a demonstrative, indeclinable in the position of the nominative, mubtadaʾ, the reference being to the Qur'an. (لسان): khabar, nominative. (عربيّ): naʿt of لسان, nominative [Note: or a second khabar, nominative.]. (مبين): a second naʿt, nominative.
The clause «نعلم..» has no grammatical position; it is the answer to the implied oath.
And the clause «يقولون ... » is in the position of the nominative, khabar of anna.
And the clause «إنّما يعلّمه بشر ... » is in the position of the accusative, the quoted speech.
And the clause «لسان الذي ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive [Note: This is the opinion of al-Zamakhsharī; Abū Ḥayyān chose that it be in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, which in his view is more forceful in rebuking them, and the pronoun in (يلحدون) is the link that ties it to the owner of the ḥāl, which is the agent of يقولون.].
And the clause «يلحدون ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذي).
And the clause «هذا لسان ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause لسان الذي ...

* Rhetoric:
- Metaphor (istiʿāra): in His saying, Exalted is He, لِسانُ الَّذِي يُلْحِدُونَ إِلَيْهِ أَعْجَمِيٌّ.
Ilḥād is inclining, from alḥada al-qabr, when one makes the digging of the grave incline away from straightness, digging in a side of it; then it was borrowed for every inclining away from straightness, so they said: "So-and-so deviated (alḥada) in his speech" and "deviated in his religion".
What is meant: that is, the language of the man towards whom they incline the speech, away from straightness, is foreign and not clear.

safi-cedvel:104-104.t:
* I'rab:
(إنّ): a particle of emphasis and accusative. (الذين): a relative noun in the position of the accusative, the noun of inna. (لا): negative. (يؤمنون): an imperfect verb, nominative. and (الواو) is the agent. (بآيات): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يؤمنون). (الله): the word of majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive. (لا): negative. (يهديهم): an imperfect verb, nominative, its nominative marker being the ḍamma implied on the yāʾ..
and (هم) is a pronoun, direct object. (الله): the word of majesty, agent, nominative. (الواو): conjunctive. (اللام): a preposition, and (هم) is a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to a preposed khabar. (عذاب): postposed mubtadaʾ, nominative. (أليم): naʿt of عذاب, nominative.
The clause «إنّ الذين ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «لا يؤمنون ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
And the clause «لا يهديهم الله ... » is in the position of the nominative, khabar of inna.
And the clause «لهم عذاب ... » is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the khabar clause.

safi-cedvel:105-105.t:
* I'rab:
(إنّما يفتري الكذب الّذين): like إنّما يعلّمه بشر [Note: in verse (103) of this sūra.]; the object is preposed and the agent postposed. (لا يؤمنون بآيات الله): their i'rab has been given before [Note: in the preceding verse (104).]. (الواو): conjunctive. (أولئك): a demonstrative, indeclinable in the position of the nominative, mubtadaʾ.. and (الكاف) is a particle of address. (هم): a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) [Note: or a detached pronoun, mubtadaʾ whose khabar is (الكاذبون), and the nominal clause is the khabar of the demonstrative.]. (الكاذبون): the khabar of the mubtadaʾ أولئك.., nominative, its nominative marker being the wāw..
The clause «يفتري.. الذين..» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «لا يؤمنون ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الّذين).
And the clause «أولئك ... الكاذبون» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the resumptive.

safi-cedvel:106-110.t:
* I'rab:
(من): a jussive conditional noun, indeclinable in the position of the nominative, mubtadaʾ. (كفر): a past verb; the agent is a latent pronoun (huwa) referring to من. (بالله): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (كفر). (من بعد): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (كفر). (إيمانه): muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, and (الهاء) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (إلّا): a particle of exception. (من): a relative noun, indeclinable in the position of the accusative as a discontinuous exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ). (أكره): a passive past verb, and the nāʾib fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "هو". (الواو): circumstantial (ḥāliyya). (قلبه): mubtadaʾ, nominative.. and (الهاء) is a muḍāf ilayhi. (مطمئنّ): khabar, nominative. (بالإيمان): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (مطمئنّ). (الواو): conjunctive. (لكن): a particle of correction. (من): a relative noun [Note: It is also permissible for it to be a conditional noun, on the basis that a mubtadaʾ is implied, because a condition does not occur after istidrāk, i.e.:
"but (they are) those who opened (their breast)", and the apodosis of the condition is His saying: فعليهم غضب من الله.] indeclinable in the position of the nominative, mubtadaʾ. (شرح): a past verb; the agent is a latent pronoun (huwa). (بالكفر): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (شرح), which is given the sense of "became content". (صدرا): tamyīz, accusative. (الفاء): redundant [Note: or it links the apodosis of the condition if (من) is parsed as a conditional noun.]. (على): a preposition, and (هم) is a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to a preposed khabar. (غضب): postposed mubtadaʾ, nominative. (من الله): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an adjective of (غضب). (الواو): conjunctive. (اللام): a preposition, and (هم) is a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to a preposed khabar. (عذاب عظيم): like عذاب أليم [Note: in verse (104) of this sūra.].
The clause «من كفر ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «كفر ... » is in the position of the nominative, khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) [Note: It is permissible for the khabar to be the two clauses of the protasis and apodosis together.].. and the apodosis of the condition is omitted, its implied form being "then he is to be held to account.." or "then for them is a severe punishment".
And the clause «أكره ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (من).
And the clause «قلبه مطمئنّ ... » is in the position of the accusative, ḥāl.
And the clause «من شرح.. عليهم غضب» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the resumptive.
And the clause «شرح ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the second relative noun (من).
And the clause «عليهم غضب ... » is in the position of the nominative, khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) [Note: The clause is accompanied by the fāʾ because the mubtadaʾ resembles a condition..].
And the clause «لهم عذاب ... » is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the last khabar clause.
(ذلك): a demonstrative, indeclinable in the position of the nominative, mubtadaʾ, the reference being to the threat, (اللام) denotes distance and (الكاف) is for address. (الباء): a preposition. (أنّهم): a particle resembling the verb..
and (هم) is a pronoun in the position of the accusative, the noun of anna. (استحبّوا): a past verb and its agent. (الحياة): direct object, accusative. (الدنيا): naʿt of (حياة), accusative, its accusative marker being the fatḥa implied on the alif. (على الآخرة): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (استحبّوا), which is given the sense of "preferred".
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّهم استحبّوا ... ) is in the position of the genitive by the bāʾ, attached to an omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ ذلك.
(الواو): conjunctive. (أنّ الله لا يهدي): like أنّهم استحبّوا. (القوم): direct object, accusative. (الكافرين): naʿt of القوم, accusative.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّ الله لا يهدي..) is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the first interpreted maṣdar.
And the clause «ذلك بأنّهم ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.
And the clause «استحبّوا ... » is in the position of the nominative, khabar of anna (the first).
And the clause «لا يهدي ... » is in the position of the nominative, khabar of anna (the second).
(أولئك): a demonstrative, indeclinable in the position of the nominative, mubtadaʾ.. and (الكاف) is for address. (الّذين): a relative noun in the position of the nominative, khabar. (طبع): a past verb. (الله): the word of majesty, agent, nominative. (على قلوبهم): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (طبع), and (هم) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (الواو): conjunctive in the three places. (سمعهم، أبصارهم): like قلوبهم and conjoined to it by the two conjunctions. (أولئك): like the first. (هم): a separating pronoun [Note: or a detached pronoun, mubtadaʾ whose khabar is (الغافلون), and the clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ أولئك.]. (الغافلون): the khabar of the mubtadaʾ أولئك.
And the clause «أولئك الّذين ... » is in the position of the accusative, ḥāl from القوم [Note: or it has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.].
And the clause «طبع الله ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
And the clause «أولئك ... الغافلون» is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the clause أولئك الذين طبع..
(لا جرم): a negative of generic negation, and its noun is indeclinable on the fatḥa in the position of the accusative [Note: See the states of the i'rab of (لا جرم) in verse (22) of sūrat Hūd and (23, 62) of this sūra.]. (أنّهم): like the first. (في الآخرة): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (الخاسرون). (هم): a detached pronoun, indeclinable in the position of the nominative, mubtadaʾ [Note: or it is a pronoun borrowed for the position of the accusative, tawkīd of the pronoun that is the noun of anna.]. (الخاسرون): khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هم), nominative, its nominative marker being the wāw.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّهم.. هم الخاسرون) is in the position of the genitive by an omitted preposition, its implied form being "في", i.e. "no doubt in that they.. are the losers", so the preposition and its noun are attached to the khabar of lā.
And the clause «لا جرم (في) أنّهم ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.
And the clause «هم الخاسرون» is in the position of the nominative, khabar of anna.
(ثمّ): a conjunction. (إنّ): a particle of emphasis and accusative. (ربّك): the noun of inna, accusative.. and (الكاف) is a muḍāf ilayhi. (اللام): a preposition. (الّذين): a relative noun in the position of the genitive, attached to the khabar of inna, i.e. "He is a supporter of them". (هاجروا): a past verb and its agent. (من بعد): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (هاجروا). (ما): a maṣdar particle. (فتنوا): a passive past verb.. and (الواو) is the nāʾib fāʿil. (ثمّ): like the first. (جاهدوا): like هاجروا, and likewise (صبروا). (إنّ ربّك من بعدها): like the first.. and (ها) is a muḍāf ilayhi. (اللام): the shifted lām, for emphasis. (غفور): khabar, nominative. (رحيم): a second khabar, nominative.
And the clause «إنّ ربّك للذين ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause لا جرم..
And the clause «هاجروا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الّذين).
And the clause «فتنوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle-relative (ما).
And the interpreted maṣdar (ما فتنوا..) is in the position of the genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause «جاهدوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause هاجروا.
And the clause «صبروا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause هاجروا.
And the clause «إنّ ربّك.. لغفور» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive, to emphasise the first clause [Note: or it is a badal from the first, with no grammatical position.].

* Morphology:
(مطمئنّ): active participle of اطمأنّ, the five-letter verb. Its wazn is مفعللّ (ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the first lām).

* Benefits:
Those tried away from their religion:
- His saying, Exalted is He: مَنْ كَفَرَ بِاللَّهِ مِنْ بَعْدِ إِيمانِهِ إِلَّا مَنْ أُكْرِهَ وَقَلْبُهُ مُطْمَئِنٌّ بِالْإِيمانِ..
When the polytheists of the people of Mecca grew severe upon the weak who had believed in what was sent down to Muḥammad ﷺ, a number of them reverted to disbelief. They were of two groups: a group that responded to the enticement of Quraysh out of fear or desire, and a group that was tortured for the sake of Allah until it was compelled to utter the word of disbelief.
Among them were ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir and his father and mother; Abū Jahl killed the two of them, and they were the first two martyrs in Islam. And among them were Ṣuhayb, Khabbāb, Bilāl and Sālim, who took refuge in precautionary dissimulation (taqiyya), so they said the word of disbelief with their tongues while their hearts were full of faith. The Messenger accepted that from them and confirmed them in it, and concerning them there was sent down of the noble Qur'an His saying, Exalted is He: إِلَّا مَنْ أُكْرِهَ وَقَلْبُهُ مُطْمَئِنٌّ بِالْإِيمانِ.

safi-cedvel:111-111.t:
* I'rab:
(يوم): direct object of an omitted verb, its implied form being "اذكر" ("remember") [Note: or it is an adverb of time, accusative, attached to رحيم.]. (تأتي): an imperfect verb, nominative, its nominative marker being the ḍamma implied on the yāʾ. (كلّ): agent, nominative. (نفس): muḍāf ilayhi, genitive. (تجادل): an imperfect verb, nominative; the agent is "she". (عن نفسها): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (تجادل), and (ها) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (الواو): conjunctive. (توفّى): a passive imperfect verb, nominative, its nominative marker being the ḍamma implied on the alif. (كلّ): nāʾib fāʿil, nominative. (نفس): like the first. (ما): a maṣdar particle. (عملت): a past verb, and (التاء) is for the feminine, and the agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "هي".
The interpreted maṣdar (ما عملت..) is in the position of the accusative, direct object, with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "the recompense of its deeds" [Note: It is permissible for (ما) to be a relative noun in the position of the accusative, with the returning pronoun omitted and the clause after it as the ṣila.].
(الواو): the wāw of ḥāl. (هم): a detached pronoun, mubtadaʾ. (لا): negative. (يظلمون): a passive imperfect verb, nominative, and (الواو) is the nāʾib fāʿil.
The clause « (اذكر) يوم ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «تأتي كلّ ... » is in the position of the genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause «تجادل ... » is in the position of the nominative, naʿt of كلّ نفس [Note: or in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl.].
And the clause «توفّى كلّ نفس» is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause تأتي.
And the clause «عملت ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle-relative (ما).
And the clause «و (هم) لا يظلمون» is in the position of the accusative, ḥāl.
And the clause «لا يظلمون» is in the position of the nominative, khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هم).

* Morphology:
(توفّى): it has an i'lāl by substitution. Its origin is توفي — with a yāʾ at the end — the yāʾ came vowelled after a fatḥa and was turned into an alif, and it was written in the form of the yāʾ because it is the fifth letter.

* Benefits:
- يَوْمَ تَأْتِي كُلُّ نَفْسٍ:
"Kull" is a noun indicating comprehensiveness and totality, or the parts of individuals. It is either indefinite, as in كُلُّ نَفْسٍ ذائِقَةُ الْمَوْتِ, or definite, as in وَكُلُّهُمْ آتِيهِ يَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ فَرْداً.
Its i'rab: it has three aspects:
The first: that it be tawkīd of a definite noun, which is the school of the Basrans.
The second: that it be a naʿt of a definite noun, indicating its perfection, as in:
«هم القوم كل القوم يا أم خالد»
(They are the people, the whole of the people, O Umm Khālid.)
The third: that it follow the governors, either annexed, as in:
كُلُّ نَفْسٍ بِما كَسَبَتْ رَهِينَةٌ,
or not annexed, as in: وَكُلًّا ضَرَبْنا لَهُ الْأَمْثالَ. Among this is its standing in for the maṣdar, in which case it is accusative as an absolute object, as in فَلا تَمِيلُوا كُلَّ الْمَيْلِ; and it may be annexed to an adverb, in which case it is parsed as mafʿūl fīhi (adverbial).
Remark: the word kull is, in its ruling, singular and masculine.
The meaning of kull depends on what it is annexed to, so the meaning of what it is annexed to is observed in indefiniteness and definiteness, singular, dual and plural, masculine and feminine, as in كل نفس ذائقة الموت, وكل حزب بما لديهم فرحون, and كل نفس بما كسبت رهينة.
In all of these examples the meaning of the muḍāf ilayhi was observed and the form of "kull" was not; so reflect and act. You have been guided to the right.

safi-cedvel:112-112.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو): resumptive. (ضرب): a past verb. (الله): the word of majesty, agent, nominative. (مثلا): direct object, accusative. (قرية): badal from (مثلا), accusative. (كانت): a defective past verb — and (التاء) is for the feminine — and its noun is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "هي". (آمنة): the khabar of كان, accusative. (مطمئنّة): a second khabar, accusative. (يأتيها): like تأتي «1», and (ها) is a pronoun, direct object. (رزقها): agent, nominative.. and (ها) is a muḍāf ilayhi. (رغدا): a maṣdar in the place of a ḥāl. (من كلّ): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يأتيها). (مكان): muḍāf ilayhi, genitive. (الفاء): conjunctive in the two places. (كفرت): like عملت «2». (بأنعم): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (كفرت). (الله): the word of majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive. (أذاقها): like عمل «3».. and (ها) is a pronoun, direct object. (الله): the word of majesty, agent, nominative. (لباس): second direct object, accusative. (الجوع): muḍāf ilayhi, genitive. (الواو): conjunctive. (الخوف): conjoined to الجوع, genitive. (الباء): a preposition. (ما): a maṣdar particle [Note: or a relative noun in the position of the genitive with the returning pronoun omitted.]. (كانوا يصنعون): like كانوا يعملون [Note: in verse (97) of this sūra.].
The interpreted maṣdar (ما كانوا..) is in the position of the genitive by the bāʾ, attached to (أذاقها).
The clause «ضرب الله ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
And the clause «كانت آمنة ... » is in the position of the accusative, naʿt of قرية.
And the clause «يأتيها رزقها» is in the position of the accusative, a third khabar of the verb كانت [Note: or in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the pronoun in آمنة.].
And the clause «كفرت ... » is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the clause كانت ...
And the clause «أذاقها الله ... » is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the clause كفرت..
And the clause «كانوا يصنعون» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle-relative (ما).
And the clause «يصنعون» is in the position of the accusative, khabar of كانوا.

* Rhetoric:
(1) Mursal figurative usage (al-majāz al-mursal): in His saying, Exalted is He, وَضَرَبَ اللَّهُ مَثَلًا قَرْيَةً, i.e. the people of a town, the relation being locality, since the place is mentioned and what is meant is what is in it.
(2) In His saying, Exalted is He, فَأَذاقَهَا اللَّهُ لِباسَ الْجُوعِ وَالْخَوْفِ there are two implicit metaphors (istiʿāratān makniyyatān).
As for the tasting (idhāqa), it has been treated by them as literal, because of its prevalence in trials and hardships and what of them touches people; they say: "So-and-so tasted misery and harm", and "He made him taste punishment": what is experienced of the effect of harm and pain was likened to what is experienced of the taste of bitter and foul things.
As for the garment (libās), it was used as the likeness because of its enveloping the wearer: what overwhelmed a person and clung to him of certain events, as though it had surrounded them and enveloped them as a garment envelops its wearer.

safi-cedvel:113-113.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو): resumptive. (اللام): the lām of an oath, for an implied oath. (قد): a particle of verification. (جاءهم): a past verb, and (هم) is a pronoun, direct object. (رسول): agent, nominative. (من): a preposition, and (هم) is a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to an adjective of رسول. (الفاء): conjunctive in the two places. (كذّبوه): a past verb and its agent, and (الهاء) is the direct object. (أخذهم): like جاءهم. (العذاب): agent, nominative. (الواو): the wāw of ḥāl. (هم): a detached pronoun, mubtadaʾ. (ظالمون): khabar, nominative, its nominative marker being the wāw.
The clause «قد جاءهم رسول ... » has no grammatical position; it is the answer to the implied oath.
And the clause «كذّبوه ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause of the answer to the oath.
And the clause «أخذهم العذاب ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause كذّبوه.
And the clause «هم ظالمون» is in the position of the accusative, ḥāl.

safi-cedvel:114-114.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء): linking the apodosis of an implied condition. (كلوا): an imperative verb, indeclinable on the omission of the nūn.. and (الواو) is the agent. (من): a preposition. (ما): a relative noun, indeclinable in the position of the genitive, attached to (كلوا). (رزقكم): a past verb.. and (كم) is a pronoun, direct object. (الله): the word of majesty, agent, nominative. (حلالا): ḥāl from the omitted second object, i.e. "Allah provided it to you" [Note: or an absolute object substituting for the maṣdar, i.e. "lawful eating", and likewise (طيّبا) .. it is also permissible for it to be a direct object, i.e. "lawful food".]. (طيّبا): a second ḥāl [Note: It is permissible for it to be a naʿt of (حلالا), accusative like it.]. (الواو): conjunctive. (اشكروا): like كلوا. (نعمة): direct object, accusative. (الله): the word of majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive. (إن): a jussive conditional particle. (كنتم): a defective past verb in the position of the jussive, the protasis.. and (تم) is the noun of kāna. (إيّاه): a detached pronoun, indeclinable in the position of the accusative, preposed direct object. (تعبدون): an imperfect verb, nominative.. and (الواو) is the agent.
The clause «كلوا ... » is in the position of the jussive, the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if the provision of Allah comes to you, then eat..".
And the clause «رزقكم الله ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
And the clause «اشكروا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause كلوا.
And the clause «كنتم.. تعبدون» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.. and the apodosis of the condition is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e. "if it is He whom you worship, then eat of His provision and give thanks for His favour".
And the clause «تعبدون» is in the position of the accusative, khabar of كنتم.

safi-cedvel:1-1.t:
* I'rab:
(أتى) a past verb [Note: either in its basic sense, meaning "drew near".. or it is future in meaning because its occurrence is certain, as if it had occurred.], indeclinable on the implied fatḥa on the alif. (أمر) fāʿil, nominative. (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive. (الفاء) the linking particle of the apodosis of an implied condition [Note: or a conjunction linking the effect to the cause..]. (لا) prohibitive and jussive. (تستعجلوه) an imperfect verb, jussive, its jussive marking being the dropping of the nūn.. and (الواو) is the fāʿil, and (الهاء) is a pronoun in the position of an accusative, mafʿūl bihi. (سبحان) mafʿūl muṭlaq of an omitted verb, and (الهاء) is a pronoun in genitive construct. (الواو) conjunction. (تعالى) a past verb like أتى; the fāʿil is "He". (عن) a preposition. (ما) a maṣdar particle [Note: or a relative noun in the position of a genitive, the returning pronoun omitted, that is "they associate with Him"]. (يشركون) an imperfect verb, nominative, its nominative marking being the retention of the nūn ... and (الواو) is the fāʿil.
The interpreted maṣdar (ما يشركون) is in the position of a genitive by the preposition, attached to (تعالى).
The clause «أتى أمر الله ...» has no grammatical position; initial (ibtidāʾiyya).
The clause «لا تستعجلوه ...» is in the position of a jussive, the apodosis of an implied condition, that is: "if you demand the matter, do not hasten it".
The clause «(نسبّح) سبحانه ...» has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «تعالى ...» has no grammatical position; conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «يشركون» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the maṣdar particle (ما).

* Benefits:
1- أَتى أَمْرُ اللَّهِ: He, Glorified, expressed the future by the past, as a proclamation of the occurrence of His command and the necessity of its realisation, and this is among the subtleties of the rhetoric of the noble Qur'an, so reflect.
2- تَعالى: this verb is defective in conjugation, and it has been said: a verb, as regards conveying a meaning, either is not connected with time or is connected with it, in two kinds: inert and conjugated.
For if it is connected with time, that calls for the variation of its forms to convey its occurrence at a specific time.
And if it is not connected with time, that necessitates its being inert in one form.
Of that are hope, through the verb «عسى», blame, through the verb «بئس», and likewise praise through the verb «نعم», then wonder; all of that does not vary with the variation of time, and that is why their verbs are inert. It either keeps to the past form, like عسى, ليس, نعم, بئس, تبارك and تعالى, or the imperfect form, or the imperative form, like هب, هات, تعال and هلمّ in the language of Tamīm.

semin-durr:6-6.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَلَكُمْ فِيهَا جَمَالٌ}: like His saying {لَكُمْ فِيهَا دِفْءٌ} [al-Naḥl: 5]. And «حين» is accusative (manṣūb) by «جَمال» itself, or by an omitted [word] on the basis that it is a naʿt (adjective) of it, or it is governed by what governs «فيها» or «لكم».
ʿIkrima and al-Ḍaḥḥāk read «حينا» with tanwīn, on the basis that the clause after it is a naʿt of it, and the referent pronoun is omitted, i.e. "a time in which you bring them home, and a time in which you send them out to pasture", like His saying, the Exalted: {واتقوا يَوْماً تُرْجَعُونَ فِيهِ} [al-Baqara: 281].
Bringing home (al-irāḥa) was placed before sending out to pasture (al-sarḥ) because the livestock are more beautiful then, with their bellies full and their udders swollen with milk.
Al-jamāl (beauty) is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of jamula (with ḍamma on the mīm), yajmulu, so he is jamīl and she is jamīla. Al-Kisāʾī reported jamlāʾ, like ḥamrāʾ, and recited:
295 - 7- فهِيَ جَمْلاءُ كَبَدْرٍ طالعٍ ... بَذَّتِ الخَلْقَ جميعاً بالجَمالْ
(She is beautiful (jamlāʾ) like a rising full moon; she surpassed all creatures in beauty.)
One says: arāḥa al-māshiya (he brought the livestock home) and harāḥahā, with hāʾ in place of the hamza. And saraḥa al-ibila, yasraḥuhā, sarḥan, i.e. he sent them out; its origin is that he sends them out to graze on the sarḥ, and the sarḥ is a tree that bears fruit, the singular being sarḥa. He said:
295 - 8- أبى اللهُ إلا أنَّ سَرْحَةَ مالكٍ ... على كلِّ افنانِ العِضاهِ تَرُوْقُ
(Allah has willed only that Mālik's sarḥa tree should excel over all the branches of the thorny trees.)
And he said:
295 - 9- بَطَلٌ كأن ثيابَه في سَرْحةٍ ... يُحْذَى نِعالَ السَّبْتِ ليس بتوْءَم
(A hero, as though his garments were on a sarḥa tree [for his tallness]; he is shod with tanned-leather sandals, and he is not a twin.)
Then it was applied to every sending forth, and it was also borrowed for divorce, so they said: sarraḥa fulānun imraʾatahu (so-and-so released his wife), just as divorce (ṭalāq) was also borrowed from releasing (iṭlāq) camels from their tethers. And from al-sarḥ the sense of going on was taken, so it was said: nāqa suruḥ, i.e. a swift she-camel. He said:
296 - 0-. . . سُرُحُ اليَدَيْن. . . . . . . . . . . ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(… swift of forelegs …)
The objects of «تُرِيْحون» and «تَسْرَحُون» were omitted out of regard for the verse-endings (fawāṣil), since they are known.

semin-durr:7-7.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {لَّمْ تَكُونُواْ}: a naʿt (adjective) of «بلد», and «إلا بشِقٍّ» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the nominative pronoun in «بالِغِيْه», i.e. "you would not reach it except while beset with hardship."
The majority read it with kasra on the shīn. Abū Jaʿfar read it with fatḥa, and this was also narrated from Nāfiʿ and Abū ʿAmr. It was said: they are two maṣdars (verbal nouns) with one meaning, i.e. hardship (al-mashaqqa); from the kasra form is his saying:
296 - 1- رأى إبِلاً تَسْعى، ويَحْسِبُها له ... أخي نَصَبٍ مِنْ شِقِّها ودُؤْوْبِ
(He saw camels on the move, and he reckons them his own — one of toil, from their hardship (shiqq) and constant labour.)
i.e. from their hardship. / It was said: the form with fatḥa is the maṣdar and the form with kasra is the noun. It was said: with kasra it means half of a thing. In the exegesis: "except with half of yourselves", just as you say "you will not attain it except with a piece of your liver", figuratively.

semin-durr:8-8.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {والخيل}: The majority read it in the accusative, conjoined to «الأنعامَ». Ibn Abī ʿAbla read it in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), the khabar (predicate) being omitted, i.e. "created" or "prepared for you to ride"; and this is not a case where the preposition with its noun stands in place of the khabar, because it is a specific being (kawn khāṣṣ).
His saying: «وزينةً»: there are several views on its accusative. The first: it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose); the verb reached the first one by means of the lām in His saying «لتركبوها», and reached this one by itself, because a condition is lacking in the first, namely that the agent is not the same: the Creator is Allah, while the riders are those addressed — unlike the second.
The second: it is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), the one it describes being either the object of «خَلَقَها» or the object of «لتركبوها»; so it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) put in the place of a ḥāl.
The third: that it is accusative by an implied verb; al-Zamakhsharī estimated it as «وخَلَقها زينة» ("and He created them as adornment"), and Ibn ʿAṭiyya and others estimated it as «وجَعَلها زينةً» ("and He made them an adornment").
The fourth: that it is the maṣdar of an omitted verb, i.e. "and they adorn themselves with them with adornment."
Qatāda read, from Ibn ʿAbbās, «لتَرْكَبوها زينةً» without the wāw; the views mentioned above apply to it, with the addition that it may be a ḥāl from the agent of «لتركبوها», i.e. "you ride them adorning yourselves with them."

semin-durr:9-9.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَمِنْهَا جَآئِرٌ}: The pronoun refers back to «السبيل» because it is treated as feminine: {قُلْ هذه سبيلي} [Yūsuf: 108]; or because it carries the meaning of «سُبُل» (paths), so it was made feminine according to the meaning of the plural.
Al-qaṣd is a maṣdar (verbal noun) used as a description, so it means qāṣid; one says sabīlun qaṣdun and qāṣidun, i.e. straight, as though it heads for the direction the traveller aims at without deviating from it. It was said: the pronoun refers back to the creatures, and this is supported by the reading of ʿĪsā and what is in the codex of ʿAbd Allāh: «ومنكم جائِزٌ», and the reading of ʿAlī: «فمنكم جائر» with fāʾ. [Translator's note: the codex reading is printed «جائِزٌ» with zāy, while ʿAlī's is «جائر»; translated as written.]
It was said: the al- in «السبيل» is for something previously known (ʿahd); on this view the pronoun refers back to the "path" implied by the meaning of the verse, as though it were said: "and of the paths", so it referred back to it although it had not been mentioned, because its counterpart indicates it. But if the al- is generic, then it refers back to its wording.
Al-jawr: deviating from straightness. Al-Nābigha said:
296 - 2-. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... يَجُور بها الملاَّحُ طَوْراً ويَهْتدي
(… the sailor veers off course with it at times, and at times keeps the right way.)
And another said:
296 - 3- ومن الطريقةِ جائرٌ وهُدىً ... قَصْدُ السبيلِ ومنه ذُو دَخْلِ
(Of the way some is deviating and some is guidance; the path is straight, and of it is some that is corrupt.)
Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "«قَصْدُ» is a maṣdar meaning the setting-straight of the path and the levelling of the path; it is not the maṣdar of qaṣadtuhu in the sense of 'I came to him'."

semin-durr:10-10.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {مَآءً لَّكُم مَّنْهُ شَرَابٌ}: «لكم» may be attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أنْزَلَ», and it may be a naʿt (adjective) of «ماءً», so it is attached to an omitted [word]. On the first view «شرابٌ» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «منه» is its khabar (predicate) placed before it, and the clause is likewise a naʿt of «ماءً»; on the second view «شرابٌ» is a fāʿil (agent) of the adverbial phrase, and «منه» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «شراب». The first «مِنْ» is partitive, and so is the second according to some of them, but it is figurative, because since [the tree's] watering is by the water, it was treated as though it were from the water, like his saying:
294 - 6- أسنِمَة الآبالِ في رَبابَهْ ...
(The camels' humps are in a white cloud.)
i.e. in a cloud, by which he means the rain by which the pasture grows that the camels eat, so that their humps grow fat. [Translator's note: the verse number is printed «294 - 6» in the source, out of sequence; reproduced as written.]
Abū Bakr ibn al-Anbārī said: "It involves the omission of a muḍāf, either from the first, meaning before the pronoun, i.e. 'from its watering and its means are trees', or from the second, meaning before «شجر», i.e. 'the drink of trees' or 'the life of trees'." Abū al-Baqāʾ made the first partitive and the second causal, i.e. "by its cause", and this is indicated by His saying: {يُنبِتُ لَكُمْ بِهِ الزرع}. [Translator's note: the source discusses «ومنه شجر», part of the same verse, without quoting it in the heading.]
Al-shajar here is every plant of the earth, even pasture-grass; in the ḥadīth: "Do not eat the shajar, for it is unlawful (suḥt)", meaning pasture-grass; it forbids fencing off freely available things that are badly needed. And he said:
296 - 5- نُطْعِمُها اللحمَ إذا عَزَّ الشجَرْ ...
(We feed them meat when the shajar [pasture] is scarce.)
And that is figurative, because shajar is what has a trunk.
His saying: {فِيهِ تُسِيمُونَ}: this is another naʿt of «ماءً». The majority read «تُسِيمون» with ḍamma on the yāʾ, from asāma, i.e. he sent them out to graze; and Zayd ibn ʿAlī read it with fatḥa, so it may be transitive, faʿala and afʿala having the same meaning, or it may be intransitive with the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "your livestock graze." [Translator's note: the source says "the yāʾ", although the word is written with tāʾ; translated as written.]

semin-durr:11-11.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {يُنبِتُ}: this clause may be resumptive or subordinate, as in its counterpart. One says "anbata Allāhu al-zarʿa" (Allah made the crops grow), so it is manbūt, though by analogy it should be munbat. It was said: anbata sometimes comes intransitive, like nabata; al-Farrāʾ recited:
296 - 6- رأيتَ ذوي الحاجاتِ حولَ بيوتِهمْ ... قَطِيناً لهم حتى إذا أَنْبَتَ البَقْلُ
(You saw the needy around their houses, staying with them until the herbage sprouted (anbata).)
Al-Aṣmaʿī rejected that, but the verse is proof against him, and interpreting it as "the herbage made itself grow", figuratively, is very far-fetched.
Abū Bakr read «نُنْبِتُ» with the nūn of majesty, / and al-Zuhrī «نُنَبِّتُ» with doubling. The apparent view is that it is the doubling of the transitive verb; it was said rather that it is for repetition. Ubayy read «يَنْبُت» with fatḥa on the yāʾ and ḍamma on the bāʾ, with «الزَّرعُ» and what follows it nominative as agents.

semin-durr:12-12.t: The disagreement of the readers about reading «الشمس» and what follows it in the nominative or the accusative, and the justification of that, has already been given in Sūrat al-Aʿrāf.

semin-durr:13-13.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {وَمَا ذَرَأَ}: conjoined to «الليل», as al-Zamakhsharī said, meaning the animals and trees He created in it. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "In the position of an accusative by an omitted verb, i.e. 'and He created and caused to grow'." It is as though he thought it unlikely that «سَخَّر» governs that, so he estimated a fitting verb. «مختلفاً» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from it, and «ألوانُه» is its fāʿil (agent).
He closed the first verse with reflection, because what is in it needs contemplation and consideration; the second with reason, because what precedes turns on it; and the third with remembrance, because it is the result of what preceded. He made «آيات» plural in the second but not in the first and third, because more is connected to it, and for that reason He mentioned reason with it.

semin-durr:14-14.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {مِنْهُ لَحْماً}: «منه» may be attached to (mutaʿalliq) «لتأكلوا», or to an omitted [word] because it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the indefinite noun after it. «مِنْ» is for the beginning of the extent or partitive, and the omission of a muḍāf is necessary, i.e. "from its animals".
«طَرِيّاً» is of the pattern faʿīl from ṭaruwa, yaṭrū, ṭarāwatan, like saruwa, yasrū, sarāwatan. Al-Farrāʾ said: "Rather one says ṭariya, yaṭrā, ṭarāwatan and ṭarāʾan, like shaqiya, yashqā, shaqāwatan and shaqāʾan." Al-ṭarāwa is the opposite of dryness, i.e. fresh and new. One says: al-thiyāb al-muṭarrāt (freshened garments). And al-iṭrāʾ is praise whose mention is renewed. As for ṭaraʾa with hamza, it means "to appear".
His saying: «حِلْيةً»: al-ḥilya is a noun for that with which one adorns oneself, and its origin is to denote a manner, like al-ʿimma and al-khimra. «تَلْبَسُونها» is a naʿt (adjective). «منه» allows what was allowed for the «منه» before it. His saying «تَرَى» is a parenthetical clause between the two causal clauses, namely «لتأكلوا» and «لِتَبْتَغُوا»; it is parenthetical only because it addresses one person between two addresses to a group.
His saying: «فيه» may be attached to «ترى», or to «مواخِرَ» because it means "cleaving", or to an omitted [word] because it is a ḥāl from «مَواخِر» or from the pronoun concealed in it.
«مَواخِر» is the plural of mākhira; al-makhr is cleaving; one says makharat al-safīnatu al-baḥra, i.e. the ship cleaved the sea, tamkhuruhu makhran and mukhūran. Ships are called banāt makhr and bakhr — with the mīm, the bāʾ being a substitute for it. Al-Farrāʾ said: "It is the sound of the running of ships." It was said: the sound of the wind blowing hard. It was said: "banāt makhr" is said of clouds that form in summer. And imtakhartu al-rīḥa and istamkhartuhā, i.e. I faced it with my nose. In the ḥadīth: "Face the wind (istamkhirū al-rīḥ) and prepare the stones", meaning when cleaning oneself after relieving oneself. Al-mākhūr is the place where wine is sold. «ترى» here is visual only.
His saying: «ولِتَبْتَغُوا»: there are three views on it. Conjoining it to «لتأكلوا», with what is between them parenthetical — as already said — and this is the apparent view. The second: it is conjoined to an omitted cause, its implied form being "so that you may benefit from that and so that you may seek", mentioned by Ibn al-Anbārī. The third: it is attached to an omitted verb, i.e. "He did that so that you may seek". In both of these there is a strain for which there is no need.

semin-durr:15-15.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {أَن تَمِيدَ}: i.e. "out of aversion to its shaking", or: "lest it shake".
His saying: «وأنهاراً»: conjoined to «رَواسي», because "casting" here means creating. Ibn ʿAṭiyya's claim that it is accusative by an implied verb, i.e. "and He placed in it rivers", is not as he stated. Abū al-Baqāʾ estimated it as "and He cleaved in it rivers", which is fitting. And «سُبُلاً», i.e. "and He made smooth", or: "and He placed in it roads".

semin-durr:16-16.t:
And {وَعَلامَاتٍ}, i.e. "and He placed in it landmarks".
His saying, the Exalted: {وبالنجم}: attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يهتدون». The majority read it with fatḥa on the nūn and sukūn on the jīm, in the singular. It was said: what is meant is a particular star, such as al-Jady (the Pole Star region) or al-Thurayyā (the Pleiades). It was said: rather it is a generic noun. Ibn Waththāb read it with ḍamma on both, and al-Ḥasan with ḍamma on the nūn only; some reversed the report from the two of them.
As for the reading with two ḍammas, there are two explanations of it. The more apparent: it is an explicit plural, because faʿl is pluralised on fuʿul, as in saqf / suquf and rahn / ruhun. / The second: its origin is al-nujūm, faʿl being pluralised on fuʿūl, as in fals / fulūs, then it was lightened by deleting the wāw, as they said asad / usūd and usud. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "And they said for khiyām: khiyam", meaning that it is its parallel, in that they deleted the long vowel from it. Ibn ʿUṣfūr said that their saying "al-nujum" is a poetic licence, and recited:
296 - 7- إنَّ الي قَضَى بذا قاضٍ حَكَمْ ... أن تَرِدَ الماءَ إذا غابَ النُّجُمْ
(The One who decreed this is a judge who has ruled that you come down to the water when the stars (al-nujum) set.)
He means: al-nujūm [Translator's note: printed «النحوم» in the source, evidently for «النجوم»], like his saying:
296 - 8- حتى إذا ابْتَلَّتْ حَلاقِيْمُ الحُلُقْ ...
(Until, when the gullets of the throats were moistened …)
He means al-ḥulūq.
As for the reading with ḍamma and sukūn, there are two views on it. One: it is a lightening of the ḍamma form. The second: it is an independent dialectal form.
The fronting of both the prepositional phrase and the mubtadaʾ (subject) conveys restriction. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: His saying {وبالنجم هُمْ يَهْتَدُونَ} departs from the course of address, the star being fronted in it and [«هم»] inserted in it, as though it were said: 'and by the star specifically, these specifically are guided' — so who are meant by them? I say: it is as though He meant Quraysh: they used to be guided by the stars in their journeys, and they had knowledge of it that others did not have, so gratitude was more incumbent on them and more binding for them." [Translator's note: the name is printed «الزمشخري» in the source, evidently for al-Zamakhsharī.]

semin-durr:17-17.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {كَمَن لاَّ يَخْلُقُ}: if by «مَنْ لا يَخْلُق» is meant all that is worshipped besides Allah, then the use of «مَنْ» is clear, because the rational is given precedence over the rest, so the whole is expressed with «مَنْ»; and had «ما» been used, that too would have been permissible. If the idols are meant by it, then there are several views on applying «مَنْ» to them. The first: their treating them like beings endowed with knowledge in worshipping them and believing that they harm and benefit, like his saying:
296 - 9- بَكَيْتُ إلى سِرْبِ القَطا إذْ مَرَرْنَ بي ... فقلتُ ومِثْلي بالبكاءِ جديرُ
أسِرْبَ القَطا هل مَنْ يُعيرُ جناحَه ... لعلِّي إلى مَن قد هَوَيْتُ أطيرُ
(I wept to the flock of sand-grouse when they passed me, and I said — and one like me is worthy of weeping —: "O flock of sand-grouse, is there one (man) who will lend his wing, so that I might fly to the one I love?")
So he applied «مَنْ» to the flock when he treated them as rational beings. The second: correspondence (mushākala) between it and «مَنْ يَخْلُق». The third: restricting it to those who know, and the meaning is: if there is a disparity between one who creates and one who does not create among beings endowed with knowledge, and one who is not a creator does not deserve worship at all, then how can the worship of inanimate things be right, which are lower in rank and fallen in status below the created among beings endowed with knowledge, as in His saying {أَلَهُمْ أَرْجُلٌ يَمْشُونَ بِهَآ} [al-Aʿrāf: 195] to the end? As for those who allow «مَنْ» to apply to non-rational beings without condition, like Quṭrub, they need no interpretation. [Translator's note: the source reads «مِنْ شرطٍ», literally "from a condition"; rendered "without condition", which the context seems to require.]
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: it is a refutation binding those who worshipped idols and the like, likening them to Allah the Exalted, and they made what is not the Creator like the Creator, so the proper form of the refutation would have been to say to them: 'Is then one who does not create like one who creates?' I say: when they made other than Allah like Allah, by calling them by His name and worshipping them, they made Him of the genus of created things and like them, so He censured them for that with His saying {أَفَمَن يَخْلُقُ كَمَن لاَّ يَخْلُقُ}."

semin-durr:19-19.t: His saying, the Exalted: {يَعْلَمُ مَا تُسِرُّونَ}: The majority read «تُسِرُّون» and «تُعْلِنون» with the tāʾ of address, and Abū Jaʿfar with the yāʾ (with dots beneath).

semin-durr:20-20.t: ʿĀṣim alone read «يَدْعُون» with yāʾ, and the rest with tāʾ (with dots above). It was also read «يُدْعَوْن» in the passive. These are all clear.

semin-durr:21-21.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {أَمْواتٌ}: it may be a second khabar (predicate), i.e. "and they are created, and they are dead". It may be that «يُخْلَقون» and «أمواتٌ» are both a single khabar, of the type "this is sweet-sour", mentioned by Abū al-Baqāʾ. And it may be the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "they are dead".
His saying: {غَيْرُ أَحْيَآءٍ}: what was said before applies to it, and it would be tawkīd (emphasis). Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It may be that by it He intended that they are at present not alive, to remove by it the misconception that His saying «أمواتٌ» refers to what comes later, since the Exalted said: {إِنَّكَ مَيِّتٌ وَإِنَّهُمْ مَّيِّتُونَ} [al-Zumar: 30]." I say: this does not take it out of the emphasis he mentioned before that.
His saying: {أَيَّانَ يُبْعَثُونَ}: «أيَّان» is accusative by what comes after it, not by what comes before it, because it is interrogative, and it suspends (muʿallaq) «يَشْعُرون», so its clause is in the position of an accusative by removal of the preposition (bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ); this is the apparent view. There is another view on the verse: that «أيَّان» is an adverb for His saying {إلهكم إله وَاحِدٌ}, meaning that God is One on the Day of Resurrection, and no one will claim divinity on that day, unlike the days of this world, for in them there have been those who claimed that. On this view the sentence is complete at His saying «يَشْعُرون». But this view takes «أيَّان» out of its original function — which is either / conditional or interrogative — into pure adverbiality in the sense of "time", annexed to the clause after it, as when you say: "At the time you go, ʿAmr is departing", where "time" is accusative by "departing" and annexed to "you go".

semin-durr:23-23.t: His saying, the Exalted: {لاَ جَرَمَ}: the discussion of this expression has already been given in Sūrat Hūd. The majority read with fatḥa on the hamza of «انَّ اللهَ», and ʿĪsā al-Thaqafī read it with kasra; there are two views on it. The more apparent: it is resumptive. The second: «لا جَرَم» is treated like an oath, so it is answered with what an oath is answered with. Some of the Arabs said: "lā jarama wa-llāhi lā fāraqtuka" (assuredly, by Allah, I will not leave you). In my view this weakens its being for an oath, since he states the oath explicitly after it, even though the Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] cited it as strengthening its being treated like an oath.

semin-durr:24-24.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {مَّاذَآ أَنْزَلَ}: the discussion of «ماذا» has already been given at the beginning of al-Baqara. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Or it is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), in the sense: what thing has your Lord sent down?" The Shaykh said: "This is not permissible according to the Basrans", meaning because it omits its accusative referent pronoun, as in "Zaydun ḍarabtu" (Zayd, I struck); the disagreement of people on this has already been given, and the correct view is that it is permissible.
What stands in place of the agent of «قيل» is the clause of His saying {مَّاذَآ أَنْزَلَ}, because it is what is said; the Basrans reject that and make what stands in its place the pronoun of the maṣdar (verbal noun), because a clause cannot be an agent nor stand in place of an agent. The omitted agent is either the believers, or some of them, or "those who divided [the Qurʾān]" (al-muqtasimūn).
«أساطيرَ» was read in the accusative, on the estimation "He sent down tales", by way of mockery, or "you mentioned tales". The majority read it in the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "what was sent down is tales", by way of mockery, or "what is mentioned is tales". Al-Zamakhsharī has a dreadful expression here that makes the hair stand on end.

semin-durr:68-68.t:
The words of the Exalted: {أَنِ اتخذي}: (أن) may be explicative (mufassira), or it may be maṣdariyya (infinitival). Some found its being explicative problematic. He said: "Because the waḥy (revelation/inspiration) here does not carry the meaning of speech, since it is an instinctive inspiration (ilhām) in which there is no speech." This is open to question, because speech for each thing is according to what befits it.
And النَّحْل (the bees) is treated as masculine and feminine, following the rule for generic nouns (asmāʾ al-ajnās). The feminine is the dialect of the Hijaz, and {أَنِ اتخذي} came in accordance with it. Ibn Waththāb read «النَحَل»; it may be an independent dialectal form, or it may be by vowel assimilation (itbāʿ).
And in {مِنَ الجبال}, «مِنْ» is partitive (li-l-tabʿīḍ), since this is not feasible for it in every mountain and every tree. The discussion of «يَعْرِشُونَ» has preceded, together with who read it with kasra and with fatḥa, in al-Aʿrāf.

semin-durr:69-69.t:
The words of the Exalted: {ذُلُلاً}: the plural of ذَلُول (tractable). It may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) of السُّبُل (the ways), i.e. Allah the Exalted has made them tractable, as in His words: {هُوَ الذي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ الأرض ذَلُولاً} [al-Mulk: 15]; or it may be a ḥāl of the fāʿil (agent) of «اسْلُكي», i.e. obedient and compliant. Both meanings are transmitted in the exegesis.
The accusative of «سُبُل» may be adverbial (ẓarfiyya), i.e. "so convey what you have eaten along the ways of your Lord", i.e. in His passages in which, by His power, He transforms the blossom and the like into honey; or it may be a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e. "travel the paths which He made you understand and taught you for the making of honey". And «مِنْ» in {مِن كُلِّ الثمرات} may be partitive, or it may denote the beginning (ibtidāʾ), in the sense that it eats something that descends from the sky, resembling manna (al-taranjabīn), onto the leaves of the trees and their fruits, not that it eats the fruits themselves — and this is very far-fetched.
His words: {يَخْرُجُ مِن بُطُونِهَا}: an iltifāt (shift of person) and a statement of that; had it come in accordance with the preceding speech it would have been said: "from your bellies". The hāʾ in «فيه» refers back to «شَراب» (drink), and this is the apparent meaning; and it is said that it refers back to the Qur'an.

semin-durr:70-70.t:
The words of the Exalted: {لِكَيْ لاَ}: there are two views on this lām. The first: it is the lām of causation (taʿlīl), and «كي» after it is nothing but maṣdariyya (infinitival); it puts the following verb in the accusative by itself, and it together with the verb it governs is interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) put in the genitive by the lām, and the lām is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «يُرَدُّ». Al-Ḥūfī said: "It is the lām of kay, and kay is for emphasis." This is open to question, because the lām is for causation while «كي» is maṣdariyya and carries no indication of causation in this situation; moreover, their governing effects differ.
The second: it is the lām of outcome (lām al-ṣayrūra).
His words: «شيئاً»: tanāzuʿ (two governors contending for one word) is possible in it, for two governors precede it: «يَعْلَمَ» and «عِلْمٍ». On the view of the Basrans — and it is the preferred one — it is in the accusative by «عِلْم», and on the view of the Kufans it is in the accusative by «يَعلم». That is rejected, since had it been so, a pronoun would have been implied in the second, and it would have been said: لكيلا يعلمَ بعد عِلْمٍ إياه شيئاً.

semin-durr:71-71.t:
The words of the Exalted: {فَهُمْ فِيهِ سَوَآءٌ}: there are several views on this clause. The first: it involves the omission of the interrogative particle, its implied form being "أَفَهُمْ فيه سواءٌ" (are they then equal in it?), and its meaning is negation, i.e. they are not equal in it. The second: it is a statement of equality, meaning that what you feed and clothe your slaves with is only My provision which I have caused to flow through their hands, so they are equal in it. The third: Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It stands in the place of a verb", and then he allowed two views in that verb. The first: it is in the accusative in answer to the negation, its implied form being: فما الذين فُضِّلوا برادِّي رزقِهم على ما ملكَتْ أيمانُهم فيَسْتَوُوا. The second: it is conjoined to the position of «برادّي», so it would be nominative, its implied form being: فما الذين فُضِّلوا يَرُدُّون فما يَسْتَوُوْن.
Abū Bakr read «تَجْحَدون» in the second person (khiṭāb), in keeping with His words «بعضَكم», and the rest in the third person (ghayba), in keeping with His words {فَمَا الذين فُضِّلُواْ}.

semin-durr:72-72.t:
The words of the Exalted: {وَحَفَدَةً}: there are several views on «حَفَدَة». The most apparent: it is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to «بنين», with the restriction of being from the spouses, and here it is explained as the children of the children (grandchildren). The second: it is a conjunction of attributes of a single thing, i.e. He made for you sons as servants, and الحَفَدَة are servants. The third: it is in the accusative by an implied «جَعَلَ»; this is according to those who explain الحَفَدَة as helpers and in-laws. An implied «جَعَلَ» was needed only because the first «جَعَلَ» is restricted by the spouses, and helpers and in-laws are not from the spouses.
And الحَفَدَة is the plural of حافِد, like خادِم and خَدَم. The exegetes have many sayings about them. Its derivation is from their saying: حَفَد يَحْفِد حَفْداً وحُفوداً وحَفَداناً, i.e. he hastened in obedience. And in the hadith: «وإليك نَسْعَى ونَحْفِدُ» (to You we strive and hasten), i.e. we hasten in obeying You. Al-Aʿshā said:
300 - 1- كَلَّفْتُ مجهولَها نُوْقاً يَمانيةً ... إذا الحُداة على أَكْسائها حَفَدُوا
(I made Yemeni she-camels cross its unknown tracts, when the camel-drivers hastened behind them.)
And another said:
300 - 2- حَفَدَ الولائدُ حولَهُنَّ وأَسْلَمَتْ ... بأكفِّهنَّ أَزِمَّةَ الأجْمالِ
(The maidservants hastened around them, and gave over with their hands the reins of the camels.)
«حَفَدَ» is also used transitively. One says: حَفَدَني فهو حافِدٌ (he served me, so he is a servant), and there was recited:
300 - 3- يَحْفِدون الضيفَ في أبياتِهمْ ... كَرَماً ذلك منهم غيرَ ذُلّْ
(They serve the guest in their tents, out of generosity on their part, not out of abasement.)
Abū ʿUbayda related that one also says «أَحْفَدَ» as a quadriliteral. Some said: "الحَفَدَة are the in-laws", and recited:
300 - 4- فلو أنَّ نفسي طاوَعَتْني لأصبحَتْ ... لها حَفَدٌ ممَّا يُعَدُّ كثيرُ
ولكنها نَفسٌ عليَّ أَبِيَّةٌ ... عَيُوفٌ لإِصهارِ اللِّئامِ قَذْوْرُ
(Had my soul obeyed me, it would have come to have many in-laws of those that are counted; but it is a soul that refuses me, disdainful and loathing of marriage ties with the base.)
And one says: سيفٌ مُحْتَفِدٌ, i.e. a sword swift in cutting. Al-Aṣmaʿī said: "The root sense of الحَفْد is shortening the stride (taking quick, close steps)."
And «مِنْ» in {مِّنَ الطيبات} is partitive.

semin-durr:73-73.t:
