The second: that He thereby alluded to the speed with which they forget the beginning of their creation. It was also said: there are omitted intermediate stages. What appears is that His saying «خَلَقَ» is an expression for bringing him into existence and rearing him until he reaches the stage of these two attributes.
And «خصيم» is faʿīl, a form of intensity, from «خَصَم» in the sense of «اختصم»; it may also be in the sense of «مُخاصِم», like «al-khalīṭ» and «al-jalīs».
[Translator's note: the phrase «وفرنٌ يَنْطِفُ بسوءٍ» in the first paragraph appears as written in the source; its wording looks corrupt (perhaps «وقَرْنٌ» or similar), and I have not emended it.]

semin-durr:5-5.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {والأنعام خَلَقَهَا}: the majority read with accusative, and there are two aspects in it. One: accusative by preoccupation (ishtighāl), which is preferable to nominative because a verbal clause precedes. The second: that it is accusative as a conjunction to «الإنسان»; al-Zamakhsharī and Ibn ʿAṭiyya said it, so «خَلَقَها» on this is an emphasis, while on the first it is an explicator. «والأنعامُ» was read nominative in an irregular reading, and it is the less preferred.
His saying: {لَكُمْ فِيهَا دِفْءٌ}: «لكم» may be attached to «خَلَقَها», that is, for your sake and your benefits, with «فيها» a fronted khabar (predicate) and «دِفْءٌ» a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject). It may be that «لكم» is the khabar, with «فيها» attached to what the khabar is attached to; or «فيها» a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «دِفْء», because were it to come after it, it would be an adjective of it; or «فيها» is the khabar, with «لكم» attached to what it is attached to, or a ḥāl from «دِفْء»; Abū l-Baqāʾ said it. The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] rejected it, saying that when the governing element of the ḥāl is abstract, it does not precede the whole clause: «قائماً في الدار زيدٌ» is not permissible; if it comes after, as in «زيدٌ في الدار قائماً», it is permissible without disagreement; and if it comes in the middle, there is disagreement — al-Akhfash allowed it and others forbade it.
I say: someone could say that since the governing element precedes it and it is with it, it is permissible to put it before it as it stands; unless he says that putting it before it when it is postponed does not entail putting it before it when it is advanced, due to the increase in ugliness.
Abū l-Baqāʾ also said: "«دِفْء» may be nominative by «لكم» or by «فيها», and the whole clause is a ḥāl from the accusative pronoun." The Shaykh said: "It is not called a clause; for the implied form is: «خلقها كائناً لكم فيها دفءٌ» or «خَلَقها لكم كائناً فيها دِفْءٌ»." I say: the disagreement has been mentioned earlier about the implied element to which the preposition phrase is attached when it falls as a ḥāl, adjective or predicate: is it implied as a verb or a noun? Perhaps Abū l-Baqāʾ inclined to the first, so his calling it a clause is correct on this view.
Al-dif': a noun for that with which one is warmed, that is, heated; its plural is adfāʾ; «دَفِئَ يومُنا فهو دَفِىءٌ» (our day grew warm), «دَفِئَ الرجلُ يَدْفَأُ دَفاءَةً ودَفَاءً فهو دَفْآنُ» (the man grew warm), and the feminine is «دَفْأَى», like «sakrān» and «sakrā». Al-mudfaʾa, lightened or doubled: camels with abundant fur and fat. It was said: al-dif' is the offspring of camels, their milk and what is of benefit from them.
Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «دِفٌ» by transferring the vowel of the hamza to the fāʾ, and al-Zuhrī likewise, except that he doubled the fāʾ, as though he treated connected reading like pausing, as in their saying «هذا فَرُخّْ» with doubling in pause. The author of «al-Lawāmiḥ» said: "Some of them compensate for this hamza by doubling the fāʾ, and it is one of the two ways of Ḥamza ibn Ḥabīb in pause." I say: doubling in pause is an independent dialect, even if nothing is omitted from the word on which one pauses.
His saying: {وَمِنْهَا تَأْكُلُونَ}: «مِنْ» here is for the beginning of the extent, and partition here is weak. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: putting the adverbial first announces specificity, and one may eat from other than them. I say: eating from them is the principle on which people rely; as for others, such as ducks, chickens and the like of game, they are as though not counted."

ukberi-tibyan:94-94.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَلَا تَتَّخِذُوا أَيْمَانَكُمْ دَخَلًا بَيْنَكُمْ فَتَزِلَّ قَدَمٌ بَعْدَ ثُبُوتِهَا وَتَذُوقُوا السُّوءَ بِمَا صَدَدْتُمْ عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ وَلَكُمْ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمٌ (٩٤)).
His saying, exalted is He: (فَتَزِلَّ): it is the answer (jawāb) to the prohibition.

ukberi-tibyan:97-97.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (مَنْ عَمِلَ صَالِحًا مِنْ ذَكَرٍ أَوْ أُنْثَى وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌ فَلَنُحْيِيَنَّهُ حَيَاةً طَيِّبَةً وَلَنَجْزِيَنَّهُمْ أَجْرَهُمْ بِأَحْسَنِ مَا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ).
His saying, exalted is He: (مِنْ ذَكَرٍ): it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «عَمِلَ».

ukberi-tibyan:98-98.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَإِذَا قَرَأْتَ الْقُرْآنَ فَاسْتَعِذْ بِاللَّهِ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ الرَّجِيمِ (٩٨)).
His saying, exalted is He: (فَإِذَا قَرَأْتَ): the meaning is "when you intend to recite"; the meaning is not "when you have finished reciting".

ukberi-tibyan:100-100.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِنَّمَا سُلْطَانُهُ عَلَى الَّذِينَ يَتَوَلَّوْنَهُ وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ بِهِ مُشْرِكُونَ (١٠٠)).
His saying, exalted is He: (إِنَّمَا سُلْطَانُهُ): the hāʾ in it refers back to Satan. The hāʾ in «بِهِ» also refers back to him, and the meaning is: those who associate partners [with Allah] because of him.
It has also been said: the hāʾ refers back to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

ukberi-tibyan:101-101.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَإِذَا بَدَّلْنَا آيَةً مَكَانَ آيَةٍ وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا يُنَزِّلُ قَالُوا إِنَّمَا أَنْتَ مُفْتَرٍ بَلْ أَكْثَرُهُمْ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ (١٠١)).
His saying, exalted is He: (وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا يُنَزِّلُ): the clause separates «إِذَا» from its answer; so it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial), or it may have no grammatical position. And it [«يُنَزِّلُ»] is with doubling (tashdīd).

ukberi-tibyan:102-102.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قُلْ نَزَّلَهُ رُوحُ الْقُدُسِ مِنْ رَبِّكَ بِالْحَقِّ لِيُثَبِّتَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَهُدًى وَبُشْرَى لِلْمُسْلِمِينَ (١٠٢)).
His saying, exalted is He: (وَهُدًى وَبُشْرَى): both are in the position of the accusative as a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), and this is conjoined to His saying «لِيُثَبِّتَ», because the implied form of the first is: "لِأَنْ يُثَبِّتَ" (in order that He make firm).
It is also possible that both are in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "وَهُوَ هُدًى" (and it is guidance), the clause being a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ in «نَزَّلَهُ».

ukberi-tibyan:103-103.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَلَقَدْ نَعْلَمُ أَنَّهُمْ يَقُولُونَ إِنَّمَا يُعَلِّمُهُ بَشَرٌ لِسَانُ الَّذِي يُلْحِدُونَ إِلَيْهِ أَعْجَمِيٌّ وَهَذَا لِسَانٌ عَرَبِيٌّ مُبِينٌ (١٠٣)).
His saying, exalted is He: (لِسَانُ الَّذِي): the well-known reading has «لِسَانُ» in a genitive construct (iḍāfa) with «الَّذِي», and its khabar (predicate) is «أَعْجَمِيٌّ». In an irregular (shādhdh) reading it was read: «اللِّسَانُ الَّذِي», with the alif and lām, «الَّذِي» being a naʿt (adjective). In either case the pause (waqf) is on «بَشَرٌ».

ukberi-tibyan:106-106.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (مَنْ كَفَرَ بِاللَّهِ مِنْ بَعْدِ إِيمَانِهِ إِلَّا مَنْ أُكْرِهَ وَقَلْبُهُ مُطْمَئِنٌّ بِالْإِيمَانِ وَلَكِنْ مَنْ شَرَحَ بِالْكُفْرِ صَدْرًا فَعَلَيْهِمْ غَضَبٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمٌ (١٠٦)).
His saying, exalted is He: (مَنْ كَفَرَ): there are two views on it. The first: it is a badal (substitute) from His saying «الْكَاذِبُونَ», i.e. "وَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الْكَافِرُونَ" [Translator's note: the source writes «الْكَافِرُونَ» here, while the preceding verse (16:105) reads «وَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الْكَاذِبُونَ»]. It has also been said: it is a badal from «أُولَئِكَ». It has also been said: it is a badal from «الَّذِينَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ». The second: it is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is «فَعَلَيْهِمْ غَضَبٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ».
His saying, exalted is He: (إِلَّا مَنْ أُكْرِهَ): an exception placed early (istithnāʾ muqaddam). It has also been said: it is not placed early, so it is like the saying of Labīd:
أَلَا كُلُّ شَيْءٍ مَا خَلَا اللَّهَ بَاطِلُ
(Truly, everything apart from Allah is vain.)
It has also been said: «مَنْ» is conditional, and its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by His saying «فَعَلَيْهِمْ غَضَبٌ».
And «إِلَّا مَنْ أُكْرِهَ» is a connected exception (istithnāʾ muttaṣil), because unbelief (kufr) is applied to both speech and belief. It has also been said: it is disconnected (munqaṭiʿ), because unbelief is a belief, and the coercion is upon speech, not upon belief.
(مَنْ شَرَحَ): a mubtadaʾ; «فَعَلَيْهِمْ» is its khabar.

ukberi-tibyan:110-110.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (ثُمَّ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ لِلَّذِينَ هَاجَرُوا مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا فُتِنُوا ثُمَّ جَاهَدُوا وَصَبَرُوا إِنَّ رَبَّكَ مِنْ بَعْدِهَا لَغَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ (١١٠)).
His saying, exalted is He: (إِنَّ رَبَّكَ): the khabar (predicate) of «إِنَّ» is «لِغَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ» [Translator's note: so written in the source; the Quranic text is «لَغَفُورٌ»], and the second «إِنَّ» with its noun is a repetition for tawkīd (emphasis). Similar to it in this same surah is: (ثُمَّ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ لِلَّذِينَ عَمِلُوا السُّوءَ بِجَهَالَةٍ).
It has also been said: the first «إِنَّ» has no khabar in the wording, because the khabar of the second made it unnecessary.
(مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا فُتِنُوا): it is read in the passive (lit. "what its agent is not named"), i.e. others tried them with unbelief and they complied; and Allah pardoned them for that, i.e. He granted them a dispensation in it.
And it is read with fatḥa on the fāʾ and the tāʾ [«فَتَنُوا»], i.e. they tried themselves, or they tried others and then embraced Islam.

ukberi-tibyan:111-111.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (يَوْمَ تَأْتِي كُلُّ نَفْسٍ تُجَادِلُ عَنْ نَفْسِهَا وَتُوَفَّى كُلُّ نَفْسٍ مَا عَمِلَتْ وَهُمْ لَا يُظْلَمُونَ (١١١)).
His saying, exalted is He: (يَوْمَ تَأْتِي): it may be an adverb (ẓarf) for «رَحِيمٌ», or a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e. "remember (اذْكُرْ)".

ukberi-tibyan:112-112.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَضَرَبَ اللَّهُ مَثَلًا قَرْيَةً كَانَتْ آمِنَةً مُطْمَئِنَّةً يَأْتِيهَا رِزْقُهَا رَغَدًا مِنْ كُلِّ مَكَانٍ فَكَفَرَتْ بِأَنْعُمِ اللَّهِ فَأَذَاقَهَا اللَّهُ لِبَاسَ الْجُوعِ وَالْخَوْفِ بِمَا كَانُوا يَصْنَعُونَ (١١٢)).
His saying, exalted is He: (قَرْيَةً): it is like His saying: (مَثَلًا عَبْدًا).
(وَالْخَوْفِ): in the genitive, conjoined to «الْجُوعِ»; and in the accusative, conjoined to «لِبَاسَ». It has also been said: it is conjoined to the position of «الْجُوعِ», because the implied meaning is: "that He clothed them with hunger and fear".

ukberi-tibyan:116-116.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَلَا تَقُولُوا لِمَا تَصِفُ أَلْسِنَتُكُمُ الْكَذِبَ هَذَا حَلَالٌ وَهَذَا حَرَامٌ لِتَفْتَرُوا عَلَى اللَّهِ الْكَذِبَ إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَفْتَرُونَ عَلَى اللَّهِ الْكَذِبَ لَا يُفْلِحُونَ (١٦٦)).
[Translator's note: the source prints the verse number as (١٦٦); this is verse 116.]
His saying, exalted is He: (أَلْسِنَتُكُمُ الْكَذِبَ): it is read with fatḥa on the kāf and the bāʾ and kasra on the dhāl [«الْكَذِبَ»], and it is accusative by «تَصِفُ», «مَا» being maṣdariyya (verbal-noun forming). It has also been said: it [«مَا»] means «الَّذِي», the returning pronoun being omitted, and «الْكَذِبَ» is a badal (substitute) from it.
It has also been said: it is accusative by an implied «أَعْنِي» (I mean). And it is read with ḍamma on the kāf and the dhāl and fatḥa on the bāʾ [«الْكُذُبَ»], which is the plural of «كِذَاب» without doubling, like «كِتَاب» and «كُتُب»; it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), and it has the meaning of the first reading.
And it is read likewise, except with ḍamma on the bāʾ [«الْكُذُبُ»], as a naʿt (adjective) of «الْأَلْسِنَة»; it is then the plural of «كَاذِب» (lying) or «كَذُوب» (great liar).
And it is read with fatḥa on the kāf and kasra on the dhāl and the bāʾ [«الْكَذِبِ»], as a badal from «مَا», whether you make it maṣdariyya or meaning «الَّذِي».

ukberi-tibyan:117-117.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (مَتَاعٌ قَلِيلٌ وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ (١١٧)).
His saying, exalted is He: (مَتَاعٌ قَلِيلٌ): i.e. "their remaining [in this world] is an enjoyment", and the like.

ukberi-tibyan:121-121.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (شَاكِرًا لِأَنْعُمِهِ اجْتَبَاهُ وَهَدَاهُ إِلَى صِرَاطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ (١٢١)).
His saying, exalted is He: (اجْتَبَاهُ): it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial), with «قَدْ» intended along with it; or a second khabar (predicate) of «إِنَّ»; or resumptive (mustaʾnaf).
(لِأَنْعُمِهِ): the lām may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to «شَاكِرًا», or attached to «اجْتَبَاهُ».

ukberi-tibyan:126-126.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَإِنْ عَاقَبْتُمْ فَعَاقِبُوا بِمِثْلِ مَا عُوقِبْتُمْ بِهِ وَلَئِنْ صَبَرْتُمْ لَهُوَ خَيْرٌ لِلصَّابِرِينَ (١٢٦)).
His saying, exalted is He: (وَإِنْ عَاقَبْتُمْ): the majority read with the alif and without doubling in both [«عَاقَبْتُمْ» and «فَعَاقِبُوا»].
And it is read with doubling and without an alif in both [«عَقَّبْتُمْ فَعَقِّبُوا»], i.e. "you pursued [them]".
(بِمِثْلِ مَا): the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida). It has also been said: it is not redundant, and the implied meaning is: "by a cause similar to that with which you were punished".
(لَهُوَ خَيْرٌ): the pronoun refers to patience, or to pardon; the preceding speech has indicated both maṣdars (verbal nouns).

ukberi-tibyan:127-127.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَاصْبِرْ وَمَا صَبْرُكَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ وَلَا تَحْزَنْ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا تَكُ فِي ضَيْقٍ مِمَّا يَمْكُرُونَ (١٢٧)).
His saying, exalted is He: (إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ): i.e. by the help of Allah, or by His granting success.
(عَلَيْهِمْ): i.e. over their unbelief. It has also been said: the pronoun refers back to the martyrs, i.e. do not grieve over them, for they have triumphed.
(فِي ضَيْقٍ): it is read with fatḥa on the ḍād, and there are two views on it. The first: it is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of «ضَاقَ», like «سَارَ سَيْرًا». The second: it is lightened from «الضَّيِّق», i.e. "in a narrow matter", like «سَيِّد» and «مَيِّت».
And it is read with kasra on the ḍād [«ضِيقٍ»], which is a dialectal variant of the maṣdar. And Allah knows best.
(مِمَّا يَمْكُرُونَ): i.e. on account of what they plot.

ukberi-tibyan:1-1.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَتَى أَمْرُ اللَّهِ فَلَا تَسْتَعْجِلُوهُ سُبْحَانَهُ وَتَعَالَى عَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ (١)).
The Exalted's saying (أَتَى): it is a past verb in its proper sense, meaning "has drawn near".
It is also said: the future is meant by it; since the report of Allah is true, it is certainly permissible to express the future with the past. The hāʾ in «تَسْتَعْجِلُوهُ» refers back to الْأَمْر; it is also said: to Allah.

ukberi-tibyan:11-11.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (هُوَ الَّذِي أَنْزَلَ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مَاءً لَكُمْ مِنْهُ شَرَابٌ وَمِنْهُ شَجَرٌ فِيهِ تُسِيمُونَ يُنْبِتُ لَكُمْ بِهِ الزَّرْعَ وَالزَّيْتُونَ وَالنَّخِيلَ وَالْأَعْنَابَ وَمِنْ كُلِّ الثَّمَرَاتِ إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لَآيَةً لِقَوْمٍ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ (١١)).
[Translator's note: the source quotes verses 10 and 11 together under the single number (١١).]
The Exalted's saying (مِنْهُ شَرَابٌ): مِنْ here is partitive (li-l-tabʿīḍ), and the second «مِنْ» is causal (li-l-sababiyya), i.e. "and because of it is the growing of trees"; this is indicated by His saying «يُنْبِتُ لَكُمْ بِهِ الزَّرْعَ».

ukberi-tibyan:12-12.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَسَخَّرَ لَكُمُ اللَّيْلَ وَالنَّهَارَ وَالشَّمْسَ وَالْقَمَرَ وَالنُّجُومُ مُسَخَّرَاتٌ بِأَمْرِهِ إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لَآيَاتٍ لِقَوْمٍ يَعْقِلُونَ (١٢)).
The Exalted's saying (وَالشَّمْسَ وَالْقَمَرَ): they are read in the accusative, conjoined to what precedes them, and in the nominative as resumptive (istiʾnāf); «النُّجُومُ» likewise. «مُسَخَّرَاتٌ» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) on the first reading and a khabar (predicate) on the second.

ukberi-tibyan:13-13.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَا ذَرَأَ لَكُمْ فِي الْأَرْضِ مُخْتَلِفًا أَلْوَانُهُ إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لَآيَةً لِقَوْمٍ يَذَّكَّرُونَ (١٣)).
The Exalted's saying (وَمَا ذَرَأَ لَكُمْ): in the position of the accusative (naṣb) by an omitted verb, i.e. "and He created" or "and He caused to grow".
And (مُخْتَلِفًا) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from it.

ukberi-tibyan:14-14.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَهُوَ الَّذِي سَخَّرَ الْبَحْرَ لِتَأْكُلُوا مِنْهُ لَحْمًا طَرِيًّا وَتَسْتَخْرِجُوا مِنْهُ حِلْيَةً تَلْبَسُونَهَا وَتَرَى الْفُلْكَ مَوَاخِرَ فِيهِ وَلِتَبْتَغُوا مِنْ فَضْلِهِ وَلَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ (١٤)).
The Exalted's saying (مِنْهُ لَحْمًا): مِنْ is for the beginning of the extent (ibtidāʾ al-ghāya).
It is also said that the implied wording is "that you may eat from its animals meat".
(فِيهِ): it may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to مَوَاخِرَ, because its meaning is "running", since مَخَرَ ("cleave the water"), شَقَّ ("split") and جَرَى ("run") are close to one another (in meaning).
It may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in مَوَاخِرَ.

ukberi-tibyan:15-15.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَأَلْقَى فِي الْأَرْضِ رَوَاسِيَ أَنْ تَمِيدَ بِكُمْ وَأَنْهَارًا وَسُبُلًا لَعَلَّكُمْ تَهْتَدُونَ وَعَلَامَاتٍ وَبِالنَّجْمِ هُمْ يَهْتَدُونَ (١٥)).
[Translator's note: the source quotes verses 15 and 16 together under the single number (١٥).]
The Exalted's saying (أَنْ تَمِيدَ): i.e. "for fear that it should shake".
And (أَنْهَارًا): i.e. "and He split open rivers".
And (عَلَامَاتٍ): i.e. "and He placed landmarks". It may also be conjoined to «رَوَاسِيَ». And «بِالنَّجْمِ» is read in the form of the singular, as a generic noun (jins). It is also said: what is meant by it is al-Jady (the Pole Star region); and it is also said: the Pleiades.
It is also read with ḍamma on the nūn and the jīm (بِالنُّجُمِ), and there are two views on it. The first: it is the plural of نَجْم, like سَقْف and سُقُف. The second: that he intended النُّجُوم and dropped the wāw, just as they said for أَسَد both أُسُود and أُسُد, and for خِيَام they said خِيَم.
It is also read with sukūn on the jīm (بِالنُّجْمِ), lightened from the form with ḍamma.

ukberi-tibyan:2-2.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يُنَزِّلُ الْمَلَائِكَةَ بِالرُّوحِ مِنْ أَمْرِهِ عَلَى مَنْ يَشَاءُ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ أَنْ أَنْذِرُوا أَنَّهُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنَا فَاتَّقُونِ (٢)).
The Exalted's saying (يُنَزِّلُ الْمَلَائِكَةَ): there are (several) readings of it, and their justifications are clear.
And (بِالرُّوحِ) is in the position of the accusative (naṣb) as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الْمَلَائِكَة, i.e. "with the spirit accompanying them", which is the revelation. And (مِنْ أَمْرِهِ) is a ḥāl from الرُّوح.
(أَنْ أَنْذِرُوا): أَنْ has the sense of أَيْ ("that is"), because the revelation implies speech, so it is explained by أَنْ; thus it has no grammatical position.
It may also be maṣdariyya, in the position of the genitive (jarr) as a badal (substitute) for الرُّوح, or (genitive) by an implied preposition according to the view of al-Khalīl, or in the position of the accusative according to the view of Sībawayh.
(أَنَّهُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنَا): the clause is in the position of the accusative as the object of «أَنْذِرُوا», i.e. "inform them of the oneness of Allah"; then He turned from the third person to direct address, saying «فَاتَّقُونِ».

ukberi-tibyan:21-21.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَمْوَاتٌ غَيْرُ أَحْيَاءٍ وَمَا يَشْعُرُونَ أَيَّانَ يُبْعَثُونَ (٢١)).
The Exalted's saying (أَمْوَاتٌ): if you wish, you make it a second khabar (predicate) of «هُمْ», i.e. "and they are created and die". If you wish, you make «يُخْلَقُونَ وَأَمْوَاتٌ» a single khabar. And if you wish, it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "they are dead".
The Exalted's saying (غَيْرُ أَحْيَاءٍ): an emphasising adjective (ṣifa muʾakkida).
It may also be that He intended by it that they are not alive at present, to remove the misconception that His saying «أَمْوَاتٌ» refers to what comes later, since the Exalted has said (إِنَّكَ مَيِّتٌ), i.e. "you will die".
And (أَيَّانَ) is accusative by «يُبْعَثُونَ», not by «يَشْعُرُونَ».

ukberi-tibyan:24-24.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمْ مَاذَا أَنْزَلَ رَبُّكُمْ قَالُوا أَسَاطِيرُ الْأَوَّلِينَ (٢٤)).
The Exalted's saying (مَاذَا أَنْزَلَ رَبُّكُمْ): concerning «مَاذَا» there are two views:
The first: «مَا» in it is interrogative and «ذَا» means الَّذِي (that which) — this has been mentioned in (Surat) al-Baqara — and the returning pronoun is omitted, i.e. أَنْزَلَهُ. [Translator's note: the second view is not stated in the source.]
And (أَسَاطِيرُ) is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being: "what you claim to be sent down is legends".
It is also read أَسَاطِيرَ in the accusative, the implied wording being "and you mentioned legends", or "He sent down legends", in mockery.

ukberi-tibyan:25-25.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لِيَحْمِلُوا أَوْزَارَهُمْ كَامِلَةً يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ وَمِنْ أَوْزَارِ الَّذِينَ يُضِلُّونَهُمْ بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ أَلَا سَاءَ مَا يَزِرُونَ (٢٥)).
The Exalted's saying (لِيَحْمِلُوا): i.e. "they said that, so that they would bear"; it is the lām of outcome (lām al-ʿāqiba).
(وَمِنْ أَوْزَارِ الَّذِينَ): i.e. "and the burdens of those who".
Al-Akhfash said: «مِنْ» is redundant (zāʾida).

ukberi-tibyan:26-26.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَدْ مَكَرَ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ فَأَتَى اللَّهُ بُنْيَانَهُمْ مِنَ الْقَوَاعِدِ فَخَرَّ عَلَيْهِمُ السَّقْفُ مِنْ فَوْقِهِمْ وَأَتَاهُمُ الْعَذَابُ مِنْ حَيْثُ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ (٢٦)).
The Exalted's saying (مِنَ الْقَوَاعِدِ): i.e. "from the direction of the foundations"; and the implied wording is "the command of Allah came".
(مِنْ فَوْقِهِمْ): «مِنْ» may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to خَرَّ, «مِنْ» being for the beginning of the extent (ibtidāʾ al-ghāya); or it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "being from above them". On both views it is a tawkīd (emphasis).

ukberi-tibyan:27-27.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (ثُمَّ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ يُخْزِيهِمْ وَيَقُولُ أَيْنَ شُرَكَائِيَ الَّذِينَ كُنْتُمْ تُشَاقُّونَ فِيهِمْ قَالَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْعِلْمَ إِنَّ الْخِزْيَ الْيَوْمَ وَالسُّوءَ عَلَى الْكَافِرِينَ (٢٧)).
The Exalted's saying (تُشَاقُّونَ): it is read with fatḥa on the nūn, the object being omitted, i.e. "you oppose the believers" or "you oppose Me".
It is also read with kasra on it with tashdīd (تُشَاقُّونِّ), the nūn of the nominative being assimilated into the nūn of protection (nūn al-wiqāya).
It is also read with kasra and without tashdīd (تُشَاقُّونِ), and that is like (فَبِمَ تُبَشِّرُونِ), which has been mentioned.
The Exalted's saying (إِنَّ الْخِزْيَ الْيَوْمَ): concerning the governor (ʿāmil) of the adverbial (ẓarf) there are two views. The first: الْخِزْي, which is a maṣdar (verbal noun) with the alif and lām. The second: it is governed by the khabar (predicate), which is the Exalted's saying (عَلَى الْكَافِرِينَ), i.e. "is upon the disbelievers today"; the two were separated by the conjoined (noun) because of their latitude with the ẓarf.

ukberi-tibyan:28-28.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (الَّذِينَ تَتَوَفَّاهُمُ الْمَلَائِكَةُ ظَالِمِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ فَأَلْقَوُا السَّلَمَ مَا كُنَّا نَعْمَلُ مِنْ سُوءٍ بَلَى إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ بِمَا كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ (٢٨)).
The Exalted's saying (الَّذِينَ تَتَوَفَّاهُمُ): (it may be) in the genitive, the accusative or the nominative; this has been mentioned in (several) places. And (تَتَوَفَّاهُمُ) means تَوَفَّتْهُمْ ("took them in death").
(فَأَلْقَوُا السَّلَمَ): it may be maʿṭūf (conjoined) to (قَالَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْعِلْمَ).
It may also be conjoined to تَوَفَّاهُمُ.
It may also be resumptive (mustaʾnaf).
And (السَّلَمَ) here means speech, as He said in the other verse (فَأَلْقَوْا إِلَيْهِمُ الْقَوْلَ). On this view, «مَا كُنَّا نَعْمَلُ مِنْ سُوءٍ» may be an explanation (tafsīr) of the السَّلَم which they offered; it may also be resumptive; and the implied wording may also be "so they offered submission, saying: we were not …".

ukberi-tibyan:4-4.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (خَلَقَ الْإِنْسَانَ مِنْ نُطْفَةٍ فَإِذَا هُوَ خَصِيمٌ مُبِينٌ (٤)).
The Exalted's saying (فَإِذَا هُوَ خَصِيمٌ): if it is said: the fāʾ indicates immediate sequence (taʿqīb), yet his being an adversary does not come immediately after his creation from a drop of sperm — the answer is in two ways:
The first: He pointed to what his state will end up as, treating the awaited as if it had occurred; this belongs to the category of expressing the beginning of a matter by its end, as in His saying (أَرَانِي أَعْصِرُ خَمْرًا), and the Exalted's saying (وَيُنَزِّلُ لَكُمْ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ رِزْقًا), i.e. the cause of provision, which is rain.
The second: it is a pointer to how quickly they forget the beginning of their creation.

ukberi-tibyan:5-6.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَالْأَنْعَامَ خَلَقَهَا لَكُمْ فِيهَا دِفْءٌ وَمَنَافِعُ وَمِنْهَا تَأْكُلُونَ (٥) وَلَكُمْ فِيهَا جَمَالٌ حِينَ تُرِيحُونَ وَحِينَ تَسْرَحُونَ (٦)).
The Exalted's saying (وَالْأَنْعَامَ): it is accusative (manṣūb) by an omitted verb; its nominative has been reported among the irregular (shādhdh) readings. And concerning (لَكُمْ) there are two views:
The first: it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to خَلَقَ; so «فِيهَا دِفْءٌ» is a clause in the position of the ḥāl (circumstantial) from the accusative pronoun.
The second: it is attached to something omitted; so دِفْءٌ is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and the khabar (predicate) is لَكُمْ.
Concerning «فِيهَا» there are two views:
The first: it is an adverbial (ẓarf) for the (notion of) settledness (al-istiqrār) in «لَكُمْ».
The second: it is a ḥāl from «دِفْءٌ». «لَكُمْ» may also be a ḥāl from «دِفْءٌ», with «فِيهَا» as the khabar. «دِفْءٌ» may also be nominative by لَكُمْ or by فِيهَا, the whole clause being a ḥāl from the accusative pronoun.
It is also read «دِفٌ» with ḍamma on the fāʾ and without hamza; its justification is that he cast the vowel of the hamza onto the fāʾ and dropped it.
And (لَكُمْ فِيهَا دِفْءٌ) is like «وَلَكُمْ فِيهَا دِفْءٌ». [Translator's note: so in the source; presumably what is meant is that (وَلَكُمْ فِيهَا جَمَالٌ) in verse 6 is analysed like (لَكُمْ فِيهَا دِفْءٌ) in verse 5.]
And (حِينَ) is an adverbial (ẓarf) for جَمَالٍ, or an adjective (ṣifa) for it, or governed by فِيهَا.

ukberi-tibyan:7-7.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَتَحْمِلُ أَثْقَالَكُمْ إِلَى بَلَدٍ لَمْ تَكُونُوا بَالِغِيهِ إِلَّا بِشِقِ الْأَنْفُسِ إِنَّ رَبَّكُمْ لَرَءُوفٌ رَحِيمٌ (٧)).
The Exalted's saying (بَالِغِيهِ): the hāʾ is in the position of the genitive (jarr) by annexation according to the majority. Al-Akhfash permitted it to be accusative, citing as evidence the Exalted's saying (إِنَّا مُنَجُّوكَ وَأَهْلَكَ); this will be dealt with fully in its place, if Allah the Exalted wills.
(إِلَّا بِشِقِّ): in the position of the ḥāl (circumstantial) from the nominative pronoun in «بَالِغِيهِ», i.e. "with hardship being laid upon you". The majority read it with kasra on the shīn; it has been read with fatḥa on it, and that is a dialectal form.

ukberi-tibyan:8-8.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَالْخَيْلَ وَالْبِغَالَ وَالْحَمِيرَ لِتَرْكَبُوهَا وَزِينَةً وَيَخْلُقُ مَا لَا تَعْلَمُونَ (٨)).
The Exalted's saying (وَالْخَيْلَ): it is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to الْأَنْعَام, i.e. "and He created horses".
And (زِينَةً): i.e. "that you may ride them, and that you may adorn yourselves with them as an adornment"; so it is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of an omitted verb.
It may also be a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. "and for adornment". It is also said that the implied wording is "and He made them an adornment".
It is also read without the wāw, and the views mentioned apply to it, along with two other views:
The first: that it is a maṣdar in the position of the ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in تَرْكَبُوا. The second: that it is a ḥāl from the hāʾ, i.e. "that you may ride them, adorning yourselves with them".

ukberi-tibyan:9-9.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَعَلَى اللَّهِ قَصْدُ السَّبِيلِ وَمِنْهَا جَائِرٌ وَلَوْ شَاءَ لَهَدَاكُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ (٩)).
The Exalted's saying (وَمِنْهَا جَائِرٌ): the pronoun refers back to السَّبِيل, which is treated as both masculine and feminine. It is also said: السَّبِيل has the sense of السُّبُل (paths), so it was made feminine according to the meaning.
And (قَصْدُ) is a maṣdar (verbal noun) meaning making the way straight, or making the way even; it is not the maṣdar of قَصَدْتُهُ in the sense of "I went to it".

ukberi-tibyan:30-30.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَقِيلَ لِلَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا مَاذَا أَنْزَلَ رَبُّكُمْ قَالُوا خَيْرًا لِلَّذِينَ أَحْسَنُوا فِي هَذِهِ الدُّنْيَا حَسَنَةٌ وَلَدَارُ الْآخِرَةِ خَيْرٌ وَلَنِعْمَ دَارُ الْمُتَّقِينَ (٣٠)).
The Exalted's saying (مَاذَا أَنْزَلَ رَبُّكُمْ): «مَا» is in the position of the accusative (naṣb) by أَنْزَلَ; this is indicated by the accusative of the answer, which is His saying (قَالُوا خَيْرًا), i.e. "He sent down good".

ukberi-tibyan:31-31.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (جَنَّاتُ عَدْنٍ يَدْخُلُونَهَا تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ لَهُمْ فِيهَا مَا يَشَاءُونَ كَذَلِكَ يَجْزِي اللَّهُ الْمُتَّقِينَ (٣١)).
The Exalted's saying (جَنَّاتُ عَدْنٍ): it may be the one specified for praise (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-madḥ), like زَيْد in نِعْمَ الرَّجُلُ زَيْدٌ ("an excellent man is Zayd").
And (يَدْخُلُونَهَا) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from it. It (جَنَّاتُ عَدْنٍ) may also be resumptive (mustaʾnaf), with «يَدْخُلُونَهَا» as the khabar (predicate).
The khabar may also be omitted, i.e. "for them are the Gardens of ʿAdn"; this is indicated by the Exalted's saying (لِلَّذِينَ أَحْسَنُوا فِي هَذِهِ الدُّنْيَا حَسَنَةٌ).
(كَذَلِكَ يَجْزِي): the kāf is in the position of the accusative (naṣb) as a naʿt (adjective) for an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun).

ukberi-tibyan:32-32.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (الَّذِينَ تَتَوَفَّاهُمُ الْمَلَائِكَةُ طَيِّبِينَ يَقُولُونَ سَلَامٌ عَلَيْكُمُ ادْخُلُوا الْجَنَّةَ بِمَا كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ (٣٢)).
The Exalted's saying (طَيِّبِينَ): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the object; and «يَقُولُونَ» is a ḥāl from الْمَلَائِكَة.

ukberi-tibyan:36-36.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَقَدْ بَعَثْنَا فِي كُلِّ أُمَّةٍ رَسُولًا أَنِ اعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ وَاجْتَنِبُوا الطَّاغُوتَ فَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ هَدَى اللَّهُ وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ حَقَّتْ عَلَيْهِ الضَّلَالَةُ فَسِيرُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ فَانْظُرُوا كَيْفَ كَانَ عَاقِبَةُ الْمُكَذِّبِينَ (٣٦)).
The Exalted's saying (أَنِ اُعْبُدُوا): «أَنْ» may have the sense of أَيْ ("that is"), or it may be maṣdariyya.
(مَنْ هَدَى): مَنْ is an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective (nakira mawṣūfa), a mubtadaʾ (subject), and what precedes it is the khabar (predicate).

ukberi-tibyan:37-37.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنْ تَحْرِصْ عَلَى هُدَاهُمْ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَهْدِي مَنْ يُضِلُّ وَمَا لَهُمْ مِنْ نَاصِرِينَ (٣٧)).
The Exalted's saying (فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَهْدِي): it is read with fatḥa on the yāʾ and kasra on the dāl, with the agent named (active voice). لَا يَهْدِي is the khabar (predicate) of إِنَّ, and «مَنْ يُضِلُّ» is the object of يَهْدِي.
It is also read «لَا يَهْدِي» with ḍamma on the yāʾ, as a verb whose agent is not named (passive) [Translator's note: i.e. لَا يُهْدَى], and there are two views on it:
The first: «مَنْ يُضِلُّ» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «لَا يَهْدِي» is a khabar. The second: «لَا يَهْدِي مَنْ يُضِلُّ» as a whole is the khabar of إِنَّ, as in your saying إِنَّ زَيْدًا لَا يُضْرَبُ أَبُوهُ ("Zayd — his father is not beaten").

ukberi-tibyan:40-40.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّمَا قَوْلُنَا لِشَيْءٍ إِذَا أَرَدْنَاهُ أَنْ نَقُولَ لَهُ كُنْ فَيَكُونُ (٤٠))
The Exalted's saying (فَيَكُونُ): it is read in the nominative, i.e. "then it is", and in the accusative, conjoined to نَقُولَ. Making it the answer to the imperative is far-fetched, for the reason we mentioned in (Surat) al-Baqara.

ukberi-tibyan:41-41.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَالَّذِينَ هَاجَرُوا فِي اللَّهِ مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا ظُلِمُوا لَنُبَوِّئَنَّهُمْ فِي الدُّنْيَا حَسَنَةً وَلَأَجْرُ الْآخِرَةِ أَكْبَرُ لَوْ كَانُوا يَعْلَمُونَ (٤١)).
The Exalted's saying (وَالَّذِينَ هَاجَرُوا): a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «لَنُبَوِّئَنَّهُمْ» is the khabar (predicate).
It may also be in the position of the accusative (naṣb) by an omitted verb which the mentioned one explains.
(حَسَنَةً): the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of نُبَوِّئَنَّهُمْ, because its meaning is "We will surely give them".
It may also be an adjective (ṣifa) for something omitted, i.e. "a good abode", because بَوَّأْتَهُ means "you lodged him".

ukberi-tibyan:42-42.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (الَّذِينَ صَبَرُوا وَعَلَى رَبِّهِمْ يَتَوَكَّلُونَ (٤٢)).
The Exalted's saying (الَّذِينَ صَبَرُوا): in the position of the nominative (rafʿ) on the implication of هُمْ ("they are"), or of the accusative (naṣb) on the assumption of أَعْنِي ("I mean").

ukberi-tibyan:44-44.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (بِالْبَيِّنَاتِ وَالزُّبُرِ وَأَنْزَلْنَا إِلَيْكَ الذِّكْرَ لِتُبَيِّنَ لِلنَّاسِ مَا نُزِّلَ إِلَيْهِمْ وَلَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ (٤٤)).
The Exalted's saying (بِالْبَيِّنَاتِ): concerning what the bāʾ is attached (mutaʿalliq) to there are three views. The first: to «نُوحِي», as you say أَوْحَى إِلَيْهِ بِحَقٍّ ("he revealed to him with truth"); (on this view) the bāʾ may also be redundant (zāʾida); or it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from what stands in place of the agent (the deputy agent), namely «إِلَيْهِمْ». The second view: that it is attached to أَرْسَلْنَا, i.e. "We sent them with the clear proofs". There is weakness in this, because what precedes «إِلَّا» does not govern what comes after it once the speech is complete with إِلَّا and what follows it; however, it has occurred in poetry, as in the poet's saying:
نُبِّئْتُهُمْ عَذَّبُوا بِالنَّارِ جَارَتَهُمْ ... وَلَا يُعَذِّبُ إِلَّا اللَّهُ بِالنَّارِ
(I was told that they tortured their female neighbour with fire — and none but Allah punishes with fire.)
The third view: that it is attached to something omitted, its implied form being "they were sent with the clear proofs". And Allah knows best.

ukberi-tibyan:47-47.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَوْ يَأْخُذَهُمْ عَلَى تَخَوُّفٍ فَإِنَّ رَبَّكُمْ لَرَءُوفٌ رَحِيمٌ (٤٧)).
The Exalted's saying (عَلَى تَخَوُّفٍ): in the position of the ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent, or from the object, in His saying «أَوْ يَأْخُذَهُمْ».

ukberi-tibyan:48-48.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا إِلَى مَا خَلَقَ اللَّهُ مِنْ شَيْءٍ يَتَفَيَّأُ ظِلَالُهُ عَنِ الْيَمِينِ وَالشَّمَائِلِ سُجَّدًا لِلَّهِ وَهُمْ دَاخِرُونَ (٤٨)).
The Exalted's saying (أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا): it is read with yāʾ and with tāʾ; before it there is both the third person and direct address, which justify both. (يَتَفَيَّأُ): it is read with tāʾ, in accordance with the femininity of the plural which is the agent, and with yāʾ because the femininity is not real. (عَنِ الْيَمِينِ): the singular was put in place of the plural. It is also said: the shade first appears from the right, then moves and spreads out from the left, and its spreading calls for the plural. And (عَنْ) is a preposition whose position is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). It may also be for passing beyond (al-mujāwaza), i.e. the shades pass beyond the right to the left. It is also said: it is a noun, i.e. "the side of the right".
And (الشَّمَائِلِ) is the plural of شِمَال. (سُجَّدًا): a ḥāl from الظِّلَال. And (هُمْ دَاخِرُونَ) is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «سُجَّدًا»; it may also be a second ḥāl, conjoined.

ukberi-tibyan:49-49.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلِلَّهِ يَسْجُدُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ مِنْ دَابَّةٍ وَالْمَلَائِكَةُ وَهُمْ لَا يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ (٤٩)).
The Exalted's saying (مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ): He mentioned «مَا» rather than «مَنْ» only because it is more general, and the prostration includes all.

ukberi-tibyan:50-50.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَخَافُونَ رَبَّهُمْ مِنْ فَوْقِهِمْ وَيَفْعَلُونَ مَا يُؤْمَرُونَ (٥٠)).
The Exalted's saying (مِنْ فَوْقِهِمْ): it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from رَبَّهُمْ. It may also be attached (mutaʿalliq) to يَخَافُونَ.

ukberi-tibyan:51-51.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَقَالَ اللَّهُ لَا تَتَّخِذُوا إِلَهَيْنِ اثْنَيْنِ إِنَّمَا هُوَ إِلَهٌ وَاحِدٌ فَإِيَّايَ فَارْهَبُونِ (٥١)).
The Exalted's saying (اثْنَيْنِ): it is a tawkīd (emphasis). It is also said: a second object; and that is far-fetched.

ukberi-tibyan:52-52.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَهُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَلَهُ الدِّينُ وَاصِبًا أَفَغَيْرَ اللَّهِ تَتَّقُونَ (٥٢)).
The Exalted's saying (وَاصِبًا): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الدِّين.

ukberi-tibyan:53-53.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَا بِكُمْ مِنْ نِعْمَةٍ فَمِنَ اللَّهِ ثُمَّ إِذَا مَسَّكُمُ الضُّرُّ فَإِلَيْهِ تَجْأَرُونَ (٥٣)).
The Exalted's saying (وَمَا بِكُمْ): «مَا» means الَّذِي (that which), and the preposition (phrase) is its ṣila (relative clause).
And «مِنْ نِعْمَةٍ» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in the preposition (phrase). (فَمِنَ اللَّهِ): the khabar (predicate).
It is also said: «مَا» is conditional, and the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) is omitted, i.e. "whatever is"; and the fāʾ is (that of) the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ).

ukberi-tibyan:54-54.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (ثُمَّ إِذَا كَشَفَ الضُّرَّ عَنْكُمْ إِذَا فَرِيقٌ مِنْكُمْ بِرَبِّهِمْ يُشْرِكُونَ (٥٤)).
The Exalted's saying (إِذَا فَرِيقٌ): it (فَرِيقٌ) is the fāʿil (agent) of an omitted verb.

ukberi-tibyan:55-55.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لِيَكْفُرُوا بِمَا آتَيْنَاهُمْ فَتَمَتَّعُوا فَسَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ (٥٥)).
The Exalted's saying (فَتَمَتَّعُوا): the majority take it as an imperative. It is also read with yāʾ (فَيَتَمَتَّعُوا), and it is then conjoined to يَكْفُرُوا; then He returned to direct address, saying «فَسَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ». This has also been read with yāʾ.

ukberi-tibyan:57-57.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَيَجْعَلُونَ لِلَّهِ الْبَنَاتِ سُبْحَانَهُ وَلَهُمْ مَا يَشْتَهُونَ (٥٧)).
The Exalted's saying (وَلَهُمْ مَا يَشْتَهُونَ): «مَا» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and لَهُمْ its khabar (predicate); or (مَا is) the agent of the adverbial (ẓarf).
It is also said: «مَا» is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to (نَصِيبًا), i.e. "and they assign what they desire to themselves".
A group declared this view weak, saying: if it were so, He would have said وَلِأَنْفُسِهِمْ ("and for themselves"); but this is open to consideration.

ukberi-tibyan:58-58.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِذَا بُشِّرَ أَحَدُهُمْ بِالْأُنْثَى ظَلَّ وَجْهُهُ مُسْوَدًّا وَهُوَ كَظِيمٌ (٥٨)).
The Exalted's saying (ظَلَّ وَجْهُهُ مُسْوَدًّا): (مُسْوَدًّا is) its khabar (predicate). Had «مُسْوَدٌّ» been read, it would have been sound, on the basis that the noun of ظَلَّ is a pronoun concealed in it and the clause is its khabar.
And (هُوَ كَظِيمٌ) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the owner of the face. It may also be from الْوَجْه, because it is part of him.

ukberi-tibyan:59-59.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَتَوَارَى مِنَ الْقَوْمِ مِنْ سُوءٍ مَا بُشِّرَ بِهِ أَيُمْسِكُهُ عَلَى هُونٍ أَمْ يَدُسُّهُ فِي التُّرَابِ أَلَا سَاءَ مَا يَحْكُمُونَ (٥٩)).
The Exalted's saying (يَتَوَارَى): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «كَظِيمٌ».
(أَيُمْسِكُهُ): in the position of the ḥāl; its implied form is "he hides, hesitating: shall he keep it or not?".
(عَلَى هُونٍ): a ḥāl.

ukberi-tibyan:62-62.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَيَجْعَلُونَ لِلَّهِ مَا يَكْرَهُونَ وَتَصِفُ أَلْسِنَتُهُمُ الْكَذِبَ أَنَّ لَهُمُ الْحُسْنَى لَا جَرَمَ أَنَّ لَهُمُ النَّارَ وَأَنَّهُمْ مُفْرَطُونَ (٦٢)).
The Exalted's saying (وَتَصِفُ أَلْسِنَتُهُمُ الْكَذِبَ): it is read in the accusative, as the object of تَصِفُ, or it is a badal (substitute) for مَا يَكْرَهُونَ. On this (reading), there are two views on His saying (أَنَّ لَهُمُ الْحُسْنَى). The first: it is a badal for الْكَذِب. The second: its implied form is بِأَنَّ لَهُمْ, and when the bāʾ was dropped it came to be in the position of the accusative according to al-Khalīl, while according to Sībawayh it is in the position of the genitive.
It is also read الْكُذُبُ with ḍamma on the kāf, the dhāl and the bāʾ, as an adjective (ṣifa) for الْأَلْسِنَة; it is a plural whose singular is كَذُوب, like صَبُور and صُبُر. On this reading the singular of الْأَلْسِنَة may be masculine or feminine, and both usages have been heard for اللِّسَان. On this reading «أَنَّ لَهُمُ الْحُسْنَى» is the object of تَصِفُ.
(لَا جَرَمَ): this has been mentioned fully in (Surat) Hūd.
(مُفْرَطُونَ): it is read with fatḥa on the rāʾ and without tashdīd; it is from أَفْرَطَ, when someone else leads him into negligence. And with kasra (مُفْرِطُونَ), attributing the act to them. And with kasra and tashdīd (مُفَرِّطُونَ), which is clear.

ukberi-tibyan:64-64.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَا أَنْزَلْنَا عَلَيْكَ الْكِتَابَ إِلَّا لِتُبَيِّنَ لَهُمُ الَّذِي اخْتَلَفُوا فِيهِ وَهُدًى وَرَحْمَةً لِقَوْمٍ يُؤْمِنُونَ (٦٤)).
The Exalted's saying (وَهُدًى وَرَحْمَةً): the two are conjoined to «لِتُبَيِّنَ», i.e. "for making clear, and for guidance and mercy".

ukberi-tibyan:66-66.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِنَّ لَكُمْ فِي الْأَنْعَامِ لَعِبْرَةً نُسْقِيكُمْ مِمَّا فِي بُطُونِهِ مِنْ بَيْنِ فَرْثٍ وَدَمٍ لَبَنًا خَالِصًا سَائِغًا لِلشَّارِبِينَ (٦٦)).
The Exalted's saying (بُطُونِهِ): concerning what the hāʾ refers back to there are six views. The first: الْأَنْعَام is treated as masculine and feminine, so the pronoun was made masculine according to one of the two usages. The second: الْأَنْعَام is a generic noun (jins), so the pronoun refers back to it according to the meaning. The third: the singular of الْأَنْعَام is نَعَم, and the pronoun refers back to its singular, as the poet said:
مِثْلُ الْفِرَاخِ نُتِّفَتْ حَوَاصِلُهْ
(Like chicks whose crops have been plucked.)
The fourth: it refers back to "what has been mentioned", so its implied form is "from what is in the bellies of what has been mentioned", as al-Ḥuṭayʾa said:
لِزُغْبٍ كَأَوْلَادِ الْقَطَا رَاثَ خَلْفُهَا ... عَلَى عَاجِزَاتِ النَّهْضِ حُمْرٍ حَوَاصِلُهْ
(For downy little ones like the young of the sandgrouse, whose provider was slow in coming to them — unable to rise, their crops red.)
The fifth: it refers back to that part of them which has milk.
The sixth: it refers back to the stallion, because milk comes from the stallion's covering the she-camel, so the origin of the milk is the stallion's water. This is weak, because even if the milk is attributed to the stallion, He made البُطُون plural, and the stallion of the livestock is not one, nor does one have (several) bellies; and if (someone) says: He meant the genus, then that has already been mentioned.
(مِنْ بَيْنِ): in the position of the accusative as an adverbial (ẓarf). It may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «مَا» or from اللَّبَن.
(سَائِغًا): the majority read it on the pattern fāʿil. It is also read «سَيِّغًا» with a doubled yāʾ, like سَيِّد and مَيِّت; its origin is from the wāw.

ukberi-tibyan:67-67.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمِنْ ثَمَرَاتِ النَّخِيلِ وَالْأَعْنَابِ تَتَّخِذُونَ مِنْهُ سَكَرًا وَرِزْقًا حَسَنًا إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لَآيَةً لِقَوْمٍ يَعْقِلُونَ (٦٧)).
The Exalted's saying (وَمِنْ ثَمَرَاتِ): the preposition (phrase) is attached (mutaʿalliq) to something omitted, its implied form being "and He created for you" or "and He made".
(تَتَّخِذُونَ): resumptive (mustaʾnaf). It is also said: an adjective (ṣifa) for something omitted, its implied form being "something (شَيْئًا) you take", in the accusative, i.e. "and among the fruits is something".
And if you wish: «شَيْءٌ» in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), with «مِنْ ثَمَرَاتِ» as its khabar (predicate). It is also said that the implied wording is "and you take from the fruits of the date-palms intoxicant", and He repeated «مِنْ» since He placed (some words) before and (others) after.
The pronoun was made masculine because it refers back to the omitted «شَيْء», or to the meaning of الثَّمَرَات, which is الثَّمَر, or to النَّخْل, i.e. "from the fruit of the date-palms", or to "the part", or to "what has been mentioned", as was said earlier on the «hāʾ» of بُطُونِهِ.

ukberi-tibyan:68-68.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَأَوْحَى رَبُّكَ إِلَى النَّحْلِ أَنِ اتَّخِذِي مِنَ الْجِبَالِ بُيُوتًا وَمِنَ الشَّجَرِ وَمِمَّا يَعْرِشُونَ (٦٨)).
The Exalted's saying (أَنِ اتَّخِذِي): i.e. "(namely) take"; or it is maṣdariyya.

ukberi-tibyan:69-69.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (ثُمَّ كُلِي مِنْ كُلِّ الثَّمَرَاتِ فَاسْلُكِي سُبُلَ رَبِّكِ ذُلُلًا يَخْرُجُ مِنْ بُطُونِهَا شَرَابٌ مُخْتَلِفٌ أَلْوَانُهُ فِيهِ شِفَاءٌ لِلنَّاسِ إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لَآيَةً لِقَوْمٍ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ (٦٩)).
The Exalted's saying (ذُلُلًا): it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from السُّبُل, or from the pronoun in «اسْلُكِي»; its singular is ذَلُول. Then He turned from direct address to the third person, saying «يَخْرُجُ مِنْ بُطُونِهَا».
(فِيهِ شِفَاءٌ): (the pronoun) refers back to الشَّرَاب; it is also said: to the Qur'an.

ukberi-tibyan:70-70.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَاللَّهُ خَلَقَكُمْ ثُمَّ يَتَوَفَّاكُمْ وَمِنْكُمْ مَنْ يُرَدُّ إِلَى أَرْذَلِ الْعُمُرِ لِكَيْ لَا يَعْلَمَ بَعْدَ عِلْمٍ شَيْئًا إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ قَدِيرٌ (٧٠)).
The Exalted's saying (لَا يَعْلَمَ بَعْدَ عِلْمٍ شَيْئًا): «شَيْئًا» is accusative by the maṣdar (verbal noun) according to the view of the Basrans, and by يَعْلَمَ according to the view of the Kufans.

ukberi-tibyan:71-71.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَاللَّهُ فَضَّلَ بَعْضَكُمْ عَلَى بَعْضٍ فِي الرِّزْقِ فَمَا الَّذِينَ فُضِّلُوا بِرَادِّي رِزْقِهِمْ عَلَى مَا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَانُهُمْ فَهُمْ فِيهِ سَوَاءٌ أَفَبِنِعْمَةِ اللَّهِ يَجْحَدُونَ (٧١)).
The Exalted's saying (فَهُمْ فِيهِ سَوَاءٌ): the clause of mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate) here stands in the place of a verb and its agent; the implied wording is: "those who were favoured would not hand over their provision to those whom their right hands possess so that they would be equal (فَيَسْتَوُوا)"; and this verb is accusative as the answer to the negation. It may also be nominative, conjoined to the position of بِرَادِّي, i.e. "those who were favoured do not hand over, so they are not equal".

ukberi-tibyan:73-73.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَيَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ مَا لَا يَمْلِكُ لَهُمْ رِزْقًا مِنَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ شَيْئًا وَلَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ (٧٣)).
The Exalted's saying (رِزْقًا مِنَ السَّمَاوَاتِ): الرِّزْق with kasra on the rāʾ is the name of what is provided.
It is also said: it is a noun of the maṣdar (ism al-maṣdar), the maṣdar being with fatḥa on the rāʾ (الرَّزْق). (شَيْئًا): there are three views on it:
The first: it is accusative by رِزْق, because the noun of the maṣdar governs as the maṣdar does, i.e. "they cannot provide anything". The second: it is a badal (substitute) for رِزْق.
The third: it is accusative in the manner of the maṣdar, i.e. "they do not possess provision in any way at all". We have mentioned parallels of it, such as His saying (لَا يَضُرُّكُمْ كَيْدُهُمْ شَيْئًا).

ukberi-tibyan:75-75.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (ضَرَبَ اللَّهُ مَثَلًا عَبْدًا مَمْلُوكًا لَا يَقْدِرُ عَلَى شَيْءٍ وَمَنْ رَزَقْنَاهُ مِنَّا رِزْقًا حَسَنًا فَهُوَ يُنْفِقُ مِنْهُ سِرًّا وَجَهْرًا هَلْ يَسْتَوُونَ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ بَلْ أَكْثَرُهُمْ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ (٧٥)).
The Exalted's saying (عَبْدًا): it is a badal (substitute) for مَثَل. It is also said that the implied wording is "a parable like a slave".
And (مَنْ) is in the position of the accusative, as an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective (nakira mawṣūfa).
(سِرًّا وَجَهْرًا): two maṣdars (verbal nouns) in the position of the ḥāl (circumstantial).

ukberi-tibyan:76-76.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَضَرَبَ اللَّهُ مَثَلًا رَجُلَيْنِ أَحَدُهُمَا أَبْكَمُ لَا يَقْدِرُ عَلَى شَيْءٍ وَهُوَ كَلٌّ عَلَى مَوْلَاهُ أَيْنَمَا يُوَجِّهْهُ لَا يَأْتِ بِخَيْرٍ هَلْ يَسْتَوِي هُوَ وَمَنْ يَأْمُرُ بِالْعَدْلِ وَهُوَ عَلَى صِرَاطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ (٧٦)).
The Exalted's saying (أَيْنَمَا يُوَجِّهْهُ): it is read with kasra on the jīm, i.e. "his master directs him".
It is also read with fatḥa on the jīm and sukūn on the hāʾ, as a verb whose agent is not named (passive).
It is also read with tāʾ and fatḥa on the jīm and the hāʾ, in the form of the past.

ukberi-tibyan:77-77.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلِلَّهِ غَيْبُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَمَا أَمْرُ السَّاعَةِ إِلَّا كَلَمْحِ الْبَصَرِ أَوْ هُوَ أَقْرَبُ إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ (٧٧)).
The Exalted's saying (أَوْ هُوَ أَقْرَبُ): هُوَ is a pronoun for الْأَمْر; and the ruling on «أَوْ» has been mentioned at (أَوْ كَصَيِّبٍ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ).

ukberi-tibyan:78-78.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَاللَّهُ أَخْرَجَكُمْ مِنْ بُطُونِ أُمَّهَاتِكُمْ لَا تَعْلَمُونَ شَيْئًا وَجَعَلَ لَكُمُ السَّمْعَ وَالْأَبْصَارَ وَالْأَفْئِدَةَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ (٧٨)).
The Exalted's saying (أُمَّهَاتِكُمْ): it is read with ḍamma on the hamza and fatḥa on the mīm, which is the original, and with kasra on both.
As for the kasra of the hamza, it is for a reason: it is said that it was made to follow the kasra of the nūn before it; and the kasra of the mīm is in harmony (itbāʿ) with the kasra of the hamza.
(لَا تَعْلَمُونَ شَيْئًا): the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the accusative pronoun in «أَخْرَجَكُمْ».

ukberi-tibyan:79-79.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَلَمْ يَرَوْا إِلَى الطَّيْرِ مُسَخَّرَاتٍ فِي جَوِّ السَّمَاءِ مَا يُمْسِكُهُنَّ إِلَّا اللَّهُ إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لَآيَاتٍ لِقَوْمٍ يُؤْمِنُونَ (٧٩)).
The Exalted's saying (أَلَمْ يَرَوْا): it is read with tāʾ because before it there is direct address, and with yāʾ as a return to the third person.
(مَا يُمْسِكُهُنَّ): the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in مُسَخَّرَاتٍ, or from الطَّيْر. It may also be resumptive (mustaʾnaf).

ukberi-tibyan:80-80.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَاللَّهُ جَعَلَ لَكُمْ مِنْ بُيُوتِكُمْ سَكَنًا وَجَعَلَ لَكُمْ مِنْ جُلُودِ الْأَنْعَامِ بُيُوتًا تَسْتَخِفُّونَهَا يَوْمَ ظَعْنِكُمْ وَيَوْمَ إِقَامَتِكُمْ وَمِنْ أَصْوَافِهَا وَأَوْبَارِهَا وَأَشْعَارِهَا أَثَاثًا وَمَتَاعًا إِلَى حِينٍ (٨٠)).
The Exalted's saying (مِنْ بُيُوتِكُمْ سَكَنًا): it is singular only because the meaning is "what you dwell in".
(يَوْمَ ظَعْنِكُمْ): it is read with sukūn on the ʿayn and with fatḥa on it; they are two dialectal forms, like النَّهْر and النَّهَر. الظَّعْن is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of ظَعَنَ ("to travel").
(أَثَاثًا): conjoined to «سَكَنًا». It is separated from the conjunction by the preposition and its genitive noun, namely the Exalted's saying (وَمِنْ أَصْوَافِهَا). This is not an objectionable separation, as was claimed in al-Īḍāḥ, because the preposition and its genitive noun is an object, and placing one object before another is regular (qiyās).

ukberi-tibyan:84-84.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَيَوْمَ نَبْعَثُ مِنْ كُلِّ أُمَّةٍ شَهِيدًا ثُمَّ لَا يُؤْذَنُ لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَلَا هُمْ يُسْتَعْتَبُونَ (٨٤)).
The Exalted's saying (وَيَوْمَ نَبْعَثُ): i.e. "and remember", or "and warn them of".

ukberi-tibyan:90-90.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَأْمُرُ بِالْعَدْلِ وَالْإِحْسَانِ وَإِيتَاءِ ذِي الْقُرْبَى وَيَنْهَى عَنِ الْفَحْشَاءِ وَالْمُنْكَرِ وَالْبَغْيِ يَعِظُكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَذَكَّرُونَ (٩٠)).
The Exalted's saying (يَعِظُكُمْ): it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «يَنْهَى», or resumptive (mustaʾnaf).

ukberi-tibyan:91-91.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَأَوْفُوا بِعَهْدِ اللَّهِ إِذَا عَاهَدْتُمْ وَلَا تَنْقُضُوا الْأَيْمَانَ بَعْدَ تَوْكِيدِهَا وَقَدْ جَعَلْتُمُ اللَّهَ عَلَيْكُمْ كَفِيلًا إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَعْلَمُ مَا تَفْعَلُونَ (٩١)).
The Exalted's saying (بَعْدَ تَوْكِيدِهَا): the maṣdar (verbal noun) is annexed to its object, and its verb is وَكَّدَ; one also says أَكَّدَ تَأْكِيدًا.
And (وَقَدْ جَعَلْتُمُ): the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «تَنْقُضُوا».
It may also be a ḥāl from the agent of the maṣdar.

ukberi-tibyan:92-92.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَا تَكُونُوا كَالَّتِي نَقَضَتْ غَزْلَهَا مِنْ بَعْدِ قُوَّةٍ أَنْكَاثًا تَتَّخِذُونَ أَيْمَانَكُمْ دَخَلًا بَيْنَكُمْ أَنْ تَكُونَ أُمَّةٌ هِيَ أَرْبَى مِنْ أُمَّةٍ إِنَّمَا يَبْلُوكُمُ اللَّهُ بِهِ وَلَيُبَيِّنَنَّ لَكُمْ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ مَا كُنْتُمْ فِيهِ تَخْتَلِفُونَ (٩٢))
The Exalted's saying (أَنْكَاثًا): it is the plural of نِكْث, which means الْمَنْكُوث, i.e. "that which is untwisted"; it is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from غَزْلَهَا.
It may also be a second object according to the meaning, because the meaning of نَقَضَتْ is "she made (it into)".
And (تَتَّخِذُونَ) is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «تَكُونُوا», or from the pronoun in the preposition (the kāf), because the implied wording is "do not be resembling".
(أَنْ تَكُونَ): i.e. "for fear that there be".
(أُمَّةٌ): the noun of كَانَ, or its agent if you make كَانَ the complete (tāmma) one.
(هِيَ أَرْبَى): a clause in the position of the accusative as the khabar (predicate) of كَانَ, or in the position of the nominative as an adjective (ṣifa). «هِيَ» may not be a separating pronoun (faṣl), because the first noun is indefinite.
The hāʾ in «بِهِ» refers back to الرَّبْو, which is increase.

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Naḥl (The Bee)
Meccan, except for three verses at its end, for they were revealed between Mecca and Medina.
﷽
His words, Exalted is He: ﴿أتى أمْرُ اللَّهِ فَلا تَسْتَعْجِلُوهُ﴾: "أمر الله" (the command of Allah) is the various kinds of punishment that Allah promised them as requital for their disbelief. The proof of this is His words: ﴿حَتّى إذا جاءَ أمْرُنا وفارَ التَّنُّورُ﴾ [Hūd: 40], that is: what We had promised them came; and likewise His words: ﴿أتاها أمْرُنا لَيْلا أوْ نَهارًا فَجَعَلْناها حَصِيدًا﴾ [Yūnus: 24]. That is because they sought to hasten the punishment and thought the matter of the Hour slow in coming, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made known that it, in its nearness, is as something that has already come, as He said: ﴿اقْتَرَبَتِ السّاعَةُ وانْشَقَّ القَمَرُ﴾ [al-Qamar: 1], and as He said: ﴿وَما أمْرُ السّاعَةِ إلا كَلَمْحِ البَصَرِ﴾ [al-Naḥl: 77].

His words: ﴿سُبْحانَهُ وتَعالى عَمّا يُشْرِكُونَ﴾: its meaning is: His being declared free of all evil. This is how it has come in the ḥadīth from the Prophet ﷺ, and this is how the authorities on the language explained it; they said: its meaning is declaring Allah free of evil, and Allah's being clear of evil. The poet said:
؎أقُولُ لِما جاءَ في فَخْرِهِ سُبْحانَ مِن عَلْقَمَةَ الفاجِرِ
(I say, when his boasting reached me: "subḥāna" from ʿAlqama the wicked!)
that is: [I declare] clearness from him.

zajjaj:10-10.t:
His words: ﴿مِنهُ شَرابٌ ومِنهُ شَجَرٌ فِيهِ تُسِيمُونَ﴾: the meaning is that it makes grow the shrubs (الشجر) which the camels graze; everything that grows on the earth is "شجر". The poet said, describing horses:
؎نَعْلُفُها اللَّحْمَ إذا عَزَّ الشَّجَرْ والخَيْلُ في إطْعامِها اللَّحْمَ ضَرَرْ
(We feed them "meat" when vegetation is scarce, and for horses there is harm in feeding them meat.)
He means that they give the horses milk to drink when the land is barren.

His words: ﴿فِيهِ تُسِيمُونَ﴾, that is: you pasture [your herds]. One says "أسَمْتُ الإبل" when you have pastured the camels, and "قد سامت، تسوم، وهي سائمة" when they have grazed. That is taken from "السُّومة", which is a mark; its interpretation is that by their grazing they leave marks on the land.

zajjaj:14-14.t: His words: ﴿وَتَرى الفُلْكَ مَواخِرَ فِيهِ﴾: the meaning of "مواخر فيه" is: running, sailing along and cleaving the water.

zajjaj:15-15.t: ﴿وَألْقى في الأرْضِ رَواسِيَ أنْ تَمِيدَ بِكُمْ﴾: "رواسي" means firm mountains, fixed. "أن تميد": its meaning is: lest it sway (كراهة أن تميد). The meaning of "تميد" is: it does not stay still. One says "ماد الرجلُ يميد ميدًا" when he feels dizzy (as if turned about), and "المَيْدى" are those who become dizzy when they ride on the sea. "أن تميد" is in the position of the accusative (fī mawḍiʿ naṣb), a mafʿūl lahā (object of purpose) [Translator's note: so in the text, i.e. mafʿūl lahu]. ﴿وَأنْهارًا وسُبُلا﴾: the meaning is: and He placed in it firm mountains, rivers and ways, because the meaning of "ألقى في الأرض رواسي" is: He placed in it firm mountains; the proof of this is His words: ﴿والجِبالَ أوْتادًا﴾ [al-Nabaʾ: 7].

zajjaj:16-16.t: His words: ﴿وَبِالنَّجْمِ هم يَهْتَدُونَ﴾: "النجم" (the star) and "النجوم" (the stars) have one meaning, just as you say "كثر الدرهمُ في أيدي الناس" (the dirham has become plentiful in people's hands) and "كثرت الدراهمُ" (the dirhams have become plentiful). Allah, exalted be His praise, created the stars for several things: among them, that they were made an adornment for the lowest heaven; among them, that they were made missiles against the devils; among them, that people are guided by them; and among them, that the number of years and reckoning are known by them.

zajjaj:2-2.t: His words: ﴿يُنَـزِّلُ المَلائِكَةَ بِالرُّوحِ مِن أمْرِهِ﴾. It is also read: "تُنَزَّلُ الملائكةُ" (the angels are sent down). Several other forms are grammatically possible in it which I do not know to have been read: "يَنْزِلُ الملائكةُ", "يُنْزِلُ الملائكةَ" and "تَنَزَّلُ الملائكةُ". "بالروح": the Spirit (الروح) — and Allah knows best — is whatever of Allah's command contains life for souls, and guidance to Allah's command. The proof of this is His words: ﴿أنْ أنْذِرُوا أنَّهُ لا إلَهَ إلا أنا فاتَّقُونِ﴾; the meaning is: warn the people of disbelief and disobedience that there is no god but Me, that is: command them to affirm My oneness and not to associate anything with Me.

zajjaj:20-20.t: His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿والَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾; it is also read "تدعون من دون الله", with tāʾ and with yāʾ. ﴿لا يَخْلُقُونَ شَيْئًا وهم يُخْلَقُونَ﴾: by this are meant the idols which the Arabs used to worship.

zajjaj:21-21.t:
﴿أمْواتٌ غَيْرُ أحْياءٍ﴾, that is: and they are dead, not living.

His words: ﴿وَما يَشْعُرُونَ أيّانَ يُبْعَثُونَ﴾, that is: they do not perceive when they will be raised. "أيّان" is in the position of the accusative by His word "يُبعثون", but it is indeclinable (mabnī), without nunation, because it has the sense of the interrogative; so it does not take case inflection, just as "كم", "متى", "كيف" and "أين" do not take case inflection — except that the nūn was given fatḥa because of the meeting of two quiescent letters.

If someone asks: why was it not given kasra? It is said: the preferred choice, when there is an alif before the last quiescent letter, is to give it fatḥa, because the fatḥa is more akin to the alif and lighter with it. Sībawayh and al-Khalīl held that if you apply tarkhīm (truncation in the vocative) to a man named "أسحارّ", you say: "يا أسحارَّ — with doubled rāʾ — أقبل" (O Asḥārr, come!), giving the rāʾ fatḥa because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. Likewise you choose fatḥa next to [a letter with] fatḥa: you say, when giving the imperative of غضّ (to lower): "غُضَّ يا هذا" (lower [your gaze], you!).

zajjaj:23-23.t:
His words: ﴿لا جَرَمَ أنَّ اللَّهَ يَعْلَمُ ما يُسِرُّونَ وما يُعْلِنُونَ﴾: the meaning of "لا جرم" is: it is true that Allah knows, and it is established.

As for "لا", it is a rejection of their deed. The poet said:
؎وَلَقَدْ طَعَنْتُ أبا عُيَيْنَةَ طَعْنَةً جَرَمَتْ فَزارَةَ بَعْدَها أنْ يَغْضَبُوا
(I pierced Abū ʿUyayna with a thrust that, after it, made it due (جرمت) for Fazāra to be angry.)
The meaning is: it made Fazāra deserving of anger.

zajjaj:24-24.t: His words: ﴿وَإذا قِيلَ لَهم ماذا أنْـزَلَ رَبُّكم قالُوا أساطِيرُ الأوَّلِينَ﴾: "ما" is the mubtadaʾ (subject), and "ذا" is in the position of "الذي" (which); the meaning is: "What is it that your Lord has sent down?" "أساطير" is nominative (marfūʿ) as the answer, as if they said: "What He sent down is the tales of the ancients", that is: the lies of the ancients; its singular is "أُسطورة".

zajjaj:3-3.t: Then He made known what of His creation points to His oneness, and said: ﴿خَلَقَ السَّماواتِ والأرْضَ بِالحَقِّ تَعالى عَمّا يُشْرِكُونَ﴾: He is exalted above those whom they associated with Him, because they create nothing while they themselves are created.

zajjaj:4-4.t: His words: ﴿خَلَقَ الإنْسانَ مِن نُطْفَةٍ فَإذا هو خَصِيمٌ مُبِينٌ﴾: He has abbreviated here, and He mentioned the changing states of man in more than one place in the Quran.

zajjaj:5-5.t:
His words: ﴿والأنْعامَ خَلَقَها لَكم فِيها دِفْءٌ﴾: "الأنعام" is accusative (manṣūb) by an implied (muḍmar) verb; the meaning is: "He created the livestock — He created them", [the overt "خلقها"] explaining the implied verb. "الدِّفء" is what keeps them warm from their camel hair and their wool. "الأنعام" is most often used specifically of camels, but it can apply to camels, sheep and cattle. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, informed us that in livestock there is what keeps us warm, and He did not say: "In them there is for you what shelters you and keeps you warm against the cold", because what shields from heat shields from cold, and what shields from cold shields from heat. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said in another place: ﴿سَرابِيلَ تَقِيكُمُ الحَرَّ﴾ [al-Naḥl: 81], and it is understood that they also protect from cold. Likewise, when it is said ﴿لَكم فِيها دِفْءٌ﴾, it is understood that they shield from cold and shield from heat.

His words: ﴿وَمَنافِعُ﴾, that is: and their benefits: their milk, their urine and other things. ﴿وَمِنها تَأْكُلُونَ﴾ ﴿وَلَكم فِيها جَمالٌ حِينَ تُرِيحُونَ وحِينَ تَسْرَحُونَ﴾ [al-Naḥl: 6]: "الإراحة" is the camels' returning in the evening from their pastures to the place where they stay. ﴿وَحِينَ تَسْرَحُونَ﴾ [al-Naḥl: 6], that is: when you let them out to graze. In what a person owns there is beauty and adornment, as He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿المالُ والبَنُونَ زِينَةُ الحَياةِ الدُّنْيا﴾ [al-Kahf: 46]. Wealth (المال) is not restricted to silver and gold coin to the exclusion of other possessions; most of the wealth of the Arabs is camels, just as most of the wealth of the people of Basra is palm trees: they say "So-and-so's wealth is at such-and-such a place", meaning the palm trees.

zajjaj:7-7.t: His words: ﴿وَتَحْمِلُ أثْقالَكم إلى بَلَدٍ لَمْ تَكُونُوا بالِغِيهِ إلا بِشِقِّ الأنْفُسِ﴾: it is read with fatḥa and with kasra [i.e. بِشَقّ and بِشِقّ], that is: "If you had taken the trouble to reach it on something other than camels, that would have been hard for you."

zajjaj:8-8.t:
His words: ﴿والخَيْلَ والبِغالَ والحَمِيرَ لِتَرْكَبُوها﴾, that is: and He created horses, mules and donkeys for riding. Many people say that this verse indicates that the flesh of horses, mules and donkeys is forbidden, because He said about camels: ﴿وَمِنها تَأْكُلُونَ﴾ [al-Naḥl: 5], ﴿وَلِتَبْلُغُوا عَلَيْها حاجَةً في صُدُورِكُمْ﴾ [Ghāfir: 80]

while He said about horses: ﴿والخَيْلَ والبِغالَ والحَمِيرَ لِتَرْكَبُوها وزِينَةً﴾, and did not mention eating with regard to them. Some people said: if they had been made forbidden by this verse, the Prophet ﷺ would not have forbidden the flesh of domestic donkeys, and what the Quran indicated would have sufficed him. This is a mistake, because the Quran has indicated that wine is forbidden, and yet the Prophet ﷺ said: «"Wine itself has been forbidden"». So the Prophet ﷺ mentioned that what was forbidden in the Book is forbidden, as emphasis of it and additional clarification. "وزينةً" is accusative as a mafʿūl lahā (object of purpose) [Translator's note: so in the text, i.e. mafʿūl lahu]; the meaning is: "and He created them as adornment".

zajjaj:9-9.t:
His words: ﴿وَعَلى اللَّهِ قَصْدُ السَّبِيلِ ومِنها جائِرٌ﴾, that is: upon Allah is making clear the straight road to Him by proofs and demonstrations.

His words: ﴿وَمِنها جائِرٌ﴾: "جائر", that is: among the ways there are roads that do not lead straight to the truth.

His words: ﴿وَلَوْ شاءَ لَهَداكم أجْمَعِينَ﴾, that is: had Allah willed, He would have sent down a sign that compels creation to believe in Him; but He, Mighty and Majestic, guides whom He wills and calls to a straight path.

zajjaj:25-25.t:
His words: ﴿لِيَحْمِلُوا أوْزارَهم كامِلَةً يَوْمَ القِيامَةِ ومِن أوْزارِ الَّذِينَ يُضِلُّونَهم بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ﴾: these people used to turn away whoever wanted to follow the Prophet ﷺ, and when they were asked about what he had brought they said: "What he has brought is the tales of the ancients." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made known that by this they bear the sins of those who disbelieved because of what they said, and that this does not diminish anything of the sin of the follower.

His words: ﴿ألا ساءَ ما يَزِرُونَ﴾: "ما" is in the position of the nominative (fī mawḍiʿ rafʿ), just as you put [a noun] in the nominative with "نعم" and "بئس". The meaning is: "Evil is the thing — their burden (ساء الشيءُ وزرُهم)"; this is as you say "بئس الشيء" (evil is the thing).

zajjaj:26-26.t: His words: ﴿قَدْ مَكَرَ الَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ فَأتى اللَّهُ بُنْيانَهم مِنَ القَواعِدِ﴾, that is: from the pillars of the building that support it. ﴿فَخَرَّ عَلَيْهِمُ السَّقْفُ مِن فَوْقِهِمْ﴾: it is related that this is in the story of Nimrod son of Canaan: he built a tower with which to plot, and its roof fell upon him and his companions. Some said: this is a parable: their deeds which they did were made like one who builds a building that falls on him; so the harm of their deeds is upon them like the harm to the builder when his building falls on him.

zajjaj:27-27.t: His words: ﴿وَيَقُولُ أيْنَ شُرَكائِيَ الَّذِينَ كُنْتُمْ تُشاقُّونَ فِيهِمْ﴾; and "تُشاقُّونِ فيهم", with kasra on the nūn. We have explained the like of this. "شركائي" (My partners) is only a reporting of their own claim; Allah, exalted be His praise, has no partner. The meaning is: where are those who, in your claim, are My partners?

zajjaj:28-28.t:
﴿فَألْقَوُا السَّلَمَ ما كُنّا نَعْمَلُ مِن سُوءٍ﴾, that is: they offered submission. He mentioned "السَّلَم" — and "السلم" is peace — because He had mentioned opposition (المشاقّة); and peace stands over against opposition and enmity.

﴿ما كُنّا نَعْمَلُ مِن سُوءٍ﴾, that is: they said: "We were not doing any evil."

zajjaj:30-30.t:
﴿وَقِيلَ لِلَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا ماذا أنْـزَلَ رَبُّكُمْ﴾: "ما" and "ذا" are like a single thing, and the meaning is: "What thing has your Lord sent down?" ﴿قالُوا خَيْرًا﴾ is [accusative] as the answer to "ماذا"; the meaning is: He sent down good. ﴿لِلَّذِينَ أحْسَنُوا في هَذِهِ الدُّنْيا حَسَنَةٌ﴾: it is possible that these words were mentioned to show that by what they said they earned a good reward, and it is possible that it is an explanation of their saying "خيرًا". "حسنةٌ" in the nominative is the reading. "للذين أحسنوا في هذه الدنيا حسنةً" [in the accusative] is grammatically possible, but do not recite it that way; its possibility is that its meaning is that "He sent down good" — [that good] was made for those who did good in this world a good thing (حسنةً), that is: it was made for them a recompense in this world, before the Hereafter.

His words: ﴿وَلَدارُ الآخِرَةِ خَيْرٌ ولَنِعْمَ دارُ المُتَّقِينَ﴾: the meaning is: "and excellent indeed is the abode of the God-fearing — the abode of the Hereafter". But what explains His words "دار المتقين" is His words: ﴿جَنّاتُ عَدْنٍ يَدْخُلُونَها﴾ [al-Naḥl: 31], which is nominative by an implied "هي" (it is); as if, when you said "ولنعم دار المتقين", in answer to one asking, that is: which abode is this praised one?, you said: "Gardens of Eden which they enter." If you wish, you may make it nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the meaning would be: "Gardens of Eden — excellent is the abode of the God-fearing."

zajjaj:33-33.t:
His words: ﴿هَلْ يَنْظُرُونَ إلا أنْ تَأْتِيَهُمُ المَلائِكَةُ﴾, that is: to take their souls, or that what Allah promised them of His punishment should come.

His words: ﴿كَذَلِكَ فَعَلَ الَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ وما ظَلَمَهُمُ اللَّهُ﴾, that is: thus they did, and Allah's command came upon them with punishment: ﴿فَأصابَهم سَيِّئاتُ ما عَمِلُوا﴾ [al-Naḥl: 34].

zajjaj:35-35.t:
His words: ﴿وَقالَ الَّذِينَ أشْرَكُوا لَوْ شاءَ اللَّهُ ما عَبَدْنا مِن دُونِهِ مِن شَيْءٍ نَحْنُ ولا آباؤُنا ولا حَرَّمْنا مِن دُونِهِ مِن شَيْءٍ كَذَلِكَ فَعَلَ الَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ﴾: there is dispute over this verse and those like it, and the people of the Quran and the Sunna ought to establish the true explanation of it, because some people have claimed that whoever says this has disbelieved, and that whoever of the servants says that he does nothing except what Allah wills has disbelieved. This is a bad interpretation. Those people only disbelieved and lied because they used to say "Had Allah willed, we would not have worshipped anything besides Him" by way of mockery.

The proof of this is that the people of Shuʿayb said to Shuʿayb: ﴿أصَلاتُكَ تَأْمُرُكَ أنْ نَتْرُكَ ما يَعْبُدُ آباؤُنا أوْ أنْ نَفْعَلَ في أمْوالِنا ما نَشاءُ إنَّكَ لأنْتَ الحَلِيمُ الرَّشِيدُ﴾ [Hūd: 87]; had they said this to him believing it, they would have been believers; they only said it mockingly.

The community has agreed that if Allah had willed that none other than He be worshipped, with a will that compels to that, no one would have been able to do otherwise; but Allah, exalted be His praise, has charged the servants with worship, granted success to whom He loved to grant success, and led astray whom He loved to lead astray. These people said this as confirming what was said to them, [while] they were deniers, since there is consensus that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is able to compel the servants to obey Him. Allah made known that they are deniers, just as those before them denied, and said: ﴿فَهَلْ عَلى الرُّسُلِ إلا البَلاغُ المُبِينُ﴾, that is: the conveying through which they make clear that they are prophets.

zajjaj:36-36.t: His words: ﴿وَلَقَدْ بَعَثْنا في كُلِّ أُمَّةٍ رَسُولا أنِ اُعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ واجْتَنِبُوا الطّاغُوتَ﴾: Allah made known that He sent the messengers with the command to worship, while it [i.e. His decree] is behind the leading astray and the guidance. So He said: ﴿فَمِنهم مَن هَدى اللَّهُ ومِنهم مَن حَقَّتْ عَلَيْهِ الضَّلالَةُ﴾; this shows that had they said that [i.e. "Had Allah willed…"] believing it, they would have been truthful. Then He confirmed that, saying: ﴿إنْ تَحْرِصْ عَلى هُداهم فَإنَّ اللَّهَ لا يَهْدِي مَن يُضِلُّ﴾ [al-Naḥl: 37]. It has also been read: "فإن الله لا يُهدى من يُضِلّ" (whom Allah leads astray is not guided), as He said: ﴿مَن يُضْلِلِ اللَّهُ فَلا هادِيَ لَهُ﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 186]. There is a third way of reading it: "لا يَهدي من يَضِلّ" (He does not guide whoever goes astray), and it is the least of the three.

zajjaj:38-38.t: His words: ﴿بَلى وعْدًا عَلَيْهِ حَقًّا﴾: "وعدًا" is accusative (manṣūb), emphatic [i.e. an emphatic maṣdar]; the meaning is: "Yes indeed, Allah will raise them — a promise binding upon Him, true." ﴿لِيُبَيِّنَ لَهُمُ الَّذِي يَخْتَلِفُونَ فِيهِ﴾ [al-Naḥl: 39]: this is of two kinds. It may be attached to the raising, the meaning being: "Yes indeed, Allah will raise them in order to make clear to them" ﴿وَلِيَعْلَمَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا أنَّهم كانُوا كاذِبِينَ﴾ [al-Naḥl: 39]. Or it may be that "ليبين لهم الذي يختلفون فيه" is attached to His words: "And We have certainly sent to every community a messenger, to make clear to them their disagreement, and that before him they were in error."

zajjaj:40-40.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿إنَّما قَوْلُنا لِشَيْءٍ إذا أرَدْناهُ أنْ نَقُولَ لَهُ كُنْ فَيَكُونُ﴾: the reading is the nominative (فيكونُ), and it has also been read in the accusative (فيكونَ). The nominative is on the basis of "فهو" (then it…), in the sense: "Whatever Allah wills, it comes to be." The accusative is of two kinds: one is that His word "فيكونَ" is conjoined to "أن نقول", [i.e.] "أن نقول فيكونَ"; and it may be accusative as the answer to "كن". "قولُنا" is nominative as the mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is "أن نقول"; the meaning is: "Our word for every thing willed is only Our saying 'Be'." In this the servants are addressed with what they can comprehend; and whatever Allah wills comes to be in every case,

and in accordance with the speed He wills. Had He willed to create the world — the heavens and the earth — in the space of the blink of an eye, He would have been able to do so; but the servants were addressed with what they can comprehend. So Allah made known to them how easy for Him is the creation of things before they exist: He made known that whenever He wills a thing, it is, and that when He says "Be", it is — not that the thing existed before it was created; the meaning is only: when We will a thing, We say on account of it, "Be, O thing willed", and it comes to be, according to the measure of Allah's will. [This was said] because the people — I mean the idolaters — denied the resurrection, and swore by Allah their most solemn oaths that Allah would not raise up one who dies; that is the meaning of His words: ﴿وَكانُوا يُصِرُّونَ عَلى الحِنْثِ العَظِيمِ﴾ [al-Wāqiʿa: 46], that is: they used to swear that they would not be raised.

It has come in the exegesis that al-ḥinth (the sin) is polytheism, because whoever believes this — let alone swears to it — is a polytheist. So He, Majestic and Exalted, said: ﴿بَلى وعْدًا عَلَيْهِ حَقًّا﴾ [al-Naḥl: 38], that is: yes indeed, He will raise them — a promise binding upon Him, true. "حقًّا" is accusative, an emphatic maṣdar (verbal noun), because when He says "He will raise them" this indicates "He promised the raising with a promise (وعد بالبعث وعدًا)". [Translator's note: the explanation given fits "وعدًا" rather than "حقًّا"; translated as written.]

zajjaj:41-41.t:
His words: ﴿والَّذِينَ هاجَرُوا في اللَّهِ مِن بَعْدِ ما ظُلِمُوا لَنُبَوِّئَنَّهم في الدُّنْيا حَسَنَةً ولأجْرُ الآخِرَةِ أكْبَرُ لَوْ كانُوا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾: these were people whom the idolaters used to torture for holding to faith; among them were Ṣuhayb and Bilāl. That was because Ṣuhayb said to the people of Mecca: "I am an old man; if I am with you I will not benefit you, and if I am against you I will not harm you. Take my wealth and let me go." So he gave them his wealth and emigrated to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq said to him: "The sale has profited, O Ṣuhayb."

And ʿUmar said: "What an excellent man Ṣuhayb is! Had he not feared Allah, he would not have disobeyed Him." Its interpretation is: even if he were secure from His punishment and penalty, he would not abandon obedience nor incline to disobedience because of his being secure from punishment.

The meaning of ﴿لَنُبَوِّئَنَّهم في الدُّنْيا حَسَنَةً﴾ is: because they came to be with the Prophet ﷺ, entered Islam, and heard Allah's praise of them.

zajjaj:43-43.t: His words: ﴿وَما أرْسَلْنا مِن قَبْلِكَ إلا رِجالا نُوحِي﴾; also "يُوحى إليهم" (it is revealed to them) and "يُوحي إليهم" (He reveals to them). The first two readings are good, and the third is weak, because He mentioned "أرسلنا" (We sent); so for the wording to be "نوحي" (We reveal) or "يوحى" is better, because "نوحي" agrees with both wording and meaning, while "يوحى" is construed only according to the meaning, since the meaning is: "Allah sent none but men to whom revelation is given." This was said to them only because they said: "Why has an angel not been sent down to him, or a warner come with him?"

zajjaj:44-44.t:
So Allah, Majestic and Mighty, made known that the messengers are human beings, except that revelation is given to them. Then He made known how the soundness of their prophethood is to be inferred, and said: ﴿بِالبَيِّناتِ والزُّبُرِ﴾, that is: with the signs and proofs. "الزُّبُر" are books; its singular is "زبور". One says "زبرتُ الكتاب" and "ذبرته" (I wrote the book) with one meaning. Abū Dhuʾayb said:
؎عَرَفْتُ الدِّيارَ كَرَقْمِ الدَّوا ةِ يَذْبُرُها الكاتِبُ الحِمْيَرِيُّ
(I recognised the abodes, like the lines of the inkwell that the Ḥimyarite scribe writes.)
His words: ﴿فاسْألُوا أهْلَ الذِّكْرِ إنْ كُنْتُمْ لا تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ [al-Naḥl: 43]: there are two views on this. It was said: ask the people of the books, the people of the Torah and the Gospel — and the people of all the books acknowledge that the prophets were all human beings. It was also said: ﴿فاسْألُوا أهْلَ الذِّكْرِ﴾ [al-Naḥl: 43], that is: ask those of the People of the Book who have believed. It is possible — and Allah knows best — that it was said to them: ask everyone who is known for knowledge, whether he agrees with the people of this religion or differs from them. The proof that "the people of the Reminder (أهل الذكر)" are the people of the books is His words, Exalted is He: ﴿وَأنْـزَلْنا إلَيْكَ الذِّكْرَ لِتُبَيِّنَ لِلنّاسِ ما نُـزِّلَ إلَيْهِمْ﴾
and His words: ﴿وَهَذا ذِكْرٌ مُبارَكٌ أنْـزَلْناهُ﴾ [al-Anbiyāʾ: 50].

zajjaj:45-45.t: His words: ﴿أفَأمِنَ الَّذِينَ مَكَرُوا السَّيِّئاتِ أنْ يَخْسِفَ اللَّهُ بِهِمُ الأرْضَ﴾, that is: do they feel secure that He will not do to them what He did to the people of Lot and those of the past nations who were destroyed by the hastening of punishment in this world? ﴿أوْ يَأْتِيَهُمُ العَذابُ مِن حَيْثُ لا يَشْعُرُونَ﴾ is conjoined to "أن يخسف".

zajjaj:46-46.t: ﴿أوْ يَأْخُذَهم في تَقَلُّبِهِمْ﴾, that is: in their going about on their journeys and in all their other comings and goings.

zajjaj:47-47.t:
﴿أوْ يَأْخُذَهم عَلى تَخَوُّفٍ﴾, that is: or that He seize them after He has made them afraid, by destroying one group so that the one next to it becomes afraid. It was also said: "على تخوّف" means: by gradual diminishing (تنقّص); the meaning of diminishing is that He diminishes them in their wealth and their fruits until He destroys them. It is related that ʿUmar said: "I did not know the meaning of ﴿أوْ يَأْخُذَهم عَلى تَخَوُّفٍ﴾ until I heard the words of the poet:
؎تَخَوَّفَ السَّيْرُ مِنها تامِكًا قَرِدًا كَما تَخَوَّفَ عُودَ النَّبْعَةِ السَّفِنُ
(The journeying wore down (تخوّف) her high, compact hump, as the rasp wears down the wood of the nabʿ tree.)"
He is describing a she-camel, and how the journeying diminishes her hump after it had been firm and full.

His words: ﴿أوْ يَأْخُذَهم عَلى تَخَوُّفٍ فَإنَّ رَبَّكم لَرَءُوفٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾, that is: it is of His mercy that He grants respite and so makes room for repentance.

zajjaj:48-48.t:
His words: ﴿أوَلَمْ يَرَوْا إلى ما خَلَقَ اللَّهُ مِن شَيْءٍ يَتَفَيَّأُ ظِلالُهُ عَنِ اليَمِينِ﴾; it is also read "تتفيّأ ظلاله" (with tāʾ). ﴿سُجَّدًا﴾ is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَهم داخِرُونَ﴾: the meaning of "داخرون" is: humbled. This verse requires reflection, and its interpretation — and Allah knows best — is that everything Allah has created, of body, bone, flesh, star and tree, is submissive to Allah, prostrating; and the disbeliever, even if he disbelieves with his heart, his tongue and his intention, the very substance of his body, his bones and his flesh, and all trees and animals, are submissive to Allah, prostrating.

The proof of this is His words: ﴿ألَمْ تَرَ أنَّ اللَّهَ يَسْجُدُ لَهُ مَن في السَّماواتِ ومَن في الأرْضِ والشَّمْسُ والقَمَرُ والنُّجُومُ والجِبالُ والشَّجَرُ والدَّوابُّ وكَثِيرٌ مِنَ النّاسِ وكَثِيرٌ حَقَّ عَلَيْهِ العَذابُ﴾ [al-Ḥajj: 18]. It is related from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: the disbeliever prostrates to other than Allah, while his shadow prostrates to Allah. The interpretation of the shadow is the interpretation of the body that casts the shadow.

His words: ﴿وَهم داخِرُونَ﴾, that is: these things are innately disposed to obedience.

zajjaj:49-49.t:
His words: ﴿وَلِلَّهِ يَسْجُدُ ما في السَّماواتِ وما في الأرْضِ مِن دابَّةٍ والمَلائِكَةُ﴾: the meaning is: to Allah prostrates whatever is in the heavens, of angels, and whatever is in the earth, of creatures that move, and the angels — that is: the angels of the earth also prostrate. The proof that there are angels in the earth as well is His words, Exalted is He: ﴿ما يَلْفِظُ مِن قَوْلٍ إلا لَدَيْهِ رَقِيبٌ عَتِيدٌ﴾ [Qāf: 18]
and His words: ﴿لَهُ مُعَقِّباتٌ مِن بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ ومِن خَلْفِهِ يَحْفَظُونَهُ مِن أمْرِ اللَّهِ﴾ [al-Raʿd: 11]
and His words: ﴿وَإنَّ عَلَيْكم لَحافِظِينَ﴾ [al-Infiṭār: 10] ﴿كِرامًا﴾ [al-Infiṭār: 11].
